### 3.4.6.34 DNET-038 No MODULE lines with MULTIMOD

Cause: The specified lines were not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.35 DNET-039 Too many MODULE lines

Cause: The specified lines were incorrect in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.36 DNET-040 MODULE specified w/o MULTIMOD

Cause: A definition was incorrect in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

<!-- PDF page 409 -->

### 3.4.6.37 DNET-041 Required field missing

Cause: A definition was incorrect in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.38 DNET-042 DEVTYPE line absent/invalid

Cause: The specified line was not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.39 DNET-043 VENDORID line absent/invalid

Cause: The specified line was not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.40 DNET-044 PRODCODE line absent/invalid

Cause: The specified line was not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.41 DNET-045 No I/O mode line supplied

Cause: The specified line was not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.42 DNET-046 No PDTCODE line supplied

Cause: The specified line was not found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

<!-- PDF page 410 -->

### 3.4.6.43 DNET-047 DeviceNet motherboard not found

Cause: The DeviceNet motherboard is not plugged into the back plane.

Remedy: Turn off the controller and make sure the motherboard is properly seated into the back plane of the controller. Cold start the controller.

### 3.4.6.44 DNET-048 Multiple DEFAULT modes; ignored

Cause: The device definition file has too many I/O access modes designated as DEFAULT. Only one mode should be designated as DEFAULT.

Remedy: Remove the DEFAULT designation from all I/O access modes except one.

### 3.4.6.45 DNET-049 Device Name not found

Cause: Text based device definition does not have the device name for the device.

Remedy: Supply a device name along with the device definition and then use the text based device definition. The device name is required and is the primary identification for that definition.

### 3.4.6.46 DNET-050 Board or network warning: Bd %d

Cause: An problem has occurred with the specified daughter board or the DeviceNet network connected to it. The problem is not severe enough to disrupt communications, but should be addressed as soon as possible.

Remedy: Refer to the next DNET alarm posted in the alarm log for specific alarm recovery information.

### 3.4.6.47 DNET-051 Netwk comm errors: Bus warning

Cause: The DeviceNet scanner has detected an abnormal number of communications errors on the network. This message is a warning that the scanner may go offline if errors continue to occur at an abnormal rate.

Remedy: Check your network topology to ensure conformance with DeviceNet standards. Check that your network terminators are in place and properly connected. Check that your network power supply is able to handle all of the devices on the network. Ensure that you are using properly shielded cables and connectors.

<!-- PDF page 411 -->

### 3.4.6.48 DNET-052 Data line too long

Cause: The specified line was incorrect in the device definition file.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.49 DNET-053 Line above DEVICE line ignored

Cause: An extraneous line was found in a device definition file.

Remedy: Check the Standard Device Definition List to see if device types have been properly loaded. If not, contact FANUC America Corporation to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.50 DNET-054 All space in shared RAM used

Cause: There is no space left in the DeviceNet I/O buffer.

Remedy: Contact FANUC America Corporation to report the problem. Provide all details of the DeviceNet network, including number and type of devices, baud rates, MAC Ids, and network wiring configuration.

### 3.4.6.51 DNET-055 Board or network error: Bd %d

Cause: An error has occurred with the specified daughter board or the DeviceNet network connected to it.

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of the cause code (displayed immediately below this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.52 DNET-056 Network power lost

Cause: Power has been removed from the DeviceNet network.

Remedy: Check the cable connecting the daughter board to the DeviceNet network. Also, check the connection to the power source. Cycle power to the controller.

### 3.4.6.53 DNET-057 Network communications error

Cause: A network communications error has occurred on the network connected to the specified board.

<!-- PDF page 412 -->

Remedy: Check that the board's baud rate corresponds to that of the devices. Check cable connections to both the board and devices. Check that the proper device definitions are selected for the devices on the network and that parameters are correct for user-defined devices. Turn off both the controller and the DeviceNet network power, then cold start the controller.

### 3.4.6.54 DNET-058 Message queue overrun

Cause: The board has received more messages than it can handle at one time.

Remedy: The problem may be momentary; attempt to bring the board on-line again. If the problem persists, check that the board baud rate corresponds to the baud rate of the devices. Turn off then turn on the controller.

### 3.4.6.55 DNET-059 Message lost

Cause: The board has missed a message over the DeviceNet network.

Remedy: The problem might be momentary; attempt to bring the board on-line again. If the problem persists, check that the board baud rate corresponds to the baud rate of the devices. Turn off then turn on power to the controller.

### 3.4.6.56 DNET-060 Xmit timeout: Network flooded

Cause: The traffic on the DeviceNet network is too heavy for the board to communicate with the devices.

Remedy: Check that the board baud rate agrees with the baud rate of the devices. If no baud rate problem exists, turn off both the controller and the DeviceNet network power, then turn on both.

### 3.4.6.57 DNET-061 No other nodes on network

Cause: All of the devices expected by the board to be on the network appear to be disconnected to the network.

Remedy: Check cable connections to the board and to the devices. If a device has been disconnected, reconnect and press RESET on the teach pendant. Check that the board baud rate is the same as baud rate of the devices.

### 3.4.6.58 DNET-062 Bus off due to comm errors

Cause: The board is not communicating to the network because there are too many errors.

<!-- PDF page 413 -->

Remedy: Check that the baud rate of the board and of the devices is the same. Make sure that power is connected to the DeviceNet network. Press RESET on the teach pendant. If the problem persists, begin removing devices from the network; after each device is removed, press RESET. When the board is brought on-line, check the device configuration and the parameters of the device definition.

### 3.4.6.59 DNET-063 Device error: Bd %d MAC %d

Cause: An error has occurred with the device at the specified board number and MAC Id.

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy for the cause code (displayed directly beneath this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.60 DNET-064 Connection error

Cause: An error has occurred when attempting connection to the specified device.

Remedy: Check that the baud rate of the device agrees with the board baud rate. Check that the device is properly connected to the network; make sure the device is receiving power from the network. Inspect the device definition to see that the I/O type, access mode, and size of I/O are correct. Press RESET on the teach pendant to re-attempt connection.

### 3.4.6.61 DNET-065 Incorrect vendor Id

Cause: The vendor Id for the device, as specified in the device definition, is incorrect.

Remedy: Delete the device from the Device List. Check the device documentation for the correct vendor Id. Make corrections in the device definition and add the device to the Device List.

### 3.4.6.62 DNET-066 Incorrect product code

Cause: The product code for the device, as specified in the device definition, is incorrect.

Remedy: Delete the device from the Device List. Check the device documentation for the correct product code. Make corrections in the device definition and add the device to the Device List.

### 3.4.6.63 DNET-067 Incorrect device type

Cause: The device type for the device, as specified in the device definition, is incorrect.

Remedy: Delete the device from the Device List. Check the device documentation for the correct device type. Make corrections in the device definition and add the device to the Device List.

<!-- PDF page 414 -->

### 3.4.6.64 DNET-068 Device timeout

Cause: The connection to the specified device has timed out.

Remedy: Check the device's connection to the network. Make sure the device baud rate agrees with the board baud rate. Attempt to bring the device on-line by pressing RESET on the teach pendant.

### 3.4.6.65 DNET-069 Unknown error code %d

Cause: An unknown error has occurred with the specified device.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative. Make sure the error code number is noted and reported.

### 3.4.6.66 DNET-070 Connection allocation error

Cause: An error has occurred when attempting connection to the specified device.

Remedy: Check that the baud rate of the device agrees with the board baud rate. Check that the device is properly connected to the network; make sure the device is receiving power from the network. Inspect the device definition to see that the I/O type, access mode, and size of I/O are correct. Press RESET on the teach pendant to re-attempt connection.

### 3.4.6.67 DNET-071 Dup dbrd: Bd:%d Mbd:%s

Cause: You have two or more DeviceNet daughter boards with the same board number configuration.

Remedy: Re-configure the DIP switches on your daughter boards so that you no longer have duplicates. DIP switch configuration information is found in the User's Guide to the FANUC America Corporation DeviceNet Interface.

### 3.4.6.68 DNET-072 Found dupl. DNet daughterboard

Cause: This cause code is posted together with DNET-071 above to allow the user to easily identify the duplicate daughter board. Please see the Cause text for DNET-071 for more information.

Remedy: Please see the Remedy text for DNET-071 to fix this problem.

<!-- PDF page 415 -->

### 3.4.6.69 DNET-073 No match on mod type look-up

Cause: The system could not find the module type corresponding to a module on the specified device.

Remedy: View the module list for the device and delete or change the module in question. If this module was previously functional, cold start the controller and attempt to use this module type again. If the problem persists, perform an INIT start and re-load the DeviceNet Interface option.

### 3.4.6.70 DNET-074 Load only at ctrl start

Cause: An I/O configuration file (.IO file) containing DeviceNet configuration data was loaded at COLD START. The DeviceNet configuration data in this file is ignored.

Remedy: Reload the .IO file at controlled start.

### 3.4.6.71 DNET-076 $DN_DEV_DEFS array is full

Cause: There is no more room in the Defined Device List system variable.

Remedy: Delete any unneeded device definitions from the Defined Device List before adding a new one.

### 3.4.6.72 DNET-077 DNet I/O inactive at CTRL start

Cause: At controlled start, I/O data assigned to DeviceNet devices is not active.

Remedy: This message is for informational purposes only. To make DeviceNet I/O active, COLD start the controller.

### 3.4.6.73 DNET-078 No room for more devices

Cause: The system variable for storage of devices is full.

Remedy: If there are devices which are off-line, delete these devices unless they are required to be kept on the Device List. After entries in the device list are freed, new devices can be added.

### 3.4.6.74 DNET-079 Unknown dev type: Bd %d MAC %d

Cause: The device type used by this device is currently unknown to the system.

Remedy: This error occurs during the I/O restore. Cold start the controller, add a new device definition corresponding to the specified device, then add the device to the device list.

<!-- PDF page 416 -->

### 3.4.6.75 DNET-080 Loaded config too large

Cause: The previous I/O configuration contains too many modules, devices, or device definitions to be loaded.

Remedy: Make sure you have the same memory configuration as the system on which the I/O configuration was saved.

### 3.4.6.76 DNET-082 Press RESET to reconnect

Cause: This message appears when a board automatically restarts communication with a DeviceNet network, but some or all devices are not designated as autoreconnecting. Pressing RESET will attempt reconnection with these devices.

Remedy: Pressing RESET will attempt reconnection with the non-communicating devices and clear this message.

### 3.4.6.77 DNET-083 Board %d auto-restarted

Cause: A board which was previously in error state has automatically restarted communications with the DeviceNet network.

Remedy: This message is intended for user notification only and does not indicate the presence of an error situation.

### 3.4.6.78 DNET-084 Board reset failed: Bd %d

Cause: The command to reset the specified board has failed.

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy for the cause code (displayed directly beneath this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.79 DNET-085 Dev reset failed: Bd %d MAC %d

Cause: The command to reset the specified device has failed.

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy for the cause code (displayed directly beneath this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.80 DNET-086 Stop scan cmd failed: Bd %d

Cause: The specified board is unable to acknowledge the stop-scanning command.

<!-- PDF page 417 -->

Remedy: Check DeviceNet connection to the board, as well as DeviceNet power to the network.
If board is already in ERROR state, this error can be disregarded.

### 3.4.6.81 DNET-087 Bd offline cmd failed: Bd %d

Cause: The board is not acknowledging the command to take it off-line.

Remedy: Check DeviceNet connection to the board, as well as DeviceNet power to the network.
If the board is already in the ERROR state, this error can be disregarded.

### 3.4.6.82 DNET-088 Ignored: Bd %d MAC %d Slot %d

Cause: The system does not recognize the module type of the module being loaded.

Remedy: Make sure the device definition data files are the same between the current system being
loaded and the system on which the I/O configuration was saved. Contact FANUC America
Corporation for the correct definition files.

### 3.4.6.83 DNET-089 Can't specify POLL and STROBE

Cause: The data file contains lines which specify both POLL access and STROBE access for
the same device.

Remedy: Contact FANUC America Corporation to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.84 DNET-090 Can't STROBE w/ num outs > 0

Cause: The device definition file specifies a strobed-access device but the number of outputs
is not equal to zero.

Remedy: Contact FANUC America Corporation to obtain the correct device definition files.

### 3.4.6.85 DNET-091 Input size error

Cause: The number of inputs specified in the device definition for this device does not match the
number expected by the scanner when it communicates with the device.

Remedy: Delete the device, correct the device definition, then re-add the device to the device list.

<!-- PDF page 418 -->

### 3.4.6.86 DNET-092 Output size error

Cause: The number of outputs specified in the device definition for this device does not match the number expected by the scanner when it communicates with the device.

Remedy: Delete the device, correct the device definition, then re-add the device to the device list.

### 3.4.6.87 DNET-093 Error reading vendor ID

Cause: The scanner board encountered an error while trying to read the device's vendor ID.

Remedy: Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Check also the device's connection to the network.

### 3.4.6.88 DNET-094 Error reading device type

Cause: The scanner board encountered an error while trying to read the device's device type.

Remedy: Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Check also the device's connection to the network.

### 3.4.6.89 DNET-095 Error reading product code

Cause: The scanner board encountered an error while trying to read the device's product code.

Remedy: Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Check also the device's connection to the network.

### 3.4.6.90 DNET-096 Error setting packet rate

Cause: The scanner board encountered an error while trying to set the communication packet rate for this device.

Remedy: Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Check also the device's connection to the network. Reset the device if possible.

### 3.4.6.91 DNET-097 Connection sync fault

Cause: The board was unable to achieve synchronization in the connection with the specified device.

Remedy: Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Check also the device's connection to the network. Reset the device if possible.

<!-- PDF page 419 -->

### 3.4.6.92 DNET-098 BROWSE failed

Cause: The BROWSE operation failed.

Remedy: Check that the board status is ONLINE. Check that the board is not the only node.

### 3.4.6.93 DNET-100 NULL cmd error ret'd by board

Cause: The board returned an error response to the command.

Remedy: This is a system error. Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC or FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.94 DNET-101 CMD cmd error ret'd by board

Cause: The board returned an error response to the command.

Remedy: This is a system error. Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC or FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.95 DNET-102 Invalid board MAC Id

Cause: The board's MAC Id is not between 0 and 63.

Remedy: Check the Board Detail screen to see if the board's MAC Id is between 0 - 63, inclusive. If it is not, change the MAC Id to a valid value and press RESET on the teach pendant. If the MAC Id appears valid, cold start the controller. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.96 DNET-103 Invalid board baud rate

Cause: The board's baud rate is not one of: 125 KB, 250 KB, or 500 KB.

Remedy: Check the Board Detail screen to see if the board's baud rate is one of the above values. If it is not, change the baud rate to a valid value and press RESET on the teach pendant. If the baud rate appears valid, cold start the controller. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.97 DNET-104 Duplicate MAC Id error

Cause: The specified device has the same MAC Id as another device on the network.

<!-- PDF page 420 -->

Remedy: Check that no other devices have the same MAC Id, particularly those connected to a different master on the same network. Change the MAC Id of the offending device at both the device and on the Device List, and attempt to bring it on-line. If the problem persists, cold start the controller and try again. If the problem continues, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.98 DNET-105 Duplicate device error

Cause: There was an attempt to add a device to the board's device list that was a duplicate of a device already on the list.

Remedy: If the desired device is already on the network and a second one is not being added, you may ignore the error. Otherwise, change the MAC Id of one of the duplicate devices.

### 3.4.6.99 DNET-106 Device not found error

Cause: A device expected to be on the network was not found.

Remedy: Check that the device is connected to the network. Check that the device baud rate matches the board baud rate. Reset the device if possible. Cycle power to the controller. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.4.6.100 DNET-107 Bus offline error

Cause: The board could not perform an operation because the bus was off-line.

Remedy: Press RESET on the teach pendant to attempt to bring the board on-line. If the problem persists, cycle power to the controller. If the problem continues to persist, cycle power to the DeviceNet network.

### 3.4.6.101 DNET-108 Scanner active error

Cause: The board could not perform an operation because the it is actively scanning the network.

Remedy: Take the board off-line and re-attempt the operation.

### 3.4.6.102 DNET-109 Bus not offline error

Cause: The board could not perform an operation because the bus is not off-line.

Remedy: Take the board off-line and re-attempt the operation.

<!-- PDF page 421 -->

### 3.4.6.103 DNET-110 Error: board scanning

Cause: The board could not perform an operation because the it is actively scanning the network.

Remedy: Take the board off-line and re-attempt the operation.

### 3.4.6.104 DNET-111 Error: board not scanning

Cause: The board could not perform an operation because the it is not actively scanning the network.

Remedy: Bring the board on-line and re-attempt the operation.

### 3.4.6.105 DNET-112 Board not ready; pls. wait

Cause: An attempt to bring the board on-line was unsuccessful because the board was busy.

Remedy: Wait ten seconds and re-attempt to bring the board on-line. If the problem persists, check board connection to the network, baud rate, and network power.

### 3.4.6.106 DNET-114 Bus fault error detected

Cause: The board has detected a fault on the DeviceNet network, and cannot communicate with devices.

Remedy: Check that the baud rate of the board matches the baud rate of all devices on the network. Also, check that power is being supplied to the network. If the problem persists, cycle power to the controller, and then to the network if the problem continues.

### 3.4.6.107 DNET-115 Invalid I/O connection attempt

Cause: A device does not support the requested I/O connection(s). and cannot communicate with devices.

Remedy: Check the device documentation to ensure that the requested I/O connection is supported.

### 3.4.6.108 DNET-119 Dup. MAC Ack Fault

Cause: This is an Ack Fault. No acknowledge was received during the Duplicate MAC ID sequence.

<!-- PDF page 422 -->

**Remedy:** Check whether the interface is not the only node on the network. Also check the baud rate of the interface and make sure it is the network baud rate. Finally, check the physical wiring of the network.

### 3.4.6.109 DNET-120 Dev online err: Bd %d MAC %d

**Cause:** The device at the specified board number and MAC Id cannot be brought on-line.

**Remedy:** Make sure the device is properly connected to the network. Check the device's MAC Id and baud rate configuration. Check the board's baud rate configuration on the Board Detail screen. Check the board's network connection. Cold Start the controller.

### 3.4.6.110 DNET-121 Device not ready: Bd %d MAC %d

**Cause:** When a device has been added to a scan list, it cannot be brought online without cycling power to the controller.

**Remedy:** Cycle power to the controller. You will then be able to bring the device online.

### 3.4.6.111 DNET-122 Device error: Bd %d MAC %d

**Cause:** An error has occurred with the device at the specified board number and MAC Id.

**Remedy:** Refer to the Cause and Remedy for the cause code (displayed directly beneath this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.112 DNET-123 Dev reset failed: Bd %d MAC %d

**Cause:** The command to reset the specified device has failed.

**Remedy:** Refer to the Cause and Remedy for the cause code (displayed directly beneath this error code on the teach pendant).

### 3.4.6.113 DNET-124 Device not autorec: Bd %d MAC %d

**Cause:** This message appears when a board automatically restarts communication with a DeviceNet network, but some or all devices are not designated as autoreconnecting. Pressing RESET will attempt reconnection with these devices.

**Remedy:** Pressing RESET will attempt reconnection with the non-communicating devices and clear this message.

<!-- PDF page 423 -->

### 3.4.6.114 DNET-125 Slave Conn. Idle: Bd %d

Cause: The slave connection of the specified board is idle The remote Master has not yet connected to the slave connection.

Remedy: Make sure the remote Master is online and configured properly.

### 3.4.6.115 DNET-130 Invalid parameter

Cause: An invalid parameter has been specified for a DeviceNet KAREL built-in.

Remedy: Refer to the cause code to determine which parameter is invalid.

### 3.4.6.116 DNET-131 Invalid board number

Cause: The specified board number is invalid.

Remedy: Make sure the board number is an integer between 1 and 4, inclusive.

### 3.4.6.117 DNET-132 Invalid MAC ID

Cause: The specified MAC ID is invalid.

Remedy: Make sure the MAC ID is an integer between 0 and 63, inclusive.

### 3.4.6.118 DNET-133 I/O Size mismatch

Cause: This indicates that there is a user device definition on the system that matches the one supplied using text-based definitions except for the I/O size. A match is indicated by name, vendor id, device type, product code and mode of operation.

Remedy: This error is for display only. No action is required.

### 3.4.6.119 DNET-134 Mode mismatch

Cause: The text-based device definition has matched with an existing user definition on the robot except for the mode of operation. A match is indicated by name, vendor id, device type and product code.

Remedy: This error is for display only. No action is required.

<!-- PDF page 424 -->

### 3.4.6.120 DNET-135 Analog size mismatch

Cause: There is a user definition on the system that matches one of the entries in the text-based user definition except the size of analog input/outputs. A match is indicated by name, vendor id, product code, device type and mode of operation.

Remedy: This is for display only. No action is required.

### 3.4.6.121 DNET-136 Name does not match

Cause: Please check MD:DNDEF.DG

Remedy: Please check MD:DNDEF.DG

### 3.4.6.122 DNET-137 Name and Analog do not match

Cause: The text-based device definition matches one that exists on the controller, except for the name and number of analog points. Any entry that has the same vendor id, product code, device type and mode of operation is considered a perfect match.

Remedy: This error is for display only. No action is required.

### 3.4.6.123 DNET-138 IDNS unsupported H/W, Bd %d

Cause: A DevicNet channel has been configured for safety. A safety DeviceNet channel requires DN4 hardware. The detected hardware is not supported for a safety channel.

Remedy: Use DN4 DeviceNet hardware or disable safety on this channel.

### 3.4.7 DPMO Alarm Code

### 3.4.7.1 DPMO-001 Offset Line Mismatch

Cause: Motion line mismatches offset motion line

Remedy: Check offset provider correct the application setting

### 3.4.7.2 DPMO-002 Cyc Offset Limit Err

Cause: Cyc Offset Limit Err

<!-- PDF page 425 -->

**Remedy:** increase the motion segment length or slow the speed

### 3.4.7.3 DPMO-003 Offset is ignored

**Cause:** Offset has be applied during interpolating stage

**Remedy:** none

### 3.4.7.4 DPMO-004 Offset is too late

**Cause:** Offset arrives beyond allowed window time

**Remedy:** Reset the window time or Check the application

### 3.4.7.5 DPMO-005 NO Zero Dist Motion

**Cause:** Motion segment length is too short

**Remedy:** Change the taught points

### 3.4.7.6 DPMO-006 NO Joint Motion

**Cause:** Joint motion is not supported

**Remedy:** Change to Linear Motion

### 3.4.7.7 DPMO-007 NO Circular Motion

**Cause:** Circular motion is not supported

**Remedy:** Chang to Linear Motion

### 3.4.7.8 DPMO-008 NO Group Motion

**Cause:** Group motion is not supported

**Remedy:** Change to Linear Motion

<!-- PDF page 426 -->

### 3.4.7.9 DPMO-009 NO CD Motion

Cause: CD motion is not supported

Remedy: Don't use CD motion

### 3.4.7.10 DPMO-010 DPM software error (PMPT)

Cause: Internal system error (PMPT)

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.4.7.11 DPMO-011 DPM software error

Cause: Internal system error (PMPT)

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.4.7.12 DPMO-012 DPM software error (SRIF)

Cause: Internal system error (SRIF)

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.4.7.13 DPMO-013 NO Sysvar Loaded

Cause: Internal system error

Remedy: reload the option

### 3.4.7.14 DPMO-014 Dest Offset Limit Error

Cause: Dest Offset Limit Error

Remedy: Check Limit Setting Check offset

### 3.4.7.15 DPMO-015 Analog IN not set

Cause: AIN is not set

Remedy: Set AIN port

<!-- PDF page 427 -->

### 3.4.7.16 DPMO-016 Group IN not set

Cause: GIN is not set

Remedy: Set GIN ports

### 3.4.7.17 DPMO-017 Bump IN not set

Cause: Bump DIN is not set

Remedy: Set Bump DIN port

### 3.4.7.18 DPMO-018 Analog IN not calibrated

Cause: Analog not calibrated

Remedy: calibrate analog input set $cal_done to TRUE

### 3.4.7.19 DPMO-019 Group IN not calibrated

Cause: Group DIN needs scalling

Remedy: Set Group DIN scalling

### 3.4.7.20 DPMO-020 Inline DPM is not set

Cause: Inline DPM is not allowed

Remedy: Set $dpm_cfg.$dpm_inline to TRUE

### 3.4.7.21 DPMO-021 WJNT is not supported

Cause: WJNT is not allowed

Remedy: don't use WJNT motion

### 3.4.7.22 DPMO-022 UTOOL is changed

Cause: UTOOL change is not allowed

Remedy: don't change UTOOL

<!-- PDF page 428 -->

### 3.4.7.23 DPMO-023 Wrong Schedule Number

Cause: Schedule number is out of range

Remedy: Check the setup and re-power the controller

### 3.4.7.24 DPMO-024 Can't control orientation

Cause: Orientation offset is not supported

Remedy: set $dpm_cfg.$ori_ctl to FALSE

### 3.4.7.25 DPMO-025 Can't enb ori_ctl for PATH

Cause: Orientation control does not support TPATH and PATH relative

Remedy: set $dpm_cfg.$ori_ctl to FALSE

### 3.4.7.26 DPMO-026 Fail to create offset frame

Cause: Invalid robot move direction

Remedy: Use TOOL or UFRAM

### 3.4.7.27 DPMO-027 Mismatch DPM type

Cause: Mismatch DPM type

Remedy: Check DPM type of CFG and SCHED

### 3.4.7.28 DPMO-028 Buffer is too short

Cause: Buffer is too short

Remedy: Increase buffer size

### 3.4.7.29 DPMO-029 No learn path found

Cause: Can't find learn path data

Remedy: need to learn path

<!-- PDF page 429 -->

### 3.4.7.30 DPMO-030 Path learn buffer short

Cause: Short learn path buffer

Remedy: increase track speed

### 3.4.7.31 DPMO-031 CD - non CD transition in tracking

Cause: CD-non CD transition in tracking

Remedy: Add/remove COORD instruction

### 3.4.7.32 DPMO-032 Path Offset Limit Error

Cause: Offset greater than max path offset

Remedy: Check max path offset setting Check offset

### 3.4.8 DTBR Alarm Code

### 3.4.8.1 DTBR-001 host name is null string

Cause: Specified host name is null string.

Remedy: Please check the 1st argument. If SR is used, please check the value.

### 3.4.8.2 DTBR-002 RPC Call timed out

Cause: Communication with specified host took time and timeout happend.

Remedy: Please make sure newtwork is working properly. If there is heavy trafic, please reduce it.

### 3.4.8.3 DTBR-003 Connection failed

Cause: Ethernet connection to specified host failed

Remedy: Please make sure newtwork is working properly. PING should always work for specified remote host

<!-- PDF page 430 -->

### 3.4.8.4 DTBR-014 Bad variable or register index (%s^7)

Cause: Specified register or position register does not exist on remote host.

Remedy: Please check parameter. Please check valid range of index for specified host.

### 3.4.8.5 DTBR-015 Illegal group number(%s^7)

Cause: Specified group does not exist on remote host.

Remedy: Please check parameter. Please check valid range of group number for specified host.

## 3.5 E

### 3.5.1 ELOG Alarm Code

#### 3.5.1.1 ELOG-009 call a service man

Cause: A system error has occurred.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that let to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

#### 3.5.1.2 ELOG-011 Power off, if you want to recover.

Cause: A system error has occurred.

Remedy: Perform a Cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that let to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

#### 3.5.1.3 ELOG-012 A system error has been occurred.

Cause: A system error has occurred.

<!-- PDF page 431 -->

Remedy: Perform a cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that let to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.5.2 EVIO Alarm Code

#### 3.5.2.1 EVIO-001 Invalid data type passed to %s

Cause: A parameter passed into the program was the wrong data type

Remedy: Verify the parameters passed into the program

#### 3.5.2.2 EVIO-003 Invalid argument %s call

Cause: An invalid argument was passed into the program.

Remedy: Verify all arguments passed into this program.

#### 3.5.2.3 EVIO-004 Error reading status in %s

Cause: The status was not returned by the vision system.

Remedy: Verify the command sent was correct, and the vision system is sending correct data to the robot.

#### 3.5.2.4 EVIO-005 Returned arguments from %s were incorrect

Cause: The values returned by the vision system did not match what the program was expecting.

Remedy: Verify the data from the vision system is correct, and it matches the format in the external vision interface manual.

#### 3.5.2.5 EVIO-006 Error setting position register for %s

Cause: The program failed to set the position register with the data returned from the vision system.

<!-- PDF page 432 -->

Remedy: Verify the position register passed into this program is a valid position register.

### 3.5.2.6 EVIO-007 Error setting register for %s

Cause: The program failed to set the numeric register.

Remedy: Verify the register passed into this program is a valid numeric register.

### 3.5.2.7 EVIO-008 Error executing %s

Cause: Typically this is caused by the socket messaging communication failing to open the connection.

Remedy: Verify the socket messaging tag is configured properly as per the manual. Verify multiple instances of the program were not attempted to run concurrently.

### 3.5.2.8 EVIO-009 No data returned for %s

Cause: The vision system did not return any data.

Remedy: Verify the command sent to the vision system is the correct syntax, and the vision system properly handles this command.

### 3.5.2.9 EVIO-010 %s failed to read return string

Cause: The program could not read a return string from the vision system.

Remedy: Verify communication is correct, and verify the vision system can handle this type of command.

### 3.5.2.10 EVIO-011 Invalid tagID %s

Cause: The tag ID was not in the range of 1-8.

Remedy: Verify the first argument to this program is 1-8

### 3.5.2.11 EVIO-012 Error connecting to server

Cause: The program failed to connect to the vision system.

Remedy: Verify network communication, verify socket messaging is correctly configured.

<!-- PDF page 433 -->

### 3.5.2.12 EVIO-013 %s not ready, no status string returned

Cause: The vision system is busy.

Remedy: Try again once the vision system is not busy.

### 3.5.2.13 EVIO-014 %s returned FAILURE

Cause: The command returned a non-zero value

Remedy: See the manual for the vision system to determine how to remedy the error indicated in the status register.

### 3.5.2.14 EVIO-015 Error doing RUN_FIND

Cause: Typically this is caused by the socket messaging communication failing to open the connection.

Remedy: Verify the socket messaging tag is configured properly as per the manual. Verify multiple instances of the program were not attempted to run concurrently.

### 3.5.2.15 EVIO-016 Position register argument 0 passed in

Cause: The PR index was 0

Remedy: This may be desired behavior. If it is not, then modify the argument passed into this program.

### 3.5.2.16 EVIO-017 Could not set project name

Cause: The external vision system failed to set the project name.

Remedy: See the vision system manual and the status value to determine the root cause and remedy.

### 3.5.2.17 EVIO-018 No MVS command sent

Cause: The command argument was blank for MVS_SEND_CMD.

Remedy: Enter a command for the string argument to send.

<!-- PDF page 434 -->

### 3.5.2.18 EVIO-019 Invalid MVS command received

Cause: An invalid command was sent to the machine vision system.

Remedy: Verify the parameters of the command.

### 3.5.2.19 EVIO-020 Both arrays are in use

Cause: More than 2 vision data buffers are in use concurrently

Remedy: Do not run more than 2 external vision processes at the same time

### 3.5.2.20 EVIO-021 Failed to send command to MVS

Cause: Sending the message to the vision system failed.

Remedy: Verify arguments passed into this program.

### 3.5.2.21 EVIO-022 Failed to read string register

Cause: Failed to read the string register passed into this program.

Remedy: Verify the string register argument is a valid string register. The argument is an integer value, not the SR[] itself

### 3.5.2.22 EVIO-023 Failed to connect to MVS

Cause: Could not connect to the machine vision system.

Remedy: Verify the socket messaging setup is correct. Verify the IP addresses are correct and tag is configured correctly.

### 3.5.2.23 EVIO-024 Error received unknown command in STATUS

Cause: The vision system did not recognize the command sent.

Remedy: Verify the command sent is valid syntax for the system.

### 3.5.2.24 EVIO-025 Cannot receive message from the MVS in %s

Cause: The machine vision system did not send a return string.

<!-- PDF page 435 -->

Remedy: This may be caused by the vision system refusing commands, possibly because it is busy processing another command. Check the status register value for more information.

### 3.5.2.25 EVIO-026 Number found is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The number of found results is not what was expected.

Remedy: Verify the vision process is accurate, and the number expected is what the vision system is seeing.

### 3.5.2.26 EVIO-027 Number of measurements is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The number of measurements for the vision process is invalid.

Remedy: Verify the number of measurements the vision process is expected to return, and the vision process is set up correctly.

### 3.5.2.27 EVIO-028 Model ID is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The model ID is not valid.

Remedy: Verify the model ID from the vision process, and the correct model ID argument is passed into GET_LOCATE.

### 3.5.2.28 EVIO-029 Position results is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The position data returned from the vision system is invalid.

Remedy: Verify the data output by the vision system matches the format expected, as per the external vision interface option manual.

### 3.5.2.29 EVIO-030 Measurement data is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The measurement data is not valid.

Remedy: Verify the data output by the vision system matches the format expected, as per the external vision interface option manual.

### 3.5.2.30 EVIO-031 Second string packet is invalid in GET_LOCATE

Cause: The second set of 254 characters from the vision system was invalid.

<!-- PDF page 436 -->

Remedy: Retry the process. If error persists, verify the command string is correct.

### 3.5.2.31 EVIO-032 Results exceeded 100

Cause: There were more than 100 vision results.

Remedy: Reduce the number of results to less than 100 Only up to 100 results at a time are supported.

### 3.5.2.32 EVIO-033 Invalid result index requested

Cause: This result index does not exist in the results.

Remedy: Verify the result values and the result index requested

### 3.6 F

### 3.6.1 FILE Alarm Code

### 3.6.1.1 FILE-001 Device not ready

Cause: Specified file device is not ready.

Remedy: Check if the device is mounted and ready to use. Check if the device name is correct.

### 3.6.1.2 FILE-002 Device is Full

Cause: Device is full. There is no more space to store data on the device.

Remedy: Delete any unnecessary files or change to a new device.

### 3.6.1.3 FILE-003 Device is protected

Cause: Device is protected. So, you cannot write to the device.

Remedy: Release the device protection.

<!-- PDF page 437 -->

### 3.6.1.4 FILE-004 Device not assigned

Cause: The device is not assigned. The specified device is not recognized by the system. If using RD, then $FILE_MAXSEC is set to 0.

Remedy: If using RD, set $FILE_MAXSEC > 0, or else a system error will occur.

### 3.6.1.5 FILE-005 Device not mounted

Cause: Device is not mounted. You should mount the device before using it.

Remedy: Mount the correct file device.

### 3.6.1.6 FILE-006 Device is already mounted

Cause: You tried to mount the device which had been already mounted.

Remedy: Mount device only once.

### 3.6.1.7 FILE-007 Illegal device number

Cause: Illegal device number is used.

Remedy: This is an internal error. Check the validity of the device number.

### 3.6.1.8 FILE-008 Illegal device name

Cause: Device name contains an illegal character.

Remedy: Check spelling and validity of device name.

### 3.6.1.9 FILE-009 Illegal logical unit number

Cause: Illegal LUN is used.

Remedy: This is an internal error. Check the validity of the logical unit number.

### 3.6.1.10 FILE-010 Directory not found

Cause: Specified directory does not exist

<!-- PDF page 438 -->

**Remedy:** Check validity of directory name.

### 3.6.1.11 FILE-011 Directory full

**Cause:** Directory is full. You tried to create a file in the root directory which exceeded the maximum number of files allowed on the device.

**Remedy:** Delete unnecessary files in the root directory.

### 3.6.1.12 FILE-012 Directory is protected

**Cause:** You tried to write to a write protected directory.

**Remedy:** Release the protection to the directory.

### 3.6.1.13 FILE-013 Illegal directory name

**Cause:** Directory name contains an illegal character.

**Remedy:** Check spelling of directory name.

### 3.6.1.14 FILE-014 File not found

**Cause:** The specified file was not found.

**Remedy:** Check that the file exists and that the file name was spelled correctly.

### 3.6.1.15 FILE-015 File is protected

**Cause:** You tried to access a protected file.

**Remedy:** Release the protection from file.

### 3.6.1.16 FILE-017 File not open

**Cause:** You tried to access a file which is not open.

**Remedy:** Open the file before accessing.

<!-- PDF page 439 -->

### 3.6.1.17 FILE-018 File is already opened

Cause: You tried to create/delete/rename a file which is already opened.

Remedy: Close file before such operations.

### 3.6.1.18 FILE-019 File is locked

Cause: You tried to access a file which is locked.

Remedy: Release the lock.

### 3.6.1.19 FILE-020 Illegal file size

Cause: File size is invalid.

Remedy: Change file size to be correct.

### 3.6.1.20 FILE-021 End of file

Cause: End of file was detected.

Remedy: This is a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

### 3.6.1.21 FILE-022 Illegal file name

Cause: File name contains an illegal character.

Remedy: Check spelling of file name.

### 3.6.1.22 FILE-023 Illegal file number

Cause: File number is illegal.

Remedy: Use a valid file number which is the ID returned from an open request.

### 3.6.1.23 FILE-024 Illegal file type

Cause: File type contains an illegal character.

Remedy: Check the spelling and validity of the file type.

<!-- PDF page 440 -->

### 3.6.1.24 FILE-025 Illegal protection code

Cause: File protection code is illegal.

Remedy: Check if the protection code is correct.

### 3.6.1.25 FILE-026 Illegal access mode

Cause: File access mode is illegal.

Remedy: Check if the access mode is correct.

### 3.6.1.26 FILE-027 Illegal attribute

Cause: File attribute in the SET_ATTRIBUTE request is illegal.

Remedy: Check that attribute specified is valid.

### 3.6.1.27 FILE-028 Illegal data block

Cause: Data block is broken which is used in FIND_NEXT request.

Remedy: You should keep the data block which is returned from the previous FIND_FIRST or FIND_NEXT request.

### 3.6.1.28 FILE-029 Command is not supported

Cause: Illegal request command is specified.

Remedy: Check if the request code is corect.

### 3.6.1.29 FILE-030 Device lun table is full

Cause: Device management table is full.

Remedy: Dismount any unnecessary devices.

### 3.6.1.30 FILE-031 Illegal path name

Cause: Path name contains an illegal character.

<!-- PDF page 441 -->

Remedy: Check if the path name is correct.

### 3.6.1.31 FILE-032 Illegal parameter

Cause: Illegal parameter is detected.

Remedy: Check that all parameters for the request are valid.

### 3.6.1.32 FILE-033 System file buffer full

Cause: File management buffer is full.

Remedy: Close unnecessary files.

### 3.6.1.33 FILE-034 Illegal file position

Cause: Illegal file position is specified.

Remedy: Check that the file position parameter from SEEK request is positive and not beyond the end of file.

### 3.6.1.34 FILE-035 Device not formatted

Cause: You tried to access a unformatted device.

Remedy: Format the device before using it.

### 3.6.1.35 FILE-036 File already exist

Cause: You tried to rename a file to an already existing file name.

Remedy: Change the new file name to be unique or delete the existing file.

### 3.6.1.36 FILE-037 Directory not empty

Cause: You tried to remove a subdirectory which contains some files or directories.

Remedy: Remove all files and directories in the subdirectory before removing subdirectory.

<!-- PDF page 442 -->

### 3.6.1.37 FILE-038 File locked by too many tasks

Cause: There are too many lock requests to same file.

Remedy: Unlock any unnecessary file lock requests.

### 3.6.1.38 FILE-039 Directory already exists

Cause: You tried to create a sub-directory that already exists.

Remedy: Use a unique name for new sub-directory

### 3.6.1.39 FILE-040 Illegal file access mode

Cause: You tried to read from a write only opened file or tried to write to a read only opened file.

Remedy: Open a file with correct access mode.

### 3.6.1.40 FILE-041 File not locked

Cause: You tried to unlock file which you had not locked.

Remedy: Don't unlock a file that is not locked. You can only unlock files which YOU have locked.

### 3.6.1.41 FILE-045 need to set $FILE_MAXSEC

Cause: $FILE_MAXSEC has not been set and must be be set before device can be formatted.

Remedy: Set variable $FILE_MAXSEC to valid value. 800 is a good default value.

### 3.6.1.42 FILE-049 File is not standard file

Cause: A file operation has been attempted on a file which is not a standard file

Remedy: Use a standard file device (e.g., FR: or RD:

### 3.6.1.43 FILE-050 PChamp %s device NOT ready - device FULL

Cause: PChamp output device NOT ready or FULL

Remedy: Check device OR delete old files on device

<!-- PDF page 443 -->

### 3.6.1.44 FILE-051 NESTED kread issued

Cause: A call to kread was made while a WOULDBLOCK read was pending

Remedy: Do not call kread again until the packet from the previous read has been rcvd

### 3.6.1.45 FILE-052 Kread re-call with different buf_p

Cause: A call to kread was made following a WOULDBLOCK read with a different buf_p

Remedy: Call kread with the same buf_p as was used in the original kread call

### 3.6.1.46 FILE-053 MC Inserted

Cause: Memory Card (MC) has been inserted and properly detected by the system

Remedy: Start MC access after receiving this message

### 3.6.1.47 FILE-054 MC Removed

Cause: Memory Card (MC) has been removed from the system

Remedy: Reinstall Memory Card if you wish to continue

### 3.6.1.48 FILE-055 MC not detected

Cause: Either the Memory Card (MC) is not properly inserted or the Card that is inserted is not a Memory Card type (SRAM or Flashdisk)

Remedy: Either insert a MC or exchange inserted card with a MC

### 3.6.1.49 FILE-056 Modem Card Inserted

Cause: Modem Card has been inserted and properly detected by the system

Remedy: Start Modem Card access after receiving this message

### 3.6.1.50 FILE-057 Modem Card Removed

Cause: Modem Card has been removed from the system

<!-- PDF page 444 -->

Remedy: Reinstall Modem Card if you wish to continue

### 3.6.1.51 FILE-058 Illegal Character in Name

Cause: Name contains an illegal character.

Remedy: Remove any non alpha numeric character which is not an underscore.

### 3.6.1.52 FILE-059 Not enough TEMP memory for file operation

Cause: The TEMP memory is too low to complete the file operation.

Remedy: Try one of the following: 1. Remove unnecessary files/programs from the system. 2. Remove unused options from the controller by reloading with fewer options. 3. Add more D-RAM to the system.

### 3.6.1.53 FILE-060 Max %d,Req %d,Ac %d

Cause: Requested RD Size (Req) exceeds Max Available (Max). RD Left at Actual Size (Ac)

Remedy: Adjust $FILE_MAXSEC Memory Size (Req) to less than or equal to the Max Available (Max)

### 3.6.1.54 FILE-061 Requested RD Sz too big

Cause: The requested RD Size (Req)exceeds the Max Available (Max). RD Left at Actual Size (Ac).

Remedy: Adjust $FILE_MAXSEC Memory Size (Req) to less than or equal to the Max Available (Max).

### 3.6.1.55 FILE-062 Backup files are not correct

Cause: The backup file is not correct.

Remedy: Try performing the file backup operation to another device, or use another media type.

### 3.6.1.56 FILE-063 (%s) is not loaded

Cause: The indicated file is not loaded when all files are restored in Automatic Software Update function.

<!-- PDF page 445 -->

Remedy: Check cause code for more information.

### 3.6.1.57 FILE-064 Unspecified DOS system error:%d

Cause: An unusual File System error has occurred. This alarm should rarely occur. The number after the error text indicates:

50 – Device was removed and replaced before flush
51 – Driver reports that the device is not working
52 – Trying to access a drive that wasn't initialized
53 – Driver reports that the device is empty
54 – Driver reports that the device is not recognized
60 – No signature found in BPB (need to format)
61 – No signature found in MBR
62 – Partition requested but none at that offset
63 – IO error reading MBR (note: MBR is first to be read on a new insert)
64 – IO error reading BPB (block 0)
65 – IO error reading FAT32 INFO struc (BPB extension)
70 – Error reading a directory block through the buffer pool
71 – Error reading a fat block through the fat buffer pool
72 – Error writing a directory block through the buffer pool
73 – Error writing a fat block through the fat buffer pool
74 – Error writing info block during fat flush

Remedy: Retry the operation. If the alarm consistently occurs then manually check that the files were read, written, etc. Using a personal computer check the media with a Check Disk or Error-checking tool. If reporting the alarm to FANUC America Corporation, be sure to include the number that is provided.

### 3.6.1.58 FILE-065 Internal DOS system error: %d

Cause: An unexpected internal File System error has occurred. This alarm should occur very rarely. The number after the error text indicates:

<!-- PDF page 446 -->

100 – Unexpected block number encountered, use a check disk
101 – Unexpected cluster encountered, use a check disk
102 – A specified path that must be a directory was not.
103 – Unexpected condition, use a check disk
110 – Out of directory object structures
111 – Out of directory and scratch blocks

Remedy: Retry the operation. If the alarm consistently occurs then manually check that the files were read, written, etc. Using a personal computer check the media with a Check Disk or Error-checking tool. If reporting the alarm to FANUC America Corporation, be sure to include the number that is provided.

### 3.6.1.59 FILE-066 UD%d Ins %s %s

Cause: The USB memory stick has been inserted and properly detected by the system.

Remedy: Start UDx: access after receiving this message.

### 3.6.1.60 FILE-067 UD%d Removed

Cause: The USB memory stick has been removed from the system.

Remedy: Reinstall the memory stick if you want to continue.

### 3.6.1.61 FILE-068 UD not detected

Cause: Either the USB memory stick is not properly inserted, or the stick that is inserted is not a the correct type.

Remedy: Try removing and reinserting the memory stick, or use a different memory stick.

### 3.6.1.62 FILE-069 USB hub Ins %s %s

Cause: A USB hub was inserted and detected as identified in the string parameters. This is informational only to identify the insertion of a hub device.

Remedy: None.

<!-- PDF page 447 -->

### 3.6.1.63 FILE-070 USB hub Removed

Cause: A USB hub was removed. This is informational only.

Remedy: None.

### 3.6.1.64 FILE-071 USB vend: %04x prod: %04x

Cause: USB device details. This will appear as a cause code to the FILE-066 alarm to identify the device inserted.

Remedy: None.

### 3.6.1.65 FILE-072 USB over current detected

Cause: The attached USB devices are drawing more than 500mA of current.

Remedy: Reduce the power draw by removing some devices, or use an external power supply.

### 3.6.1.66 FILE-073 USB error %d

Cause: An unusual USB File System error has occurred. This alarm should rarely occur

Remedy: Report the error number to the FANUC America Corporation Help Hotline.

### 3.6.1.67 FILE-074 USB not supported

Cause: The USB device is not supported on this hardware.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.6.1.68 FILE-075 No media inserted or detected

Cause: The appropriate media is not inserted or properly inserted, or the media that is inserted is not of the correct type.

Remedy: Insert the appropriate media, such as a USB memory stick or a memory card. Try removing and reinserting the media, or use a different one.

<!-- PDF page 448 -->

# **3.6.1.69 FILE-076 %s invalid sector size %d**

**Cause:** The device has an invalid sector size and can not be used by the file system.

**Remedy:** Try a different device.

# **3.6.1.70 FILE-077 Auto backup start (%s)**

**Cause:** Auto backup start.

**Remedy:** None.

# **3.6.1.71 FILE-078 Auto backup complete**

**Cause:** Auto backup was finished.

**Remedy:** None.

# **3.6.1.72 FILE-079 Error Auto backup %s**

**Remedy:** Check

# **3.6.1.75 FILE-082 Backup file not found: %s**

**Cause:** This occurs with the alarm: Backup file is not correct. This alarm indicates the file or one of the files that was not found.

### 3.6.1.76 FILE-083 A Backup file is empty: %s

Cause: This occurs with the alarm: Backup file is not correct. This alarm indicates the file or one of the files that was found to be empty or have a zero length.

### 3.6.1.77 FILE-084 The format operation failed

Cause: The device has some problem or is worn out.

### 3.6.1.78 FILE-085 chkdsk %s

Cause: CHKDSK has determined that the file device has an error.

### 3.6.1.79 FILE-086 Failed to save MC:

### 3.6.1.80 FILE-087 Failed to save UD1:

Cause:Failed to save UD1:.

Remedy:This is just message.

### 3.6.1.81 FILE-088 Failed to save UT1:

Cause:Failed to save UT1:.

Remedy:This is just message.

<!-- PDF page 450 -->

### 3.6.1.82 FILE-089 USB kb Ins %s %s

Cause:USB device key board is installed and detected.

### 3.6.1.83 FILE-090 USB kb Removed

Cause:USB device key board is removed.

### 3.6.1.84 FILE-091 USB mouse Ins %s %s

### 3.6.1.87 FILE-094 USB ram dma %d

### 3.6.1.88 FILE-095 (%s) is not loaded

### 3.6.1.89 FILE-096 on line %d, %s

### 3.6.1.91 FILE-098 Over 1000 programs

### 3.6.1.92 FILE-099 Wrong end of file

Cause: Wrong description.

### 3.6.1.93 FILE-100 Wrong tag/item/character code

Remedy: Fix description.

### 3.6.1.94 FILE-101 Over 35 definitions

### 3.6.1.95 FILE-102 Over limit value

### 3.6.1.96 FILE-103 %s isn't prepared

Cause: Displayed device isn't prepared.

### 3.6.1.97 FILE-104 File is too large

Cause: The file is over the max size allowed.

### 3.6.1.98 FILE-105 Max %d,Req %d,Ac %d

Cause: Requested Memory Size ($FILE_MAXSEC) exceeds Max Available. TD Left at Actual Size.

### 3.6.1.99 FILE-106 Requested TD Sz too big

Cause: Requested TD Size (Req) exceeds Max Available (Max). TD Left at Actual Size (Ac).

Remedy: Adjust $FILE_TD_SEC Memory Size (Req) to less than or equal to the Max Available (Max)

### 3.6.1.100 FILE-107 This is not integer

Cause: Described value is not integer.

### 3.6.1.101 FILE-108 Auto backup is executed frequently

### 3.6.1.102 FILE-110 %s
