### 3.7.1.51 HOST-115 PROXY: %s listen error

Cause: The robot controller Proxy was not able to listen on a TCP network socket.

Remedy: This alarm generally implies that either the Proxy or the TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. Verify network connectivity to the robot controller using the ping utility (on the robot, and also on the local PC). Check for abnormal activity with all installed Internet options. Obtain the ethernet.dg file from the MD: device, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.52 HOST-116 PROXY: Remote proxy error

Cause: The External Proxy Server is not configured with a valid Hostname or IP Address.

Remedy: Configure the External Proxy Server with a valid Hostname or IP Address. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.53 HOST-117 PROXY: PMON error

Cause: The Ethernet address needs to be set.

Remedy: Set the Ethernet address in Configuration Menu.

### 3.7.1.54 HOST-126 Invalid Ethernet address

Cause: The Ethernet address needs to be set.

Remedy: Set the Ethernet address in Configuration Menu.

### 3.7.1.55 HOST-127 Ethernet firmware not loaded

Cause: The Ethernet Board firmware is not loaded.

Remedy: Load the Ethernet Board firmware in BMON.

<!-- PDF page 530 -->

# **3.7.1.56 HOST-128 Ethernet hardware not installed**

**Cause:** The Ethernet Board needs to be reinitialized.

**Remedy:** Install or reseat the Ethernet Board.

# **3.7.1.57 HOST-129 Receiver error**

**Cause:** Data received from external device is invalid. Most likely caused by electrical noise on receivers.

**Remedy:** The error can be cleared by Stopping and Starting the Tag in Host Comm Setup Menu.

# **3.7.1.58 HOST-130 Buffer alignment wrong**

**Cause:** A buffer was passed to the Serial Port Driver which can not be accessed.

**Remedy:** Ensure program can run on this version of controller. You might need to retranslate your program.

# **3.7.1.59 HOST-131 Wrong state**

**Cause:** The Host Comm system can not execute the requested command in the present operating mode.

**Remedy:** Stop and Start the Host Comm Tag in the Host Comm Setup Menu to reset the operating mode.

# **3.7.1.60 HOST-132 Can't allocate memory**

**Cause:** The Host Comm system can not allocate memory buffers for receiving or transmitting messages

**Remedy:** Either add more memory to the controller or reduce the number of simultaneous connections.

# **3.7.1.61 HOST-133 Wrong setup conditions**

**Cause:** The Host Comm system is receiving messages but can not decode them.

**Remedy:** Correct port settings: data rate, data size, stop bits, etc to match external device.

<!-- PDF page 531 -->

### 3.7.1.62 HOST-134 BCC or CRC error

Cause: The Host Comm system is receiving checksum errors on all messages.

Remedy: Ensure that the external device is using the same protocol.

### 3.7.1.63 HOST-135 Timeout

Cause: There has not been any network activity on the Comm Tag for a period specified by Inactivity Timeout. The Comm Tag has been stopped as a result.

Remedy: Restart the Comm Tag.

### 3.7.1.64 HOST-136 Device not ready

Cause: The remote device is connected but is not responding to requests.

Remedy: Check cabling between the devices and/or insure the device is powered.

### 3.7.1.65 HOST-137 Request cancelled

Cause: The remote device indicates the operation was successfully terminated.

Remedy: The cancel command was successful.

### 3.7.1.66 HOST-138 Request aborted

Cause: The remote device did not indicate operation was terminated.

Remedy: The command might have been completed before the cancel command was received.

### 3.7.1.67 HOST-139 Invalid function

Cause: The Host Comm Protocol does not support the requested function.

Remedy: Check the Host Comm Protocol to ensure the function is supported.

### 3.7.1.68 HOST-140 Device offline

Cause: The remote device is connected but it is not online.

<!-- PDF page 532 -->

Remedy: Set the remote device online.

### 3.7.1.69 HOST-141 Protocol Start/Stop error

Cause: The Host Comm Protocol could not be started (Mounted) or stopped (dismounted) on the selected comm tag.

Remedy: Either use another Comm Tag or Stop and Undefine the selected Comm Tag under Menus-Setup-HostComm-Show

### 3.7.1.70 HOST-142 Connection error

Cause: The Host Comm Protocol could not establish communication with the remote device. Possible software mismatch.

Remedy: Ensure both local and remote are using compatible software versions.

### 3.7.1.71 HOST-143 Comm port cannot be closed

Cause: The selected hardware port defined for the Comm Tag could not be closed.

Remedy: Power the controller OFF and then ON and try again. If the error occurs again a cabling or hardware problem might exist with the port.

### 3.7.1.72 HOST-144 Comm Tag error

Cause: The Comm Tag either does not have a protocol defined or if required does not have a port assigned.

Remedy: DEFINE a protocol to the Comm Tag or assign a port.

### 3.7.1.73 HOST-145 Permission denied

Cause: An attempt has been made either to read a file opened for write access only or to write a file opened for read access only.

Remedy: If possible, close and reopen the file with the correct access parameters.

### 3.7.1.74 HOST-146 Bad address for Comm Tag

Cause: A bad address has been detected.

<!-- PDF page 533 -->

Remedy: Verify the tag has a supported protocol then UNDEFINE and DEFINE the Comm Tag

### 3.7.1.75 HOST-147 Block device required

Cause: The selected protocol requires a device port.

Remedy: First ensure the Port has No Use from Port Init Setup. Then assign it to the selected Comm Tag.

### 3.7.1.76 HOST-148 Mount device busy

Cause: Either the Comm Tag is STARTED or it is presently in use.

Remedy: Either STOP the Comm Tag or select another Tag.

### 3.7.1.77 HOST-149 No such device

Cause: The passed Device Type is not a Comm Tag type (Cx or Sx).

Remedy: Only Comm Tags can be used with this command.

### 3.7.1.78 HOST-150 Invalid argument

Cause: The system does not support selected protocol.

Remedy: Either select another protocol or install the selected protocol.

### 3.7.1.79 HOST-151 No more Ethernet buffers.

Cause: The System has run out of buffers to communicate with the Ethernet Remote PCB.

Remedy: Reduce the number of simultaneous connections as there is not enough memory.

### 3.7.1.80 HOST-158 FTP: no connection available

Cause: An error occurred in the networking software.

Remedy: Consult your network administrator. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 534 -->

# **3.7.1.81 HOST-159 FTP: login failed**

**Cause:** The Comm Tag does not have a valid username and password.

**Remedy:** Enter a valid username and password for the Comm Tag.

# **3.7.1.82 HOST-160 FTP: tag dismount request ignored**

**Cause:** An error occurred in the networking software.

**Remedy:** Consult your network administrator. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

# **3.7.1.83 HOST-161 FTP: need remote host name**

**Cause:** The Comm Tag does not have a remote host defined.

**Remedy:** Enter a remote host name in SETUP TAGS menu Current Remote and Startup Remote fields.

# **3.7.1.84 HOST-162 FTP: Error on Ethernet Init.**

**Cause:** The Ethernet PCB isn't initialized properly.

**Remedy:** Ensure both Ethernet PCB firmware and Main PCB Ethernet tasks are activated.

# **3.7.1.85 HOST-163 EXMG: Invalid Buffer Size**

**Cause:** Invalid buffer size in call

**Remedy:** Ensure correct buffer size

# **3.7.1.86 HOST-164 EXMG: Read Pending**

**Cause:** Attempt to write before read.

**Remedy:** Make a read call after write before making a new write call.

# **3.7.1.87 HOST-165 EXMG: Internal Error**

**Cause:** Error in Explicit Messaging Task.

<!-- PDF page 535 -->

Remedy: Unrecoverable - Contact Help Desk.

### 3.7.1.88 HOST-166 EXMG: Write Pending

Cause: Attempt to read before write.

Remedy: A write should precede read.

### 3.7.1.89 HOST-167 EXMG: Connection Error

Cause: Explicit Messaging Connection broken

Remedy: Check cable and remote device. Close connection and open again.

### 3.7.1.90 HOST-168 EXMG: Invalid Channel

Cause: Invalid Channel specified. Channel may not be online.

Remedy: Make sure the channel specified is online or specify the correct channel

### 3.7.1.91 HOST-169 EXMG: Invalid Path

Cause: Invalid Path Specified.

Remedy: Verify Path format specified EM:/DNET/1/10/40 DNET-Protocol, 1-Channel,10-MAC Id 40-buffer size Also verify values are legal.

### 3.7.1.92 HOST-170 EXMG: Invalid Name

Cause: Invalid Name specified.

Remedy: Verify Explicit Messaging mapping system variables are correctly set and the values are legal.

### 3.7.1.93 HOST-171 EXMG: Message Truncated

Cause: Connection Buffer size small.

Remedy: Reopen connection with correct buffer size.

<!-- PDF page 536 -->

# **3.7.1.94 HOST-172 DNS: Host Not Found**

**Cause:** Domain Name Does Not exist

**Remedy:** Make sure your host name and local domain name are correct. Your DNS server may not have the. current host listed.

# **3.7.1.95 HOST-173 DNS: Server Failure**

**Cause:** Problem with DNS server.

**Remedy:** Verify that you DNS server is running. Check with your DNS administrator to verify that the server is working properly.

# **3.7.1.96 HOST-174 DNS: Format or Recovery Error**

**Cause:** DNS Recovery Error .

**Remedy:** Verify that the host name and local domain name and formatted correctly. Verify that your server supports recursive queries. Verify that your server grants access to your robot.

# **3.7.1.97 HOST-175 DNS: Server Has No Address**

**Cause:** Server has no IP address listed.

**Remedy:** Your host name is valid and is recognized by the DNS server. The server has no IP address for the host queried on. Have your DNS administrator provide the server with an IP address for the host queried on.

# **3.7.1.98 HOST-176 DNS: Configuration Error**

**Cause:** DNS is not properly configured

**Remedy:** Go to the DNS configuration menu and verify that the server IP address and local domain name are correct.

# **3.7.1.99 HOST-177 Router Name Not Defined**

**Cause:** No router name has been defined. The router name has been set to the robot name.

**Remedy:** If your network has a router, then define a router in the TCP/IP set up menu.

<!-- PDF page 537 -->

### 3.7.1.100 HOST-178 Router Address Not Defined

Cause: The router does not have an address listed in the local host table.

Remedy: If your network has a router, then define an address for it in the TCPIP SETUP screen.

### 3.7.1.101 HOST-179 IP Address mis-configuration

Cause: The entered IP address is invalid.

Remedy: Reconfigure the Ethernet interfaces such that each interface is on a different subnet, or only configure a single interface.

### 3.7.1.102 HOST-180 NETMEM: buffer is not created

Cause: Internal software problem. Network memory service request occurs before any memory is not created.

Remedy: Network memory should be created before accessing.

### 3.7.1.103 HOST-181 NETMEM: time out

Cause: Timeout occured at getting memory access right.

Remedy: Network may overload if this error occurs frequently.

### 3.7.1.104 HOST-182 NETMEM: BD error

Cause: Internal software problem. Specified network memory buffer descriptor was not correct.

Remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

### 3.7.1.105 HOST-183 NETMEM: buffer is auto ack mode

Cause: Internal software problem. Network memory update request issued to automatic acknowledge transmit memory.

Remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

<!-- PDF page 538 -->

### 3.7.1.106 HOST-184 NETMEM: transmit BD error

Cause: Internal software problem. Specified buffer descriptor is not for transmit buffer.

Remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

### 3.7.1.107 HOST-185 NETMEM: receive BD error

Cause: Internal software problem. Specified buffer descriptor is not for receive buffer.

Remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

### 3.7.1.108 HOST-186 NETMEM: send socket open fail

Cause: UDP open for datagram sending was failed.

Remedy: Confirm that UDP port was consumed by another network application.

### 3.7.1.109 HOST-187 NETMEM: receive socket open fail

Cause: UDP open for datagram receiving was failed.

Remedy: Verify that there is RLSYNC entry in $SERVENT system variable. Verify that port number for RLSYNC is correct.

### 3.7.1.110 HOST-188 PPP init on port %d fails

Cause: invalid port/insufficient memory

Remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

### 3.7.1.111 HOST-189 Invalid port number

Cause: invalid port/insufficient memory

Remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

### 3.7.1.112 HOST-190 Invalid baud rate

Cause: invalid port/insufficient memory

<!-- PDF page 539 -->

Remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

### 3.7.1.113 HOST-191 Invalid device type

Cause: invalid port/insufficient memory

Remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

### 3.7.1.114 HOST-192 PPP channel already initialized

Cause: invalid port/insufficient memory

Remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

### 3.7.1.115 HOST-193 TLNT:Login to %s

Cause: login made to a device using telnet

Remedy: This is not an error

### 3.7.1.116 HOST-194 TLNT:Logout of %s

Cause: logout made out of device using telnet

Remedy: This is not an error

### 3.7.1.117 HOST-195 TLNT:rejected conn request

Cause: TELNET connection attempt rejected. Please look at cause code for further information

Remedy: Correct the cause of failure and try again

### 3.7.1.118 HOST-196 TLNT:%s already connected

Cause: the device is already connected

Remedy: ensure the device is not connected and try again

<!-- PDF page 540 -->

### 3.7.1.119 HOST-197 TLNT:invalid login id

Cause: invalid login id supplied

Remedy: ensure the login id is valid and try again

### 3.7.1.120 HOST-198 TLNT:invalid password %s

Cause: invalid password supplied

Remedy: ensure the password is valid and try again

### 3.7.1.121 HOST-199 TLNT:timeout on %s

Cause: the inactivity timer for the device expired

Remedy: log in again or increase the timer value for the device from the TELNET screens

### 3.7.1.122 HOST-200 TLNT:FSAC no access lvl for %s

Cause: the FSAC security feature is enabled and the client PC doesn't have sufficient privileges

Remedy: make an entry for the PC in the FSAC table

### 3.7.1.123 HOST-201 TLNT:no access lvl for %s

Cause: Insufficient access level

Remedy: check the access level for the device from the TELNET screens

### 3.7.1.124 HOST-202 TLNT:invalid port for %s

Cause: valid port not configured for device

Remedy: configure a valid port for device from Port Init screens first

### 3.7.1.125 HOST-203 TLNT:from %s

Cause: connection from remote host detected

Remedy: not an error

<!-- PDF page 541 -->

### 3.7.1.126 HOST-204 SM: Remote Client Name is invalid

Cause: The host name in the Client tag is not set correctly. If DNS is enabled, DNS server did not resolve the name.

Remedy: Change the host name to be a valid name in the client tags.

### 3.7.1.127 HOST-205 SM: Tag Already Mounted

Cause: A request to mount a tag which was already mounted was received.

Remedy: Do not try to remount a tag without dismounting it.

### 3.7.1.128 HOST-206 SM: Bad Port Number

Cause: The system variable $server_port in the Client tag or the host tag was invalid.

Remedy: Set the $hosts_cfg[n].$server_port sysvar for the server tag or $hostc_cfg[n].$server_port for the client to a valid number

### 3.7.1.129 HOST-207 SM: Tag is not mounted

Cause: The requested tag is not mounted

Remedy: Mount the tag before using it

### 3.7.1.130 HOST-208 SM: Not Yet Connected

Cause: The requested tag is not yet connected to the remote host/device

Remedy: Use MSG_CONNECT to connect the tag before opening it.

### 3.7.1.131 HOST-209 SM: Connection Aborted

Cause: The connection was aborted by remote host

Remedy: Check the remote host and reconnect to it

### 3.7.1.132 HOST-210 SM: Connection Timed Out

Cause: Connection was timed out by remote.

<!-- PDF page 542 -->

**Remedy:** Reconnect to remote host.

### **3.7.1.133 HOST-211 SM: Connection Write Buffer is full**

**Cause:** Write buffer is full. The remote host may not be responding or the network is down.

**Remedy:** Check remote host and network connection.

### **3.7.1.134 HOST-212 SM: Write Direction shut down by Peer**

**Cause:** Write direction was shutdown by remote.

**Remedy:** Check remote and reconnect to remote host

### **3.7.1.135 HOST-213 SM: Read Direction shut down by Peer**

**Cause:** Read direction was shutdown by remote.

**Remedy:** Check remote and reconnect to remote host

### **3.7.1.136 HOST-214 SM: Connection is Pending**

**Cause:** Remote host has not yet connected.

**Remedy:** Wait for remote to connect.

### **3.7.1.137 HOST-215 SM: Connection is in use**

**Cause:** The requested tag is in use.

**Remedy:** Stop using the remote tag. If necessary close any open file to the tag and disconnect the tag by using MSG_DISCO.

### **3.7.1.138 HOST-216 SM: Invalid Socket**

**Cause:** A request was received for a socket which is invalid

**Remedy:** Re-establish the connection.

<!-- PDF page 543 -->

### 3.7.1.139 HOST-217 SM: Socket Error

Cause: A socket error was returned by the tcpip library.

Remedy: Retry the operation. All sockets may be use. Free some resources by closing some connections to telnet, ftp or socket mesg If that is not feasible, the same error may occur again.

### 3.7.1.140 HOST-218 DTP: Connect %s

Cause: A diagnostic TP session was connected in interactive mode. Input is allowed.

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.141 HOST-219 DTP: Monitor %s

Cause: A diagnostic TP session was connected in monitor mode. Input is not allowed.

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.142 HOST-220 DTP: Disconnect %s

Cause: A diagnostic TP session was disconnected.

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.143 HOST-221 DTP: ident %s

Cause: connection from remote browser detected

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.144 HOST-222 DHCP: server %s

Cause: response from DHCP server detected

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.145 HOST-223 DHCP: using IP %s

Cause: A response from the DHCP server was detected.

<!-- PDF page 544 -->

Remedy: None.

### 3.7.1.146 HOST-224 DHCP: No response from server

Cause: No response exists from the DHCP server.

Remedy: Check your cable and server configuration, and retry the operation.

### 3.7.1.147 HOST-225 DHCP: duplicate IP %s

Cause: The DHCP server returned an IP address which is already in use.

Remedy: Check the DHCP server configuration. Identify the device that is using the same IP address that the DHCP server assigned to the robot controller. This is strictly a DHCP server configuration/IP address management problem.

### 3.7.1.148 HOST-226 DHCP: Lease time expired

Cause: The DHCP lease time expired and the robot could not renew the DHCP lease on the robot controller's IP address.

Remedy: Check the Ethernet cables and make sure the robot controller is still connected to the Ethernet network. Check that the DHCP server is online. Check the DHCP server configuration and verify it is able to assign IP address to the robot controller.

### 3.7.1.149 HOST-227 DHCP: shutting down ethernet

Cause: The Ethernet interface was shut down.

Remedy: The lease might have expired. Check the cabling/server configuration and start DHCP again from the DHCP screens.

### 3.7.1.150 HOST-228 DHCP: invalid reply from server

Cause: this may be normal protocol operation

Remedy: not an error

### 3.7.1.151 HOST-229 DHCP: request rejected by server

Cause: Normal protocol operation has occurred.

<!-- PDF page 545 -->

Remedy: None.

### 3.7.1.152 HOST-230 DHCP: renewal attempt failed

Cause: The robot tried to renew IP address, but the renew attempt failed.

Remedy: Check the network cabling and DHCP server setup.

### 3.7.1.153 HOST-231 Initializing

Cause: The DHCP operation is initialized.

Remedy: None.

### 3.7.1.154 HOST-232 In progress

Cause: The DHCP operation is in progress.

Remedy: No action is required.

### 3.7.1.155 HOST-233 Failed

Cause: The DHCP operation failed.

Remedy: Check the network cabling for defects, or the DHCP server setup for possible errors.

### 3.7.1.156 HOST-234 Success

Cause: The DHCP operation succeeded.

Remedy: This is a status message. No remedy is required.

### 3.7.1.157 HOST-235 Disabled

Cause: The DHCP operation is disabled.

Remedy: This is a status message. No remedy is required.

<!-- PDF page 546 -->

### 3.7.1.158 HOST-236 FTP: servers not auto-started

Cause: After loading the FTP option, the FTP servers could not be automatically started.

Remedy: Start the FTP servers from the Hostcomm Server SETUP screen.

### 3.7.1.159 HOST-237 FTP: server tags not available

Cause: The system was unable to start the FTP servers because no free server tags were found.

Remedy: Start FTP servers manually.

### 3.7.1.160 HOST-239 KCL option not loaded

Cause: A web page tried to issue a KCL command, but KCL is not loaded on the robot controller.

Remedy: Load the KCL option on the robot controller at Controlled Start.

### 3.7.1.161 HOST-240 EMAIL: Email send failed

Cause: An SMTP server failure has occurred.

Remedy: Check and verify your SMTP configuration. On an iPendant, this is done using the DRC menus. Otherwise, see the $SMTP_CTRL system variable. It is likely that $SMTP_CTRL.$SERVER was not set with the IP address of an SMTP server.

### 3.7.1.162 HOST-241 EMAIL: Email send successful

Cause: An SMTP message was delivered.

Remedy: This warning can be disabled from the DRC menus: Data Services Setup. The warning can also be disabled by setting the system variable $SMTP_CTRL.$POST_DLVR to FALSE.

### 3.7.1.163 HOST-242 SNTP: NTP server unreachable

Cause: No packets were received from NTP server.

Remedy: Check to make sure the NTP server IP address is correct. If it is not, correct the address and try the operation again.

<!-- PDF page 547 -->

### 3.7.1.164 HOST-243 ACD: duplicate IP %s

Cause: The Address Conflict Detection has detected a duplicate IP address on the network.

Remedy: Change the configured IP address to an IP address not on the network. If using DHCP, consult your network administrator.

### 3.7.1.165 HOST-244 Ethernet Throttle

Cause: Important robot operations might be effected by the high level of traffic on the Ethernet network.

Remedy: Contact your system administrator to fix the network problem.

### 3.7.1.166 HOST-245 Illegal Hostname

Cause: The robot name configured for the TCP/IP interface is illegal.

Remedy: Change the robot Hostname in the Host Comm TCP/IP screen to a legal name. A legal Hostname is a text string of characters drawn from the alphabet (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and minus sign (-). No blank or space characters are permitted as part of a name, nor is the underscore character (_). The first character must be an alpha character. The last character must not be a minus sign.

### 3.7.1.167 HOST-246 Illegal Hosttable Entry %d %d

Cause: A Hosttable entry is configured with an illegal name. If n1 = 1, the illegal name is in the local host table. If n1 = 2, the illegal name is in the shared host table. n2 indicates the entry number of the name in the respective table.

Remedy: Change the robot Hosttable entry in the Host Comm TCP/IP screen to a legal name. A legal Hostname is a text string of characters drawn from the alphabet (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and minus sign (-). No blank or space characters are permitted as part of a name, nor is the underscore character (_). The first character must be an alpha character. The last character must not be a minus sign.

### 3.7.1.168 HOST-260 GigE: Invalid Handle

Cause: The camera handle was not found.

Remedy: Be sure the camera is initialized.

<!-- PDF page 548 -->

### 3.7.1.169 HOST-261 GigE: Access Denied

Cause: Could not get access rights to camera. Some other device might be using it.

Remedy: Be sure the robot can get exclusive rights to the camera.

### 3.7.1.170 HOST-262 GigE: Cam parms not set

Cause: The parameter setting failed.

Remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

### 3.7.1.171 HOST-263 GigE: Invalid Argument

Cause: Internal GigE Error.

Remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

### 3.7.1.172 HOST-264 GigE: Camera Not Supported

Cause: A configuration error has occurred.

Remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

### 3.7.1.173 HOST-265 GigE: Image XFER Error

Cause: Failed to get image.

Remedy: This could be caused by a temporary network issue See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

### 3.7.1.174 HOST-266 GigE: Invalid IP Address

Cause: The camera IP address is not on same subnet as the robot.

Remedy: The camera and the robot should be on same subnet.

### 3.7.1.175 HOST-267 GigE: Camera Mismatch

Cause: The Mac address does not match camera. The camera might have been swapped.

Remedy: Set up a new camera.

<!-- PDF page 549 -->

### 3.7.1.176 HOST-268 GigE: Fail to add Camera

Cause: Could not add camera definition.

Remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT. There might be too many .CAM files.

### 3.7.1.177 HOST-279 GigE: Command Failed

Cause: The GigE command to the camera failed.

Remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

### 3.7.1.178 HOST-280 SMB: Invalid response from PC

Cause: The PC responded to a robot PC Share request in a way the robot couldn't understand.

Remedy: Verify your PC is running a supported platform. Supported operating systems include Windows XP, Windows Vista, and Linux running Samba 3.2. If problems persist on supported platforms, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.179 HOST-281 SMB: Time-out waiting for PC

Cause: The robot timed-out while waiting for the PC to respond to a PC Share request.

Remedy: Verify the PC is properly connected to the network, and can be pinged on the network. Verify the PC Share client tag is properly configured, and the PC has properly shared the location/directory being accessed. The default timeout value can be changed in System Variables. If the PC is too slow for the default timeout, set a more reasonable timeout value in seconds in $SMB_CLNT[X].$RSPTMOUT, and power-cycle the controller. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.180 HOST-282 SMB: No share configured

Cause: The requested file operation can not be performed unless the client tag is configured with a share.

Remedy: Configure the client tag with a shared drive to perform the requested file operation. Make sure the shared drive is porperly configured on the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 550 -->

### 3.7.1.181 HOST-283 SMB: Netbios configuration error

Cause: NetBios name resolution is not properly configured.

Remedy: Either configure a valid WINS server, or enable broadcast name resolution. Both settings can be configured in the PC Share protocol page in the HOST COMM screen. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.182 HOST-284 SMB: Secure Signature from PC failed

Cause: The Secure Signature failed on a network message sent from the PC to the robot controller.

Remedy: The PC server has message signing enabled. This forces the robot controller to perform Secure Signatures to verify communication integrity. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.183 HOST-285 SMB: DOS error: File not found

Cause: The PC server was unable to find the requested file.

Remedy: Verify the Remote Path/Share field is properly configured in the client tag setup screen. Verify the requested file exists on the remote PC server by performing a directory listing from the robot controller FILE menu. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.184 HOST-286 SMB: DOS error: Path not found

Cause: The PC server was unable to find the requested path.

Remedy: Verify the Remote Path/Share field is properly configured in the client tag setup screen. Verify the requested path exists on the remote PC server by performing a directory listing from the robot controller FILE menu. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.185 HOST-287 SMB: DOS error: Too many open files

Cause: The PC server was unable to open the requested file, because the robot controller has too many files opened to the remote PC.

Remedy: Close some files that the robot controller has opened on the PC Share client tag associated with the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 551 -->

### 3.7.1.186 HOST-288 SMB: DOS error: Access denied

Cause: The PC server denied the robot controller access to a file, share, or directory path.

Remedy: Verify your username and re-enter your password in the robot controller client tag setup screens. Verify permissions have been properly set on the shared folder on the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.187 HOST-289 SMB: DOS error: Requested share does not exist

Cause: The PC server cannot find the Share requested by the robot controller.

Remedy: Verify on the remote PC that a folder has been properly shared. Verify that the share name is configured in the robot controller client tag setup screen. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.188 HOST-299 SMB: DOS Error %d from PC

Cause: The PC responded to a PC share request with a DOS File Error.

Remedy: First, check for an alarm cause code for more information on the specific DOS error. If no alarm cause code exists, note the DOS error code. Lookup the DOS error code in the PC Share manual. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.7.1.189 HOST-300 Can't connect to CNC(%s)

Cause: Robot cannot connect to CNC.

Remedy: Check the communication setup.

### 3.7.1.190 HOST-301 Not Connected(Tag=%s)

Cause: The CNC is not connected.

Remedy: Connect the CNC to the robot controller.

### 3.7.1.191 HOST-302 CNC doesn't Connected

Cause: The CNC is not connected.

Remedy: Connect the CNC to the robot controller.

<!-- PDF page 552 -->

### 3.7.1.192 HOST-303 Not supported CNC

Cause: The CNC is not supported.

Remedy: Change the CNC to a supported type.

### 3.7.1.193 HOST-304 Cycle power to change CNC No.

Cause: The CNC No. was changed.

Remedy: Cycle power on the robot controller to activate the change.

### 3.7.1.194 HOST-305 Start Comm. with CNC No.%d

Cause: Starting the communication with the specified CNC.

Remedy: This is for notification only.

### 3.7.1.195 HOST-306 Input I/O number for CNC No.

Cause: The I/O number entered is not for the selected CNC.

Remedy: Enter the proper I/O number for the selected CNC.

### 3.7.1.196 HOST-307 CNC No. is duplicated

Cause: You entered a duplicate CNC no.

Remedy: Enter a CNC no. which is not already in use.

### 3.7.1.197 HOST-308 Add CNC to be connected

Cause: The CNC number is greater than the maximum number allowed.

Remedy: Control Start and set the maximum number of connected CNCs allowed.

### 3.7.1.198 HOST-309 Please set CNC No.%d

Cause: The CNC No. is not set.

Remedy: Enter the CNC No.

<!-- PDF page 553 -->

### 3.7.1.199 HOST-310 TP disable

Cause: You press the OPR enable button but TP is disable.

Remedy: Set TP enable.

### 3.7.1.200 HOST-311 Interlock Mode signal is off

Cause: You press the OPR enable button but interlock signal is off.

Remedy: Set the interlock signal ON.

### 3.7.1.201 HOST-312 Operation isn't available

Cause: You try to jog machine tool but operation isn't available.

Remedy: Set the operation available

### 3.7.1.202 HOST-313 Do M.Tool Operation enable

Cause: You try to jog machine tool but Machine Tool Operation in Setup Machine I/F isn't available.

Remedy: Set the Machine Tool Operation available.

### 3.7.1.203 HOST-380 Syser 0x%x,0x%x

Cause: This is a system error.

Remedy: Power-down and up the controller. If the problem occurs again, write down the number in the message, record the software version and any significant events leading up to this problem and contact FANUC. There may be other error messages that shows the cause of this alarm. Open active alarm screen and report all to FANUC. Open alarm history screen and select the alarms and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. Report all massage to

### 3.7.1.204 HOST-381 Syser. See alarm before this

Cause: This is a system error.

Remedy: Power-down and up the controller. If the problem occurs again, write down the number in the alarm before this alarm, record the software version and any significant events leading up to this problem and contact FANUC. There may be other error messages that shows the cause of this

<!-- PDF page 554 -->

alarm. Open alarm history screen and report all to FANUC. Select the alarms and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. Report all messages to track the problem.

### 3.7.1.205 HOST-382 Syser 0x%x,%s

Cause: This is a system error.

Remedy: Power-down and up the controller. If the problem occurs again, write down the error message, record the software version and any significant events leading up to this problem and contact FANUC. There may be other error messages that shows the cause of this alarm. Open alarm history screen and report all to FANUC. Select the alarms and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. Report all messages to track the problem.

### 3.7.1.206 HOST-390 RSI: ONLYSEND in RSI configuration XML should be TRUE

Cause: ONLYSEND in RSI configuration XML is other than TRUE

Remedy: Change ONLYSEND to TRUE

### 3.7.1.207 HOST-391 RSI: 1st argument in RSI_WRXML_I is not supported

Cause: 1st argument in RSI_WRXML_I is not supported.

Remedy: Change 1st argument in RSI_WRXML_I to supported one.

### 3.7.1.208 HOST-392 RSI: 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I should be 1 character

Cause: 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I is not 1 character.

Remedy: Change 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I to 1 character.

### 3.7.1.209 HOST-401 HSSB board is not found

Cause: HSSB board is not found in option board slot of robot.

Remedy: Insert HSSB board.

### 3.7.1.210 HOST-410 TLIF_READ timeout in KAREL for Tool Interface function

Cause: KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ for Tool Interface function is timed out.

<!-- PDF page 555 -->

Remedy: This warning is just for information. Data received until timeout is read and the size is returned to 2nd argument of TLIF_READ. You may have to greater the timeout value, which is 1st argument of TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.211 HOST-411 Requested size from TLIF_READ is larger than $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ in KAREL

Cause: Requested size of KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ for Tool Interface function is greater than $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ.

Remedy: Greater $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ or decrease request size, which is 2nd argument of TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.212 HOST-412 Internal error for Tool Interface function %s

Cause: An internal error was occured in Tool Interface function.

Remedy: Contact FANUC service representative and tell the the last number of this alarm if exists and tell the alarm messages which is occured with this alarm.

### 3.7.1.213 HOST-413 Receive buffer overflow for Tool Interface function

Cause: Receive buffer for KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ in Tool Interface function is overflowed.

Remedy: Greater $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ or decrease the size of receive data.

### 3.7.1.214 HOST-414 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE in KAREL is invalid for Tool I/F function

Cause: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function isn't initialized or less than 1.

Remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means send length, of TLIF_WRITE.

### 3.7.1.215 HOST-415 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE in KAREL is greater than 2nd argument size

Cause: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than 2nd argument size.

<!-- PDF page 556 -->

Remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means send length, or fix the array length of the 2nd argument, which is an array of BYTE for send data, in TLIF_WRITE.

### 3.7.1.216 HOST-416 2nd argument of TLIF_READ is uninit or less than 1 in KAREL

Cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function isn't initialized or less than 1.

Remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read data, of TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.217 HOST-417 2nd argument of TLIF_READ in KAREL is greater than 3rd argument size

Cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than 3rd argument size.

Remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read data, or fix the array length of the 3rd argument, which is read array of BYTE where read data is set, in TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.218 HOST-418 1st argument of TLIF_READ is uninit or less than -1 in KAREL for Tool

Cause: 1st argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is uninit or less than -1.

Remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means timeout of TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.219 HOST-419 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 is illegal in KAREL for Tool I/F function

Cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is uninit or less than 1 or larger than 32767.

Remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means length of the data, of TLIF_CRC16.

### 3.7.1.220 HOST-420 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 in KAREL is greater than 1st argument size

Cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than the array length of the 1st argument.

<!-- PDF page 557 -->

Remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means length of the data, or fix 1st argument array length of BYTE of TLIF_CRC16.

### 3.7.1.221 HOST-421 3rd argument size of TLIF_CRC16 in KAREL for Tool I/F is smaller than 2

Cause: 3rd argument size of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is smaller than 2.

Remedy: Fix 3rd argument array size of BYTE larger than 1 in TLIF_CRC16.

### 3.7.1.222 HOST-422 2nd argument of TLIF_READ is less than 1 in KAREL for Tool I/F function

Cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is less than 1.

Remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read, in TLIF_READ.

### 3.7.1.223 HOST-423 Send buffer overflow by TLIF_WRITE in KAREL for Tool Interface function

Cause: Send buffer for TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is overflowed.

Remedy: Greater $TLIF,$SND_BUF_SZ or make more interval of calling TLIF_WRITE.

### 3.7.1.224 HOST-424 IO is not updated during $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT [ms] for Tool I/F function

Cause: IOs for Tool Interface function are not updated during $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT [ms].

Remedy: Greater $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT or check cables for Tool Interface function.

### 3.7.1.225 HOST-425 Tool Interface communication error (%d)

Cause: Tool answer may later than $TLIF.$TLANS_TMOUT [ms] or communication error happens.

Remedy: Greater $TLIF.$TLANS_TMOUT or faster the answer of tool or check cables for Tool Interface function. Pay attention that I/O update is done after tool answers by RS485 if robot controller send data to tool by RS485. If tool answers later, I/O update becomes later.

<!-- PDF page 558 -->

### 3.7.1.226 HOST-426 Tool Interface board major version error. Board = %d, Controller = %d

Cause: Tool Interface board version is old.

Remedy: Contact FANUC service representative and tell this alarm message and version number in this alarm.

### 3.7.1.227 HOST-427 ROBOGUIDE doesn't support KAREL built-in for Tool Interface function

Cause: ROBOGUIDE doesn't support KAREL built-in for Serial Communication of Tool Interface Communication Function.

Remedy: This warning is just for notification.

### 3.7.2 HRTL Alarm Code

### 3.7.2.1 HRTL-001 Not owner

Cause: An error occurred in the Ethernet networking software (TCP/IP).

Remedy: Consult your network administrator or call the FANUC America Corporation Service Hotline for assistance.

### 3.7.2.2 HRTL-002 File/Comm Tag does not exist

Cause: Either the file or the Comm Tag could not be found

Remedy: Either retype the file name or DEFINE the Comm Tag. Please refer to the section of Defining and Starting FTP on a Device in the manual of Ethernet Controller Backup and Restore-FTP Setup and Operations.

### 3.7.2.3 HRTL-003 No such process

Cause: An error occurred in the Ethernet networking software (TCP/IP).

Remedy: Consult your network administrator or call the FANUC America Corporation Service Hotline for assistance.

<!-- PDF page 559 -->

### 3.7.2.4 HRTL-004 Interrupted system call

Cause: An error occurred in the Ethernet networking software (TCP/IP).

Remedy: Consult your network administrator or call the FANUC America Corporation Service Hotline for assistance.

### 3.7.2.5 HRTL-005 I/O error

Cause: An error occurred in the Ethernet networking software (TCP/IP).

### 3.8.1.92 IBSS-205 Please power off for Slave

Cause: Setting is modified and power off is required.

Remedy: Power off/on the controller to activate new setting.

### 3.8.1.93 IBSS-206 Firmware Updating Mode

Cause: Controller started in firmware updating mode.

Remedy: Firmware should be updated only in firmware updating mode. Update the firmware if it is needed. Power off/on the controller to return normal mode.

### 3.8.1.94 IBSS-207 Firmware update successful

Cause: Firmware is updated successfully.

Remedy: Power off/on the controller to return normal mode.

### 3.8.1.95 IBSS-208 Firmware update failed %d

Cause: Error occurs during firmware update.

Remedy: Write down the number displayed in the error message. Please consult Phoenix Contact.

### 3.8.1.96 IBSS-209 Firmware file error %d

Cause: Error occurs in accessing the firmware file.

Remedy: Please check if the firmware file is broken.

### 3.8.1.97 IBSS-210 No firmware

Cause: The name of the firmware file is wrong.

Remedy: The name of the firmware file is supposed to start by IBS. Please check if you use the correct firmware for the slave board.

### 3.8.1.98 IBSS-211 System Error %d %d

Cause: Internal Error

Remedy: Write down the numbers displayed in the error message. Contact FANUC America Corporation to report the problem.

Cause: Slave board is defective.

Remedy: Please exchange slave board.

### 3.8.1.100 IBSS-213 Error code %x

Remedy: Write down the number displayed in the error message. Please see the remedy of the error message displayed together.

### 3.8.1.101 IBSS-214 PCP Init Error %d

Cause: Error is PCP initialization.

Remedy: The number displayed in the error message is the error code returned by the firmware. Please consult Phoenix Contact about the error.

### 3.8.1.102 IBSS-215 PCP Init Stopped %d

Remedy: Please check the PCP setting. For example, the number of elements.

### 3.8.1.297 IBSS-572 Set Master-Only HW. setting

Cause: Master-Only board is found but hardware type setting is disabled.
Remedy: Set $IBPX_HW.$HW_TYPE = 1 and cycle power.

<!-- PDF page 617 -->

### 3.8.1.298 IBSS-573 Remove Master-Only HW. setting

Cause: System coupler board is found but hardware type setting is enabled.

Remedy: Set $IBPX_HW.$HW_TYPE = 0 and cycle power.

### 3.8.1.299 IBSS-574 Use CMD for Master-Only HW.

Cause: Use CMD is disabled but Master-Only board is found.

Remedy: Enable Use CMD setting and cycle power.

### 3.8.1.300 IBSS-575 SVC type mismatch

Cause: The SVC file stored in the controller does not match the type of current InterBus board.

Remedy: Load SVC file again.

### 3.8.1.301 IBSS-576 ibbdfil.iba type mismatch

Cause: The IBA file being restored to the controller does not match the type of current InterBus board.

Remedy: Check that the IBA file for the installed InterBus board.

### 3.8.2 ICRZ Alarm Code

### 3.8.2.1 ICRZ-001 Wait for right robot

Cause: Too close to right robot.

Remedy: Wait for right robot to move away.

### 3.8.2.2 ICRZ-002 Wait for left robot

Cause: Too close to left robot.

Remedy: Wait for left robot to move away.

<!-- PDF page 618 -->

### 3.8.2.3 ICRZ-003 Unhold robot

Cause: UNHOLD robot.

Remedy: Robot is ready to move.

### 3.8.2.4 ICRZ-004 Right robot zone cleared

Cause: Right robot moves away from the interferenced rail zone.

Remedy: None.

### 3.8.2.5 ICRZ-005 Left robot zone cleared

Cause: Left robot moves away from the interferenced rail zone.

Remedy: None.

### 3.8.2.6 ICRZ-006 Dead lock condition

Cause: Both robots are moving to same rail zone

Remedy: Unlock the robots and jog robots away from deadlock zone.

### 3.8.2.7 ICRZ-007 Zone disable while robot held

Cause: Zone check is disabled while robot is being held

Remedy: Enable the zone check.

### 3.8.2.8 ICRZ-008 GOUT is not set for right robot

Cause: GOUT is not set properly for right robot.

Remedy: set Group DOUT for right robot.

### 3.8.2.9 ICRZ-009 GOUT is not set for left robot

Cause: GOUT is not set properly for left robot.

Remedy: Set GOUT for left robot.

<!-- PDF page 619 -->

### 3.8.2.10 ICRZ-010 GIN is not set for right robot

Cause: GIN is not set properly for right robot.

Remedy: Set GIN for right robot.

### 3.8.2.11 ICRZ-011 GIN is not set for left robot

Cause: GIN is not set properly for left robot.

Remedy: Set GIN for left robot.

### 3.8.2.12 ICRZ-012 Right robot is not set

Cause: Right is not set properly or not enabled.

Remedy: Set and enable right robot.

### 3.8.2.13 ICRZ-013 Left robot is not set

Cause: Left is not set properly or not enabled.

Remedy: Set and enable left robot.

### 3.8.2.14 ICRZ-014 Upper Barrier Limit

Cause: Reach upper rail limit.

Remedy: Change rail motion range.

### 3.8.2.15 ICRZ-015 Lower Barrier Limit

Cause: Reach lower rail limit.

Remedy: Change rail motion range.

### 3.8.2.16 ICRZ-016 Diag axis not supported

Cause: Diagonal linear axis can not supported for Rail Zone.

Remedy: Change linear axis type

<!-- PDF page 620 -->

### 3.8.3 IFPN Alarm Code

#### 3.8.3.1 IFPN-001 Pos %d wrong output signal(push button:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Output signal of I/F panel push button cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

#### 3.8.3.2 IFPN-002 Pos %d wrong output signal(push button lamp:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Output signal of I/F panel push button lamp cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

#### 3.8.3.3 IFPN-003 Pos %d wrong status signal(push button lamp:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Status signal of I/F panel push button lamp cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

#### 3.8.3.4 IFPN-004 Pos %d wrong signal(left/up)(2 contact point switch:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Signal(Left/Up) of I/F panel 2 contact point switch cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

#### 3.8.3.5 IFPN-005 Pos %d wrong signal(right/down)(2 contact point switch:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Signal(Right/Down) of I/F panel 2 contact point switch cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

<!-- PDF page 621 -->

### 3.8.3.6 IFPN-006 Pos %d wrong signal(lamp:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Signal of lamp of I/F panel cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

### 3.8.3.7 IFPN-007 Pos %d wrong signal(%d)(digital switch:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Signal of I/F panel digital switch cannot be read. If the number in ( ) is N, the Nth signal cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

### 3.8.3.8 IFPN-008 Pos %d wrong signal(%d)(digital lamp:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: Signal of I/F panel digital lamp cannot be read. If the number in ( ) is N, the Nth signal cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed

Remedy: Please check if I/O type and index is correct or not.

### 3.8.3.9 IFPN-009 Press shift key

Cause: Button of I/F panel was pressed without pressing shift key.

Remedy: Press the button while holding shift key.

### 3.8.3.10 IFPN-010 Enable Interface panel

Cause: Button of I/F panel was pressed but I/F panel was disabled. Enable switch of I/F was OFF.

Remedy: Turn on enable switch of I/F panel before pressing button of I/F panel.

### 3.8.3.11 IFPN-011 Out of range(%d - %d)

Cause: Input value is out of range.

Remedy: Confirm input value and valid range. Input valid value again.

<!-- PDF page 622 -->

### 3.8.3.12 IFPN-012 I/F panel is displayed

Cause: Requested operation cannot be performed now. I/F panel is displayed by another pane.

Remedy: Stop display of panel by another screen on all panes, including remote display by PC. Then try again.

### 3.8.3.13 IFPN-013 The button is configured in another pane

Cause: Another pane is displaying detail screen of the button that you tried to display or change setup.

Remedy: Stop display of detail screen of the button. Then try again.

### 3.8.3.14 IFPN-014 Button type setup screen is displayed

Cause: Requested operation cannot be performed now. Button type setup screen is displayed by another pane.

Remedy: Stop display of button type setup screen. Then try again.

### 3.8.3.15 IFPN-015 Not enough memory

Cause: Software for I/F panel could not get enough memory to display I/F panel.

Remedy: Reduce usage of temporary memory by other functions or use DRAM of larger size.

### 3.8.3.16 IFPN-016 Max value decided by the number of signals is %d

Cause: The number you input or increment of number is not allowed. The value exceeds maximum value decided by specified number of signals for the button.

Remedy: Input number that can be represented by specified number of signals.

### 3.8.3.17 IFPN-017 Detail setup screen is displayed

Cause: Another pane is displaying I/F panel detail setup screen. You cannot perform the operation you tried.

Remedy: Close I/F panel detail setup screen, including remote display by PC.

<!-- PDF page 623 -->

### 3.8.3.18 IFPN-018 TP Estop is pressed

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of dead man switch is specified and TP Estop is pressed

Remedy: Turn off TP Estop switch and try again.

### 3.8.3.19 IFPN-019 TP is disabled

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of TP enable switch is specified and TP is disabled

Remedy: Turn OF TP enable switch and try again.

### 3.8.3.20 IFPN-020 Deadman switch is not gripped properly

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of dead man switch is specified and it is not gripped properly.

Remedy: Grip dead man switch properly and try again.

### 3.8.3.21 IFPN-021 Pos %d wrong condition signal

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of condition signal is specified and it cannot be read.

Remedy: Check if specified signal is correct.

### 3.8.3.22 IFPN-022 Condition signal is OFF

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of condition signal is specified and its value is OFF.

Remedy: Turn on the signal and try again.

### 3.8.3.23 IFPN-023 Condition signal is ON

Cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of condition signal is specified and its value is ON.

Remedy: Turn off the signal and try again.

<!-- PDF page 624 -->

### 3.8.3.24 IFPN-024 Pos %d register doesn't exist(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. Register specified for EditBox does not exist. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check index of register.

### 3.8.3.25 IFPN-025 Pos %d System variable doesn't exist(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. System variable specified for EditBox does not exist. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check system variable name. If the system variable is array, element must be specified by [ ]. Position data type like POSITION or XYZWPR cannot be used including its internal data of coordination. For example, $MNUTOOL[1,1].$X cannot be specified.

### 3.8.3.26 IFPN-026 Pos %d KAREL program doesn't exist(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. KAREL program specified for EditBox does not exist. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check KAREL program name and if the program is loaded or not. Variable (VR) must exist at least.

### 3.8.3.27 IFPN-027 Pos %d KAREL variable doesn't exist(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. KAREL variable specified for EditBox does not exist. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check KAREL variable name. The variable must be variable of specified KAREL program. Please check KAREL program name, too.

<!-- PDF page 625 -->

### 3.8.3.28 IFPN-028 Pos %d Variable type is not supported(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. KAREL variable or System variable is specified for EditBox. However, data type of the variable is not supported by EditBox. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check KAREL variable name and its data type. INTEGER, SHORT, BYTE, REAL BOOLEAN and STRING are supported. You cannot specify structure or array as a whole.

### 3.8.3.29 IFPN-029 Pos %d String register doesn't exist(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. String register specified for EditBox does not exist. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check index of string register.

### 3.8.3.30 IFPN-030 Pos %d wrong signal(EditBox:page%d,row%d,col%d)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. AO or GO specified for EditBox cannot be read. Position number, page number, row and column of the button when alarm was posted are displayed.

Remedy: Please check I/O type and index.

### 3.8.3.31 IFPN-031 Out of range(EditBox:%s - %s)

Cause: This is alarm of Interface Panel function. Input value was out of range. The maximum and minimum values are displayed.

Remedy: Please check input value and valid range. Input valid value again.

### 3.8.3.33 IFPN-033 Variable cannot be written

### 3.8.3.34 IFPN-034 Panel name setup screen is displayed

### 3.8.4 INTP Alarm Code

### 3.8.4.1 INTP-001 Cannot lock the motion grp

Cause: Motion control for the specified group cannot be locked.

Remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

### 3.8.4.2 INTP-002 Program manager internal error

Cause: Internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.8.4.3 INTP-003 Invalid request

Cause: Internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 627 -->

### 3.8.4.4 INTP-004 Cannot ATTACH with TP enabled

Cause: The ATTACH statement requires the teach pendant to be disabled.

Remedy: Disable the teach pendant.

### 3.8.4.5 INTP-005 Cannot release motion control

Cause: Motion control cannot be released.

Remedy: Abort the running or paused program.

### 3.8.4.6 INTP-100 (%s^4, %d^5) Internal error (PXnn)

Cause: Internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.8.4.7 INTP-101 (%s^4, %d^5) Internal error (system)

Cause: An internal system error has occurred.

Remedy: Perform a cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.8.4.8 INTP-102 (%s^4, %d^5) Code format is invalid

Cause: Program data is corrupted.

Remedy: For TPE programs, if possible, reload program from back-up device. If a back-up is not available, it may be necessary to re-create the particular routine. For KAREL programs, re-translate and re-load the program.

Cause: Skip startment can exist in one in each line

Remedy: Delete the extra skip statement

### 3.8.4.123 INTP-270 (%s^4, %d^5) Different group cannot BWD

Cause: During backward execution, a move is encountered that has a different group number from the previous motion statement.

Remedy: Use FWD execution carefully

### 3.8.4.124 INTP-271 (%s^4, %d^5) Excessive torque limit value

Cause: Torque limit value exceeds maximum value. Torque limit value was modified to the maximum value.

Remedy: Set torque limit value less than or equal to the maximum value.

### 3.8.4.125 INTP-272 (%s^4, %d^5) Unsupported operator

Cause: This operator is not supported.

Remedy: Check the operator Refer to the KAREL and TPP Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

<!-- PDF page 646 -->

### 3.8.4.126 INTP-273 (%s^4, %d^5) Too many conditions

Cause: The number of the condition exceeds the maximum number.

Remedy: Reduce the number of condition.

### 3.8.4.127 INTP-274 (%s^4, %d^5) CH program error

Cause: This monitor statement cannot be executed.

Remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

### 3.8.4.128 INTP-275 Invalid sub type of CH program

Cause: The sub type of specified ch program cannot be used.

Remedy: Check the sub type of this CH program.

### 3.8.4.129 INTP-276 (%s^4, %d^5) Invalid combination of motion option

Cause: The motion option instructions (SKIP, TIME BEFORE/AFTER, and application instruction) cannot be taught together

Remedy: Delete the motion option instruction

### 3.8.4.130 INTP-277 (%s^4, %d^5) Internal MACRO EPT data mismatch

Cause: The EPT index in macro table doesn't point the program name defined in macro table. That is, the EPT index in macro table is incorrect.

Remedy: Please set the correct EPT index for the program name defined in macro table.

### 3.8.4.131 INTP-278 %s^7

Cause: The DI monitor alarm for auto error recovery function occurs.

Remedy: This alarm is defined by the customer. Therefore the customer knows the remedy for this alarm.

<!-- PDF page 647 -->

### 3.8.4.132 INTP-279 (%s^4, %d^5) Application instruction mismatch

Cause: The application instruction was executed. But this application instruction doesn't match to the application process data of this program.

Remedy: Please change the application process data of this program to the adequate application for this application instruction.

### 3.8.4.133 INTP-280 (%s^4, %d^5) Application data mismatch

Cause: The application data of called program is different from that of the original program.

Remedy: Please change the structure of program

### 3.8.4.134 INTP-281 No application data

Cause: This program doesn't have the application data

Remedy: Please define the application data in the program detail screen

### 3.8.4.135 INTP-283 (%s^4, %d^5) Stack over flow for fast fault recovery

Cause: Stack over flow to record the fast fault recovery nesting data

Remedy: Reduce the nesting of the program

### 3.8.4.136 INTP-284 No detection of fast fault recovery

Cause: The point for the fast fault recover cannot detected

Remedy: Reduce the nesting of the program

### 3.8.4.137 INTP-285 Karel program cannot entry in fast fautl recovery

Cause: The fast entry cannot be performed in the karel program.

Remedy: Use TP program.

### 3.8.4.138 INTP-286 MAINT program isn't defined in fast fautl recovery

Cause: MAINT program is not defined in fast fault recovery.

<!-- PDF page 648 -->

Remedy: Use TP program.

### 3.8.4.139 INTP-287 Fail to execute MAINT program

Cause: It failed to execute MAINT program

Remedy: Confirm the MAINT program name is correct or MAINT program exist in acutual.

### 3.8.4.140 INTP-288 (%s^4, %d^5) Parameter does not exist

Cause: The parameter designated by AR register does not exist.

Remedy: Please confirm the index of AR register and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main program.

### 3.8.4.141 INTP-289 Can't save ffast point at program change

Cause: When fast fault is enabled, the program was paused at the part of program change

Remedy: Check whether the CONT terminaton exists at end of sub-program If exist, please change it to FINE. This is the limitation of the fast fault recovery function.

### 3.8.4.142 INTP-290 Fast fault recovery position is not saved

Cause: During fast fault recovery sequence, any alarm occurs. So the fast fault recovery position is not saved.

Remedy: Check whether the CONT terminaton exists at end of sub-program If exist, please change it to FINE. This is the limitation of the fast fault recovery function.

### 3.8.4.143 INTP-291 (%s^4, %d^5) Index for AR is not correct

Cause: The parameter designated by AR register does not exist. But this error does not occur at present.

Remedy: Please confirm the index of AR register and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main program.

### 3.8.4.144 INTP-292 more than 6 motion with DB executed

Cause: More than six Distance Before (DB) motion options were processed at the same time.

<!-- PDF page 649 -->

Remedy: Either change the termination type from CNT to FINE as in the example below, or reduce the number of DB motion options being used consecutively: 1: L P[1] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[1] = ON 2: L P[2] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[2] = ON 3: L P[3] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[3] = ON 4: L P[4] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[4] = ON 5: L P[5] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[5] = ON 6: L P[6] 2000mm/sec FINE 7: L P[7] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[7] = ON 8: L P[8] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[8] = ON 9: L P[9] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[9] = ON 10: L P[10] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[10] = ON 11: L P[11] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[11] = ON

### 3.8.4.145 INTP-293 (%s,%d)DB too small(away)(%dmm).

Cause: A Distance Before condition was not established.

Remedy: Change the program so that the TCP moves into the trigger region or increase the size of trigger region in order for the Distance Before condition to take effect.

### 3.8.4.146 INTP-294 TPE parameter error

Cause: The parameter designed in CALL/MACRO instruction is not correct. This error is internal error.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.8.4.147 INTP-295 (%s,%d)DB too small(away)(%dmm).

Cause: A Distance Before condition was not established.

Remedy: Change the program so that the TCP moves into the trigger region or increase the size of trigger region in order for the Distance Before condition to take effect.

### 3.8.4.148 INTP-296 (%s,%d) $SCR_GRP[%d].$M_POS_ENB is FALSE.

Cause: Distance Before doesn't work if $SCR_GRP[ ].$M_POS_ENB is FALSE.

Remedy: Please set $SCR_GRP_[ ].$M_POS_ENB to TRUE.

### 3.8.4.149 INTP-297 (%s,%d)DB too small(done)(%dmm)

Cause: Motion completed before trigger of DB condition.

Remedy: Please change distance value.

**Remedy:** Check the dimensions of the arrays.

Cause: KAREL program error. The UNHOLD statement cannot be executed.

### 3.8.4.201 INTP-351 (%s^4, %d^5) Stop motion failed

Cause: KAREL program error. The STOP statement cannot be executed.

Remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

Cause: KAREL program error. The CANCEL statement cannot be executed.

### 3.8.4.203 INTP-353 (%s^4, %d^5) Resume motion failed

Cause: KAREL program error. The RESUME statement cannot be executed.

Remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

### 3.8.4.204 INTP-354 (%s^4, %d^5) Break point failed

Cause: KAREL program error. The break point function cannot be executed.

### 3.8.4.205 INTP-355 (%s^4, %d^5) AMR is not found

Cause: KAREL program error. The AMR operated by the RETURN_AMR built-in routine was not found.

Remedy: Check program operation.

### 3.8.4.206 INTP-356 (%s^4, %d^5) AMR is not processed yet

Cause: KAREL program error. The RETURN_AMR built-in routine cannot be used for an unoperated AMR.

Remedy: Operate the AMR using the WAIT_AMR built-in routine.

### 3.8.4.207 INTP-357 (%s^4, %d^5) WAIT_AMR is cancelled

Cause: KAREL program error. The execution of the WAIT_AMR built-in routine was cancelled.

Remedy: The program executing the WAIT_AMR must be restarted.

### 3.8.4.208 INTP-358 (%s^4, %d^5) Timeout at read request

Cause: KAREL program error. The READ statement timed out.

<!-- PDF page 659 -->

Remedy: Check the device being read.

### 3.8.4.209 INTP-359 (%s^4, %d^5) Read request is nested

Cause: KAREL program error. Another READ statement was executed while a READ statement was waiting for input.

Remedy: Remove nested reads.

### 3.8.4.210 INTP-360 (%s^4, %d^5) Vector is 0

Cause: KAREL program error. The vector value was invalid.

Remedy: Check the vector value.

### 3.8.4.211 INTP-361 (%s^4, %d^5) FRAME:P2 is same as P1

Cause: KAREL program error. The X-axis direction cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P1 and P2 are the same point.

Remedy: Teach P1 and P2 as different points.

### 3.8.4.212 INTP-362 (%s^4, %d^5) FRAME:P3 is same as P1

Cause: KAREL program error. The X-Y plane cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P1 and P3 are the same point.

Remedy: Teach P1 and P3 as different points.

### 3.8.4.213 INTP-363 (%s^4, %d^5) FRAME:P3 exists on line P2-P1

Cause: KAREL program error. The X-Y plane cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P3 is located in the X-axis direction.

Remedy: Teach P3 out of the X-axis direction.

### 3.8.4.214 INTP-364 (%s^4, %d^5) String too short for data

Cause: KAREL program error. The target string was too short.

Remedy: Increase the target string size.

<!-- PDF page 660 -->

### 3.8.4.215 INTP-365 (%s^4, %d^5) Predefined window not opened

Cause: KAREL program error. A FILE pre-defined by the system is not opened.

Remedy: Check the use of this file.

### 3.8.4.216 INTP-366 (%s^4, %d^5) I/O status is not cleared

Cause: KAREL program error. The last file operation failed.

Remedy: Reset the error using the CLR_IO_STAT built-in routine.

### 3.8.4.217 INTP-367 (%s^4, %d^5) Bad base in format

Cause: KAREL program error. I/O mode operates only from binary to hexadecimal.

Remedy: Check the specified mode.

### 3.8.4.218 INTP-368 (%s^4, %d^5) Cannot use specified program

Cause: KAREL program error. The specified program cannot be used.

### 3.8.4.219 INTP-369 (%s^4, %d^5) Timeout at WAIT_AMR

Remedy: If an AMR was expected within the time-out value check logic in the task that sould have posted the AMR

### 3.8.4.220 INTP-370 (%s^4, %d^5) Vision CPU not plugged in

Cause: KAREL program error. The vision CPU board is not plugged in.

Remedy: Plug in the vision CPU board.

### 3.8.4.221 INTP-371 (%s^4, %d^5) Vision built-in overflow

Cause: KAREL program error. The operation overflowed in the vision built-in routine.

<!-- PDF page 661 -->

Remedy: Modify program so fewer vision builtins are executing at the same time.

### 3.8.4.222 INTP-372 (%s^4, %d^5) Undefined vision built-in

Cause: KAREL program error. The vision built-in routine is not defined.

Remedy: Check the appropriate option is loaded.

### 3.8.4.223 INTP-373 (%s^4, %d^5) Undefined vision parameter type

Cause: KAREL program error. The parameter to the vision built-in routine is invalid.

Remedy: Check the parameter of the vision built-in routine.

### 3.8.4.224 INTP-374 (%s^4, %d^5) Undefined vision return type
