### 3.15.7.545 PNT2-675 Wrong valve state in EMPTY CAN event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for the Empty Can event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pDump valve OR pPE + pTRIG valves are in the step before the Empty Can event to correct the problem.

### 3.15.7.546 PNT2-676 Wrong valve state in FAST FILL event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for the Fast Fill event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pCI valve is enabled in the step before the Fast Fill event to correct the problem.

### 3.15.7.547 PNT2-677 Wrong valve state in CAN FULL event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for the Can Full event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pCI valve is enabled in the step before the Can Full event to correct the problem.

<!-- PDF page 1289 -->

### 3.15.7.548 PNT2-678 Wrong valve state in PRESET motion%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for a preset motion instruction.

Remedy: Ensure that the pCI valve is enabled in the same step as the preset instruction if retracting the canister. Ensure that the pDump valve OR pPE + pTRIG valves are enabled in the same step as the preset instruction if extending the canister.

### 3.15.7.549 PNT2-679 Canister Dir - retracting: %s

Cause: An attempt was made to retract the canister but the valve state was incorrect. This could have been during a fill cycle or other commanded motion on the process axis.

Remedy: Ensure that the correct CC control valves are in the proper state. pCI valve should be ON.

### 3.15.7.550 PNT2-680 Low can Pressure after Fill: %s

Cause: A fill cycle was just completed, but the fluid pressure in the can was found to be lower than the minimum expected.

Remedy: Increase the Minimum Fill Torque in the setup screen, or ensure that the canister is full of fluid (check the in- coming fluid pressure).

### 3.15.7.551 PNT2-681 Canister Dir - extending: %s

Cause: An attempt was made to extend the canister but the state of the valves were incorrect. This could have been during a cleanout cycle or other commanded motion on the process axis.

Remedy: Ensure that the correct CC control valves are in the proper state. The pDump valve should be ON or the pPE + TRIG valves should be on. Ensure that the pCI valve is OFF.

### 3.15.7.552 PNT2-682 Zero Flow Programmed: %s

Cause: Zero Flow was programmed in CC.

Remedy: Ensure that a flow rate is setup in the CC preset data.

<!-- PDF page 1290 -->

### 3.15.7.553 PNT2-683 %sHIGH Negative Canister TORQUE

Cause: The maximum compression force on the ball screw has been exceeded. When this occurs, its usually when the ball screw is extending.

Remedy: Ensure that the canister speed is not too fast when spraying the job. Ensure that the pTrig and pCE valves are open during job execution. Ensure that the injector tip is not clogged. The nozzle tip tapers to a smaller diameter; ensure that the paint did not dry inside the nozzle, causing it to clog. Ensure that the pDUMPvalve is operating correctly during the cleanout cycle. If the ball screw is worn out, then it needs to be replaced.

### 3.15.7.554 PNT2-684 %sHIGH Positive Canister TORQUE

Cause: The maximum tensile force on the ball screw has been exceeded. When this occurs, its usually when the ballscrew is retracting. There may be a vacuum in the canister which is causing excessive torque when the motor is retracting the canister's piston.

Remedy: Ensure that the retraction speed is not too fast during the fast fill cycle. Ensure that the pCI and pCCvalves are open during the fill cycles.

### 3.15.7.555 PNT2-685 %sAir in Canister detected

Cause: The piston was retracted from the fluid after the Fill sequence and torque was still detected on the face of the piston. The torque should not exist if the canister is completely full of paint, therefore, compressed air could me mixed with the paint.

Remedy: Check the paint supply for the current color in the canister to verify air in not being introduced into paint supply.

### 3.15.7.556 PNT2-686 %sLow Trigger Torque

Cause: The torque threshold on the canister motor did not reach the minimum torque threshold value during the fillthrough trigger step of the fill or refill cycle.

Remedy: Check the paint supply for the current color in the canister or reduce the torque threshold value or the fill through trigger timeout value.

### 3.15.7.557 PNT2-687 Wrong valve state in EMPTY CAN event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for the Empty Can event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pDump valve OR pPE + pTRIG valves are in the step before the Empty Can event to correct the problem.

<!-- PDF page 1291 -->

### 3.15.7.558 PNT2-688 Wrong valve state in FAST FILL event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't been satified for the Fast Fill event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pCI valve is enabled in the step before the Fast Fill event to correct the problem.

### 3.15.7.559 PNT2-689 Wrong valve state in CAN FULL event%s

Cause: The wrong valve state was programmed in the color change cycle. The valve interlocking requirements haven't beensatified for the Can Full event in the color change cycle.

Remedy: Ensure that the pCI valve is enabled in the step before the Can Full event to correct the problem.

Remedy: Ensure that the retraction speed is not too fast during the fast fill cycle. Ensure that the pCI and pCCvalves are open during the fill cycles.

### 3.15.7.567 PNT2-697 %sAir in Canister detected

Cause: The piston was retracted from the fluid after the Fill sequence and torque was still detected on the face of the piston. The torque should not exist if the canister is completely full of paint, therefore, compressed air could me mixed with the paint.

Remedy: Check the paint supply for the current color in the canister to verify air in not being introduced into paint supply.

<!-- PDF page 1293 -->

### 3.15.7.568 PNT2-698 %sLow Trigger Torque

Cause: The torque threshold on the canister motor did not reach the minimum torque threshold value during the fill through trigger step of the fill or refill cycle.

Remedy: Check the paint supply for the current color in the canister or reduce the torque threshold value or the fill through trigger timeout value.

### 3.15.7.569 PNT2-699 %sIllegal macro argument

Cause: The macro argument selected an invalid arm ID.

Remedy: Verify the robot program calling the macro does not identify itself in the macro argument. Make sure arguments are in the following list: Robots: R1,R2,R3,R4,R5,R6,R7,R8
Door Openers: D1,D2,D3,D4,D5,D6 Hood/Deck Openers: H1,H2,H3,H4,H5,H6

### 3.15.7.570 PNT2-700 %sMacro waiting for aborted robot

Cause: The robot program is waiting for program on another robot that is already aborted.

Remedy: Cancel the robot and send it home.

Cause: The previous macro was not acknowledged.

Remedy: Change the teach pendant program so that this waits on the other robot between release macros.

### 3.15.7.582 PNT2-716 %sHood/Deck Opener Lost Part

Cause: The Hood/Deck opener lost the part while Part Monitoring was enabled, causing the robot to fault.

Remedy: Determine the cause for the Hook to lose the part. Determine if the TP program needs to disable Part Monitoring prior to this location. A cancel can be initiated, which automatically disables ServoTool and Part Monitoring.

### 3.15.7.611 PNT2-771 %sEstat over uA warning

Cause: While operating in Voltage mode, the current draw is within 10% of the limit.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.612 PNT2-772 %sEstat over KV warning

Cause: The actual Voltage is within 10% of the internal safety limit.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.613 PNT2-773 %sEstat under KV warning

Cause: While operating in current mode, the load is so great that the voltage is within 110% of the low threshold.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.614 PNT2-777 %sEstat H/W fault

Cause: A serious internal fault has occurred, or the High Voltage was enabled while a Fault existed.

Remedy: Verify the voltage was not enabled during a fault or replace the power supply.

<!-- PDF page 1301 -->

### 3.15.7.615 PNT2-778 %sEstat comm. fault

Cause: One of the parameters was sent to the power supply out of the expected range.

Remedy: Review the process setup and verify parameters are used within their range limits.

### 3.15.7.616 PNT2-779 %sEstat low KV fault

Cause: While operating in current mode, the applicator draws so much current that the power supply was not able to attain minimal KV value.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.617 PNT2-780 %sEstat DV/DT fault

Cause: While operating in Voltage mode with DX/DT enabled, the rate of voltage rise over time exceeded the DV/DT setpoint.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.618 PNT2-781 %sEstat DI/DT fault

Cause: While operating in Voltage mode with DX/DT enabled, the rate of current rise over time exceeded the DI/DT setpoint.

Remedy: Possible sources include: dirty applicator covering, a line not blown out during color change, or applicator too close to part being processed.

### 3.15.7.619 PNT2-782 %sEstat min. output fault

Cause: Either Voltage or Current feedback has been detected with the minimum output of the power supply.

Remedy: Check cable(s) between the power supply and cascade, replace the cascade.

### 3.15.7.620 PNT2-783 %sEstat max. output fault

Cause: Either Voltage or Current feedback was not able to reach the setpoint before reaching the maximum output of the power supply.

Remedy: Check cable(s) between the power supply and cascade, replace the cascade.

<!-- PDF page 1302 -->

### 3.15.7.621 PNT2-784 %sEstat over KV fault

Cause: The KV feedback from the cascade has exceeded the internal safety limit or the parameter KV limit.

Remedy: Review the application to verify the limit is set correctly. Clean applicator and adjust the path as needed.

### 3.15.7.622 PNT2-785 %sEstat over uA fault

Cause: The KV feedback from the cascade has exceeded the parameter uA limit.

Remedy: Review the application to verify the limit is set correctly. Clean applicator and adjust the path as needed.

### 3.15.7.623 PNT2-786 %sEstat cable fault

Cause: Either a short circuit or open circuit has been detected with the voltage or current feedback circuit from the cascade to the power supply.

Remedy: Check the cable(s) from the power supply to the cascade to verify insulation has not been compromised.

### 3.15.7.638 PNT2-804 %sEstat Imax threshold warning

Cause: The actual current is greater than the warning level. The warning level is determined by:
((SETPOINT WARNING TOLERANCE/100) *(KV SETPOINT + IMAX FACTOR)).

Remedy: No action is required.

iPackHV.

<!-- PDF page 1306 -->

Remedy: Replace iPackHV unit.

Cause: Internal Failure.

Remedy: Replace iPackHV unit.

### 3.15.7.646 PNT2-812 "%sEstat over temperature

Cause: Internal Failure.

Remedy: Replace iPackHV unit.

### 3.15.7.647 PNT2-813 %sEstat Imax fault

Cause: Excessive current is drawn from the HV system. IMAX fault can be caused by the applicator being too close to a grounded component. It can also be caused by too much current leaking into the paint delivery system. Excessive overspray accumulation can also be the cause of an IMAX fault.

Remedy: Inspect target distance and Move robot away from grounded components and try to isolate excessive current path. Is the fault produced with a specific paint type? Unplug the HV cable and confirm problem is isolated to robot application system. If the problem still occurs with the HV cable removed/unplugged from the HV controller then it is likely a bad HV controller.

### 3.15.7.648 PNT2-814 %sEstat spark detected fault

Cause: The HV system has detected a discharge. A spark fault can be caused by the applicator being too close to a grounded component. It can also be caused by a fault in the paint delivery system, i.e. a dielectric break down, air entrapped in the paint, or when using highly conductive metallic paint. Excessive overspray accumulation can also be the cause of an Spark fault.

Remedy: Inspect target distance and correct. Move robot away from grounded components and try to isolate problematic voltage path. Is the fault produced with a specific paint type? Unplug the HV cable and confirm problem is isolated to robot application system. If the problem still occurs with the HV cable removed/unplugged from the HV controller then it is likely a bad HV controller.

### 3.15.7.649 PNT2-815 %sEstat output overvoltage fault

Cause: The output voltage has exceeded the safe operating limit.

Remedy: This may occur if the internal cascade is damaged.

<!-- PDF page 1307 -->

### 3.15.7.650 PNT2-816 %sEstat no setpoint fault

Cause: The KV set point was not reached for the duration of the Set Point timer. This could occur when the current limiting function is enabled and system cannot achieve the voltage set point at the limiting current setting.

Remedy: Inspect target distance and correct. Move robot away from grounded components and try to isolate problematic voltage path. Is the fault produced with a specific paint type? Unplug the HV cable and confirm problem is isolated to robot application system. If the problem still occurs with the HV cable removed/unplugged from the HV controller then it is likely a bad HV controller.
