Cause: Too many devices exist in PROFINET project.

Remedy: Decrease the number of stations, I/O modules and interface modules.

### 3.15.8.306 PRIO-649 PNIO: Need firmware %s

Cause: Firmware version is too old to perform the operation.

Remedy: Update the firmware of PROFINET board to the the displayed version, or later.

### 3.15.8.307 PRIO-650 Too many I/O comments

Cause: Too many I/O comments were set.

Remedy: Delete some unnecessary I/O coments.

### 3.15.8.308 PRIO-651 %s

Cause: Alarm is indicated by CP1616.

<!-- PDF page 1365 -->

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.309 PRIO-652 PNIO(C) station %d deactivated

Cause: The device with the specified station number is deactivated.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.310 PRIO-653 PNIO(C) alarm storm, st %d

Cause: Alarm storm is detected. A device has been faulty and keeps on sending many alarms and diagnostics.

Remedy: Find out and fix the faulty device. Then release alarm storm status by TP screen or by system variable.

### 3.15.8.311 PRIO-654 PNIO(C) alarm storm cleared

Cause: Alarm storm has been released.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.312 PRIO-655 PNIO: XDB backup started

Cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board has started.

Remedy: Wait until backup finishes. Don't turn off the controller during backup.

### 3.15.8.313 PRIO-656 PNIO: XDB backup finished

Cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board has completed successfully.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.314 PRIO-657 PNIO: XDB backup failed

Cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board failed.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

<!-- PDF page 1366 -->

### 3.15.8.315 PRIO-658 PNIO: FW. backup started

Cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board has started.

Remedy: Wait until backup finishes. Don't turn off the controller during backup.

### 3.15.8.316 PRIO-659 PNIO: FW. backup finished

Cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board completed successfully.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.317 PRIO-660 PNIO: FW. backup failed

Cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board failed.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.318 PRIO-661 PNIO: XDB segment error

Cause: XDB backup failed because of a segment of data was dropped.

Remedy: This is an additional information.

### 3.15.8.319 PRIO-662 PNIO: Backup is running

Cause: PROFINET communication is suspended because backup operation is running.

Remedy: Wait until backup operation finishes.

### 3.15.8.320 PRIO-663 PNIO: Needs more free memory

Cause: There is not enough memory in COMM processor for backup operation.

Remedy: Put underbar character before device path, for example, _UD1: in order to perform backup in memory saving mode, however, it will take much longer time to finish than normal mode.

<!-- PDF page 1367 -->

### 3.15.8.321 PRIO-664 PNIO(D): Bad Module setting

Cause: There is a bad setting in I/O Device module setting. For example, slot number = 0 can't be used with V2.6 firmware.

Remedy: Check the cause code for what is bad setting. In the example case, Open I/O Device module list/detail screen. Renumber the slot number of the modules from slot 1. Then cycle power the controller.

### 3.15.8.322 PRIO-665 PNIO: unconfirmed FW. %d.%d.%d.%d

Cause: The version of the firmware currently installed on the PROFINET board is not equal to that of tested firmware.

Remedy: This is an information of firmware version mismatch. It doesn't necessarily mean any problem is present. It is up to operator how to react this. For example, the operator may download the tested version, or keep using the version. On the other hand, when there is a problem, this error message shows that firmware version mismatch might cause the problem.

### 3.15.8.323 PRIO-666 PNIO(D): Wrong GSD in partner cfg

Cause: Error is found in I/O Device configuration from partner, the I/O Controller that tries to connect the robot. For example, the module of slot number 0 is present, which is not permissible when V2.6 firmware is used. This kind of error is caused probably because wrong GSD file is used when the partner is configured.

Remedy: Check the manual to see which GSD file should be used according to the software version of the robot controller and the firmware version of the firmware on PROFINET board. Install the proper GSD file to the configuration tool if needed. Correct the configuration of the partner. For example, replace robot I/O device by that from proper GSD file, compile the project and download it to the partner.

### 3.15.8.324 PRIO-667 PNIO(C): XDB backup mismatch

Cause: XDB backup file in the specified device path doesn't match the configuration on PROFINET board.

Remedy: Check if configuration is on PROFINET board. If there is no configuration, downloading XDB might be required. If there is configuration, the XDB backup file in the specified device path might be old. It is up to the operator to download XDB backup file to PROFINET board, or to update XDB backup file.

<!-- PDF page 1368 -->

### 3.15.8.325 PRIO-668 PNIO(C): XDB backup check failed

Cause: The operaton of comparing XDB backup file in the specified device path fails.

Remedy: This is a system error. The cause code is the error status.

### 3.15.8.326 PRIO-669 PNIO(C): XDB backup not found

Cause: There is no XDB backup file in the specified device path.

Remedy: Confirm the device path. Create the backup file if required.

### 3.15.8.327 PRIO-670 PNIO(C): No config on board

Cause: There is no configuration on PROFINET board.

Remedy: Download configuration to PROFINET board if I/O Controller function is used.

### 3.15.8.328 PRIO-671 PNIO(C): Config check failed

Cause: It isn't possible to check if configuration is present on PROFINET board. Possible causes: config in update, no communication with firmware.

Remedy: This is an information.

### 3.15.8.329 PRIO-672 PNIO: Special Setting found

Cause: The setting displayed in the cause code has the value with special meaning.

Remedy: Please see the cause code for which setting is special. In some cases, setting is changed for specific purpose. It is up to operator to decide the setting is correct or not. If the value is correct, just ignore the alarm.

### 3.15.8.330 PRIO-673 PNIO: Safety disabled

Cause: PROFINET Safety is installed but can't be enabled for some reason. For example, the firmware version of PROFINET board doesn't meet the requirement. The slot number for safety module doesn't match that defined in GSD file.

Remedy: Check the firmware version on PROFINET board by looking $PNIO_DIAG.$FW_VERSION. Refer to PROFINET I/O function operation manual for the required firmware version and the GSD file for it. Download the required firmware to PROFINET board, and confirm the GSD is used in configuration tool. Check the slot number of safety module.

<!-- PDF page 1369 -->

### 3.15.8.331 PRIO-674 PNIO: Download FW. %s

Cause: The firmware on PROFINET board can't be used with the current setting of robot. This may be because of replacement of PROFINET board.

Remedy: Download the firmware of the displayed version to PROFINET board.

### 3.15.8.332 PRIO-675 PNIO: Old backup is loaded

Cause: Backup file of PROFINET I/O function is loaded. Old identification information and configuration are found.

Remedy: This is an information.

### 3.15.8.333 PRIO-676 PNIO(D): DeviceID set to 0x%x

Cause: Identification number of PROFINET I/O Device is set to the specified number.

Remedy: This is an information. The I/O Controller that connects to the robot I/O Device may need to be configured again by the GSD file with the device identification number.

### 3.15.8.334 PRIO-677 No SignOff signal assignment

Cause: SignOff function is enabled, but there is no assignment for SignOff signal.

Remedy: Assign SignOff signal, or disable SignOff function.

### 3.15.8.335 PRIO-678 PROFIEnergy enabled

Cause: I/O Device starts with PROFIEnergy enabled.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.336 PRIO-679 PROFIEnergy disabled

Cause: I/O Device starts with PROFIEnergy disabled.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

<!-- PDF page 1370 -->

### 3.15.8.337 PRIO-680 PNPE: Start_Pause 0x%x

Cause: User application has acknowledged Start_Pause with the displayed PE_Mode.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.338 PRIO-681 PNPE: End_Pause

Cause: User application has acknowledged End_Pause.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.339 PRIO-682 PNIO(C) controller closed

Cause: I/O Controller has been closed.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.340 PRIO-683 PNIO(D) device closed

Cause: I/O Device has been closed.

Remedy: This is just a notification.

### 3.15.8.341 PRIO-684 PNIO(D) mod %d incomplete

Cause: Defective module setting is found around the displayed number in the module list of I/O Device. The module list should be filled with complete module setting. No intermediate empty or incomplete setting is permitted.

Remedy: Check module list of I/O Device, and remove all intermediate empty or incomplete setting.

### 3.15.8.342 PRIO-685 PROFIsafe F_iPar_CRC Error %x

Cause: PROFIsafe is stopped due to F_iPar_CRC check.

Remedy: If F_iPar_CRC check is enabled, F_iPar_CRC must be present in F-Parameter sent from Safety PLC, and it must be equal to that calculated by robot based on current DCS parameters, otherwise PROFIsafe is stopped. If F_iPar_CRC check is disabled, F_iPar_CRC must not be present in F-Parameter sent from Safety PLC, otherwise PROFIsafe is stopped. F_iPar_CRC check enable/disable should be used by default setting because robot GSDML file determines if F_iPar_CRC is present in F-Parameter sent from PLC.

<!-- PDF page 1371 -->

### 3.15.8.343 PRIO-686 PNIO(D) Too many submodules

Cause: The number of I-device submodule exceeds the limit.

Remedy: Decrease the transfer area of I-Device in configuration tool.

### 3.15.8.344 PRIO-687 PNIO(D) mod data out of area

Cause: The number of I/O for I-Device is not enough for mapping the data of the submodule.

Remedy: Increase the number of I/O for I-Device, or decrease the length of I-Device data.

### 3.15.8.345 PRIO-688 More than 1 safe mod %d %d

Cause: More than 1 submodules have the subslot ID of safety submodule.

Remedy: Only 1 safety submodule is permissible at the beginning of I-Device transfer area. Change the subslot ID of the specified submodule other than 0x1001 - 0x1008.

### 3.15.8.346 PRIO-689 PNIO : to STOP mode (SUSPEND)

Cause: The mode of PROFINET has changed to STOP mode (former SUSPEND mode).

Remedy: This is just an information.

### 3.15.8.347 PRIO-690 PNIO(%s) Close Start

Cause: PROFINET interface is closing. It might be because of configuration error.

Remedy: Check alarm history to see if any error in I/O controller or I-Device.

### 3.15.8.348 PRIO-691 PNIO(%s) Stop Request

Cause: Stop of PROFINET interface is requested, for example by manual operation.

Remedy: This is just an information.

### 3.15.8.349 PRIO-692 PNIO(%s) Restart Request

Cause: Restart of PROFINET interface is requested, for example by manual operation.

<!-- PDF page 1372 -->

Remedy: This is just an information.

### 3.15.8.350 PRIO-693 PNIO: FW. reset started

Cause: Reset of the firmware on the PROFINET board started.

Remedy: This is just an information.

### 3.15.8.351 PRIO-694 PNIO: FW. reset finished

Cause: Reset of the firmware on the PROFINET board finished.

Remedy: This is just an information.

### 3.15.8.352 PRIO-695 PNIO: STOP before operation

Cause: Requested Operation requires PROFINET to be stopped.

Remedy: Stop PROFINET before operation.

### 3.15.8.353 PRIO-696 PNIO: Too many number of I/O

Cause: More than DI2048/DO2048 are used in PFORINET, then Main board C (with High Speed COMM CPU) is required but it is not used.

Remedy: Reduce the number of DI/DO used in PROFINET, or replace the main board by Main Board C.

### 3.15.8.354 PRIO-700 CC-IE Board not installed

Cause: No CC-Link IE PCB is installed.

Remedy: Install CC-Link IE PCB.

### 3.15.8.355 PRIO-701 CC-IE Sys err (%d,%xh)

Cause: Internal system error occurred.

Remedy: When size is changed in master, this alarm may happen. Cycle power the controller. If this alarm happens even after cycle power, contact FANUC service representative. The ID number in the brackets is required to track the problems.

<!-- PDF page 1373 -->

### 3.15.8.356 PRIO-702 CC-IE off line

Cause: CC-Link IE become off line

Remedy: Check CC-Link IE settings and cable. If you changed RX,RY,RWr,RWw size to larger in master, robot setting should be changed to the larger size and robot should be cycling power.

### 3.15.8.357 PRIO-703 CC-IE R[%d] data invalid

Cause: A outlying numerical value is set to a remote register.

Remedy: Reset, this alarm is only 1 shot. If register is changed, judgement for this alarm is done again. CC-Link IE function of robot supports unsigned or signed 16bits word data. Do not enter another type of value to remote register. You can send float value, which is larger than -32769 and smaller than 65536, if $CCIE.$AUTO_REGCHG is set to 1. The value is sent with integer by cutting off the floating part. Severity of this alarm can be changed to warning if $CCIE.$REG_ER_WARN is set to 1.

### 3.15.8.358 PRIO-704 CC-IE I/O data size is changed

Cause: Cyclic data size has been reduced by the master.

Remedy: Only notification for user.

### 3.15.8.359 PRIO-710 AI/O Conv. data is invalid

Cause: AI/O conversion setting ($AIO_CNV) is invalid.

Remedy: Check and change $AIO_CNV setting.

### 3.15.8.360 PRIO-711 AI/O value is out of range

Cause: Value of AI/O is out of range. This AI/O port is used conversion data. And range is defined in $AIO_CNV.

Remedy: Check AI/O value. Check and change $AIO_CNV setting.

### 3.15.8.361 PRIO-800 EtherCAT Board not installed

Cause: No EtherCAT PCB is installed.

Remedy: Install EtherCAT PCB.

<!-- PDF page 1374 -->

### 3.15.8.362 PRIO-801 EtherCAT off line

Cause: EtherCAT become off line.

Remedy: Check EtherCAT settings and cable.

### 3.15.8.363 PRIO-802 EtherCAT input size different

Cause: EtherCAT input size is different from master.

Remedy: Check EtherCAT settings.

### 3.15.8.364 PRIO-803 EtherCAT output size different

Cause: EtherCAT output size is different from master.

Remedy: Check EtherCAT settings.

### 3.15.8.365 PRIO-804 EtherCAT Com Soft Update Mode

Cause: Mode switch on EtherCAT board is communication soft update mode.

Remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

### 3.15.8.366 PRIO-805 EtherCAT EEPROM Update Mode

Cause: Mode switch on EtherCAT board is EEPROM update mode.

Remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

### 3.15.8.367 PRIO-806 EtherCAT Update file not found

Cause: EtherCAT update file is not found.

Remedy: Check system variables $BOOT2 $BOOT3 $ECAT_SOFT $EEPROM_IMG under $ECAT and check the file.

### 3.15.8.368 PRIO-807 EtherCAT Update finished

Cause: Update for EtherCAT communication soft or EEPROM is finished.

<!-- PDF page 1375 -->

Remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

### 3.15.8.369 PRIO-808 EtherCAT comm. error %x

Cause: EtherCAT communication error happen.

Remedy: Tell FANUC with the number displayed.

### 3.15.8.370 PRIO-809 EtherCAT system error %x

Cause: EtherCAT system error happens.

Remedy: Tell FANUC with the number displayed.

### 3.15.8.371 PRIO-810 %s

Cause: See the message displayed.

Remedy: None.

### 3.15.8.372 PRIO-811 EtherCAT Com Soft mismatch

Cause: EtherCAT Com Soft on EtherCAT Slave board is older or newer than the robot software.

Remedy: Update EtherCAT Com Soft and EEPROM image by the procedure written in EtherCAT operation manual.

### 3.15.8.373 PRIO-812 Required %s, Current %s

Cause: This message shows up together with PRIO-811 to inform the required and the current version of EtherCAT Com Soft.

Remedy: Update EtherCAT Com Soft and EEPROM image by the procedure written in EtherCAT operation

### 3.15.9 PROC Alarm Code

### 3.15.9.1 PROC-001 Allocated memory full.

Cause: The memory size allocated in $PRCREP.$maxmem_siz has been filled.

<!-- PDF page 1376 -->

Remedy: Delete old programs not used anymore to clear old logged data, or clear all log data to start fresh logging.

### 3.15.9.2 PROC-002 Memory too LOW for logging.

Cause: There is not enough FROM or DRAM to log any new process data.

Remedy: Delete old programs not used anymore to clear old logged data, or clear all log data to start fresh logging.

### 3.15.9.3 PROC-003 Process Data remotely cleared.

Cause: This is a notification that process data was remotely cleared.

Remedy: No remedy required.

### 3.15.9.4 PROC-004 Process Data cleared from TP.

Cause: This is a notification that process data was cleared from the TP.

Remedy: No remedy required.

### 3.15.9.5 PROC-005 %s out of tol for PROG %s, PROCESS ID=%d

Cause: Alarm monitoring for specified item is enabled, and logged value is not within upper and lower tolerances.

Remedy: Check your process to verify it is within tolerance Adjust upper and lower tolerances as needed.

### 3.15.10 PROF Alarm Code

### 3.15.10.1 PROF-000 System error(%d)

Cause: System internal error

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

<!-- PDF page 1377 -->

### 3.15.10.2 PROF-001 PROFIBUS PCB not installed

Cause: PROFIBUS is not installed

Remedy: Please install PROFIBUS PCB.

### 3.15.10.3 PROF-002 PROFIBUS PCB abnormal(%d)

Cause: PROFIBUS PCB is abnormal.

Remedy: Please exchange PROFIBUS PCB

### 3.15.10.4 PROF-003 Slave Config data error

Cause: Configuration data is abnormal.

Remedy: Please change configuration data on Master

### 3.15.10.5 PROF-004 Slave Param data error

Cause: Parameter data is abnormal.

Remedy: Please change parameter data on Master

### 3.15.10.6 PROF-005 Master Slave Param error(%d)

Cause: Slave Parameter sets is abnormal.

Remedy: Please change Slave Parameter sets on the Master.

### 3.15.10.7 PROF-006 Another Master Lock(%d)

Cause: Setting of slave is abnormal.

Remedy: Please change slave setting.

### 3.15.10.8 PROF-007 Parameter Fault(%d)

Cause: Setting of slave is abnormal.

Remedy: Please change slave setting.

<!-- PDF page 1378 -->

# **3.15.10.9 PROF-008 Invalid Slave Responce(%d)**

**Cause:** Setting of slave is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please change slave setting.

# **3.15.10.10 PROF-009 Slave not supported(%d)**

**Cause:** Setting of slave is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please change slave setting.

# **3.15.10.11 PROF-010 Config Fault(%d)**

**Cause:** Setting of slave is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please change slave setting.

# **3.15.10.12 PROF-011 Slave not ready(%d)**

**Cause:** Setting of slave is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please change slave setting.

# **3.15.10.13 PROF-012 Slave not existent(%d)**

**Cause:** Setting of slave is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please change slave setting.

# **3.15.10.14 PROF-013 CMI error(code = %d)**

**Cause:** Master firmware is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please exchange PROFIBUS PCB

# **3.15.10.15 PROF-014 DP error(code = %d)**

**Cause:** Master firmware is abnormal.

**Remedy:** Please exchange PROFIBUS PCB

<!-- PDF page 1379 -->

### 3.15.10.16 PROF-015 DP sub error(code = %d)

Cause: Master firmware is abnormal.

Remedy: Please exchange PROFIBUS PCB

### 3.15.10.17 PROF-016 Slave communicatin stop

Cause: PROFIBUS PCB is abnormal.

Remedy: Exchange the PROFIBUS PCB.

### 3.15.10.18 PROF-017 Slave disconnected

Cause: Slave is disconnected.

Remedy: Please connect cable to Slave.

### 3.15.10.19 PROF-018 Exist specific diag(%d)

Cause: A status message exists in the slave specific diagnostic area in the received diagnostic data.

Remedy: Please invstigate the specific diagnostic data.

### 3.15.10.20 PROF-019 Multi-boards are not supported

Cause: Multiple Profibus boards are not supported.

Remedy: Please set only one Profibus board.

### 3.15.10.21 PROF-020 Karel argument is invalid

Cause: Argument for PR_ONLN or PR_OFFLN is invalid.

Remedy: It should be integer and 1 to 32.

<!-- PDF page 1380 -->

### 3.15.11 PROG Alarm Code

#### 3.15.11.1 PROG-001 Invalid pointer is specified

**Cause:** This indicates an internal system error.

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

#### 3.15.11.2 PROG-002 Invalid task name is specified

**Cause:** The task name specified is invalid.

**Remedy:** Check the task name.

#### 3.15.11.3 PROG-003 Invalid prog name is specified

**Cause:** The program name specified is invalid.

**Remedy:** Check the program name.

#### 3.15.11.4 PROG-005 Program is not found

**Cause:** The specified program cannot be found.

**Remedy:** Check the program name.

#### 3.15.11.5 PROG-006 Line is not found

**Cause:** The specified line number cannot be found.

**Remedy:** Check the line number.

#### 3.15.11.6 PROG-007 Program is already running

**Cause:** The specified program is already being executed.

**Remedy:** Check the program name.

<!-- PDF page 1381 -->

### 3.15.11.7 PROG-008 In a rtn when creating a task

Cause: Execution cannot be started in sub-routine program.

Remedy: Check the line number.

### 3.15.11.8 PROG-009 Line not same rtn as paused at

Cause: Resumption was attempted at a different line from the paused line.

Remedy: Check the line number.

### 3.15.11.9 PROG-010 Not same prg as paused

Cause: Resumption was attempted in a different program from the paused one.

Remedy: Check the program name.

### 3.15.11.10 PROG-011 Cannot get the motion control

Cause: Motion control cannot be obtained.

Remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

### 3.15.11.11 PROG-012 All groups not on the top

Cause: There is paused motion later than motion that was attempted to resume.

Remedy: Resume the motion paused the last time.

### 3.15.11.12 PROG-013 Motion is stopped by program

Cause: This motion was paused by the MOTION PAUSE instruction. Only the RESUME MOTION program instruction can can resume the motion.

Remedy: Use RESUME MOTION instruction in the program.

### 3.15.11.13 PROG-014 Max task number exceed

Cause: The number of programs you attempted to start exceeded the maximum number.

<!-- PDF page 1382 -->

**Remedy:** Abort dispensable programs or perform a CTRL start and select PROGRAM INIT option to increase the number of tasks allowed.

### 3.15.11.14 PROG-015 Cannot execute backwards

**Cause:** Backward execution cannot be used.

**Remedy:** Do not use backward execution at this point

### 3.15.11.15 PROG-016 Task is not found

**Cause:** The specified task is not running or paused.

**Remedy:** Check the task name. The task name is always the name of the program that was run. The task name will not change even if the running program calls a routine from a different program.

### 3.15.11.16 PROG-017 Task is not running

**Cause:** The specified task is not running.

**Remedy:** Check the task name.

### 3.15.11.17 PROG-018 Motion stack overflowed

**Cause:** Too many programs are paused.

**Remedy:** Resume or abort some programs.

### 3.15.11.18 PROG-019 Ignore pause request

**Cause:** The request to pause the program was ignored.

**Remedy:** Change the NOPAUSE task attribute or use the KCL PAUSE command with the FORCE option.

### 3.15.11.19 PROG-020 Task is already aborted

**Cause:** The specified program was already aborted.

**Remedy:** Check the program name.

<!-- PDF page 1383 -->

### 3.15.11.20 PROG-021 Ignore abort request

Cause: The request to abort the program was ignored.

Remedy: Change the NOABORT task attribute or use the KCL ABORT command with the FORCE option.

### 3.15.11.21 PROG-023 Task is not paused

Cause: The specified program is not paused.

Remedy: Pause the program.

### 3.15.11.22 PROG-024 Not have motion history

Cause: The motion path record is lost.

Remedy: Do not attempt backwards execution at this time.

### 3.15.11.23 PROG-025 Cannot execute backwards

Cause: Backward execution cannot be used.

Remedy: Do not use backwards execution here.

### 3.15.11.24 PROG-026 No more motion history

Cause: Backward execution cannot be used any more. The current line is on top of the memorized path.

Remedy: Do not use backwards execution here.

### 3.15.11.25 PROG-027 Invalid task number

Cause: The task number specified is invalid.

Remedy: Check the task number.

### 3.15.11.26 PROG-029 Buffer size is not enough

Cause: This indicates an internal system error.

<!-- PDF page 1384 -->

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### **3.15.11.27 PROG-030 Attribute is not found**

**Cause:** The specified task attribute is not found.

**Remedy:** Check the attribute.

### **3.15.11.28 PROG-031 Attribute is write protected**

**Cause:** The specified task attribute is write protected.

**Remedy:** Do not try to change the attribute.

### **3.15.11.29 PROG-032 Invalid value for attribute**

**Cause:** The value for the specified attribute is invalid.

**Remedy:** Check the attribute value.

### **3.15.11.30 PROG-034 Routine not found**

**Cause:** The specified routine cannot be found.

**Remedy:** Check the routine name and verify it is loaded.

### **3.15.11.31 PROG-035 Not locked the specified group**

**Cause:** Motion control for the specified group cannot be locked.

**Remedy:** Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

### **3.15.11.32 PROG-036 The length of trace array is 0**

**Cause:** Not enough memory or the task attribute is not set correctly.

**Remedy:** Set the trace buffer length using the KCL SET TASK TRACELEN command.

<!-- PDF page 1385 -->

### 3.15.11.33 PROG-037 No data in the trace array

Cause: There is no execution record in memory.

Remedy: Turn on tracing using the KCL SET TRACE ON command.

### 3.15.11.34 PROG-039 locked, but not get mctl

Cause: Motion control for the specified group was reserved, but it cannot be obtained.

Remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

### 3.15.11.35 PROG-040 Already locked by other task

Cause: Motion control for the specified group was already reserved by another program.

Remedy: Check the other running programs to determine who has motion control.

### 3.15.11.36 PROG-041 mctl denied because released

Cause: Motion control is released. The teach pendant currently has motion control. The robot cannot be started until motion control is obtained.

Remedy: Disable the teach pendant.

### 3.15.11.37 PROG-042 Already released

Cause: Motion control was already released.

Remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

### 3.15.11.38 PROG-043 Already released by you

Cause: Motion control was already released by request of this program.

Remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

<!-- PDF page 1386 -->

### 3.15.11.39 PROG-044 Arm has not been released yet

Cause: Motion control was not released yet.

Remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already locked the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check LOCK_GROUP usage.

### 3.15.11.40 PROG-045 Other than requestor released

Cause: Motion control was already released by the request of another program.

Remedy: If you had expected that another task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

### 3.15.11.41 PROG-046 TP is enabled while running (%s^7)

Cause: The teach pendant was enabled while the program is executing.

Remedy: Disable the teach pendant and resume the program.

### 3.15.11.42 PROG-047 TP is disabled while running (%s^7)

Cause: The teach pendant was disabled while the program is executing.

Remedy: Enable the teach pendant and use shift-FWD to resume execution.

### 3.15.11.43 PROG-048 Shift released while running (%s^7)

Cause: The shift key was released while the program is executing.

Remedy: Hold the shift key and press the FWD key to resume execution.

### 3.15.11.44 PROG-049 Cannot release, robot moving

Cause: Motion control cannot be released because the robot is moving.

Remedy: Check the status of robot motion.

### 3.15.11.45 PROG-050 Abort still in progress

Cause: The program is in the process of being aborted.

<!-- PDF page 1387 -->

Remedy: Wait a second. If this error continues to occur, perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.15.11.46 PROG-051 Cannot skip the return stmt

Cause: The specified lines to which a move was attempted exceed the number of lines in the program.

Remedy: Check the line number.

### 3.15.11.47 PROG-052 Process is aborted while executing

Cause: The user application task was forced to abort while the application is executing. The AMR may not have been completely processed.

Remedy: This requires no special action for the user.

### 3.15.11.48 PROG-053 User AX is not running

Cause: The user application task was not executed.

Remedy: Start the user application task before executing the application.

### 3.15.11.49 PROG-054 FWD released while running (%s^7)

Cause: FWD key was released while the program is executing.

Remedy: Hold the FWD key with shift key to resume execution.

### 3.15.11.50 PROG-055 BWD released while running (%s^7)

Cause: BWD key was released while the program is executing.

Remedy: Hold the BWD key with shift key to resume execution.

### 3.15.11.51 PROG-056 Motion data out is enable

Cause: Motion data output function is enable instead of machin lock id disable.

<!-- PDF page 1388 -->

Remedy: Please disable motion data output in test cycle menu.

### 3.15.11.52 PROG-057 Power Fail Recover memory is cleared

Cause: The backup of the execution memory failed. Then, the system restarted automatically.

Remedy: Cycle power to the controller.

### 3.15.11.53 PROG-058 Pause[P]

Cause: Pausing when using M-TP. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

Remedy: Push the OK button, restart the program, or push servo-ON button on M-TP to reset this warning.

### 3.15.11.54 PROG-059 Abnormal communication[P]

Cause: Abnormal communication with the M-TP. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

Remedy: Power OFF and ON the controller.

### 3.15.11.55 PROG-060 Don't set FANUC's uframe[P]

Cause: An attempt was made to set FANUC's uframe. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

Remedy: Don't set FANUC's uframe when using the M-TP.

### 3.15.11.56 PROG-061 Set GD[%s][P]

Cause: GD variable which is used by SHIFT-ON command is not set. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

Remedy: Set the GD variable.

### 3.15.11.57 PROG-062 Using in SHIFT-ON[P]

Cause: This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

Remedy: Set the GD variable.

<!-- PDF page 1389 -->

### 3.15.11.58 PROG-063 Robot is moving by JOG

Cause: This error happens only when using PROGRAM/JOG OVERRIDE function(J579). PROGRAM was executed during jog operation is executed.

Remedy: Stop jog operation is executed.

### 3.15.11.59 PROG-064 Collections cannot be executed

Cause: Execution is not allowed for TP Collection programs.

Remedy: Do not try to execute TP Collection.

### 3.15.12 PTPG Alarm Code

### 3.15.12.1 PTPG-000 Paint Plug-In internal error

Cause: This error is caused when a internal problem has occurred within the Paint Plug In software. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The path is too fast 2. The instructions (PPS and PPE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your Paint Plug In Setup are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed.

Remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communication activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occurred. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

### 3.15.12.2 PTPG-001 %s

Cause: This error is caused when a internal problem has occurred within the Paint Plug In software. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The path is too fast 2. The instructions (PPS and PPE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your Paint Plug In Setup are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed.

Remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communication activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occurred. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

<!-- PDF page 1390 -->

### 3.15.12.3 PTPG-002 Karel Application Task Failure

Cause: A critical task required to run the Paint Plug In software is missing or not running.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation representative.

### 3.15.12.4 PTPG-003 Missing %s TP program

Cause: A TP Event Instruction was called (PPS[x] or PPE), but the corresponding TP program or sub-program was not loaded. This caused the Paint Plug-In to abort the job.

Remedy: Ensure the missing TP program is loaded.

### 3.15.12.5 PTPG-004 Critical IO is invalid

Cause: This error is usually caused by a system failure.

Remedy: Check TPE instructions. Cycle power on controller.

### 3.15.12.6 PTPG-005 Index incorrect

Cause: The schedule index value of the current instruction execution is invalid.

Remedy: Check the index value of instruction.

### 3.15.12.7 PTPG-006 Job %s aborted

Cause: The current Job has been aborted due to a fatal error.

Remedy: Correct the cause of this error, which is usually posted immediately before this error is posted.

### 3.15.12.8 PTPG-007 %s:Invalid Group Mask

Cause: The Group Mask attribute in the TP header of the specified program is set.

Remedy: Ensure that the Group mask is NOT set for the specified program.

### 3.15.12.9 PTPG-008 %s:Unknown Paint Event

Cause: The Paint Plug-In detected an unknown Paint Event, which caused the system to fault.

<!-- PDF page 1391 -->

Remedy: Determine the cause for this unknown event to execute.

### 3.15.12.10 PTPG-009 %s:Event TP Prog Timeout

Cause: An Event TP program did not complete processing within the specified time.

Remedy: Ensure that the TP program instruction is correct.

### 3.15.12.11 PTPG-010 No PPE Instruction

Cause: The Paint Plug-In detected a Paint Start(PPS[]) TP instruction without a matching Paint End (PPE) instruction.

Remedy: Ensure that a PPE instruction is included at the end of the job.

### 3.15.12.12 PTPG-011 %s No PPS Instruction before PPE

Cause: The Paint Plug-In detected a Paint End (PPE) instruction without a Paint Start (PPS).

Remedy: Ensure that a PPS instruction is included before a PPE instruction.

### 3.15.13.48 PWD-066 Bad password data

Cause: There are 2 causes for this alarm. The first is that the password USB device has incorrect username and password. This will be the cause code for PWD-062 Login from USB device is cancelled. The second is that a password configuration file, FRS:PASSWORD.DT, is invalid.

Remedy: For the first cause, check the password USB device. Your INSTALL user may have to add your username and password using the SETUP Passwords menu. For the second cause, the INSTALL user should IMPORT a correct password configuration file using the SETUP Passwords menu. This file will replace FRS:PASSWORD.DT. It becomes a binary file for protection. It is possible that an invalid configuration file was restored because someone tried to break into the password system.

### 3.15.13.54 PWD-072 Protected in AUTO mode

### 3.16 Q

### 3.16.1 QMGR Alarm Code

### 3.16.1.1 QMGR-001 Queue is full

Cause: An attempt was made to add entry to a queue when the queue was full.

Remedy: Use GET_QUEUE to remove entries or use a larger value for queue size in the INIT_QUEUE call.

### 3.16.1.2 QMGR-002 Queue is empty

Cause: An Attempt to use GET_QUEUE when there are no entries in the queue This is the normal result when no entries have been added or all have been removed by previous calls.

Remedy: No remedy is required.

### 3.16.1.3 QMGR-003 Bad sequence no

Cause: A bad sequence_no value is used in an INSERT_QUEUE or DELETE_QUEUE call. The value may be less than 1 or greater than the sequence number of the last entry in the queue.

<!-- PDF page 1401 -->

Remedy: Correct the value

### 3.16.1.4 QMGR-004 Bad n_skip value

Cause: n_skip parameter in COPY_QUEUE call is less than zero

Remedy: Use zero or a positive value

### 3.17 R

### 3.17.1 RIPE Alarm Code

### 3.17.1.1 RIPE-001 Time is resynchronized

Cause: System network timing has been lost. The system has automatically been reestablished.

Remedy: If this continues to happen, the physical Network wiring configuration and setup should be checked for errors. Usually this is just a result of a re-power of one of the controllers.

### 3.17.1.2 RIPE-002 FRS:ROSIPCFG.XML not found

Cause: System network timing has been lost but the system has automatically reestablished timing.

Remedy: If this continues to happen, the configuration and setup should be checked for errors.

### 3.17.1.3 RIPE-003 FRS:ROSIPCFG.XML has %d warnings

Cause: The syntax of ROSIPCFG.XML is not correct.

Remedy: Consult TD:RIPINIT.TXT for detailed warnings and correct them.

### 3.17.1.4 RIPE-004 Tracking error

Cause: An internal error has occurred.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1402 -->

### 3.17.1.5 RIPE-005 %s bad configuration

Cause: The rosipcfg.xml is different among the controllers in the RING

Remedy: Make sure that all controllers have identical rosipcfg.xml files

### 3.17.1.6 RIPE-006 Bad destination CPU ID

Cause: An internal error has occurred.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.1.7 RIPE-007 %s is offline

Cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned off or unplugged.

Remedy: None

### 3.17.1.8 RIPE-008 %s is online

Cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned on or plugged in.

Remedy: None

### 3.17.1.9 RIPE-009 Member data is updated

Cause: Information about a member is updated. This is only posted in a system which is not automatically synchronized.

Remedy: None

### 3.17.1.10 RIPE-010 %s has been reset

Cause: The indicated robot has had its protocol reset. This might be the cause of some other error.

Remedy: None

<!-- PDF page 1403 -->

### 3.17.1.11 RIPE-011 This robot is not in the ring

Cause: The IP address of this robot is not found anywhere in FRS:ROSIPCFG.XML.

Remedy: The configuration must include the correct IP addresses.

### 3.17.1.12 RIPE-012 Initial time synchronization

Cause: An initial tick time synchronization has occurred. This message is posted after all robots are powered up.

Remedy: None

### 3.17.1.13 RIPE-013 Robot not found in ring data

Cause: A robot specified in a destination is not part of the ring defined in ROSIPCFG.XML.

Remedy: The configuration must include information on all robots in the ring.

### 3.17.1.14 RIPE-014 Packet is too large

Cause: The system has attempted to send a packet which is too large. The limit is 1472 bytes.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.1.15 RIPE-015 Packet cannot round trip

Cause: A packet sent to all robots cannot be a round trip packet.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.1.16 RIPE-016 Robot time not synchronized

Cause: A call was made to get network tick before the system ticks are synchronized.

Remedy: Wait for the synchronized message before requesting tick value.

<!-- PDF page 1404 -->

### 3.17.1.17 RIPE-017 Time tracking inconsistent

Cause: A call was made to get network tick before the system ticks are synchronized.

Remedy: Wait for the synchronized message before requesting tick value.

### 3.17.1.18 RIPE-018 Robot is offline

Cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned off or unplugged.

Remedy: None

### 3.17.1.19 RIPE-019 Overrun condition

Cause: More than 48 requests are queued to RIPE have not been processed

Remedy: Check the network hardware. Structure the application to limit or throttle RIPE packet sends

### 3.17.1.20 RIPE-020 Bad configuration

Cause: The ROSIPCFG.XML file is not the same among the robots.

Remedy: Make the ROSIPCFG.XML file the same.

### 3.17.1.21 RIPE-021 Robot has been reset

Cause: A robot has had its protocol reset similar to going online and offline.

Remedy: This is for information only but could be the result of a packet send on an unstable network.

### 3.17.1.22 RIPE-022 Robot has resequenced

Cause: Messages were received out of sequence. This could be due to bad network hardware.

Remedy: Power cycle may be required to reset depending on the number of robots involved.

<!-- PDF page 1405 -->

### 3.17.1.23 RIPE-023 Robot resequence response

Cause: Messages were received out of sequence. This could be due to bad network hardware.

Remedy: Power cycle may be required to reset depending on the number of robots involved. None

### 3.17.1.24 RIPE-024 RIPE CPU busy %d

Cause: CPU is busy, RIPE may experience difficulties.

Remedy: Check/reduce CPU load.

### 3.17.2 RMIT Alarm Code

### 3.17.2.1 RMIT-001 Internal System Error.

Cause: Remote Motion interface internal system error.

Remedy: Power off to recover. If problem persists, please reload the controller.

### 3.17.2.2 RMIT-002 Invalid UTool Number.

Cause: The user tool number is not valid.

Remedy: Please make sure the tool number is within range.

### 3.17.2.3 RMIT-003 Invalid UFrame Number.

Cause: The user frame number is not valid.

Remedy: Please make sure the user frame number is within range.

### 3.17.2.4 RMIT-004 Invalid Position Register.

Cause: The position register number is not valid.

Remedy: Please make sure the position register number is within range.

<!-- PDF page 1406 -->

### 3.17.2.5 RMIT-005 Invalid Speed Override.

Cause: Invalid speed override value

Remedy: Please make sure the speed override set between 1 to 100

### 3.17.2.6 RMIT-006 Cannot Execute TP program.

Cause: Robot Controller cannot start Teach Pendant program execution in AUTO mode

Remedy: Please make sure the Teach Pendant is disabled and the controller is in AUTO mode. Please clear/reset any error and the controller's servo is on before sending FRC_Initialize command.

### 3.17.2.7 RMIT-007 Controller Servo is Off.

Cause: Robot Controller's servo is off.

Remedy: Please clear/reset any error.

### 3.17.2.8 RMIT-008 Teach Pendant is Enabled.

Cause: The teach pendant is enabled.

Remedy: Please turn off the teach pendant and put controller in AUTO mode.

### 3.17.2.9 RMIT-009 RMI is Not Running.

Cause: The RMI TP program is not running.

Remedy: Please use FRC_Initialize to start RMI Motion Interface again.

### 3.17.2.10 RMIT-010 TP Program is Not Paused.

Cause: The RMI TP progam cannot be paused.

Remedy: Use FRC_Abort to abort the TP program and FRC_Initialize to restart the program.

### 3.17.2.11 RMIT-011 Cannot Resume TP Program.

Cause: The RMI TP progam can not be resumed.

<!-- PDF page 1407 -->

Remedy: Use FRC_Initialize to restart Remote Motion Interface.

### 3.17.2.12 RMIT-012 Cannot Reset Controller.

Cause: FRC_Reset command cannot clear all errors.

Remedy: Check robot controller for error that prevents the reset command.

### 3.17.2.13 RMIT-013 Invalid RMI Command.

Cause: Controller received invalid command.

Remedy: Check RMI manual to make sure correct RMI command is sent to robot controller.

### 3.17.2.14 RMIT-014 RMI Command Fail.

Cause: RMI command failed.

Remedy: The RMI command has no effect on the robot controller due to current robot controller status.

### 3.17.2.15 RMIT-015 Invalid Controller State.

Cause: The controller is in error state when receiving the RMI command.

Remedy: Make sure the robot controller is in valid state before sending RMI command

### 3.17.2.16 RMIT-016 Please Cycle Power.

Cause: RMI Does not work when controller has HOT start enabled.

Remedy: Remote Motion Interface disable Hot start for next cycle start. Please cycle power.

### 3.17.2.17 RMIT-017 Invalid Payload Schedule.

Cause: Invalid Payload schedule number.

Remedy: Make sure a valid payload schedule number is sent to the controller.

<!-- PDF page 1408 -->

### 3.17.2.18 RMIT-018 Invalid Motion Option.

Cause: Invalid motion option in motion instruction, or the controller is not loaded with the required option.

Remedy: Make sure to send the correct motion option to controller.

### 3.17.2.19 RMIT-019 Invalid Vision Register.

Cause: The input vision register number is not valid.

Remedy: Please make sure the vision register number is within range.

### 3.17.2.20 RMIT-020 Invalid RMI Instruction.

Cause: An invalid TP instruction is received by the controller.

Remedy: Check the instruction string to make sure correct RMI instruction is sent to robot controller. Make sure number of executing instruction is less or equal to eight.

### 3.17.2.21 RMIT-021 Invalid Value.

Cause: The input value is out of acceptable range.

Remedy: Please check the value specified in the text string to make sure they are in the acceptable range.

### 3.17.2.22 RMIT-022 Invalid Text String

Cause: The controller cannot parse the input text string.

Remedy: Please check the text string to make sure it comply with format specified in the manual

### 3.17.2.23 RMIT-023 Invalid Position Data

Cause: The position data is invalid.

Remedy: Please make sure the position data text comply with the specification defined in the manual.

<!-- PDF page 1409 -->

### 3.17.2.24 RMIT-024 RMI is In HOLD State

Cause: RMI is in HOLD state due to error in previous instruction packet.

Remedy: Please send FRC_Reset to reset the controller before sending new RMI instruction.

### 3.17.2.25 RMIT-025 Remote Device Disconnected.

Cause: Remote device is not connected to the controller.

Remedy: Please send FRC_Connect packet to controller to establish the connection.

### 3.17.2.26 RMIT-026 Robot is Already Connected.

Cause: Robot is already connected to an external device

Remedy: Make sure there is no other remote device is connected to the robot controller. Or use FRC_Disconnect to disconnect previous connection.

### 3.17.2.27 RMIT-027 Wait for Command Done.

Cause: Controller is still executing previous command.

Remedy: Please wait for controller to complete current command before sending next command packet.

### 3.17.2.28 RMIT-028 Wait for Instruction Done.

Cause: Controller is still executing previous instructions.

Remedy: Please wait for controller to complete previous instruction before sending next instruction packet.

### 3.17.2.29 RMIT-029 Invalid sequence ID number.

Cause: The new instruction has an invalid sequence ID number.

Remedy: Make sure the sequence ID is consecutive and monotonic increasing before sending next instruction packet.

<!-- PDF page 1410 -->

# **3.17.2.30 RMIT-030 Invalid Speed Type.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid speed type.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct string for speed type.

# **3.17.2.31 RMIT-031 Invalid Speed Value.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid speed value.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct string for speed value.

# **3.17.2.32 RMIT-032 Invalid Term Type.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid termination type.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct termination type.

# **3.17.2.33 RMIT-033 Invalid Term Value.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid termination value.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct termination value.

# **3.17.2.34 RMIT-034 Invalid LCB Port Type.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid local condition port. type.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct local condition port type.

# **3.17.2.35 RMIT-035 Invalid ACC Value.**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid ACC value.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct ACC value.

# **3.17.2.36 RMIT-036 Invalid Destination Position**

**Cause:** The motion instruction has an invalid destination position.

**Remedy:** Make sure the motion string includes correct destination position data.

<!-- PDF page 1411 -->

### 3.17.2.37 RMIT-037 Invalid VIA Position.

Cause: The motion instruction has an invalid via position.

Remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct via position data.

### 3.17.2.38 RMIT-038 Invalid Port Number.

Cause: The instruction has an invalid port number.

Remedy: Make sure instruction string includes correct port number.

### 3.17.2.39 RMIT-039 Invalid Group Number.

Cause: Instruction has an invalid group number.

Remedy: Make sure the group number in the instruction string is a valid one.

### 3.17.2.40 RMIT-040 Invalid Group Mask.

Cause: Instruction has an invalid group mask.

Remedy: Make sure group mask in the instruction string match the controller's figuration.

### 3.17.2.41 RMIT-041 Joint motion with COORD.

Cause: COORD option does not allow follower with joint motion

Remedy: Change the motion type to linear motion.

### 3.17.2.42 RMIT-042 Incremental motn with COORD

Cause: COORD option does not allow incremental motion.

Remedy: Remove INC motion option.

### 3.17.2.43 RMIT-043 Robot is in Single Step Mode

Cause: Robot Controller is in single step mode.

Remedy: Press STEP button to disable single step.

<!-- PDF page 1412 -->

### 3.17.2.44 RMIT-044 Invalid Position Data Type

Cause: The position data is in different representation than specified by the instruction.

Remedy: Change the position data to match the instruction's specification.

### 3.17.2.45 RMIT-040 Invalid Group Mask.

Cause: Instruction has an invalid group mask.

Remedy: Make sure group mask in the instruction string match the controller's figuration.

### 3.17.2.46 RMIT-041 Joint motion with COORD.

Cause: COORD option does not allow follower with joint motion

Remedy: Change the motion type to linear motion.

### 3.17.2.47 RMIT-042 Incremental motn with COORD

Cause: COORD option does not allow incremental motion.

Remedy: Remove INC motion option.

### 3.17.2.48 RMIT-043 Robot is in Single Step Mode

Cause: Robot Controller is in single step mode.

Remedy: Press STEP button to disable single step.

### 3.17.2.49 RMIT-044 Invalid Position Data Type

Cause: The position data is in different representation than specified by the instruction.

Remedy: Change the position data to match the instruction's specification.

### 3.17.2.50 RMIT-045 Not Ready for ASCII Packet

Cause: RMI is not ready to receive next ASCII instruction.

Remedy: Please wait for FRC_AsbnReady before sending next ASCII instruction.

<!-- PDF page 1413 -->

### 3.17.2.51 RMIT-046 ASCII Conversion Failed.

Cause: RMI cannot convert the ASCII string to TP instruction.

Remedy: Please Check the ASCII string so it matches the text in /MN section of a LS file.

### 3.17.2.52 RMIT-047 Invalid ASCII Instruction.

Cause: Some /MN ASCII instructions are not supported in RMI.

Remedy: Please do not use this ASCII instruction in RMI application

### 3.17.2.53 RMIT-048 Invalid Number of Groups.

Cause: Number of position data does not match controllers group number.

Remedy: Please make sure the input packet has the correct number of position data that matches the group mask set by the FRC_Initialize command.

### 3.17.2.54 RMIT-049 Invalid Instruction Packet.

Cause: Instruction packet is invalid when $RMI_CFG.$ASBN_ENB = TRUE

Remedy: Please set $RMI_CFG.$ASBN_ENB to FALSE and recycle power to use Instruction packet.

### 3.17.2.55 RMIT-050 Invalid ASCII Packet.

Cause: ASCII packet is invalid when $RMI_CFG.$ASBN_ENB = FALSE

Remedy: Please set $RMI_CFG.$ASBN_ENB to TRUE and recycle power to use ASCII packet.

### 3.17.2.56 RMIT-051 Invalid ASCII String Size.

Cause: ASCII string exceed 128 bytes limit.

Remedy: Please make sure ASCII string does not exceed 128 bytes.

<!-- PDF page 1414 -->

### 3.17.2.57 RMIT-052 Invalid Application Tool.

Cause: The controller has a different application tool setting than the specified tool string in FRC_Initialize packet.

Remedy: Please make sure the TOOL value is compatible with controller's application tool.

### 3.17.2.58 RMIT-053 Invalid Call Program Name.

Cause: The CALL program name is not valid.

Remedy: Please provide an existing and valid TP program name for the CALL instruction.

### 3.17.2.59 RMIT-054 Joint Motion with ALIM.

Cause: Joint motion does not support ALIM motion option.

Remedy: Change the motion type to linear motion.

### 3.17.2.60 RMIT-055 ALIM option is not loaded.

Cause: Controller does not have ALIM option loaded.

Remedy: Please load ALIM (R921) option to the controller.

### 3.17.3 ROOP Alarm Code

### 3.17.3.1 ROOP-001 Internal abort error %s

Cause: Internal CP Resume Offset on Path error.

Remedy: Contact FANUC Support with error and information on events leading up to the error.

### 3.17.3.2 ROOP-002 Resume offset on path not enabled

Cause: Resume Offset on Path feature has not been enabled.

Remedy: Enable feature at CTRL start in ROOP MENU.

<!-- PDF page 1415 -->

### 3.17.3.3 ROOP-003 Robot is not calibrated

Cause: Robot is not calibrated.

Remedy: Calibrate robot before using ROOP.

### 3.17.3.4 ROOP-004 Invalid motion group specified

Cause: Either an invalid motion group or mask has been specified. ROOP only supports group G1 for dispensing.

Remedy: Make sure TP Program only uses Group G1.

### 3.17.3.5 ROOP-005 Path size not initialized

Cause: Internal ROOP path variable size is not initialized.

Remedy: Go to ROOP CTRL start menu and set ROOP max number of nodes > 0 and press F3 APPLY.

### 3.17.3.6 ROOP-006 Failed current pos Cartesian conversion

Cause: During ROOP playback, robot current position conversion from Joint to Cartesian failed.

Remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.7 ROOP-007 Failed last record Cartesian conversion

Cause: During ROOP playback, recorded position conversion from Joint to Cartesian failed.

Remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.8 ROOP-008 Failed to setup stored position

Cause: Internal setup for or edit of TP program failed.

Remedy: Contact FANUC Support with information on events leading up to the error. If present, refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1416 -->

### 3.17.3.9 ROOP-009 Robot is%smm from recorded position

Cause: Distance between current robot position and recorded motion being issued is too large.

Remedy: Try one or more of the following: Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP speed and press F3 APPLY. Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP node exec delay and press F3 APPLY. Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP distance tol and press F3 APPLY.

### 3.17.3.10 ROOP-010 Auto error recovery not ready

Cause: ROOP attempted to use Auto Error Recovery but was unsuccessful.

Remedy: Review Auto Error Recovery setup for proper settings.

### 3.17.3.11 ROOP-011 Adjusting path length failed

Cause: Internal ROOP path node append or delete failed.

Remedy: Contact FANUC Support with information on events leading up to the error. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.12 ROOP-012 Program has no motion

Cause: No motion has been recorded for ROOP playback.

Remedy: Review circumstances when the original program paused. This is when data is recorded. Refer to the alarm history for more possible information.

### 3.17.3.13 ROOP-013 Recorded path capacity is at 90%

Cause: Capacity is at 90% for recorded ROOP path.

Remedy: This is just a warning. If capacity reaches 100%, the program will ABORT. To reduce amount of recorded data, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase capacity, Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP max number of nodes and press F3 APPLY.

### 3.17.3.14 ROOP-014 Reached maximum path capacity

Cause: Capacity is FULL for recorded ROOP path.

<!-- PDF page 1417 -->

Remedy: To reduce amount of recorded data, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase capacity, Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP max number of nodes and press F3 APPLY.

### 3.17.3.15 ROOP-015 %s lock group failed

Cause: ROOP attempt to lock group G1 failed.

Remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.16 ROOP-016 Cannot find group mask

Cause: Either an invalid motion group or mask has been specified.

Remedy: Make sure TP Program has at least one valid motion group in group mask. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.17 ROOP-017 Create TP program failed

Cause: Internal create TP program failed.

Remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.18 ROOP-018 Open TP editor failed

Cause: Internal open TP program failed.

Remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.19 ROOP-019 Close TP editor failed

Cause: Internal close TP program failed.

Remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1418 -->

### 3.17.3.20 ROOP-020 Edit TP program failed

Cause: Internal edit TP program failed.

Remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

### 3.17.3.21 ROOP-021 Gun resume time warning

Cause: This is only a warning. This indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate. If posted by itself, the ROOP setup Gun delay or an internal timing calculation is out of limits.

Remedy: Review circumstances when the original program paused. Refer to the alarm history for more possible information.

### 3.17.3.22 ROOP-022 Resume offset distance warning

Cause: This is only a warning. The ROOP setup menu Resume Offset is out of limits. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.

Remedy: Set the ROOP setup menu Resume Offset within limits. Doing this may require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however.

### 3.17.3.23 ROOP-023 Resume offset > CP data available

Cause: This is only a warning. The robot cannot move as far back as requested because not enough CP data exists. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.

Remedy: To reduce the backup distance, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase the data available for CP resume offset, do one or more of the following the Resume Offset setup menu: Increase the Max Offset Res Dist. Decrease the Nominal Process Speed. Press DONE and allow the robot to cycle power, then manually cycle power again. Doing any of this will require re-tuning of all Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delays for all dispense equipments however.

### 3.17.3.24 ROOP-024 Insufficient CP data for return to pause

Cause: This is only a warning. The robot cannot move back to the original fault position because not enough CP data exists. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.

<!-- PDF page 1419 -->

Remedy: To increase the data available for CP resume offset, do one or more of the following the Resume Offset setup menu: Increase the Max Offset Res Dist. Decrease the Nominal Process Speed. Press DONE and allow the robot to cycle power, then manually cycle power again. Doing any of this will require re-tuning of all Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delays for all dispense equipments however.

### 3.17.3.25 ROOP-025 Gun Delay value warning

Cause: This is only a warning. The ROOP setup menu Gun Delay is out of limits. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.

Remedy: Set the ROOP setup menu Gun Delay within limits. If a decreased Gun Delay does not allow the gun to resume at the proper timing then the backup distance must be decreased. To reduce the backup distance, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however.

### 3.17.3.26 ROOP-026 Unable to perform ROOP

Cause: Unable to perform CP Resume Offset on Path and therefore resuming is prohibited in order to prevent shortcut motion.

Remedy: Verify correct setup for Auto Error Recovery and Resume Offset menus.

### 3.17.4 ROUT Alarm Code

### 3.17.4.1 ROUT-022 Bad index in ORD

Cause: Incorrect number is specified for ORD builtin routine.

Remedy: Specify a number less than the string length.

### 3.17.4.2 ROUT-023 Bad index in SUBSTR

Cause: Incorrect number is specified for SUBSTR builtin routine.

Remedy: Specify a number less than the string length.

### 3.17.4.3 ROUT-024 SUBSTR length less than 0

Cause: Negative number is specified for length argument for SUBSTR builtin routine.

<!-- PDF page 1420 -->

Remedy: Specify a positive number.

### 3.17.4.4 ROUT-025 Illegal semaphore number

Cause: Incorrect number is specified for semaphore id.

Remedy: Specify a number between 1 and 32.

### 3.17.4.5 ROUT-026 Illegal group number

Cause: Invalid group number is specified.

Remedy: Specify exisiting group number.

### 3.17.4.6 ROUT-027 String size not big enough

Cause: Specified string variable does not have enough room to hold the return data.

Remedy: specify larger size string variable.

### 3.17.4.7 ROUT-028 Illegal file attribute number

Cause: Incorrect file attribute id was specified.

Remedy: Specify correct file attribute id.

### 3.17.4.8 ROUT-029 Illegal file attribute value

Cause: Incorrect file attribute value was specified.

Remedy: Specify correct attribute value.

### 3.17.4.9 ROUT-030 Non existent register number

Cause: A non-existent register number is specified.

Remedy: Specify a correct register number.

<!-- PDF page 1421 -->

### 3.17.4.10 ROUT-031 Illegal register type

Cause: Incorrect register type is specified.

Remedy: Specify the correct register type for the attempted operation.

### 3.17.4.11 ROUT-032 Position type mismach

Cause: Position type is not correct for the operation.

Remedy: Specify correct position type.

### 3.17.4.12 ROUT-033 Illegal attribute type

Cause: Illegal attribute id was specified.

Remedy: Specify correct attribute id.

### 3.17.4.13 ROUT-034 Not a TPE program

Cause: A non-tpe is specified.

Remedy: Specify a program name other than a Karel program.

### 3.17.4.14 ROUT-035 Value is out of range

Cause: The specified value is out of range.

Remedy: Specify a value within the range.

### 3.17.4.15 ROUT-036 Illegal port id value

Cause: Incorrect port id was used

Remedy: Specify correct port id.

### 3.17.4.16 ROUT-037 Bad TPE header size

Cause: Value used in SET_HEAD_TPE for bfr_size is invalid.

Remedy: Use buffer size in the range 1-255.

<!-- PDF page 1422 -->

### 3.17.4.17 ROUT-038 Uninitialized TPE position

Cause: Attempt to access position data or type from TPE program when the position has not been recorded.

Remedy: Record position data using the TPP TOUCHUP function

### 3.17.4.18 ROUT-039 Executing motion exists

Cause: Cannot unlock group while motion is executing.

Remedy: Wait until executing motion has completed.

### 3.17.4.19 ROUT-040 Stopped motion exists

Cause: Cannot unlock group while stopped motion exists.

Remedy: Resume stopped motion and wait until motion has completed or cancel stopped motion.

### 3.17.4.20 ROUT-041 Dym. disp. var. not static

Cause: Variable displayed for dynaoic display is not a static variable. Parameter may be a local or constant. Neither of these is permitted as the displayed variable in INI_DYN_DIS calls.

Remedy: Copy constant or local variable to static variable and use this inINI_DYN_DIS* call.

### 3.17.4.21 ROUT-042 TPE parameters do not exist

Cause: The parameter designated by param_no does not exist.

Remedy: Confirm the param_no and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main TPE program.

### 3.17.4.22 ROUT-043 TPE parameter %s wrong data type

Cause: The parameter data type does not match the CALL/MACRO argument data type.

Remedy: Confirm the parameter data type in CALL/MACRO command in main TPE program.

<!-- PDF page 1423 -->

### 3.17.4.23 ROUT-044 Tag name too long

Cause: Tag name supplied in MSG_CONNECT, MSG_DISCO, or MSG_PING call was too long.

Remedy: Use tag name not over 12 characters.

### 3.17.4.24 ROUT-045 Dictionary name too long

Cause: Dictionary name supplied in built-in call is too long.

Remedy: Use name of 4 or less characters.

### 3.17.4.25 ROUT-046 Option array not initialized

Cause: Call to apnd_mtn_opt, write_xyzwpr, or write_joint with option array not initialized

Remedy: Initialize the array by calling INIT_MTN_OPT

### 3.17.4.26 ROUT-047 Stream buffer full

Cause: Stream instruction program buffer is full.

Remedy: Wait for stream program execution to complete more instructions, then retry.

### 3.17.4.27 ROUT-048 Stream not active

Cause: The streaming program is not currently running.

Remedy: Issue the function on an active stream program.

### 3.17.4.28 ROUT-049 Invalid motion options

Cause: The motion option data supplied in the motion write routine call is not valid, or does not match the specified motion type.

Remedy: Initialize and fill the motion options correctly.

### 3.17.4.29 ROUT-050 SET comment builtin string too long

Cause: A string containing over 16 characters passed as comment argument in SET_TPE_CMT call. Argrument truncated to 16 characters.

<!-- PDF page 1424 -->

Remedy: Use comment string of 16 or fewer characters.

### 3.17.5 RPC Alarm Code

#### 3.17.5.1 RPC-001 Can't encode arguments

Cause: The client could not encode its arguments in a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

#### 3.17.5.2 RPC-002 Can't decode result

Cause: The client could not decode the results of a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

#### 3.17.5.3 RPC-003 Unable to send

Cause: The client could not send the data for a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

#### 3.17.5.4 RPC-004 Unable to receive

Cause: The client could not receive a reply from a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

#### 3.17.5.5 RPC-005 Call timed out

Cause: The client timed out while waiting for a reply from a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the server connection.

#### 3.17.5.6 RPC-006 Incompatible versions of RPC

Cause: The server received an older version of the RPC protocol.

Remedy: Update the client software to use the same version of the RPC protocol.

<!-- PDF page 1425 -->

### 3.17.5.7 RPC-007 Authentication error

Cause: The client or server received an unauthorized remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

### 3.17.5.8 RPC-008 Program unavailable

Cause: The server received a remote procedure call for a program which it does not support.

Remedy: Update the server software.

### 3.17.5.9 RPC-009 Program/version mismatch

Cause: The server received a remote procedure call which uses the wrong version of a program.

Remedy: Update the client or server software.

### 3.17.5.10 RPC-010 Procedure unavailable

Cause: The server received a remote procedure call for a procedure which it does not support.

Remedy: Update the server software.

### 3.17.5.11 RPC-011 Server can't decode arguments

Cause: The server could not decode the arguments of a remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the client software.

### 3.17.5.12 RPC-013 Unknown host

Cause: The client could not determine the server for the remote procedure call.

Remedy: Check the system variables which configure the offline RPC server.

### 3.17.5.13 RPC-016 Remote procedure call failed

Cause: The remote procedure call failed.

Remedy: Check the cause code.

<!-- PDF page 1426 -->

### 3.17.5.14 RPC-018 Low = %d, High = %d

Cause: The server received a remote procedure call which uses the wrong version of a program. The versions supported are shown.

Remedy: Update the client or server software.

### 3.17.5.15 RPC-019 PC Interface option not loaded

Cause: This operation requires the PC Interface option to be loaded on the controller.

Remedy: Install the PC Interface software option on the controller. Refer to the FANUC America Corporation Software Installation Manual for more information.

### 3.17.6 RPM Alarm Code

### 3.17.6.1 RPM-001 n_buffers invalid

Cause: The value for $RPM_CONFIG.$N_BUFFERS is invalid

Remedy: Set $RPM_CONFIG.$N_BUFFERS in the range 1-100

### 3.17.6.2 RPM-002 record_size invalid

Cause: The value for $RPM_CONFIG.$DATA_SIZE is invalid

Remedy: Set $RPM_CONFIG.$DATA_SIZE in the range 4-32

### 3.17.6.3 RPM-005 memory allocation failed

Cause: There is not enough cmos memory for this rpm segment

Remedy: Increase the cmos memory by deleting unused TPE Or increase pitch value so that rpm do not need so much cmos space.

### 3.17.6.4 RPM-009 segment not in buffer

Cause: Attempt to playback a segment that is not recorded in the specified buffer

Remedy: Check that RECORD is active for this segment and using the correct buffer number.

<!-- PDF page 1427 -->

### 3.17.6.5 RPM-013 invalid buffer no

Cause: Buffer number specified is invalid

Remedy: Use a buffer number in the range 1-$RPM_CONFIG.$N_BUFFERS

### 3.17.6.6 RPM-014 record not stored

Cause: This segment was not recorded

Remedy: Re-record the whole path

### 3.17.6.7 RPM-020 read record not stored

Cause: There is no rpm data is stored in this segment

Remedy: Check the position number Or re-record again

### 3.17.6.8 RPM-026 Pitch value too small.

Cause: Pitch value is too small

Remedy: Time pitch value have to equal or greater than 100

### 3.17.6.9 RPM-027 Illegal arc instruction.

Cause: Stand alone arc start used

Remedy: Use motion attached arc start instruction

### 3.17.6.10 RPM-028 Segment too short

Cause: The segment for RPM is either zero length move or too short

Remedy: Zero length RPM motion is not allow

### 3.17.6.11 RPM-039 Incompatible RPM data:nonCD/CD

Cause: RPM data has coordinated motion but TPE doesn't have. Or RPM data has non-coordinated motion but TPE has.

<!-- PDF page 1428 -->

Remedy: Use same coordinated motion type (CD or non-CD) to both TAST and RPM program.

### 3.17.6.12 RPM-050 Max segment limit

Cause: reach max segments in recording

Remedy: Check segment length and increase the segment length.

### 3.17.6.13 RPM-051 Stationary trk disabled

Cause: Stationary track is disabled.

Remedy: None.

### 3.17.7 RRMC Alarm Code

### 3.17.7.1 RRMC-001 Internal PLAN error (G: %d^2)

Cause: Internal PLAN error. This class of error should not be encountered during normal operation

Remedy: The system may have been corrupted. This may have been caused by any of a number of reasons including: Incorrect loading and setup loading incompatible options, mixing software version when adding options and other memory corruption problems. The following is a list of possible remedies: 1. Perform a cold start. 2. Perform an init start and setup the robot again 3. Confirm that any options or additional software not on the original software distribution media is the same version number. If the main system software was supplied on several disks or memory cards, make sure that you are using a matched set. Also make sure that the installation manual being used is for this version of software. If any of the software version are not matched, a complete re-load with the correct software will be necessary. 4. Confirm that no incompatible or mutually exclusive option have been loaded. 5. Full software reload. 6. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.
