### 3.17.8 RTCP Alarm Code

#### 3.17.8.1 RTCP-001 Wrist Joint is not allow

Cause: Wrist joint orient type resume is not allow in RTCP motion.

Remedy: Change $MCR_GRP[*].$RSM_ORIENT to 1 (OR_RS_WORLD).

#### 3.17.8.2 RTCP-002 VRTCP not calibrated

Cause: Invalid UTool for VRTCP.

Remedy: Change UTool No. for VRTCP.

#### 3.17.8.3 RTCP-003 VRTCP Invalid UTool No.

Cause: Some VRTCPs have same Leader GP No.

Remedy: Use different Leader GP No.

#### 3.17.8.4 RTCP-004 VRTCP overlapped Leader Group

Cause: Some VRTCPs have same Remote TCP No.

Remedy: Use different Remote TCP No.

#### 3.17.8.5 RTCP-005 VRTCP overlapped RTCP No.

Cause: Conversion failure from pulse to angle.

Remedy: Do COLD start.

#### 3.17.8.6 RTCP-006 VRTCP pulse to angle conv.

Cause: A conversion failure occurred from pulse to angle.

Remedy: Perform a Cold start.

<!-- PDF page 1433 -->

### 3.17.8.7 RTCP-007 DRTCP use FINE for transition

Cause: DRTCP use FINE as term type for a DRTCP transition.

Remedy: Change the termination type to FINE for the transition line.

### 3.17.8.8 RTCP-008 DRTCP Joint pos not allow

Cause: Data recorded can not be a joint representation type for a DRTCP line. That includes the transition line.

Remedy: Re-Record the position with Cartesian type.

### 3.17.8.9 RTCP-009 DRTCP Joint move not allow

Cause: DRTCP coordinate jog does not allow joint jog.

Remedy: Use a Cartesian move instead.

### 3.17.8.10 RTCP-010 DRTCP INC move not allow

Cause: DRTCP does not allow incremental instruction

Remedy: Use absolute recording position

### 3.17.8.11 RTCP-011 DRTCP Internal Error 1

Cause: DRTCP internal error 1.

Remedy: Perform a Cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.8.12 RTCP-012 DRTCP Internal Error 2

Cause: DRTCP internal error 2

Remedy: Perform a Cold start:

<!-- PDF page 1434 -->

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.8.13 RTCP-013 DRTCP Internal Error 3

Cause: DRTCP internal error 3

Remedy: Perform a Cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.17.8.14 RTCP-014 RTCP not supported with COORD

Cause: Program with RTCP option was executed while COORD option is loaded on controller. RTCP cannot be used when COORD is loaded.

Remedy: Remove RTCP option from TP program.

### 3.17.8.15 RTCP-015 Option+RTCP not supported

Cause: This option (Weave, Touch sensing, TAST, RPM..) is enabled with a RTCP Motion RTCP cannot be used when this option is enabled.

Remedy: Remove the RTCP option from the teach pendant program.

### 3.17.8.16 RTCP-017 DRTCP C move not allow

Cause: DRTCP does not allow Circular Motion

Remedy: Use Arc motion.

### 3.18 S

### 3.18.1 SCIO Alarm Code

### 3.18.1.1 SCIO-003 Cannot teach any more.

Cause: You cannot add the instruction to the same line. The size of mnemonic code exceeds maximum size of one line data.

Remedy: Please reduce the instruction like a parameter string.

### 3.18.1.2 SCIO-016 Prog uses un-installed option.

Cause: The TPP program being loaded uses an option which is not installed on the controller where the program is being loaded (target controller).

Remedy: Determine what options are installed on the controller on which the program was saved (source cptroller) and are not installed on the target controller Then, on the source controller, check which of these is used in the program. Assuming the option(s) are authorized for the target controller, install the necessary options. If some of these options are not authorized, it ay be necessary to remove uses of the unauthorized option uses and re-save the program on the source controller.

### 3.18.1.3 SCIO-020 LBL[%d] exists in line %d:

Cause: This label number exists in another line.

Remedy: Select another label number.

### 3.18.1.4 SCIO-030 JOINT motion in slave program

Cause: Robot Link slave program and slave alone program can not use JOINT motion statement.

Remedy: Record this line as LINER or CIRCULAR motion statement

### 3.18.1.5 SCIO-031 JOINT position in slave program

Cause: Robot Link slave program and slave alone program can not use JOINT position representation.

Remedy: Record this line as CARTESIAN position representation

<!-- PDF page 1436 -->

### 3.18.1.6 SCIO-032 Master UT mismatch

Cause: Current Tool frame number of Master robot is different from Master Tool Number specified in Program detail menu.

Remedy: Change Tool frame number of Master Robot or change master tool number in Program detail menu.

### 3.18.1.7 SCIO-033 Slave can have ony one motion line

Cause: Robot link Slave program can have only one motion line.

Remedy: Please teach only one line in slave program.

### 3.18.1.8 SCIO-034 Illegal fn code of TUI FN instruction

Cause: An illegal FN code is found in the TUI FN instruction.

Remedy: The program might be broken. The system software might be older than where the program is made. Delete the program and make a new one.

### 3.18.1.9 SCIO-036 Too many items in mixed logic line

Cause: Too many items are taught in mixed logic line.

Remedy: Please delete some items in this line.

### 3.18.1.10 SCIO-037 Invalid item in mixed logic line

Cause: Invalid item is taught in mixed logic line.

Remedy: Please delete invalid item in this line.

### 3.18.2.48 SDTL-048 Wrong data type(Line %s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Wrong data type (identifier) is specified in CSV file.

Remedy: Displayed line of specified file has problem. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Even if the string is valid identifier for X_DTCOPY, it may not be supported by X_DYNDAT. Actually most of valid identifier of X_DTCOPY are not supported by X_DYNDAT. Please specify identifier that is supported by X_DYNDAT.

### 3.18.2.49 SDTL-049 Illegal terminator(Line %s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Terminator is expected at the end of a line of CSV file but it was not found.

### 3.18.2.50 SDTL-050 Illegal index(Line %s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Wrong index is specified in CSV file.

Remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Check the string, data type and its data format. If index is out of range, specify proper value.

### 3.18.2.51 SDTL-051 Illegal group(Line %s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Wrong formatted data is found where group number should be specified.

Remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Check the string, data type and its data format.

<!-- PDF page 1445 -->

### 3.18.2.52 SDTL-052 Illegal data(Line %s)

Cause:Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Unexpected data is found at displayed line of specified CSV file.

Remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. Check data type and its data format.

### 3.18.2.53 SDTL-053 Illegal config(Line %s)

Cause:Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Position register of Cartesian data type needs configuration data. Wrong data is specified in CSV file.

Remedy:Check displayed line of CSV file. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Specify configuration data properly.

### 3.18.2.54 SDTL-054 Out of range(Line %s)

Cause:Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Integer value in CSV file was out of range.

Remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. Wrong value, minimum value and maximum value are displayed, too. Write proper data in CSV file.

### 3.18.2.55 SDTL-055 Empty field does not exist(Line %s)

Cause:Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. CSV file doesn't have empty field (field that doesn't have character) where it is expected. If data for an identifier is composed of 2 or more lines, the 2nd or later lines must start with empty field.

Remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Check data type and its data format. Input data in proper format.

### 3.18.2.56 SDTL-056 Converted to real of out of range(Line %s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Very large (or small) value is specified as real value of register. It was interpreted as value of out of range. Data should be larger than -1.0E16 and less than 1.0E16. Scientific notation cannot be used in CSV file.

Remedy: Make absolute value smaller.

<!-- PDF page 1446 -->

### 3.18.2.57 SDTL-057 Index of SR is wrong(%s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT without argument causes this error. In this case, path of CSV file is decided by string register. Index of string register is decided by KAREL variable, [X_DYNDAT]IDEFSRIDX (KAREL variable IDEFSRIDX of KAREL program X_DYNDAT). String register of specified index doesn't exist.

Remedy: Check value of [X_DYNDAT]IDEFSRIDX. Change its value to valid index of string register.

### 3.18.2.58 SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file(%s)

Cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. %s shows specified path of CSV file. If X_DYNDAT is used without argument, string register used to decide file path is displayed, too. Following table shows examples. In all cases, specified file could not be opened.

Table 3-1. Examples

[tbl-0.md](tbl-0.md)

Please refer to cause code, too. For example, if error is posted like following, please check if specified file exists or not.

SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file (MC:\CP_0100.CSV)

FILE-014 File not found.

Remedy: Check displayed file path. Check if specified file exists.

Cause: String of file path doesn't include :\\. %s shows specified file path.

Remedy: Include :\\ in file path string.

<!-- PDF page 1447 -->

### 3.18.2.60 SDTL-061 Illegal file path (%s)

Cause: Specified file path is not proper. %s shows specified file path.

Remedy: Correct file string path.

### 3.18.2.61 SDTL-062 Last char is not \\ (%s)

Cause: The last character of file path string is not \\. %s shows specified file path.

Remedy: Correct file path string.

### 3.18.2.62 SDTL-063 Failed to copy (%s)

Cause: File copy failed. %s shows destination file name.

Remedy: Check whether specified file device and sub directory can be used

### 3.18.2.63 SDTL-064 TP Program does not exist (%s)

Cause: Specified TP program does not exist on the controller. %s shows specified TP program name.

Remedy: Please specify program that exists on controller.

### 3.18.2.64 SDTL-065 Program name is not specified %s

Cause: Program name was not specified. If string register is specified, information of the string register is displayed. SR[1] for example.

### 3.18.2.65 SDTL-066 * cannot be used (%s)

Cause: Program name for STWRPRT and CRWRPRT contains "*". You cannot use the character to specify program name.

### 3.18.2.66 SDTL-067 Failed to turn write protect on(%s)

Cause: Write protection could not be turned on. %s shows program name. If string register is specified, information of the string register is also displayed.

### 3.18.2.67 SDTL-068 Index of SR is wrong(%s)

Cause: Index of string register is wrong. %s shows specified index is displayed.

For example, when STWRPRT or CRWRPRT was called without argument, IDEFSRIDX of each program is used. The value should be checked.

### 3.18.2.68 SDTL-069 Failed to turn write protect off(%s)

Cause: Write protection could not be turned off. %s shows program name. If string register is specified, information of the string register is also displayed.

Remedy: Displayed program is used. Try again in a state that displayed program is not used. Please refer to cause code.

### 3.18.2.69 SDTL-070 Specified program is not TP(%s)

Cause: Specified program is not TP program.

Remedy: Specify TP program.

### 3.18.2.70 SDTL-077 Payload center position is out of range(%s)

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Payload center is out of range. It is specified by register. Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is 101. Center of gravity of payload is specified by R[102]. If its value is -20.5, (X, 102, -20.500) is displayed.

Remedy: Check index of register and its value. Set proper value

<!-- PDF page 1449 -->

### 3.18.2.71 SDTL-078 Payload inertia is out of range(%s)

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Inertia of payload is out of range. It is specified by register. Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is 101. Inertia of payload around X axis is specified by R[105]. If its value is -20.5, (X, 105, -20.500) is displayed.

Remedy: Check index of register and its value. Set proper value

### 3.18.2.72 SDTL-079 TPE parameter %s wrong data type

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Data type of parameter is wrong.

### 3.18.2.73 SDTL-080 Failed to get TPE parameter %s

Remedy: Modify TP program to set proper parameter

### 3.18.2.74 SDTL-081 Register for payload does not exist(%s).

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload does not exist.

Remedy: The 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is index of register of payload Set proper value.

### 3.18.2.75 SDTL-082 Register for payload center(%s) does not exist.

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload center does not exist. coordinate (X or Y or Z) and index are displayed, too.

Remedy: Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is n. STPAYLOD uses R[n], R[n+1], ... R[n+6] Modify the 3rd argument so that the 7 registers exist. Set proper value to the 3rd argument

### 3.18.2.76 SDTL-083 Register for payload inertia (%s) does not exist.

Cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload inertia does not exist. coordinate (X or Y or Z) and index are displayed, too.

<!-- PDF page 1450 -->

**Remedy:** Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is n. STPAYLOD uses R[n], R[n+1], ... R[n+6] Modify the 3rd argument so that the 7 registers exist.

### 3.18.2.77 SDTL-071 Torque Limit Function not installed

**Cause:** Torque Limit Function is not installed.

**Remedy:** Buy and install Torque Limit Function option

### 3.18.2.78 SDTL-072 Torque Limit disabled

**Cause:** Torque Limit Function is disabled

**Remedy:** Enable torque limit function

### 3.18.2.79 SDTL-073 Group %s not mastered

**Cause:** Specified group is not mastered

**Remedy:** Perform mastering from the calibration screen.

### 3.18.2.80 SDTL-074 Illegal group(%s)

**Cause:** This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD The 1st argument is group number. Specified group doesn't exist.

**Remedy:** Check the 1st argument of STPAYLOD. Specify motion group that exists on the controller.

### 3.18.2.81 SDTL-075 Illegal Payload schedule number(%s)

**Cause:** This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. The 2nd argument is payload schedule number. Specified payload schedule number doesn't exist.

**Remedy:** Check the 2nd argument of STPAYLOD. Specify payload schedule number that exists on the controller.

### 3.18.2.82 SDTL-076 Payload is out of range(%s)

**Cause:** This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Payload that is set in specified register is out of range. Index of register that is used to specify payload is displayed.

<!-- PDF page 1451 -->

Its value, which should be payload, is displayed, too. Suppose R[5] is specified and its value is -10.5 (5, -10.500) is displayed

Remedy: Check index of register and its value. Set proper payload

### 3.18.2.83 SDTL-101 Too many Plugins defined

Cause: Number of plugins exceeded maximum.

Remedy: Uninstall plugins that are not needed.

### 3.18.2.84 SDTL-102 Operation canceled

Cause: Current operation has been canceled by the operator.

Remedy: Do the operation again.

### 3.18.2.85 SDTL-103 Non-conforming Program Name

Cause: Non-conforming Program name.

Remedy: Program name has to start with the PlugIn ID.

### 3.18.2.86 SDTL-104 Invalid Plugin software (%s)

Cause: The Content of IPL file is invalid.

Remedy: Make sure the content is valid.

### 3.18.2.87 SDTL-105 Unsupported Robot type

Cause: This robot type is not supported for this plugin.

Remedy: This plugin is incompatible with the robot type, and cannot be loaded to this robot.

### 3.18.2.88 SDTL-106 Option (%s) is required

Cause: This plugin requires the specified option.

Remedy: This plugin cannot function without the specified feature (option). Please load the specified option before loading the plugin.

<!-- PDF page 1452 -->

### 3.18.2.89 SDTL-111 Getting menu data

Cause: Fail to get menu info file in the specified path.

Remedy: Make sure the valid menu file is on the specified path.

### 3.18.2.90 SDTL-112 Menu data syntax

Cause: Syntax error in the menu info file.

Remedy: Make sure the valid menu data is in the menu data file.

### 3.18.2.91 SDTL-113 System Error

Cause: System error getting Screen ID system variable.

Remedy: Make sure the Screen ID variable exists.

### 3.18.2.92 SDTL-114 System Error

Cause: System error setting Screen ID system variable.

Remedy: Make sure the Screen ID variable exists.

### 3.18.3 SEAL Alarm Code

### 3.18.3.1 SEAL-000 Dispensetool internal error

Cause: This error is caused when Dispensetool encounters a problem it is unable to solve internally. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The sealing path is too fast 2. The sealing instructions (SS and SE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your sealing schedules are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed

Remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communication activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occurred. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

<!-- PDF page 1453 -->

### 3.18.3.11 SEAL-010 Processing error at line %d

Cause: When an line tracking program is processed, it is scanned for the extreme values within each sealing segment. If an error occurs during this scanning process, an error is posted. The error may occur for several reasons: A jump instruction during a sealing segment, or an unsupported instruction during a sealing segment.

Remedy: Verify that every instruction between the first SS and the SE instructions is supported by DispenseTool. Also verify that no JUMP instructions exist between the first SS and the SE instruction.

### 3.18.3.12 SEAL-021 Gun on/off too late: Sch %d

Cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Gun On signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fore 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when the gun will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE: Time_Before = EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.

Remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn the gun on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

### 3.18.3.13 SEAL-022 Meter on too late: Sch %d

Cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Start Meter signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fire 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when this signal will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = PRE_PRESSURE_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE[n]: Time_Before = DE_PRESSURE_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.

Remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn this signal on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the pre/de_pressure_delay or

<!-- PDF page 1457 -->

equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

### 3.18.3.14 SEAL-023 Air on/off too late: Sch %d

Cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Atomizing Air signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fire 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when this signal will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = ATOMIZING_ON_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE[n]: Time_Before = ATOMIZING_OFF_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.

Remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn this signal on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the atomizing_on/off/_delay or equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

### 3.18.3.15 SEAL-024 Error in motion triggering

Cause: The high performance I/O triggering system (Motion Trigger) has returned a bad status. When this occurs, the redundant triggering system will take over, but the quality of the SSs and SEs will be poor. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. A Gun On output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 2. A Start Meter output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 3. A Atomizing Air output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 4. There is a problem with the software setup of the I/O system. 5. There is a problem with the hardware setup of the I/O system.

Remedy: Go to the Equipment Output menu and verify that all the Gun on, Start Meter, and Atomizing Air outputs are correctly defined or their indexes are set to zero. If the VALUE of a output port is '***', then the index number must be set to zero and the robot must be cold started. You must cold start the robot after changing anything on this menu.

### 3.18.3.26 SEAL-041 Seal not ready

Cause: The system ready signal(DI) turns off when the sealant is dispensed.

Remedy: Check the system ready signal of the sealing equipment or disable the system ready signal.

### 3.18.3.27 SEAL-042 Part ID mismatch detected

Cause: Transmitted and received part IDs to dispensing equipments do not match.

Remedy: Check wiring of group I/O line for part ID and part ID acknowledge signals. Check dispensing equipment for proper operation.

### 3.18.3.28 SEAL-043 High pressure

Cause: The pressure signal is above its upper limit for set time when the sealant is dispensed.

Remedy: Check the pressure signal of the sealing equipment, disable to check the high pressure signal, or set the time high pressure timeout to a larger value.

### 3.18.3.29 SEAL-044 Low pressure (E%d)

Cause: The pressure signal is below its lower limit for set time when the sealant is dispensed.

Remedy: Check the pressure signal of the sealing equipment, disable to check the low pressure signal, or set the time low pressure timeout to a larger value.

<!-- PDF page 1460 -->

### 3.18.3.30 SEAL-045 High pressure (E%d)

Cause: The pressure signal is above its upper limit for set time when the sealant is dispensed.

Remedy: Check the pressure signal of the sealing equipment, disable to check the high pressure signal, or set the time high pressure timeout to a larger value.

### 3.18.3.31 SEAL-046 Seal not start

Cause: The gun full open signal(DI) has been on for the set time since sealing start.

Remedy: Check the gun full open signal of the sealing equipment, disable the check for this feature, or set the timeout for a longer period.

### 3.18.3.32 SEAL-047 Seal interrupt

Cause: The gun full open signal(DI) has been on for the set time since sealing start.

Remedy: Check the gun full open signal of the sealing equipment, disable the check for this feature, or set the timeout for a longer period.

### 3.18.3.33 SEAL-048 Dispenser mode mismatch (E%d)

Cause: Dispenser switch position does not match equipment set up

Remedy: Check key switch on the dispensing equipment and equipment setup

### 3.18.3.34 SEAL-049 Calibrations not complete (E%d)

Cause: One or more calibration procedures are not complete

Remedy: Visit equipment SETUP menu and complete all calibration procedures

### 3.18.3.35 SEAL-050 Shot meter not full (E%d)

Cause: The dispenser should be full at this point, and is not.

Remedy: Check that the dispenser is full for this operation.

<!-- PDF page 1461 -->

### 3.18.3.36 SEAL-051 Both Drums are empty (E%d)

Cause: Both drums are empty

Remedy: Check sealant supply drums to be sure they are properly filled

### 3.18.3.37 SEAL-052 Same fault posted repeatedly (E%d)

Cause: Same fault occurs repeatedly

Remedy: Check dispensing equipment and clear the reported fault

### 3.18.3.38 SEAL-053 Robot is in dry run mode

Cause: Dry run parameter is ON.

Remedy: Set DRY RUN parameter to OFF and run calibration again.

### 3.18.3.39 SEAL-054 Robot lock mode is ON

Cause: Robot lock parameter is ON.

Remedy: Set ROBOT LOCK parameter to OFF and run calibration again.

### 3.18.3.40 SEAL-055 Part ID out of range

Cause: The Part ID in the JOB header is out of the allowed range for this robot.

Remedy: Make sure the Part ID in the JOB header is between 0 and the maximum Part ID allowed on this equipment.

### 3.18.3.41 SEAL-056 Dispenser not ready (E%s)

Cause: Dispenser ready input signal from dispenser is OFF.

Remedy: Check dispenser manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.42 SEAL-057 Dispenser fault (E%s)

Cause: A fault was detected at the dispensing controller.

<!-- PDF page 1462 -->

Remedy: Perform the standard dispenser fault recovery procedure. See the dispensing controller's manual for more information.

### 3.18.3.43 SEAL-058 Flow rate fault (E%s)

Cause: The dispenser has detected a abnormally low or high material flow rate. This could be caused by a plugged gun.

Remedy: See the dispensing equipment manual for more information. You could try cleaning and purging the gun.

### 3.18.3.44 SEAL-059 Not calibrated warning (E%s)

Cause: One or more calibration procedures are not complete

Remedy: Visit equipment SETUP menu and complete all calibration procedures

### 3.18.3.45 SEAL-060 High pressure (E%d)

Cause: The high pressure signal(DI) has been on for the configured time during sealing.

Remedy: Check the sealing equipment high pressure signal, disable the check for the high pressure signal, or set the timeout value for a longer period

### 3.18.3.46 SEAL-061 Seal not ready

Cause: The system ready signal(DI) turns off when sealant is being dispensed.

Remedy: Check the sealing equipment ready signal or disable the check of the equipment ready signal.

### 3.18.3.47 SEAL-062 Reload fault (E%d)

Cause: There is a reload problem with the meter

Remedy: Check the shot meter

### 3.18.3.48 SEAL-063 High pressure

Cause: The high pressure signal(DI) has been on for the configured time during sealing.

<!-- PDF page 1463 -->

Remedy: Check the sealing equipment high pressure signal, disable the check for the high pressure signal, or set the timeout value for a longer period

### 3.18.3.49 SEAL-064 Not at purge position

Cause: Robot is not at purge position

Remedy: Make sure the robot returns to purge position at the end of each cycle

### 3.18.3.50 SEAL-065 Maximum purge count reached

Cause: The Auto Purge feature has determined that the robot should purge now, but the maximum number of purges it is allowed to perform in a row (as set in the equipment setup menu) has been reached.

Remedy: Increase the maximum number of purges allowed or remove the disposable mixing tip from the gun, to prepare it for long term inactivity.

### 3.18.3.51 SEAL-066 Seal not start

Cause: The gun full open signal(DI) has been on for the set time since sealing start.

Remedy: Check the gun full open signal of the sealing equipment, disable the check for this feature, or set the timeout for a longer period.

### 3.18.3.52 SEAL-067 Seal interrupt

Cause: Gun full open signal(DI) has been on for too long while dispensing.

Remedy: Check the gun full open signal of sealing equipment, disable the checking of this alarm, or set the timeout value to a longer time.

### 3.18.3.53 SEAL-068 Flow command excessive%s

Cause: Flow command output voltage is larger than the maximum output.

Remedy: Decrease the motion speed or increase the maximum output.

### 3.18.3.54 SEAL-069 Dispenser malfunction (E%d)

Cause: The dispensing equipment controller has detected a fault in its hardware.

<!-- PDF page 1464 -->

**Remedy:** Perform maintenance and debug procedures as described in the dispensing equipment manual.

### **3.18.3.55 SEAL-070 Gun malfunction (E%d)**

**Cause:** A dispensing gun malfunction has been detected by the dispensing controller.

**Remedy:** Perform dispensing gun maintenance and debug procedures.

### **3.18.3.56 SEAL-071 Gun full open too long (E%d)**

**Cause:** A low pressure condition has been detected by the dispensing controller

**Remedy:** Check the pressure sensors at all points in the system. Perform standard system debug and maintenance procedures.

### **3.18.3.57 SEAL-072 High nozzle pressure (E%d)**

**Cause:** A high pressure condition has been detected in the dispensing gun nozzle. In specific, nozzle pressure signal is greater than (NOZZLE SENSOR RATING/100) * 5 volts for over one second.

**Remedy:** Reduce system pressure if it is permissible. Select a nozzle pressure transducer with a wider operating range.

### **3.18.3.58 SEAL-073 High dispensed volume (E%d)**

**Cause:** The volume of material dispensed on the previous job was above the preset limit.

**Remedy:** Verify that the volume limits are correct for the specified job.

### **3.18.3.59 SEAL-074 Low dispensed volume (E%d)**

**Cause:** The volume of material dispensed on the previous job was below the preset limit

**Remedy:** Verify that the volume limits are correct for the specified job.

### **3.18.3.60 SEAL-075 Flow meter fault (E%d)**

**Cause:** A error was detected in the flow meter readings.

<!-- PDF page 1465 -->

Remedy: Verify that the flowmeter is operating correctly.

### 3.18.3.61 SEAL-076 Bead defect detected (E%d)

Cause: An incorrect bead condition was detected.

Remedy: Perform dispensing gun maintenance procedures.

### 3.18.3.62 SEAL-077 Sealer equipment fault (E%d)

Cause: An unknown error code was received from the dispensing controller.

Remedy: Check the dispensing controller for an error condition. Also check the communication link between the dispensing controller and robot controller.

### 3.18.3.63 SEAL-078 Dispenser comm fault (E%d)

Cause: An error was encountered reading fault data from the dispenser

Remedy: Check the communications link between the dispenser and robot

### 3.18.3.64 SEAL-079 Dispenser E-stop (E%d)

Cause: An Emergency Stop condition was detected at the dispensing controller

Remedy: Clear the fault and perform the proper Emergency Stop recovery procedure.

### 3.18.3.65 SEAL-080 Dispenser fault (E%d)

Cause: A fault was detected at the dispensing controller.

Remedy: Perform the standard dispenser fault recovery procedure. See the dispensing controller's manual for more information.

### 3.18.3.66 SEAL-081 Volume comp at maximum (E%d)

Cause: Interim value for volume has exceeded maximum interim limit.

Remedy: Re-learn part or increase maximum limit.

<!-- PDF page 1466 -->

### 3.18.3.67 SEAL-082 Drum A empty (E%d)

Cause: The first of the two drums is empty

Remedy: This is a warning to the operator that the drum might need service

Cause: The second of the two drums is empty.

Cause: Flow command output voltage is lower than the minimum output.

Remedy: Increase the motion speed or decrease the minimum output.

Cause: The Dispenser On signal (from the dispenser to the robot) has dropped.

<!-- PDF page 1472 -->

### 3.18.3.106 SEAL-121 Dispense signal fault (E%d)

Cause: The Dispensing signal (from the dispenser to the robot) should be high during dispensing, but it is not.

Remedy: Perform dispenser maintenance procedures to determine why dispensing is not occurring as it should. Also verify that the dispensing schedule data is correct, and that the dispenser I/O to/from the robot has been mapped correctly.

### 3.18.3.107 SEAL-122 Sealing task already active

Cause: You tried to run a JOB or PROC TPP while another JOB or PROC TPP is already running in another task.

Remedy: Only one sealing task may be running at any time. This means that only one JOB or PROC may be running at any time. You must abort the JOB or PROC which is already running before starting a new one.

### 3.18.3.108 SEAL-123 Job aborted

Cause: The current Job has been aborted due to a fatal error.

Remedy: Correct the cause of this error, which is usually posted immediately after this one.

### 3.18.3.109 SEAL-124 Critical IO is invalid

Cause: This error is usually caused by an IO point which is required by Dispensetool being set to an invalid index number or type.

Remedy: Make sure that all inputs and outputs on the Dispenser IO screen are set to valid IO points (the VALUE is not shown as ***) or the index number has been is set to 0. Cold start the robot controller after making any changes to this screen.

### 3.18.3.110 SEAL-129 Index incorrect

Cause: The index value of seal start instruction is invalid.

Remedy: Check the index value of this SS instruction.

<!-- PDF page 1473 -->

### 3.18.3.111 SEAL-131 SS/SE timing invalid

Cause: This error is caused by timing problems with Sealing commands (SS or SE). Timing problems could occur if the robot does not have enough time to plan for a sealing instruction before the robot passes that point in the path. For example: If the user is using a sealing schedule with a gunon delay of 1000ms and a gunoff delay of -1000ms and the robot executes the seam in 1500ms, the Dispensetool will detect the logic problem and post this fault. A path which has many sealing instructions very close to each other (closer than 30mm at 500mm/sec) is likely to have this problem.

Remedy: Make sure there is adequate time for each SS and SE to execute. You may do this by making sure you have only the minimum number of points in your path that you require. Dispensetool works best with as few points as possible. Also, make sure none of your schedules have gunon, gunoff, or equipment delays beyond that which is needed (usually between -100ms and +100ms is adequate). NOTE: Whenever a SEAL-131 occurs, the robot MUST be cold started to recover.

### 3.18.3.112 SEAL-132 Seam segment too short

Cause: There was not enough time between a SS and the next SS or SE for the flow rate computations to be done.

Remedy: Step through your sealing PROCess program, making sure there is at least a centimeter between the points attached to each sealing instruction. Increase the distance between sealing instructions, delete one of the sealing instructions, or slow the robot down.

### 3.18.3.113 SEAL-144 Joint motion

Cause: Robot moved with joint motion during sealing.

Remedy: Change motion type from joint to linear or circular.

### 3.18.3.114 SEAL-147 Equipment does not exist

Cause: This equipment is not exist.

Remedy: Check the equipment number in the program detail display.

### 3.18.3.115 SEAL-148 No SE Instruction

Cause: SE instruction is not exist.

Remedy: Add an SE instruction.

### 3.18.3.136 SEAL-177 EOAT timed out: Flip

Cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the FLIP sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct FLIP/UNFLIP position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.

Remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

### 3.18.3.137 SEAL-178 EOAT timed out: Unflip

Cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the UNFLIP sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct UNFLIP/FLIP position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.

Remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

### 3.18.3.138 SEAL-179 EOAT timed out: Extend

Cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the EXTEND sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct EXTEND/RETRACT position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.

Remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

### 3.18.3.139 SEAL-180 EOAT timed out: Retract

Cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the RETRACT sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct RETRACT/EXTEND position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.

Remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

This could be caused by terminating the job early, causing much less material to be dispensed. This could also be caused by problems with the material, such as using material which has exceeded its shelf life.

Remedy: This warning is normal if it was caused by terminating a job early. If this error happens during normal production, examine the quality of the dispensed job and verify that the dispenser and material are in good condition.

### 3.18.3.163 SEAL-221 Bubble detected (E%d)

Cause: A significant bubble was dispensed with the material during the job. This is usually caused by improper loading of new material. NOTE: This will often cause poor quality sealing. Examine the finished part for any gaps in the sealant bead.

Remedy: Make sure any new material is loaded properly into the supply pump. Make sure all excess air has been drained off before using any new material.

### 3.18.3.221 SEAL-282 Meter Empty (E%d, Mtr %s)

Cause: This warning is posted when the system detects that the meter has reached to its stroke limit during dispensing. After this condition, the system automatically switches to the other meter, and continue dispensing.

Remedy: 1. Reposition the meter prior to start dispensing for the seam. 2. Lower the flow rate so that it can cover the entire seam

### 3.18.3.222 SEAL-283 Both Meters Empty

Cause: This warning is posted when the system detects that both meters have reached to their stroke limit during dispensing. This situation occurs if the material supply pressure is too low. After this condition, the system automatically stops dispensing, but the robot keeps moving. Use Error table to change the severity to PAUSE if you want to pause the program with this warning.

Remedy: 1. Increase the material supply pressure. 2. Lower the flow rate.

### 3.18.3.223 SEAL-284 Plugged Tip Detected (E%d)

Cause: The system has detected that the material flow has been blocked.

Remedy: 1. Check and clean the gun tip.

<!-- PDF page 1491 -->

### 3.18.3.224 SEAL-285 Premature Reload Term (E%d)

Cause: One meter could not complete reloading before the other meter has come to near-empty zone.

Remedy: 1. Increase the material supply pressure 2. Lower the flow rate

### 3.18.3.225 SEAL-287 Cmd prs NOT achieved (E%d)

Cause: The material pressure did not reach the specified pressure within the specified time.

Remedy: 1. Check the IPD air supply pressure 2. Increase the pressure tolerance ($ipd_config[].press_tol)

### 3.18.3.226 SEAL-288 Application setup not done

Cause: The application specific TPPs and macros have not been loaded.

Remedy: Perform a controlled start, then select SETUP APPLICATION under the FCTN menu while the application disk is in the drive.

### 3.18.3.227 SEAL-289 Macro table already full

Cause: Dispenstool has attempted to install additional macros, but the macro table (under menu SETUP:Macros) was already full.

Remedy: Reduce number of macros needed and remove them from the macro table or contact FANUC and request a update to expand macro table size.

### 3.18.3.228 SEAL-290 Invalid call to SL__INST

Cause: SL__INST has been called, but there was no valid macro index number in register 32.

Remedy: Do not run SL__INST as a program, only call SL__INST from a macro after setting a valid macro index number up in register 32.

### 3.18.3.229 SEAL-291 No start sealing input defined

Cause: The PNS Ack Verified input, which is needed with the current communication configuration, has not been defined.

Remedy: Set up a PNS Ack Verified in the Cell Input I/O menu and restart the robot.

<!-- PDF page 1492 -->

### 3.18.3.230 SEAL-292 Max Error table entry exceeded

Cause: In setting up the Default error table the maximum number of error table entries ($ERRSEV_NUM) was exceeded.

Remedy: Go into controlled start, Press MENU-0, then choose PROGRAM SETUP. Change the Error Severity Table entry to be a larger number in order to contain all default errors, and press FCTN-START (COLD). After Cold Start, go back into the Error Table setup screen and manually enter in those error that were not setup correctly.

### 3.18.3.231 SEAL-293 No SLSHELL has been loaded!!!

Cause: The dispense shell is not loaded.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.18.3.256 SEAL-318 Bubble detected (E%s)

### 3.18.3.263 SEAL-325 Override less than 100%

Cause: General override is less than 100% when the system executes SS with TCPP flow type in wet and non-step mode. This alarm is posted for NEMO Pump only.

Remedy: Set the general override to 100%.

### 3.18.3.264 SEAL-326 Line Tracking not allowed.

Cause: Line Tracking is NOT allowed with Dispensing in SpotTool+.

Remedy: Use Select->Detail menu to disable tracking (schedule = 0) to disable Tracking for this program.

### 3.18.3.265 SEAL-327 Tracking detect queue cleared (G:%s)

Cause: This is only a warning message to indicate that all of the triggers / part detects in the tracking queue have been cleared. There are 4 different causes: 1. The CLRQUE key has been used on the MANUAL FUNCTIONS Line Track menu. 2. The Clear Track Que input on the Cell Inputs menu has been set high. 3. The detect queue was full and another detect was received. In this case a SEAL-330 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was full. The queue is cleared because an extra trigger was detected so the data in the queue cannot be trusted. 4. A Tracking queue read error was posted.

<!-- PDF page 1498 -->

Remedy: The remedies for the 4 scenarios above are: 1. Do not use CLRQUE key. 2. Do not set Clear Track Que input high. 3. Also see remedy for SEAL-330 error. Since the detect queue was full, this shows one of 2 possibilities: A. The maximum queue size is not sufficient to handle the number of detects needed in the queue. To increase the queue size, set SSPTK_CFG[x].MAX_QUE_SIZE and cycle power on the robot. B. Extra part detects are being sent to the robot and are mistakenly added to the queue. In this case the Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. Alternately - a system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is SSPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately. 4. See remedy for SEAL-332 error.

### 3.18.3.266 SEAL-328 Waiting for tracking part detect (G:%s)

Cause: If the GET_PART macro is called and there are no triggers in the part detect queue then the macro waits for a valid detect to be placed into the queue. If the time that the robot is waiting for a detect exceeds a specified value then this warning message is generated.

Remedy: The detect wait condition is satisfied once a valid part detect is placed into the queue. If desired, the amount of wait time before this message is posted can be changed by setting the system variable SSPTK_CFG[x].WAIT_MSG_TO in ms. The default value is 3000ms. It can be set to (-)1 to prevent the message from being posted. Changes take effect immediately.

### 3.18.3.267 SEAL-329 Tracking detect ignored - min distance (G:%s)

Cause: This is a message to indicate that the distance the part / conveyor has travelled since the previous part detect has not met / exceeded a minimum defined distance. This debounce logic prevents unwanted detects from being added to the part detect queue.

Remedy: Since extra part detects are being sent to the robot, two remedies are: 1. The Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. 2. A system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is SSPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately.

### 3.18.3.268 SEAL-330 Tracking detect queue full (G:%s)

Cause: This message indicates that the part detect queue was full and another detect was received. In this case a SEAL-337 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was subsequently cleared because an extra trigger was detected - so the data in the queue cannot be trusted.

Remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. Since the detect queue was full, this shows one of 2 possibilities: 1. The maximum queue size is not sufficient to handle the number of detects needed in the queue. To increase the queue size, set

<!-- PDF page 1499 -->

$SPTK_CFG[x].MAX_QUE_SIZE and cycle power on the robot. 2. Extra part detects are being sent to the robot and are mistakenly added to the queue. In this case the Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. Alternately - a system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately.

### 3.18.3.269 SEAL-331 Tracking encoder scale not > 0 (G:%s)

Cause: The Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu is not set to a value greater than 0.

Remedy: The tracking encoder should be set up such that the encoder counts are increasing as the conveyor moves in the forward direction. Consequently, the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu should be set to a value that is greater than 0. Cycle power on the robot after setting this value. Note that only tracking schedule #1 is used. All related programs should not be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

### 3.18.3.270 SEAL-332 Tracking queue read error (G:%s)

Cause: An error was encountered while reading trigger data from the part detect queue. An error will also be posted to indicate the specific queue error encountered. A SEAL-337 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was subsequently cleared because the data in the queue cannot be trusted.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

### 3.18.3.271 SEAL-333 Tracking detect is stale (G:%s)

Cause: The trigger that was read from the part detect queue is stale. This indicates that the conveyor has already travelled far beyond the limits where the trigger would be usable.

Remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. 1. Verify that triggers are being added to and read from the part detect queue correctly as the conveyor moves forward and the job program executes. 2. Verify that no extraneous part detect triggers are being sent to the robot. 3. A system variable exists to limit the distance travelled past robot zero (or rail 0 if equipped) where the part detect trigger is usable. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MAX_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 8000.0mm. It can be set to a large value to delay when this error is posted. Changes take effect immediately.

<!-- PDF page 1500 -->

### 3.18.3.272 SEAL-334 Tracking encoder rollover (G:%s)

Cause: While the conveyor was moving the encoder value passed from the maximum positive integer value the minimum negative integer value (or vice-versa).

Remedy: This is only a warning message and no remedy is needed. All operation should remain as normal.

### 3.18.3.273 SEAL-335 Tracking encoder scale is 0 (G:%s)

Cause: The Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu is not set to a value of 0.0

Remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. The tracking encoder should be set up such that the encoder counts are increasing as the conveyor moves in the forward direction. Consequently, the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu should be set to a value that is greater than 0. Cycle power on the robot after setting this value. Note that only tracking schedule #1 is used.

### 3.18.3.274 SEAL-336 Tracking detect count invalid (G:%s)

Cause: A check has been made of the current detect value before adding it to the part detect queue. It is compared to the previous detect value in light of the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu to ensure it is sensible. When posted, an additional code is also posted to provide further detail. Causes for codes are as follows:

Key: PD = Previous Detect

CD = Current Detect

+S = Positive Enc Scale Factor

-S = Negative Enc Scale Factor

ROL = Rollover

Ps0 = Passed 0 count

Er1: PD>0 CD>0 +S CD<PD

Er2: PD>0 CD>0 -S CD>PD

Er3: PD <0 CD<0 +S PD>CD

Er4: PD <0 CD <0 -S CD<PD

Er5: PD>0 CD=0 +S PD>CD

<!-- PDF page 1501 -->

Er6: PD=0 CD>0 -S CD>PD

Er7: PD<0 CD=0 -S CD>PD

Er8: PD=0 CD<0 +S PD>CD

Er9: Ps0 PD>0 CD<0 +S PD>CD

Er10: ROL PD>0 CD<0 -S PD>CD

Er11: Ps0 PD <0 CD>0 -S PD<CD

Er12: ROL PD <0 CD>0 +S PD<CD

Er98: PD=0 CD=0 PD=CD

Er99: unknown error

Remedy: See causes above to determine the specific problem and possible inferred solution. If the problem persists, then the minimum part detect distance check can be disabled as follows: A system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately. Otherwise document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

### 3.18.3.275 SEAL-343 Proc logger I/O read failure (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor I/O via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The DATA_TYPE or DATA_INDEX fields refer to an invalid I/O point.

Remedy: Set the DATA_TYPE or DATA_INDEX fields to refer to a valid I/O point. If you do not wish to monitor an I/O point then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.276 SEAL-344 Proc logger reg data invalid (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor a data register via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The type of data in that register was found to be invalid.

<!-- PDF page 1502 -->

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.277 SEAL-345 Proc logger reg read failure (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor a data register via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The DATA_INDEX field refers to an invalid data register.

Remedy: Set the DATA_INDEX field to refer to a valid data register. If you do not wish to monitor a data register then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.278 SEAL-346 Proc logger sysvar data invalid (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor other system variables via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The type of data in that system variable was found to be invalid.

Remedy: Only variables of type INTEGER, REAL, or BOOLEAN are supported. Change the VAR_STRING field to refer to a system variable of one of these types only. If you do not wish to monitor a system variable then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.279 SEAL-347 Proc logger sysvar read failure (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor other system variables via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The system variable referred to by the VAR_STRING field is invalid.

Remedy: Change the VAR_STRING field to refer to a valid system variable. If you do not wish to monitor a system variable then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.280 SEAL-348 Proc logger item field invalid (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor items via: $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The item type referred to by the ITEM field is invalid.

<!-- PDF page 1503 -->

Remedy: Change the ITEM field to refer to a valid item type. Valid values for ITEM are: 0 for no use 1 for I/O (signed short) 2 for I/O (unsigned short) 3 for Data number register 4 for String for sysvar If you do not wish to monitor an item then set the ITEM field to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.281 SEAL-349 Proc logger process_id not found (E%d)

Cause: For the Process logger option, when a program is executed (planned) a process_id # is assigned to the TP program line containing a SE statement. This unique identifier will be set to the position number or, if it is a standalone SE statement without motion then it will be set equal to the program line number. When the SE statement is executed a matching process_id must be found. In this case, no matching process_id was found.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.282 SEAL-350 Proc logger internal error %d (E%d)

Cause: This is an internal error for the Process logger option.

Remedy: Record the error string parameters. Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

### 3.18.3.283 SEAL-359 Disp shutoff: OP E-stop (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to an operator panel emergency stop.

Remedy: Clear the operator panel emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.284 SEAL-360 Disp shutoff: TP E-stop (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a teach pendant emergency stop.

Remedy: Clear the teach pendant emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

<!-- PDF page 1504 -->

### 3.18.3.285 SEAL-361 Disp shutoff: Servo off (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a servo disconnect input.

Remedy: Reset the servo disconnect and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.286 SEAL-362 Disp shutoff: NTED (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a Non Teacher Enabling Device (NTED) input.

Remedy: Reset the Non Teacher Enabling Device (NTED) and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.287 SEAL-363 Disp shutoff: Deadman release (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the deadman switch being released while the teach pendant is enabled.

Remedy: Press the deadman switch and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.288 SEAL-364 Disp shutoff: Fence open (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the fence input.

Remedy: Reset the fence input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.289 SEAL-365 Disp shutoff: Hand broken (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the hand broken input.

Remedy: Reset the hand broken input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

<!-- PDF page 1505 -->

### 3.18.3.290 SEAL-366 Disp shutoff: Ext E-stop (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to an external emergency stop.

Remedy: Clear the external emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.291 SEAL-367 Disp shutoff: IMSTP (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the user operator panel (UOP) IMSTP signal.

Remedy: Reset the user operator panel (UOP) IMSTP input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.292 SEAL-368 Disp shutoff: robot faulted (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the controller being faulted.

Remedy: Clear the cause of the fault and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.293 SEAL-369 Disp shutoff: robot held (E%s)

Cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the controller being held.

Remedy: Clear the cause of the hold condition and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

### 3.18.3.294 SEAL-370 Data Monitor is disabled

Cause: Data Monitor subsystem has been disabled, by user choice or automatically because limit on data files set by the user has been reached

Remedy: Enable Data Monitor Operation from the Utilities- Data Monitor screen. On Setup-Diagnostics screen, consider increasing Max Data Files Stored or setting Disable After Max

<!-- PDF page 1506 -->

Files to NO, if these settings caused Data Monitor to to be disabled. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations Manual Advanced Functions for more information.

### 3.18.3.295 SEAL-371 Maximum DMON Data Files exceeded

Cause: The limit on data files that may be stored by the Data Monitor subsystem has been reached.

Remedy: On Setup-Diagnostics screen, consider increasing Max Data Files Stored or setting Disable After Max Files to NO. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions) for more information on these items.

### 3.18.3.296 SEAL-372 DMON in progress, item locked

Cause: Data Monitor session is in progress and user tried to change setup that could affect the current session.

Remedy: Wait till the end of Data Monitor session. If in Automatic Sampling mode, this happens at job end. If sampling in Asynchronous mode, set SAMPLE NOW, under Setup-Diagnostics to STOP, to stop current session.

### 3.18.3.297 SEAL-373 Asynchronous DataMonitor disabled

Cause: Asynchronous Data Monitoring has been disabled

Remedy: To re-enable, ensure that Utilities-Data Monitor-Data Monitor Operation is enabled. Set Setup-Diagnostics-Auto Sample Each Job to NO.

### 3.18.3.298 SEAL-374 Asynchronous DataMonitor enabled

Cause: Asynchronous Data Monitor has been enabled.

Remedy: None.

### 3.18.3.299 SEAL-375 DMON file management disabled

Cause: File management features have been disabled because user set Setup-Diagnostics-Max Data Files Stored to 0. Stored data will be over-written by subsequent sampling sessions.

Remedy: No action required. To re-enable, you may set Max Data Files to non-zero value Ensure that destination data storage device has adequate space. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions)

<!-- PDF page 1507 -->

### 3.18.3.300 SEAL-376 DMON file management enabled

Cause: File management features have been enabled because user set Setup-Diagnostics-Max Data Files Stored value. Data Monitor will store as many old data files as indicated.

Remedy: No action required if destination data storage device has adequate space. To disable, set value to 0. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions) for more information.

### 3.18.3.301 SEAL-377 Sample_start builtin exec failed

Cause: Karel builtin SAMPLE_START returned a bad status.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC service representative.

### 3.18.3.302 SEAL-378 Sample_end builtin exec failed

Cause: Karel builtin SAMPLE_END returned a bad status.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC service representative.

### 3.18.3.303 SEAL-379 Monitor session not started

Cause: Data Monitor session not started.

Remedy: Ensure that these items on the Dispense Diagnostics Setup menu are set correctly: Auto sample each job: Asynch. start enable:

### 3.18.3.304 SEAL-380 Processing error for sldiagdb.dt

Cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered an error while processing the sldiagdb.dt to set up the option.

Remedy: If sldiagdb.dt has been modified, then verify that it has been created and loaded correctly. Refer to FR:DGERRORS.LS for a summary of any errors encountered during processing. Refer to FR:DIAGVARS.LS for a summary of the settings that have been successfully made.

### 3.18.3.305 SEAL-381 Processing OK for sldiagdb.dt

Cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered NO errors while processing the sldiagdb.dt to set up the option.

Remedy: No action required.

<!-- PDF page 1508 -->

### 3.18.3.306 SEAL-382 Copy to rd:diag.dt failed

Cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered an error while attempting to copy the output DT file to rd:diag.dt.

Remedy: Refer to cause code on this alarm for failure reason. If -File not found- is also posted then please set Max data files stored to zero on the Dispense Diagnostics menu and try again. If -Device is full- is also posted then the RAM Disk free area is too small to accommodate the file. You may also try to power down the controller to clear out memory in the RAM Disk and try again. If this does not work then $FILE_MAXSEC may need to be changed to increase the RAM disk size. Refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations Manual for help. If you do not wish to have the diag.dt file copied to the RAM Disk following every monitoring session then set the following variable: [SLVRPADG]copy_dt = FALSE.

### 3.18.4 SEC Alarm Code

### 3.18.4.1 SEC-001 Security Config Mismatch

Cause: The security configuration file has been modified and requires approval.

Remedy: A valid security configuration must be reloaded from the menu on the teach pendant. This error is indicative of modification of security settings using unauthorized methods.

### 3.18.4.2 SEC-002 Last Good Security Config Used

Cause: The security configuration was modified without approval so the last authorized configuration has been loaded.

Remedy: A valid security configuration must be reloaded from the menu on the teach pendant. This error is indicative of modification of security settings using unauthorized methods.

### 3.18.4.3 SEC-003 Security Config Forced to HIGH

Cause: The security configuration was modified without approval and the last authorized configuration is invalid. A high security configuration has been enforced.

Remedy: A valid security configuration must be reloaded from the menu on the teach pendant. This error is indicative of modification of security settings using unauthorized methods.

### 3.18.4.4 SEC-004 FSAC %s^1 deny connect %s^2

Cause: FSAC has denied an incoming connection request to the specified task from the specified IP address

<!-- PDF page 1509 -->

Remedy: Repeated connections from a restricted IP address can indicate the improper configuration of client software or an unauthorized attempt to access the robot controller.

### 3.18.4.5 SEC-005 FSAC %s^1 allow connect %s^2

Cause: FSAC has allowed an incoming connection request to the specified task from the specified IP address

Remedy: FSAC has allowed the client to connect to the robot controller using the specified protocol.

### 3.18.4.6 SEC-006 Security Error loading %s

Cause: A valid security configuration file failed to be loaded.

Remedy: A valid security configuration must be reloaded from the menu on the teach pendant and the controller restarted.

### 3.18.5 SENC Alarm Code

### 3.18.5.1 SENC-001 exceed sec err tol (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Difference between joint command and secondary joint angle exceeded tolerance

Remedy: Check that secondary encoder reading is correct. Reduce speed. If alarm persists, report this issue

### 3.18.5.2 SENC-002 enter accuracy mode (G:%d)

Cause: entered accuracy mode

Remedy: none

### 3.18.5.3 SENC-003 exit accuracy mode (G:%d)

Cause: exited accuracy mode

Remedy: none

<!-- PDF page 1510 -->

### 3.18.5.4 SENC-004 fail to enter acc mode (G:%d)

Cause: Fail to enter accuracy mode. Robot is moving, or difference between primary and secondary encoders angles exceed tolerance

Remedy: Enter accuracy mode only when robot is not moving. If robot is already stationary, check secondary encoder calibration

### 3.18.5.5 SENC-005 already in acc mode (G:%d)

Cause: already in accuracy mode

Remedy: none

### 3.18.5.6 SENC-006 already exit acc mode (G:%d)

Cause: already out of accuracy mode

Remedy: none

### 3.18.5.7 SENC-007 exceed del ang tol (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: difference between primary and secondary encoders angles exceed tolerance

Remedy: exit accuracy mode and check secondary encoder calibration

### 3.18.5.8 SENC-008 fail to exit acc mode (G:%d)

Cause: Fail to exit accuracy mode. Robot is moving

Remedy: Exit accuracy mode only when robot is not moving

### 3.18.5.9 SENC-009 pls not established (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Master before pulse is established.

Remedy: Establish pulse before mastering.

### 3.18.5.10 SENC-010 no initial master (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Master before initial mastering.

<!-- PDF page 1511 -->

Remedy: Perform initial mastering.

### 3.18.6 SENS Alarm Code

#### 3.18.6.1 SENS-000 Unknown error

Cause: System internal error

Remedy: Notify FANUC

#### 3.18.6.2 SENS-001 Hardware error occured

Cause: During data reception, parity, overrun and framing errors occurred.

Remedy: Check that the communication setting between the robot and sensor sides is not wrong.

#### 3.18.6.3 SENS-002 DSR off when transmission

Cause: An attempt was made for data transmission, but DSR signal at the sensor side is in OFF-state.

Remedy: Check that the specification and desconnection of cable connecting the robot and sensor.

#### 3.18.6.4 SENS-003 Undefined TCC received

Cause: The undefined TCC was received from the sensor.

Remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

#### 3.18.6.5 SENS-004 Invalid software parity

Cause: BCC of thereceived data from the sensor is wrong.

Remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

#### 3.18.6.6 SENS-005 Invalid data format

Cause: The format of the received data is wrong.

Remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

<!-- PDF page 1512 -->

### 3.18.6.7 SENS-006 Response time over

Cause: The answer from the sensor is not received within the allowable time.

Remedy: Check that the sensor side does not stop due to an error, for example.

### 3.18.6.8 SENS-007 Interval time over

Cause: The interval of characters sent from the sensor exceeded the allowable time.

Remedy: Check that the sensor side does not stop due to an error, for example.

### 3.18.6.9 SENS-008 Calculate matrix error

Cause: Calculating transform matrix is impossible.

Remedy: Check the compensation data sent from the sensor.

### 3.18.7 SHAP Alarm Code

### 3.18.7.1 SHAP-000 KW ovrd reg. is out of range.

Cause: The value of Kerf Width is not in a valid range.

Remedy: Set the kerf width in a range of 0 to 4.99. If a range > 4.99 is needed, use the KWMINMAX.TP program.

### 3.18.7.2 SHAP-001 Speed ovrd reg. out of range.

Cause: The value in the register for TRAVEL SPEED override is not in a valid range.

Remedy: Set the travel speed in the speed override register to a value less than 2000.

### 3.18.7.3 SHAP-002 Values cannot be duplicated.

Cause: The registers for each shape function such as kerf width override, speed override, and so forth in the Shape Setup menu must be unique. If you try to use the same register twice, this error will occur.

Remedy: Insure that each register is not used more than one time.

<!-- PDF page 1513 -->

### 3.18.7.4 SHAP-003 Corner radius is too large.

Cause: The scheduled corner radius is larger than the computed working radius of the scheduled diameter.

Remedy: Reduce the scheduled corner radius or increase the scheduled diameter.

### 3.18.7.5 SHAP-004 Slot Len. must be > than wid.

Cause: The scheduled width for the slot is larger than the scheduled length for the slot.

Remedy: Make the slot width smaller than the length or make the slot length larger than the width

### 3.18.7.6 SHAP-005 Shape Template was modified!!

Cause: The Shape Template FOR A CUT MACRO (ex: CUT_CIR.TP) has been modified and is no longer valid for this operation.

Remedy: Undo the modifications if you can or if you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

### 3.18.7.7 SHAP-006 Invalid schedule number used.

Cause: The passed in schedule number for the shape in the teach pendant program is out of range.

Remedy: Set the value in the range of 1 to 100.

### 3.18.7.8 SHAP-007 Error Opening Cut Shape Macro

Cause: The shape program requested could not be opened or the shape cut program was modified and an expected line is missing.

Remedy: The shape program might have been deleted. If you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

### 3.18.7.9 SHAP-008 Error Writing to Shape Macro.

Cause: Could not update the shape macro with values in the shape schedule.

Remedy: If you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

<!-- PDF page 1514 -->

### 3.18.7.10 SHAP-009 Blend-in distance too large.

Cause: The blend-in distance is too large for the specified shape.

Remedy: Decrease the blend-in distance.

### 3.18.7.11 SHAP-010 Length must be > Major dia.

Cause: The length for the key shape must be larger than Major diameter of the key shape.

Remedy: Increase the length of the key shape or decrease the size of the major diameter.

### 3.18.7.12 SHAP-011 Maj dia must be > Min dia.

Cause: The key shape major diameter, must be larger than the key shape minor diameter.

Remedy: Increase the size of the key shape major diameter or decrease the size of the key shape minor diameter.

### 3.18.7.13 SHAP-012 Program name must be set first.

Cause: The shape shift utility was executed without the name of the program entered correctly.

Remedy: Select a valid program for the shift function.

### 3.18.7.14 SHAP-013 Position num must be set first.

Cause: The shape shift utility was executed without the position number entered correctly.

Remedy: Select a valid position for the shift function.

### 3.18.7.15 SHAP-014 Shift must be cleared first.

Cause: Program name column was modified or position num column was modified.

Remedy: Clear the shape shift schedule.

### 3.18.7.16 SHAP-016 Position doesn't exist in prog.

Cause: The selected position does not exist in the selected program.

<!-- PDF page 1515 -->

Remedy: Verify that you have the correct program selected and verify the position number is correct.

### 3.18.7.17 SHAP-017 Posn [REPRE] must be cartesian.

Cause: The position type of the position register being used, has been changed to joint representation.

Remedy: Change the position type back to Cartesian.

### 3.18.7.18 SHAP-021 Center posn PR[1] uninitialized

Cause: The center position for the Custom shape, has not been taught in the 'Center Position' position register.

Remedy: Record the center position for the custom shape in the position register.

### 3.18.7.19 SHAP-022 %s - Joint moves not allowed

Cause: The Custom Shape cut program has joint motions which are not allowed.

Remedy: Change the joint move to a linear move.

### 3.18.7.20 SHAP-031 Macro %s not set

Cause: The macro table was not set correctly.

Remedy: The controller will try to set up the macro table again at the next Controlled start. It is possible that the macro table needed to be expanded and that can only be done by restarting the controller in Controlled start mode.
