Remedy: Turn off the controller power, and disconnect the power cable from the servo amplifier indicated by the alarm message. Also disconnect the brake cable to avoid the axis falling unexpectedly.

1. In the above condition, supply controller power again and check if this alarm occurs again. If this alarm occurs again, replace the servo amplifier.
2. About the power cable, check the insulation of their U, V, W and the GND lines each other. If there is a short-circuit, replace the power cable.

<!-- PDF page 1567 -->

3. About the power cable, measure the resistance between their U and V,V and W and W and U with an ohmmeter that has a very low resistance range. If the resistances at the three places are different from each other, the motor, the power cable is defective. Check each item in detail and replace it if necessary.

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### 3.18.11.46 SRVO-046 OVC alarm (Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the servo system exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the motor and amplifier from damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause:

1. Overload
2. External force to the robot
3. Disconnection of the brake cable
4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply
5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis)
6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis
7. Amplifier failure
8. Motor failure
9. Motor power cable or brake cable failure

# Remedy:

1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load.
2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point.
3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly.
4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification.
5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when Reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis.
6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit.
7. If this alarm cannot be reset, the troubles of related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

<!-- PDF page 1568 -->

# **3.18.11.47 SRVO-047 LVAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)**

**Cause:** The control power supply voltage to servo amplifier is excessively low.

**Remedy:** There is possibly trouble with the servo amplifier and/or the power supply unit. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

# **3.18.11.48 SRVO-048 MOH alarm (Group:%d Axis:%d)**

**Cause:** Never occurs on R-Model J.

**Remedy:** None applicable.

# **3.18.11.49 SRVO-049 OHAL1 alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)**

**Cause:** The thermostat in the transfer worked. Alternatively, the fuse in the servo amplifier has blown.

**Remedy:** Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual.

(Paint) Some paint systems use two transformers. This is indicates by having two A cabinets with separate disconnects stacked on each other. The alarm does not indicate which transformer is overheated.

# **3.18.11.50 SRVO-050 Collision Detect alarm (G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** A collision was detected. (An excessively large disturbance torque was estimated by the servo software.) Probable causes are:

1. Collision (Tip stick) / External force to the robot
2. Overload / Heavy acceleration
3. Increasing of the friction by low temperature
4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply
5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis)
6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis
7. Amplifier failure
8. The E-Stop unit failure
9. Motor failure
10. Motor power cable or brake cable failure
11. Reducer failure

<!-- PDF page 1569 -->

# Remedy:

1. Check whether the robot has collided with an object. To release this alarm, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. Release only RESET key. Still pressing the SHIFT key, and press any jog key to the axis away from the collision.
2. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly.
3. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load. If you use the ACC override more than 100, please reduce the value of ACC override. Allowable disturbance threshold level can be changed from STATUS/Axis/Disturb screen.
4. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed.
5. Check whether the motor power cable/connector and brake cable/connector are connected correctly. Especially, check whether the power cable/connector are not connected to other motors.
6. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification.
7. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when RESET is pressed or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis.
8. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit.
9. There might be a failure with the following parts. Replace it or contact your FANUC technical representative.

- Aux. brake unit (if it is used.)
- Servo amplifier
- Servo motor
- Robot connection cable (power/brake line)
- Cable in the mechanical unit (power/brake line)
- Reducer

(Paint) Identify the correct axis and investigate if there was a collision or other mechanical interference with the joint."

### 3.18.11.51 SRVO-051 CUER alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The offset of the current feedback value is excessively large. Current detection circuit failure is in the amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1570 -->

### 3.18.11.52 SRVO-052 Discharge excess (Amp:%d)

Cause: Not used.

Remedy: None needed.

### 3.18.11.53 SRVO-053 Disturbance excess(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Disturbance estimated in the software exceeds the threshold value. There is a possibility that SRVO-050 occurs when the robot runs leaving this warning.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly.
2. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load.
3. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed.

### 3.18.11.54 SRVO-054 DSM memory error (DSM:%d)

Cause: An access to the servo module memory failed. Note: Before you continue to the next step, perform a complete controller backup to save all of your programs and settings from memory for this robot. After you complete the next step, restore the saved data to the new main board if the memory has been lost. Otherwise, you could injure personnel, damage equipment, or lose data. Refer to the application-specific Setup and Operations Manual for information on how to back up controller memory.

Remedy: Replace the axis control card on the main board.

### 3.18.11.55 SRVO-055 FSSB com error 1 (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and the servo amplifier. (from main board to servo amplifier.)

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

(Paint) Possible issue with fiber optic cable or DC power to the communication circuit of the servo amplifier. On dual arm systems with two transformers it is important to power up the remote controller at or before the same time the main controller is powered up. This fault may also occur if the Fiber Optic cable length is over 42 meters between any two FSSB devices. Additionally a short on the 5V in the pulsecoder/cable will crowbar the supply needed to communicate on the FSSB. Having the software configured for a line tracking module but not having the module present on the network may also cause FSSB faults.

<!-- PDF page 1571 -->

### 3.18.11.56 SRVO-056 FSSB com error 2 (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and servo amplifier. (from servo amplifier to main board.)

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

(Paint) See SRVO-055.

### 3.18.11.57 SRVO-057 FSSB disconnect (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Communication was interrupted between the main board and the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

(Paint) See SRVO-055.

### 3.18.11.58 SRVO-058 FSSB %d init error (%d)

Cause: FSSB initializing is failed.

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm.

(Paint) See SRVO-055.

### 3.18.11.59 SRVO-059 Servo amp init error

Cause: Servo amplifier initializing has failed.

Remedy: Check the servo amplifier and its wiring. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.60 SRVO-060 FSSB 2 init error

Cause: Communication between the auxiliary axis board and servo amplifier was interrupted.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the optical cable between the auxiliary axis board and servo amplifier is connected securely.
2. Replace the auxiliary axis board.

<!-- PDF page 1572 -->

3. Replace the servo amplifier. Before executing the following, perform a complete controller back-up to save all your programs and settings.
4. Replace the main board.
5. Replace the backplane. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.61 SRVO-061 CKAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The clock for the rotation counter in the Pulsecoder is abnormal.

Remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering.

Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

### 3.18.11.62 SRVO-062 BZAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: This alarm is issued when the battery for backing up the absolute position data of the Pulsecoder is not connected or is empty. The battery cable inside the robot might have become disconnected.

Remedy: Replace the battery in the battery box of the robot base or the Pulsecoder. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Correct the cause of the alarm, then turn on the power again after doing PULSE RESET operation. Mastering is required. There are the following two methods for PULSE RESET.

- Method 1: Move the cursor to $MCR.$SPC_RESET on the system variable screen, and select F4 TRUE. It becomes TRUE momentarily, it writes in FALSE at once. Then push the reset button.
- Method 2: F3 RES_PCA is pushed on the MASTER/CAL screen, and select F4 YES. Then press the alarm release button.

Note The MASTER/CAL screen is not usually displayed.

(Paint) There are 5 D batteries and a fuse in this circuit located on the ACP door. Verify all connections at the BIM are secure. Replace the Fuse, batteries, or BIM.

### 3.18.11.63 SRVO-063 RCAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The built-in rotation counter on the Pulsecoder is abnormal.

Remedy:

1. Replace the Pulsecoder.
2. After replacing, set the system variable $MCR.$SPC_RESET to TRUE, and turn the power off and then on again. Master the robot.

<!-- PDF page 1573 -->

Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

### 3.18.11.64 SRVO-064 PHAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: This alarm is issued when the phase of a pulse signal generated by the Pulsecoder is abnormal.

Remedy:Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering.

Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

(Paint) Identify the proper axis and replace the pulsecoder.

### 3.18.11.65 SRVO-065 BLAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The battery voltage for the Pulsecoder has dropped below the allowable minimum.

Remedy: Replace the battery. Note: When this alarm is issued, immediately replace the battery while the system power is turned on. If the BZAL alarm is issued because the battery is not replaced in time, position data will be lost, thus necessitating robot mastering.

(Paint) There are 5 D batteries in this circuit located on the ACP door. Replace the Batteries.

### 3.18.11.66 SRVO-066 CSAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The Pulsecoder ROM checksum data is abnormal.

Remedy:Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering.

Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

### 3.18.11.67 SRVO-067 OHAL2 alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)

Cause: The temperature inside the Pulsecoder has become too high, causing the built-in thermostat to actuate.

Remedy:

1. Check the operating conditions of the robot. If any of the rating specified for the robot, such as its rated duty cycle or load, are exceeded, modify the use of the robot such that the ratings are not exceeded.

<!-- PDF page 1574 -->

2. If this alarm is issued, even when the power is turned on and the motor has not overheated, replace the motor.

(Paint) Verify the Purge Air is on since that also cools the motors. Verify the axis is not overloaded.

### 3.18.11.68 SRVO-068 DTERR alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)

Cause: A request signal was sent to the serial Pulsecoder, but no serial data was returned.

Remedy:

1. Check the connection of the cable between the Pulsecoder and servo amplifier. (If the alarm is occurred at robot axes, check the connection of the robot interconnection cable (for the Pulsecoder)).
2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate.
3. Replace the Pulsecoder.
4. Replace the servo amplifier.
5. Replace the robot interconnection cable (for the Pulsecoder).

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when the CPU cannot communicate with the pulsecoder(s). Possible causes include damaged Pulsecoder, damaged cable, damaged EIM.

### 3.18.11.69 SRVO-069 CRCERR alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)

Cause: Serial data changed during transfer.

Remedy: Refer to the SRVO-068 Remedy.

(Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

### 3.18.11.70 SRVO-070 STBERR alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)

Cause: A serial data start bit or stop bit error occurred.

Remedy: Refer to the SRVO-068 Remedy.

(Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

<!-- PDF page 1575 -->

### 3.18.11.71 SRVO-071 SPHAL alarm (Grp:%d Ax:%d)

Cause: The excessively large feedback speed was detected.

Remedy:

1. This alarm does not indicate the main cause of the problem if issued together with the PHAL alarm (SRVO-064).
2. It might be mis-detection by the noise. Check whether the ground/shield is connected correctly. If possible, enhance the ground/shield.
3. Replace the Pulsecoder of the motor. Mastering is required.
4. Replace the servo amplifier
5. Replace the robot connection cable
6. Replace the cable in the mechanical unit

(Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

### 3.18.11.72 SRVO-072 PMAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The Pulsecoder might be faulty.

Remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering.

### 3.18.11.73 SRVO-073 CMAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The Pulsecoder may be faulty, or noise may be causing the Pulsecoder to malfunction.

Remedy:

1. Improve the shielding.
2. Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering.

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

### 3.18.11.74 SRVO-074 LDAL alarm(Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The LED on the Pulsecoder has become disconnected.

Remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering.

<!-- PDF page 1576 -->

### 3.18.11.75 SRVO-075 Pulse not established(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The absolute position of the Pulsecoder has not yet been established. This alarm appears normally after BZAL or CMAL.

Remedy: Reset the alarm, and jog the axis on which the alarm has occurred until the same alarm does not occur again. (Jog one motor revolution). This alarm must be cleared before mastering.

### 3.18.11.76 SRVO-076 Tip Stick Detection(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An excessive disturbance was calculated in the servo software at the beginning of motion. (An abnormal load was detected. The cause might be welding.)

Remedy: Perform the same action as that described for SRVO-050 (CALM alarm). Note: The threshold level for the tip stick detection cannot be changed from STATUS/Axis/Disturb screen.

### 3.18.11.77 SRVO-077 Dynamic brake alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The line tracking pulse count overflowed.

Remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.18.11.78 SRVO-078 Servo param update(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The servo parameter has been updated.

Remedy: Press RESET and continue.

### 3.18.11.79 SRVO-079 Stroke exceeded during press(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The gun tip position during the pressuring operation (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) exceeded the stroke limit for the gun. The squeezing operation stopped because the gun axis had over-extended.

Remedy: Check the master position and close stroke limit for the gun. If these values are incorrect, then update them. If these values are correct, then install new tips so that the gun can operate within the stroke limits, during pressuring.

### 3.18.11.80 SRVO-080 OVC alarm (Group:%d Axis:%d)

Cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the servo system exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the motor and amplifier

<!-- PDF page 1577 -->

from a damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection of the brake cable 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis 7. Amplifier failure 8. Motor failure 9. Motor power cable or brake cable failure

Remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly. 4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when Reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit. 7. If this alarm cannot be reset, the troubles of related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

### 3.18.11.81 SRVO-081 EROFL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The pulse count for the line tracking encoder (incremental Pulsecoder) has overflowed.

Remedy:

1. Reduce the encoder speed (conveyor speed).
2. Replace the incremental Pulsecoder for the line tracking.
3. Replace the line tracking cable.
4. Replace the line tracking interface board.

### 3.18.11.82 SRVO-082 DAL alarm(Track encoder:%d)

Cause: The line tracking Pulsecoder has not been connected.

Remedy:

1. Check the connection cable at each end (the line tracking I/F board and the Pulsecoder)
2. Check whether the shielding of the connection cable is connected securely to the grounding plate.
3. Replace the line tracking cable.
4. Replace the Pulsecoder.
5. Replace the line tracking interface board.

(Paint) See the system drawings for conveyor encoder connections.

<!-- PDF page 1578 -->

### 3.18.11.83 SRVO-083 CKAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The clock for the rotation counter in the line tracking Pulsecoder is abnormal.

### 3.18.11.84 SRVO-084 BZAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: This alarm is issued when the battery for backing up the absolute position data for the Pulsecoder is not connected.

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-062 BZAL alarm.

### 3.18.11.85 SRVO-085 RCAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The built-in rotation counter on the line tracking Pulsecoder is abnormal.

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-063 RCAL alarm.

### 3.18.11.86 SRVO-086 PHAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: This alarm is issued when the phase of a pulse signal generated by the Pulsecoder is abnormal.

Remedy: See the description for SRVO-064 PHAL alarm.

### 3.18.11.87 SRVO-087 BLAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: This alarm is issued when the battery voltage for backing up the absolute position data of the Pulsecoder has dropped below the allowable minimum.

Remedy: See the description for SRVO-065 BLAL alarm.

### 3.18.11.88 SRVO-088 CSAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The line tracking Pulsecoder ROM checksum data is abnormal.

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-066 CSAL alarm.

### 3.18.11.89 SRVO-089 OHAL2 alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The motor has overheated.

### 3.18.11.90 SRVO-090 DTERR alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.

2. Check whether the shielding of the connection cable is connected securely to the grounding plate.
3. Replace the line tracking cable.
4. Replace the Pulsecoder.
5. Replace the line tracking interface board.

### 3.18.11.91 SRVO-091 CRCERR alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.

### 3.18.11.92 SRVO-092 STBERR alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.

Remedy: Refer to the SRVO-090 Remedy.

### 3.18.11.93 SRVO-093 SPHAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: An excessive speed was detected with the line tracking encoder.

Remedy:

1. This alarm does not indicate the main cause of the problem if issued together with the PHAL alarm(SRVO-086). Refer to SRVO-086.

2. Reduce the encoder speed (conveyor speed).
3. Check whether the shield of the line tracking cable is connected to earth bar in the controller.

### 3.18.11.94 SRVO-094 PMAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

### 3.18.11.95 SRVO-095 CMAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: It is likely that the Pulsecoder is abnormal or the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise.

2. Replace the Pulsecoder.

### 3.18.11.96 SRVO-096 LDAL alarm (Track enc:%d)

Cause: The LED on the Pulsecoder has become disconnected.

### 3.18.11.97 SRVO-097 Pulse not established(Enc:%d)

Cause: The absolute position of the Pulsecoder has not yet been established.

Remedy: See the description for SRVO-075 Pulse not established.

(Paint) Jog all applicable axes at least one motor revolution and master/calibrate. One motor revolution may be up to 15 degrees on a rotational axis and up to 150mm on a linear application.

### 3.18.11.98 SRVO-098 ACC sensor DTERR alarm

Cause: The acceleration sensor has not been connected. Otherwise, an error occurred during communication between the acceleration sensor and the main board.

<!-- PDF page 1581 -->

Remedy:

1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable.
2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate.
3. Replace the above cable.
4. Replace the acceleration sensor. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings.
5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

### 3.18.11.99 SRVO-099 ACC sensor CRCERR alarm

Cause: Data changed during transfer from the acceleration sensor.

Remedy: Refer to the SRVO-098 Remedy.

### 3.18.11.100 SRVO-100 ACC sensor STBERR alarm

Cause: A stop bit error of the data from the acceleration sensor occurred.

Remedy: Refer to the SRVO-098 Remedy.

### 3.18.11.101 SRVO-101 Robot overtravel(Group:%d)

Cause: A Robot overtravel limit switch has been pressed.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-005.

### 3.18.11.102 SRVO-102 Hand broken (Group:%d)

Cause: The hand broken (*HBK) robot input is asserted.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-006.

### 3.18.11.103 SRVO-103 Air pressure alarm(G:%d)

Cause: The pneumatic pressure (PPABN) robot input is asserted.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-009.

<!-- PDF page 1582 -->

### 3.18.11.104 SRVO-104 Welding electrode

Cause: No longer occurs. Welding electrode of controller. This might occur only for the R-J Dual arm controller.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.105 SRVO-105 Door open or E.Stop

Cause:

1. The controller door is opened or E.stop signals are detected for a short time.
2. The specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller.

Remedy:

1. Close the controller door, and press RESET.
2. Check the specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller. For instance, the teach pendant of the RIA/CE specification is used in the controller of non-RIA/CE specification, this alarm might occur. Connect the teach pendant corresponding to the controller.
3. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) This is a general fault indicating the run chain is open for unknown reasons. Troubleshoot other error codes first.

### 3.18.11.106 SRVO-106 Door open/E.Stop(Robot:%d)

Cause:

1. The controller door is opened or E.stop signals are detected for a short time.
2. The specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller.

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-105 Door open or E.Stop.

### 3.18.11.107 SRVO-107 Ext brake abnormal(Rbt:%d)

Cause: The FET current for brake of an extended axis (brake number 2 or greater) exceeded the specification.

Remedy: Check the brake for zero or abnormally low impedance. Then check the brake cable. Then check 200VAC. Then check the servo amplifier or emergency stop control PCB if brake ports are used.

<!-- PDF page 1583 -->

### 3.18.11.108 SRVO-108 ACC sensor livecode error

Cause: The error may have occurred in communication of the force sensor.

Remedy: See the error message about the force sensor.

### 3.18.11.109 SRVO-109 ACC sensor ID mismatch %d

Cause:

1. The acceleration sensor has not been connected.
2. A sensor other than acceleration sensor is detected.

Remedy:

1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable.
2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate.
3. Replace the above cable.
4. Replace the acceleration sensor. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings.
5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

### 3.18.11.110 SRVO-110 GS3D-ACC disabled %d (G:%d A:%d)

Cause:

1. Pulse module channel setting is wrong on the axis.
2. GS3D-ACC sensor is disabled on the axis.
3. The axis assignment is already used on Line-tracking or Full-closed control.
4. Setting for GS3D-ACC sensor is wrong on the axis.

Remedy:

1. Please set servo parameter No.290 of the axis GS3D-ACC sensor is assigned with correct channel number on your pulse module(1-8), and cycle power.
2. Please set servo parameter No.10/Bit7=ON of the axis GS3D-ACC sensor is assigned, and cycle power.
3. You cannot assign GS3D-ACC sensor to the axis. Please assign GS3D-ACC sensor to another axis, and cycle power.
4. Please set following parameters, and cycle power. - $ENC_STAT[ch].$ENC_EXISTS = TRUE - $SCR.$ENC_AXIS[ch] = hardware axis number(1-56) (ch indicates channel number(1-8) of GS3D-ACC sensor on your pulse module).

<!-- PDF page 1584 -->

### 3.18.11.111 SRVO-111 Softfloat time out(G:%d)

Cause: Follow-up time is over when softfloat is OFF. (When $SFLT_ERRTYP=0)

Remedy:

1. Check whether external force is not applied to the robot before the softfloat is turned on.
2. Check whether the robot does not move as posture greatly changes during softfloat.
3. If needed, make $SFLT_FUPTIM larger.

### 3.18.11.112 SRVO-112 Softfloat time out(G:%d)

Cause: Follow-up time is over when softfloat is OFF. (When $SFLT_ERRTYP=1)

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-111 Softfloat time out.

### 3.18.11.113 SRVO-113 Cart. error excess(G:%d %s)

Cause: While Cartesian Softfloat is being executed, the position error on the rectangular coordinates becomes greater than the tolerance that is set by the user.

Remedy: Find and remove the cause of the position error becoming greater. Or, make the tolerance larger, turn off and then turn on the controller. The tolerance is the value of the following system variables. X direction [mm] : $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IX Y direction [mm] : $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IY Z direction [mm] : $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IZ

### 3.18.11.114 SRVO-114 Singularity Detected

Cause: A singularity was detected during robot motion.

Remedy: Re-teach the program points, use WJNT, or use JOINT MOTYPE.

### 3.18.11.115 SRVO-115 Limit error (G:%d, A:%s)

Cause: The linear path passes outside of the axis limit.

Remedy: Re-teach program points, or use JOINT MOTYPE

### 3.18.11.116 SRVO-116 Axis Limit Exceeded (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: One or more of the robot axes have exceeded an axis soft limit while executing SOFFLOAT.

<!-- PDF page 1585 -->

Remedy: Jog the robot within the limits to resume. Adjust the program or process to keep robot axes within limits, or increase the axis limits.

### 3.18.11.117 SRVO-117 Brake Number Conflict

Cause: Machinelock has been set on a group that is using the same brake number as a different group that is not machinelocked.

Remedy:

1. Set machinelock for all groups using the common brake.
2. Change brake connections so the same brake number is not used by different groups.

### 3.18.11.118 SRVO-118 SFIGET err %s

Cause: This error indicates that an error occurs during SFIGET execution.

Remedy: Perform an action according to the number that is displayed in the alarm message. 5: The schedule number is not specified or abnormal schedule number other than 1~10 integral value is specified. Specify the correct softfloat schedule number with SFIGET. 1,2,3,4: This error indicates that the software internal error occurs during SFIGET execution. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.119 SRVO-119 OVR not 100%%

Cause: Override is not 100 % when execute SFIGET program.

Remedy: Set override 100% and re-execute SFIGET program again.

### 3.18.11.120 SRVO-120 SFIVAL abnml(Scd:%d G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The difference between the integrator torque just before soft float execution starts and $SFLT_GRP. $SFLT_IVAL exceeded a specified value ($SFLT_GRP. $SFIVALLIM).

Remedy: Execute SFIGET program again, or set $SFLT_GRP. $SFIVALLIM more larger.

### 3.18.11.121 SRVO-121 Excessive acc/dec time(G:%d)

Cause: Acceleration time is too long.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1586 -->

# **3.18.11.122 SRVO-122 Bad last ang(internal)(G:%d)**

**Cause:** The last angle update request does not match the current angle.

**Remedy:** Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

# **3.18.11.123 SRVO-123 Fan motor rev slow down(%d)**

**Cause:** The rotation speed of fan motor on backplane unit has slowed down. Number in the bracket indicates which fan is abnormal.

(1): fan above the slot1
(2): fan above the slot2
(3): both fans

**Remedy:**

1. Check the fan motor and its cables. Replace them if necessary.
2. Replace the backplane unit. Before executing the remedy 3, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings.
3. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

**Note** If SRVO-014 appears after SRVO-123, refer SRVO-014.

# **3.18.11.124 SRVO-124 Check HardStop if Hit(G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** If 'SRVO-024 Move Error excess' Alarm occurs and the group is not calibrated, this alarm is posted too.

**Remedy:** Refer to the Remedy of SRVO-024

# **3.18.11.125 SRVO-125 Quick stop speed over (G:%d)**

**Cause:** The quick stop speed is too high.

**Remedy:** Reduce the speed when a quick stop is executed.

# **3.18.11.126 SRVO-126 Quick stop error (G:%d)**

**Cause:** The program was over during the process of quick stop.

<!-- PDF page 1587 -->

Remedy: Press RESET.

### 3.18.11.127 SRVO-127 Unsupported power supply software

Cause: Unsupported power supply software is loaded.

Remedy: contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.128 SRVO-129 Position not reachable (G:%d^2)

Cause: The cartesian path passes outside of the reachable region.

### 3.18.11.129 SRVO-130 OHAL1(PS) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Heat sink temperature of the main circuit of the Power Supply (αiPS) has risen abnormally.

Remedy:

1. Check the rotation of the cooling fan of the Power Supply (αiPS).
2. Decrease the duty cycle of operation.
3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

### 3.18.11.130 SRVO-131 LVAL(PS) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The control power supply voltage on the Power Supply (αiPS) is abnormally low.

Remedy:

1. Check the input power supply.
2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

### 3.18.11.131 SRVO-132 HCAL(PSM) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The current in the main power circuit of the servo amplifier exceeded specification.

Remedy: Refer to the maintenance manual.

<!-- PDF page 1588 -->

### 3.18.11.132 SRVO-133 FSAL(PS) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The cooling fan for the Control circuit of the Power Supply (aiPS) stopped.

Remedy:

1. Check the status of the cooling fan. And replace it if it was abnormal.
2. Replace the Power Supply (aiPS).

### 3.18.11.133 SRVO-134 SERVO DCLVAL alarm (G:%d A:%d), SRVO-134 DCLVAL (PS) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The DC voltage (DC link voltage) of the main circuit power supply for the 6-axis amplifier is abnormally low. Number in the bracket shows the group number and the axis number in the group. For a 6-axis amplifier, this alarm is posted on the 1st axis and 2nd axis or the 1st axis, 2nd axis and 3rd axis of the 6-axis amplifier.

Remedy:

1. It is possible that an instant disconnection of power source caused this alarm. Check whether an instant disconnection occurred.
2. Verify that the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage. Verify that the transformer setting is correct.
3. Modify the program such that robot and the auxiliary axis do not accelerate simultaneously in a system with an auxiliary axis.
4. In a system with an auxiliary axis, this alarm may occur if a reset signal is input at the same time as an emergency stop signal such as SVOFF or Fence open. Do not input a reset signal for 2 seconds after the emergency stop signal is input.
5. Replace the E-stop unit.
6. Replace the 6-axis amplifier.
7. Replace the Power Supply (aiPS).

Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

(Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

### 3.18.11.134 SRVO-135 FSAL alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The cooling fan for the Control circuit stopped.

Remedy:

<!-- PDF page 1589 -->

1. Replace the internal fan motor of the auxiliary servo amplifier that is indicated by the alarm message.
2. Replace the servo amplifier that is indicated by the alarm message.

### 3.18.11.135 SRVO-136 DCLVAL alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The DC voltage (DC link voltage) of the main circuit power supply on the auxiliary servo amplifier (aiSV) which drives the group/axis shown in the alarm message is abnormally low.

Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

Remedy:

- This alarm occurred when robot is moving.

1. Check that the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage and there is no missing phase. Also check that the setting of the transformer is correct.
2. It is possible that an instant disconnection of the power source caused this alarm. Check whether an instant disconnection occurred.
3. Replace the E-stop unit.
4. Replace the servo amplifier (aiSV) of which axis is shown in the alarm message.

- If this alarm occurred before the magnetic contactor is turned on:

1. Check whether the circuit breaker in the E-stop unit is OFF. If it is OFF, check the servo amplifier and the wiring between the servo amplifier and the E-stop unit. If anything is abnormal, replace it. If not, turn on the breaker.
2. Check that the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage and no missing phase. Also check that the setting of the transformer is correct.
3. Replace the E-stop unit.
4. Replace the servo amplifier (aiSV) of which axis is shown in the alarm message.

- In a system with an auxiliary axis, this alarm may occur if a reset signal is input at the same time as an emergency stop signal such as SVOFF or Fence open. Do not input a reset signal for 2 seconds after the emergency stop signal is input.

- In an auxiliary axis system and if this alarm occurred right after the EMERGENCY STOP button was pressed, check whether the auxiliary axis unit is installed correctly.

1. Check the wiring of the servo amplifier (aiSV) of which axis is shown in the alarm message.
2. Check whether the auxiliary axis unit is installed correctly.

(Paint) See SRVO-134.

<!-- PDF page 1590 -->

### 3.18.11.136 SRVO-137 DAL alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: DAL alarm of an amplifier.

Remedy: Refer to the maintenance manual.

### 3.18.11.137 SRVO-138 SDAL alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A Pulsecoder signal error was detected by the software. The probable cause is noise or a failure (disconnection) in the Pulsecoder internal circuit.

Remedy:

1. If a normal operation can be resumed by turning the controller power off and on again, it is likely that the cause is noise. Enhance the shielding of the Pulsecoder cable.
2. If a normal operation cannot be resumed by cycle power, the Pulsecoder is defective. Replace it, and perform mastering.

### 3.18.11.138 SRVO-141 OHAL1(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A servomotor's built-in thermostat was actuated.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-049.

### 3.18.11.139 SRVO-142 OHAL1(INV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The servo amplifier overheated.

Remedy: If the robot is overloaded or the duty cycle exceeds specification, this alarm occurs. Check the regenerative discharge transistor. Check the thermostat on the servo amplifier after the servo amplifier has cooled. It should not be open. If the problem persists, replace the servo amplifier. Check the controller cabinet fans for blocked filters; clean them if necessary.

### 3.18.11.140 SRVO-143 PSFLAL(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Input power applied to the amplifier has been lost.

Remedy: Check the connections and cables of the input power.

### 3.18.11.141 SRVO-144 LVAL(INV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is excessively low.

<!-- PDF page 1591 -->

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-047.

### 3.18.11.142 SRVO-145 LVAL(CNV-DC) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: This alarm indicates a problem with the back-up charge circuit for the amplifier.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-147.

### 3.18.11.143 SRVO-146 LVAL(INV-DC) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is too low.

Remedy: Check each interphase voltage of the three-phase voltage (200 VAC) applied to the servo amplifier. If the applied voltage is found to be 170 VAC or less, check the input power supply voltage. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.144 SRVO-147 LVAL(DCLK) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: This alarm indicates a problem with the back-up charge circuit for the amplifier.

Remedy: 1. Check the cable between the servo amplifier (CN1) and the MCC. Replace it if necessary. 2. For a model using the B cabinet, check whether the transformer fuses (F1 and F3) have blown. 3. Replace the printed circuit board for emergency stop control. 4. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.145 SRVO-148 HCAL(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The current in the main power circuit of the servo amplifier exceeded specification.

Remedy: Disconnect the motor power wires from the servo amplifier and turn on power. If an HCAL occurs, replace the transistor module or servo amplifier. Measure the resistance between GND and U, V, W individually on the cable terminals. If shorted, determine if the cable or motor is bad. Check the resistance between U-V, V-W, and W-U using a measuring instrument sensitive enough to detect small resistances at the cable terminations. If the resistances are the same, replace the servo amplifier. If the resistances are different, determine if the cable or motor is bad. If the problem persists, replace the SIF module on the axis control for the defective axis.

### 3.18.11.146 SRVO-149 HCAL(INV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An excessively high current flowed through the main circuit of a servo amplifier.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-045.

<!-- PDF page 1592 -->

### 3.18.11.147 SRVO-150 FSAL(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The cooling fan for the control circuit stopped.

Remedy: Check the fan. Replace it if necessary.

### 3.18.11.148 SRVO-151 FSAL(INV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The cooling fan for the control circuit stopped.

Remedy: Check or replace the fan.

### 3.18.11.149 SRVO-152 IPMAL(INV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The IPM module has trouble.

Remedy: 1. The IPM might be overheated. Reset the emergency stop after approximately ten minutes. Disconnect the power lines from the terminals on the amplifier, and check the insulation of PE from U, V, and W. 2. If there are short circuits, disconnect the motor connector power lines and check the insulation of PE from U, V, and W. 1) Replace the motor if U, V, and W short-circuit with PE. 2) Replace the power lines if U, V, and W do not short-circuit with PE. 3. Noise on the actual current (IR, IS) running in the amplifier module might cause this alarm. Remove this noise such as with taking ground of sealed earth. 4. Replace the amplifier.

### 3.18.11.150 SRVO-153 CHGAL(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The main circuit could not be charged within the specified time.

Remedy:

1. A short circuit might have occurred in the DC link. Check the connection.
2. The charging current control resistor might be faulty. Replace the E-Stop unit.
3. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.151 SRVO-154 HVAL(CNV-DC) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is abnormally high.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-044.

<!-- PDF page 1593 -->

### 3.18.11.152 SRVO-155 DCAL(CNV) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The energy produced by regenerative discharge is excessive.

Remedy: Refer to SRVO-043.

### 3.18.11.153 SRVO-156 IPMAL alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Abnormally high current flowed through the main circuit of the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-045.

### 3.18.11.154 SRVO-157 CHGAL (PS) alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The capacitor on the servo amplifier was not charged properly within the specified time after the servo power turned on. The number in the bracket shows the group number and the axis number in the group. For a 6-axis amplifier, this alarm is posted on the 1st axis and 2nd axis or the 1st axis, 2nd axis and 3rd axis of the 6-axis amplifier.

Probable causes:

1. Low voltage of the power supply
2. Hardware failure

Remedy:

1. If an auxiliary axis servo amplifier (aiSV) is installed, SRVO-157 could occur if $SCR_GRP[group].$AXISORDER[axis] is changed manually. If you changed $SCR_GRP[group].$AXISORDER[axis], restore it to the original value. If the original value is lost, document the events that led to the error, and contact your local FANUC representative. Then provide FANUC with the accurate number in the alarm message.
2. Check the input voltage to the controller when the servo power is turned on.
3. Check that the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage and no phase is missing. Also check that the setting of the transformer is correct.
4. Check that the circuit breaker of the E-Stop unit is on and has not tripped.
5. Make sure that the servo amplifier CRRA12 and the emergency stop board CRRA12 connector are connected tightly. If power supply (aiPS) is used, make sure that the power supply (aiPS) CRRA12 connector is connected tightly.
6. In a system with an auxiliary axis, this alarm may occur if a reset signal is input at the same time as an emergency stop signal such as SVOFF or Fence open. Do not input a reset signal for 2 seconds after the emergency stop signal is input.
7. Replace the power supply (aiPS).
8. Replace the 6-axis amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1594 -->

9. Replace the E-stop unit.

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

When you contact your local FANUC representative, please provide them with the accurate number in the alarm message.

Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.155 SRVO-160 Panel/External E-stop

Cause: The emergency stop button on the operator panel was pressed, or the external emergency stop function was activated. EMGIN1 and EMGINC are not strapped to each other. Or, EMGIN2 and EMGINC are not strapped to each other.

Remedy: Release the emergency stop button. If the external emergency stop function has been activated, remove the cause. If no cause can be found, and no jumper is installed between EMGIN1 and EMGINC or between EMGIN2 and EMGINC on the terminal block of the emergency stop control printed circuit board, but cables are connected to the terminals, check the cables.

### 3.18.11.156 SRVO-161 Fence open or Deadman SW

Cause: The teach pendant deadman switch is released or the fence circuit is open.

Remedy: Press teach pendant deadman switch or determine the cause of the fence and then press RESET.

### 3.18.11.157 SRVO-162 Deadman/Fence or Panel/External E-stop

Cause: The deadman switch is released, the fence circuit is open, the operator panel ESTOP button is pressed, or the external ESTOP signal is received.

Remedy: Remove the cause then press RESET.

### 3.18.11.158 SRVO-163 DSM hardware mismatch

Cause: Different DSM (Digital Servo Module) are mounted on the controller

Remedy: Change the DSM hardware to be same.

<!-- PDF page 1595 -->

### 3.18.11.159 SRVO-164 DSM/Servo param mismatch

Cause: The DSM (Digital Servo Module) type is mismatched to the servo parameter version.

Remedy: Change the current DSP-IV module to DSP_V or initialize the robot library again to load the correct servo parameter file.

### 3.18.11.160 SRVO-165 Panel(SVON abnormal) E-stop

Cause: The operator panel emergency stop push button is pressed and miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.

Remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Twist the operator panel emergency stop push button clockwise to release. Press RESET.

### 3.18.11.161 SRVO-166 TP(SVON abnormal) E-stop

Cause: The teach pendant emergency stop push button is pressed and miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.

Remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Twist the teach pendant emergency stop push button clockwise to release. Press RESET.

### 3.18.11.162 SRVO-167 Deadman switch (SVON abnormal)

Cause: The teach pendant deadman switch is released while the teach pendant is enabled. And miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.

Remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Press teach pendant deadman switch. Press RESET.

### 3.18.11.163 SRVO-168 External/SVON (SVON abnormal) E-stop

Cause: Refer to SRVO-007 or SRVO-019. And miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.

Remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. And Refer to SRVO-007 or SRVO-019.

### 3.18.11.164 SRVO-169 Ext.E-stop/SVOFF/ServoDisconnect

Cause: The external emergency stop signal or the servo disconnect signal or SVOFF signal is asserted.

<!-- PDF page 1596 -->

**Remedy:**

1. Release the external emergency stop signal and press RESET.
2. If the servo disconnect signal or SVOFF signal is used, release it and press RESET.

**3.18.11.165 SRVO-170 Lack of DSP (ID:%d)**

**Cause:** The number of DSPs on the axis card is lacking.

**Remedy:** 1. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number). 2. Replace the axis card with a card has enough DSPs for your system. 3. Add an auxiliary axis board.

**3.18.11.166 SRVO-171 MotorSpd lim/DVC(G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** The motor can not rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.

**Remedy:** None.

**3.18.11.167 SRVO-172 MotorSpd lim/DVC0(G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** The motor cannot rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.

**Remedy:** This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

**3.18.11.168 SRVO-173 MotorSpd lim/DVC1(G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** The motor cannot rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.

**Remedy:** This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

**3.18.11.169 SRVO-174 MotorAcc lim/DVC(G:%d A:%d)**

**Cause:** The motor cannot accelerate as much as the calculated acceleration required for the current motion.

**Remedy:** This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

**3.18.11.170 SRVO-176 CJ/Illegal Mode %d,%d**

**Cause:** An incorrect CJ mode was used.

<!-- PDF page 1597 -->

Remedy: This is an internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.171 SRVO-179 Motor torque limit(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The torque of the axis has exceeded the limit.

Remedy: None.

### 3.18.11.172 SRVO-180 Control axis not exist

Cause: Controllable axis does not exist on any group.

Remedy: Please execute aux axis setting at controlled start. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.173 SRVO-181 Mcmd input while estimating(G:%d)

Cause: The robot was going to move while identifying the payload.

Remedy: Press RESET. Be careful not to move the robot while identifying the payload.

### 3.18.11.174 SRVO-182 Needed init. has not been done

Cause: This is an error internal to the system. A system variable or internal work memory has not been initialized normally.

Remedy:

1. Turn the power off and on again.
2. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.175 SRVO-183 ROBOT isn't ready

Cause: The servo is off.

Remedy: Remove the factor that turned servo off, and press the RESET button.

<!-- PDF page 1598 -->

### 3.18.11.176 SRVO-184 Other task is processing

Cause: The data area that this instruction tried to use had been locked by another task.

Remedy:

1. If this alarm is occurred when the Payload Estimation is restarted, execute the Payload Estimation after it waits for a while.
2. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle.
3. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.177 SRVO-185 Data is for other group

Cause: This is an error internal to the system.

Remedy:

1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle.
2. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.178 SRVO-186 Needed Data has not been got

Cause: This is an error internal to the system.

Remedy:

1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle.
2. If the alarm is still issued document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.179 SRVO-187 Need specfing Mass

Cause: Estimating the load information of this type requires specifying the mass of the load.

Remedy: Specify the mass of the load before Payload Estimation.

### 3.18.11.180 SRVO-188 Memory is lacking

Cause: The system could not allocate the enough memory area on the DRAM for Payload Estimation.

<!-- PDF page 1599 -->

Remedy:

1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle.
2. If the alarm is still issued, you need to update the memory size of DRAM. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.181 SRVO-189 I/O-Link livecode error

Cause: The error may have occurred in communication of the force sensor.

Remedy: See the error message about the force sensor.

### 3.18.11.182 SRVO-190 Pulsecoder ID mismatch %d

Cause: A sensor other than Serial Pulsecoder is detected.

Remedy: 1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable. 2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the above cable. 4. Replace the Serial Pulsecoder. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

### 3.18.11.183 SRVO-191 Illegal Joint Speed (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The motion command exceeded the specification.

Remedy: This is an internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.184 SRVO-192 Fence open/SVON input

Cause: The fence circuit is open or the SVON input circuit is open.

Remedy: Close the fence circuit or SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

### 3.18.11.185 SRVO-193 SVON input

Cause: The SVON input circuit is open.

Remedy: Close SVON input circuit, and then press RESET. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

<!-- PDF page 1600 -->

### **3.18.11.186 SRVO-194 Servo disconnect**

**Cause:** A servo disconnect input signal is turned off.

**Remedy:**

1. If a servo disconnect switch is connected, release the switch, and then press RESET.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### **3.18.11.187 SRVO-195 NTED/Servo disconnect**

**Cause:** The Non Teacher Enabling Device is released or servo is disconnected.

**Remedy:** Press the Non Teacher Enabling Device or connect servo, and then press RESET. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

### **3.18.11.188 SRVO-196 Fence open/SVON input (SVON abnormal)**

**Cause:** The fence circuit is open or the SVON input circuit is open and mis-wiring on the SVON is detected.

**Remedy:** Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON. Close the fence circuit or SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

### **3.18.11.189 SRVO-197 SVON input (SVON abnormal)**

**Cause:** The SVON input circuit is open and mis-wiring on SVON is detected.

**Remedy:** Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON. Close the SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

### **3.18.11.190 SRVO-198 Alarm Detected**

**Cause:** An Alarm was detected during robot motion.

**Remedy:** After this alarm, Overheat alarm etc. are detected. See the remedy of those alarms for more information.

### **3.18.11.191 SRVO-199 Controlled Stop**

**Cause:** A Controlled Stop has been done.

<!-- PDF page 1601 -->

Remedy: After this alarm, a Fence open or SVOFF input alarm is detected. See the remedy of those alarms for more information.

### 3.18.11.192 SRVO-200 Control box fan abnormal

Cause: The control box fan motor has failed.

Remedy: Check and/or replace the fan. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

### 3.18.11.193 SRVO-201 Panel E-stop or SVEMG abnormal

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator's panel/operation box was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy:

1. Release the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button, then press RESET.
2. When the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

### 3.18.11.194 SRVO-202 TP E-stop or SVEMG abnormal

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy:

1. Release the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button, then press RESET.
2. When the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

### 3.18.11.195 SRVO-203 SVON input(SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: The SVON signal line was opened while the SVEMG wiring is incorrect.

Remedy: Correct any SVEMG wiring errors. Input an SVON signal, and turn the power off and then on again. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

<!-- PDF page 1602 -->

### 3.18.11.196 SRVO-204 External(SVEMG abnormal) E-stop

Cause: The external emergency stop push button was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm.

(Paint) In addition to the above comments, this may be the interlock to the paint system. See applicable system drawings.

### 3.18.11.197 SRVO-205 Fence open(SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: The fence circuit was opened, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.198 SRVO-206 Deadman switch (SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: The teach pendant deadman switch was released while the teach pendant was enabled, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.199 SRVO-207 TP switch abnormal or Door open

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP line has been disconnected although there is no e-stop factor.

Remedy:

1. Replace the teach pendant.
2. Replace the teach pendant cable.
3. Replace the operator's panel/operation box.
4. Replace the E-stop unit.
5. Replace the servo amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1603 -->

### 3.18.11.200 SRVO-208 Extended axis brake abnormal

Cause: The FET current for the brake of an extended axis (brake number 2 or greater) exceeded the specification.

Remedy: Check the brake for zero or abnormally low impedance. Then check the brake cable. Then check 200VAC. Then check servo amplifier or emergency stop control PCB if brake ports are used. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

### 3.18.11.201 SRVO-209 Robot-%d SVEMG abnormal

Cause: An abnormality of the emergency stop line of robot 2 or later was detected.

Remedy:

1. Replace the E-Stop unit of robot 2 or later.
2. Replace the servo amplifier of robot 2 or later.
3. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.202 SRVO-210 EX_robot SVEMG abnormal

Cause: Mis-wiring of SVEMG signal on Extended robot is detected.

Remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVEMG on controller of Extended robot. Close fence circuit and then press reset.

### 3.18.11.203 SRVO-211 TP OFF in T1,T2

Cause: The teach pendant was disabled while the mode switch was set in the T1 or T2 position and robot 1 and 2 were disconnected. Alternatively, there is a failure in the hardware.

Remedy:

1. Set the teach pendant enable/disable switch to on, and press RESET.
2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.204 SRVO-212 Trans over heat

Cause: The fuse on Panel PCB is blown

Remedy: Replace fuse on 6 Panel PCB

<!-- PDF page 1604 -->

### 3.18.11.205 SRVO-213 E–STOP Board FUSE2 blown

Cause: A fuse (FUSE) on the emergency stop board has blown.

Remedy: Replace the fuse (FUSE2) on the emergency stop board or the emergency stop board. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) Make sure the EXT24 and EXT0 are either supplied or jumped to INT signals on the ESTOP Unit.

### 3.18.11.206 SRVO-214 6ch amplifier fuse blown(R:%d)

Cause: The fuse on the servo amplifier has blown. Number in the bracket indicates which 6ch amplifier is abnormal.

Remedy: Replace the fuse on the servo amplifier. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### 3.18.11.207 SRVO-215 Brake Unit fuse blown(R:%d)

Cause: The fuse FUSE1 on the brake unit has blown. Number in the bracket indicates which 6ch amplifier the brake unit is connected.

Remedy: Replace this fuse after replacing the brake cable because it might be defective. (If this fuse has blown, it may be caused by some defect of the brake cable.)

(Paint) The 6-ch AMP sees that the brake fuse signal is active via the connection on CRM97. Check the process axis brake control PCB/fuse.

### 3.18.11.208 SRVO-216 OVC(total) (%d)

Cause: The current flowing through the robot cable has exceeded its limit. Number in the bracket indicates which amplifier number is abnormal.

Remedy:

1. Slow the motion of the robot where possible. Check the robot operation conditions. If the robot is used with a condition exceeding the duty or load weight robot rating, reduce the load condition value to the specification range.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1605 -->

### 3.18.11.209 SRVO-217 E-STOP Board not found

Cause: The emergency stop board is not found when the controller power is turned on.

Remedy: 1. Check whether fuse FUSE1 on the emergency stop board has blown. If the fuse has blown, check and correct the cause then replace the fuse. 2. Check the cable between emergency stop board and main board. Replace them if necessary. 3. Replace the E-Stop unit. Before executing the remedy 4, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 4. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

(Paint) This alarm is posted when either the estop board or Safety I/O card is missing from the Safety buss. Check/replace the cable and Estop Board/Safety I/O board.

### 3.18.11.210 SRVO-218 Ext.E-stop/ServoDisconnect

Cause: The external emergency stop signal or the servo disconnect signal is asserted.

Remedy:

1. Release the external emergency stop signal and press RESET.
2. If the servo disconnect signal is used, release it and press RESET.

### 3.18.11.211 SRVO-220 SDI fuse blown

Cause: The fuse for SDI has blown.

Remedy: Replace the fuse on the main board or main board itself. Refer to the Mate Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### 3.18.11.212 SRVO-221 Lack of DSP (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A controlled axis card corresponding to the set number of axes ($SCR_GRP.$AXISORDER) is not mounted.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the set number of axes is valid. If the number is invalid, set the correct number.
2. Replace the axis control card with a card corresponding to the set number of axes.

<!-- PDF page 1606 -->

### 3.18.11.213 SRVO-222 Lack of Amp (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The servo amplifiers were not found at the power up sequence. Numbers in parentheses show the group number and the axis number in the group. (In software version V9.10P/14 or earlier, there is only one number in parentheses, and it means the amplifier number.)

Remedy:

1. When any LED on the servo amplifier does not light with the power supply of the controller turned on, the power is not supplied to the servo amplifier. Confirm whether there is neither disconnecting nor loosening in each connector on the servo amplifier and the E-Stop unit.
2. Turn off the power of the controller, disconnect the Pulsecoder cable JF1,JF2 from the servo amplifier and turn on the power of the controller again. If this alarm does not occur, the Pulsecoder cable may have a ground fault. (The LED of the servo amplifier may display blinking '—' in this case.)
3. Check whether the servo amplifier for auxiliary axis for the R-30/A controller is connected to the R-30/B controller.
4. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number, hardware start axis number).
5. Replace the servo amplifier for auxiliary axis.
6. Replace the 6-axis servo amplifier.
7. Replace the optical fiber cable.
8. Replace the servo card or the auxiliary axis servo card.

### 3.18.11.214 SRVO-223 DSP dry run (%d,%d)

Cause: A servo DSP initialization failure occurred due to hardware failure or wrong software setting. Then, the software entered DSP dry run mode. The first number indicates the cause of the failure. The second number is extra information.

Remedy: Perform an action according to the first number that is displayed in the alarm message.

1: This is a warning due to $scr.$startup_cnd=12.
2,3,4,7: Replace a servo card.
5: Invalid ATR setting. Software axis config (FSSB line number, amplifier axis number) might be wrong.
6: SRVO-180 occurs simultaneously. Controllable axis does not exist on any group. Execute aux axis setting to add axis at controlled start.
8,10: SRVO-058 (FSSB init error) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-058.
9: There is no amplifier that is connected to the servo card.

- Check the hardware connection.
- Check the optical fiber cable.
- Check whether the servo amplifier power is supplied.
- Check whether the fuse on the servo amplifier has blown.
- Replace the optical fiber cable.

<!-- PDF page 1607 -->

- Replace the servo amplifier.

11: Invalid axisorder setting. Non-existing axis number is specified. Software axis config (FSSB line number) might be wrong or auxiliary axis board is necessary.
12: SRVO-059 (Servo amp init error) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-059.
13,14,15: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC representative.
16: SRVO-181 (Up to 4 aux axes allowed in a group) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-181.
17: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your local FANUC representative. (In software version 7DF1/14 or earlier, this alarm can occur also when software axis config is wrong. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number).)

Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.215 SRVO-224 Slot changed (AuxBrd%d,%d>%d)

Cause: Hardware slot of the auxiliary axis board has been changed.

Remedy: Please verify this change is valid. If this change is due to a simple mistake, please restore the hardware configuration to its original condition.

### 3.18.11.216 SRVO-225 Unsupported servo card (%d)

Cause: This servo card is not supported.

Remedy: Replace the servo card according to the number that is displayed in the alarm message.
1: Servo card, 2: Auxiliary axis board 1, 3: Auxiliary axis board 2

### 3.18.11.217 SRVO-226 Motor current setting mismatch (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Mismatch between the motor current setting and the amplifier current is detected.

Remedy: Please change the motor current limit to a proper value.

### 3.18.11.218 SRVO-230 Chain 1 abnormal %x,%x

Cause:

1. A failure occurred in chain 1 (+24V)/chain2(0V) of emergency stop circuit.
2. There is a possibility that the specification of the teach pendant is incorrect when occurring immediately after turning on of the power supply. For instance, this might occur if the teach pendant of non-RIA/CE specification is connected with the controller of the RIA/CE specification.

<!-- PDF page 1608 -->

# Remedy:

1. In the above case 2, connect a correct teach pendant.
2. Confirm the history of the alarm on the Alarm Log screen. If occurring with either 'Operator panel E-stop', 'Teach pendant E-stop' or 'Deadman switch released', the emergency stop button is released, and it presses again. For deadman switch, the deadman switch is gripped once and it released again. Chain abnormal state was released if occurring SRVO-236 'Chain failure is repaired'. Release e-stop button, deadman and press reset button.

3. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary.

a. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and release it.
b. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen.
c. Press RESET.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the safety circuit close. Verify that the EA, EG, and EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

### 3.18.11.219 SRVO-231 Chain 2 abnormal %x,%x

# Cause:

1. A failure occurred in chain 1 (+24V)/chain2(0V) of emergency stop circuit.
2. There is a possibility that the specification of the teach pendant is incorrect when occurring immediately after turning on of the power supply. For instance, this might occur if the teach pendant of non-RIA/CE specification is connected with the controller of the RIA/CE specification.

Remedy: See the description for the SRVO-230 Chain 1 abnormal.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the safety circuit close. Verify that the EA, EG, and EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

### 3.18.11.220 SRVO-232 NTED input

Cause: The NTED (non-teacher enabling device) was detected.

# Remedy:

1. Press the NTED (non-teacher enabling device), and then press the reset key.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1609 -->

### 3.18.11.221 SRVO-233 TP OFF in T1,T2/Door open

Cause: The mode switch is set in the T1 or T2 position, and the teach pendant is disabled. Alternatively, the controller door is open. There is also a failure in the hardware.

Remedy:

1. After setting the teach pendant enable/disable switch to on, close the controller door, and press the reset key.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) If you should be in Auto mode, look at the Mode selector inputs. If you should be in Teach mode, verify the pendant is enabled then replace the teach pendant.

### 3.18.11.222 SRVO-234 Deadman switch released

Cause: The deadman switch on the teach pendant was released.

Remedy: None.

### 3.18.11.223 SRVO-235 Short term Chain abnormal

Cause: A temporary chain failure was detected.

Remedy:

1. Press the e-stop button on the teach pendant or the operator panel again. If occurring SRVO-236 'Chain failure is repaired'. Release e-stop button and Press RESET.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary.
  a. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released.
  b. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen.
  c. The reset button is pressed.

### 3.18.11.224 SRVO-236 Chain failure is repaired

Cause: A chain failure was removed.

Remedy: When the system checked for the chain failure again, the chain failure had been removed. Press RESET.

<!-- PDF page 1610 -->

### 3.18.11.225 SRVO-237 Cannot reset chain failure

Cause: An attempt to reset the chain failure failed.

Remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-230.

### 3.18.11.226 SRVO-238 Chain 1 (SVON) abnormal

Cause: A single chain 1 (+24V) failure occurred when the SVON (Servo ON/OFF switch) input was asserted.

Remedy: Repair the circuit of chain 1 (+24V) on the SVON hardware. Set CHAIN FAILURE detection to TRUE on the SYSTEM/CONFIG screen. Press RESET on the teach pendant.

### 3.18.11.227 SRVO-239 Chain 2 (SVON) abnormal

Cause: A single chain 2 (0V) failure occurred when a SVON (Servo ON/OFF switch) input was asserted.

Remedy: Repair the circuit of the chain 2 (0V) on SVON the hardware. Set CHAIN FAILURE detection to TRUE on the SYSTEM/CONFIG screen. Press RESET on the teach pendant.

### 3.18.11.228 SRVO-240 Chain 1 (FENCE) abnormal

Cause: Although the fence circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.

Remedy: A problem exists with either the panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary.

1. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and then release it.
2. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen.
3. Press the RESET button.

### 3.18.11.229 SRVO-241 Chain 2 (FENCE) abnormal

Cause: Although the fence circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.

Remedy: A problem exists with either the panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary.

1. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and release it.
2. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen.
3. Press the RESET button.

### 3.18.11.230 SRVO-242 Chain 1 (EXEMG) abnormal

Cause: Although the external emergency stop circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.

After measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1) The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2) F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3) The reset button is pressed.

### 3.18.11.231 SRVO-243 Chain 2 (EXEMG) abnormal

Cause: Although the external emergency stop circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.

1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released.
2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen.
3. The reset button is pressed.

Cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().

### 3.18.11.233 SRVO-245 Chain 2 abnormal(Rbt:%d)

Cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().

<!-- PDF page 1612 -->

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

### 3.18.11.234 SRVO-246 Chain 1 abnormal(EX_robot)

Cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().

Remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

### 3.18.11.235 SRVO-247 Chain 2 abnormal(EX_robot)

Cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().

### 3.18.11.236 SRVO-248 Deadman switch status abnormal

Cause: The status of two DIs of DEADMAN switch do not match.

Remedy:

1. Release both deadman switches at once. If SRVO-236 Chain failure is repaired occurred, there is no hardware problem. This alarm could occur when deadman switch is pressed halfway.
2. When SRVO-236 does not occur, please replace hardware in following order. - Teach pendant - Cable between teach pendant and the emergency stop board - the emergency stop board - Cable between the emergency stop board and main board.
3. After measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary.
  - The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released.
  - F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen.
  - The reset button is pressed.

### 3.18.11.237 SRVO-250 SVEMG/MAINON1 abnormal

Cause: Status of MAINON1 signal is still OFF even if SVEMG is ON It is abnormal of E.STOP circuit

Remedy: Repair the circuit of E.Stop hardware Power off/on again

<!-- PDF page 1613 -->

### 3.18.11.238 SRVO-251 DB relay abnormal(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An abnormality was detected in the internal relay (DB relay) of the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.239 SRVO-252 Current detect abnl(G:%d A:%d)

3. The reset button is pressed.
