### 3.18.11.261 SRVO-277 Panel E-stop(SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: The emergency stop line was not disconnected although the emergency stop button on the operator's panel was pressed.

Remedy:

1. Release the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button, then cycle controller power again.
2. When the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

Note

<!-- PDF page 1618 -->

1. Need power cycle to release this alarm.
2. This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed too slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the ACP mounted estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the pendant estop button because they are in series.

### 3.18.11.262 SRVO-278 TP E-stop(SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.

Remedy:

1. Release the TP EMERGENCY STOP button, then the controller power cycle again.
2. When the TP EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

Note

1. Need power cycle to release this alarm.
2. This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed too slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the teach pendant estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the ACP estop button because they are in series.

### 3.18.11.263 SRVO-279 Circuit abnormal 3 (%d)

Cause: The Emergency stop circuit is abnormal.

Remedy:

1. Replace the Emergency Stop Unit.
2. Replace the Servo Amplifier.

Note: Cycle controller power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.264 SRVO-280 SVOFF input

Cause: The SVOFF (servo off signal) was input.

Note The paint controller is placed in this alarm state when using the manual brake release function. When the BRAKE ENABLE switch is placed in the ON position, this alarm is generated.

<!-- PDF page 1619 -->

If your controller is a paint controller with manual brake release functionality, make sure that the BRAKE ENABLE switch is in the OFF position before trying to reset this alarm.

# **Remedy:**

1. Find out what caused the SVOFF to be input, and remove the cause. Press the RESET button.
2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the Robot-Specific Maintenance Addendums for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement.

### 3.18.11.265 SRVO-281 SVOFF input(SVEMG abnormal)

Cause: When the SVOFF signal was asserted, an SVEMG error was detected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.

# **Remedy: If the RDY LED (green) is lit:**

1. Check the switch and cable connected to 9 (EGS1) - 10 (EGS11) and 11 (EGS2) - 12 (EGS21) on operator panel terminal TBOP4.
2. Replace the panel board.
3. Replace the EStop unit.
4. Replace the servo amplifier.
5. Replace the connection cable between the EStop unit and the panel board.

# **If the RDY LED (green) is not lit:**

1. Replace the cable connecting between the main board (JRS11) and the panel board (JRS11).
2. Replace the panel board. Note: Before executing the next step, perform a complete controller back-up to save all of your programs and settings. Failure to perform this task could result in damage to the equipment or lost data.
3. Replace the main board.

(Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the robot specific maintenance addendums for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement.

Note: If the SYST-067 Panel HSSB disconnect alarm occurs simultaneously or the RDY LED is turned off, the following alarms are also generated:

- SRVO-001 Operator panel E-Stop
- SRVO-004 Fence open
- SRVO-007 External emergency stop

<!-- PDF page 1620 -->

- SRVO-204 External (SVEMG abnormal) E-Stop
- SRVO-280 SVOFF input

Check the alarm history display on the teach pendant.

### 3.18.11.272 SRVO-291 IPM over heat (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: It was detected that the IPM element in the amplifier had overheated.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the amplifier fan rotates normally.
2. Decrease the duty cycle of operation.
3. If this symptom occurs frequently, replace the amplifier.

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### 3.18.11.273 SRVO-292 EXT.FAN alarm (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The external fan for the servo amplifier module (SVM, alpha iSV) is faulty.

Remedy: Replace the cooling fan.

### 3.18.11.274 SRVO-293 HCAL(PS) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The three-phase input power supply is abnormal or the Power Supply (αiPS) module is faulty.

Remedy:

1. Check the three-phase input power supply.
2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

### 3.18.11.275 SRVO-294 EXT.FAN(PS) alarm(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The external fan for the Power Supply (αiPS) is faulty.

Remedy: Replace the external fan.

### 3.18.11.276 SRVO-295 AMP com error(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: A communication error occurred between the Power Supply (αiPS) and the servo amplifier .Remedy:

1. Replace the 6-axis amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1622 -->

2. Replace the cable for communication the Power Supply (αiPS) and servo amplifier.
3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).
4. Replace the servo amplifier (αiSV).

### 3.18.11.277 SRVO-296 Excess regeneration(PS) (G:%d A:%d)

Cause:

1. The cooling fan for the regenerative resistance of the Power Supply (αiPS) stops.
2. The use condition is too hard for the regenerative resistance of the Power Supply (αiPS).

Remedy:

1. Check the fan for the regenerative resistor is working. If it stops, replace the fan.
2. Lower the teaching speed in the program.
3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

### 3.18.11.278 SRVO-297 Improper input power(PS)(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Three-phase input power supply voltage is low.

Remedy:

1. Check the voltage of the three-phase input power.
2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).
3. Replace the 6-axis amplifier.
4. Replace the E-stop unit.

Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

(Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.293 SRVO-314 Lack of LIU (LIU:%d)

Cause: The servo amplifiers were not found at the power up sequence.

Remedy: See SRVO-222.

### 3.18.11.294 SRVO-315 MPDT failed(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) for 3rd party motor failed. Probable causes are:

1. The motor power cable is disconnected.
2. The axis falls down by the gravity during performing of MPDT.
3. Other alarm occurs during performing of MPDT.
4. The motor cannot move due to large load or friction.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the motor power cable is connected correctly.
2. MPDT cannot be applied for gravity axis. If possible, change the posture.
3. Remove the reason of other alarms which occurred at same time.
4. Check whether the axis which requires to perform MPDT does not contact with any object.
5. Confirm that brake is not engaged.

### 3.18.11.295 SRVO-316 MPDT time is up(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process time is up. Probable cause:

1. The axis fell down because of gravity during performing of MPDT.
2. Other alarms occurred during performing of MPDT.

Remedy:

1. MPDT cannot be applied for gravity axis. If possible, change the posture.
2. Remove the reason of other alarm which occurred at the same time.

<!-- PDF page 1626 -->

### 3.18.11.296 SRVO-317 MPDT cannot start(Machine Lock)

Cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process cannot start because machine lock is enabled for that group.

Remedy: Disable machine lock for that group.

### 3.18.11.297 SRVO-318 MPDT cannot start(SRDY Off)

Cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process cannot start because servo ready (SRDY) is off.

Remedy: Remove the reason of servo ready (SRDY) off.

### 3.18.11.298 SRVO-322 SVOFF input / E.STOP

Cause: The SVOFF (Servo off signal) is input.

Remedy:

1. Release the SVOFF signal and press RESET.
2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.299 SRVO-323 Torque limit (G%d A%d L%d)

Cause: Torque limit reached. The third number indicates the line number of the TP program.

Remedy: Modify TP program to be less aggressive.

### 3.18.11.300 SRVO-324 Disturbance excess(G%d A%d L%d)

Cause: Disturbance estimated in the software exceeds the threshold value. There is possibility that SRVO-050 occurs when the robot runs leaving this warning.

Remedy:

1. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly.
2. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load.
3. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed.

<!-- PDF page 1627 -->

### 3.18.11.301 SRVO-325 Alarm %d

Cause: Varies by alarm number:

Alarm 101: fail to send command to MPC
Alarm 102: fail to send command to DSP (buffer full)
Alarm 103: fail to send command to FLTR
Alarm 105: illegal axis number
Alarm 106: CPMCWT was OFF when first command
Alarm 107: NOCPMC is detected
Alarm 108: ANACC is detected
Alarm 109: limit error is detected

Remedy: Please turn on servo again.

### 3.18.11.302 SRVO-326 Abnormal Mcmd (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The different between motion command and machine pulse exceeded specified threshold.

Remedy: Internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.303 SRVO-327 Cart error excess (G:%d,%s)

Cause: The servo positional error on the cartesian coordinates exceeds a specified value ($PARAM2_GRP.$CARTERRLIM). The first argument that is shown in the alarm message indicates the group number. The second argument indicates which cartesian direction (X/Y/Z/Euclidean distance) the servo positional error exceeds the threshold.

Remedy: Perform the same action as that described for SRVO-023.

### 3.18.11.304 SRVO-328 Retry count err(G:%d A:%d Enc:%d)

Replace the Pulsecoder cable. 4. Replace the Line tracking I/F board. 5. If the error is not cleared with the above remedies, refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-090(DTERR).

### 3.18.11.324 SRVO-348 DCS MCC OFF alarm %x,%x

Cause: A command was issued to turn on the magnetic contactor, but the magnetic contactor was not turned on.

1. Replace the E-stop unit.
2. Replace the servo amplifier.

(Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the auxiliary contacts on a contactor on the E-Stop board does not toggle properly. The issue may be with a contactor in the E-Stop unit in the main or remote A-cabinet. Replace the E-Stop unit.

### 3.18.11.333 SRVO-357 DCS ENABLED alarm %x,%x

Cause:

1. Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check is enabled for a motion group that does not exist.
2. Joint Position Check or Joint Speed Check is enabled for an axis that does not exist.
3. Joint Position Check or Joint Speed Check is enabled for an axis that is excluded.
4. Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check is enabled for a motion group that has an excluded axis that is not an auxiliary extended axis.

Remedy: Disable Joint Position Check, Joint Speed Check, Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check.

### 3.18.11.334 SRVO-358 DCS INVPRM alarm %x,%x

Cause:Invalid data is set in the DCS parameters.

Remedy:Check DCS setting. Load backup files that were saved when the parameters were correct.

### 3.18.11.335 SRVO-359 DCS SYSTEM alarm %x,%x

Cause:

1. When config Signature Date/Time is ACTUAL in DCS CIP Safety menu, System clock setting is invalid. (Valid year is 2004-2150.)
2. Invalid data is set in the DCS parameters.

<!-- PDF page 1634 -->

Remedy:

1. Config Signature Date/Time to FIXED, or set correct date/time to system clock.
2. Check DCS setting. Load backup files that were saved when the parameters were correct.

Remedy:

3. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board.
4. Replace the emergency stop board.

Note In order to clear this fault, the chain fault will need to be reset. To reset the chain fault press F4 RES_1CH on the active alarm menu and press F4 YES to reset the single channel fault.

(Paint) SFDI signals exist on the Estop Board(s) and optional Safety I/O Board(s). This alarm will be posted if there is an issue with the Estop Board, Safety I/O Board or cable.

### 3.18.11.370 SRVO-397 J2 Aggressive Motion(G:%d L:%d)

Cause: J2 motion is too aggressive. This warning means J2 motion has been slowed down.

Remedy: None required.

### 3.18.11.371 SRVO-399 TorsionCompException(ID:%d

Cause: This is a notification that Torsion Compensation failed to execute. This message is shown by Tool Torsion Compensation option etc.

When ID is 0: robot is not mastered or not calibrated yet.

When ID is 1: an invalid schedule number is specified.

When ID is 2: an invalid tool number is specified in current schedule.

When ID is 3 or 4: direction is not defined.(in schedule to compensate along the direction defined by TCP velocity vector)

Remedy: When ID is 0: master and calibrate the robot.

When ID is 1: specify valid schedule number.

When ID is 2: specify valid tool number in current schedule.

When ID is 3 or 4: in these schedules, start compensation while TCP is moving.

Cause: CIP Safety communication error occurs.

### 3.18.11.373 SRVO-402 DCS Cart. pos. limit(%d,G%d,M%d) %02x

Cause: Cartesian Position Check function detected that a model is out of a safe zone.

The first value : Cartesian Position Check No.

G : Group number

M : User model number (0: Robot model)

Remedy:If the robot is actually out of the safe zone, press SHIFT key and RESET key, and jog the robot to the safe zone.

<!-- PDF page 1642 -->

### 3.18.11.376 SRVO-405 DCS Joint speed limit(%d,G%d,A%d) %02x

Cause: Joint Speed Check function detected over speed.

The first value : Joint Speed Check No.

G : Group number

A : Axis number

Remedy: Decrease Joint speed.

<!-- PDF page 1643 -->

### 3.18.11.383 SRVO-412 DCS COUNT3 alarm %x,%x

Cause: DCS servo on process is stopped.

Remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

### 3.18.11.384 SRVO-413 DCS CC_SAFEIO alarm %x,%x

Cause:Results of Safe I/O process by 2 CPU are different. This alarm sometimes occurs when the safety input signals on the emergency stop board and Safe I/O board such as External E-STOP or SFDI are changed repeatedly in a very short time. It can also occur when other safety input signals, such as Cartesian Position Check (CPC), Cartesian Speed Check (CSC), Joint Position Check (JPC), and Joint Speed Check (JSC) are changing repeatedly in a very short time.

Remedy:

1. Check the connection of the safety input signals on the emergency stop board and Safe I/O board.
2. Check that the Permissible Distance is greater than 0 mm for all enabled Joint Speed Checks and Cartesian Speed Checks with a Limit of 0 mm.
3. Check the other alarms for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1644 -->

Note: you need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.385 SRVO-414 DCS WORK CRC alarm %x,%x

Cause: DRAM failure is detected.

Remedy: Check the other alarms for more information. Replace CPU card. Replace main board.

### 3.18.11.386 SRVO-415 DCS Invalid tool (G%d) %x,%x

Cause:

1. Selected DCS tool frame number is not defined.
2. Verify I/O of DCS tool frame is not set in the selected DCS tool frame

Remedy: Check DCS TCP setting.

### 3.18.11.387 SRVO-416 DCS Tool mismatch(G%d) %x,%x

Cause: All Verify I/O of DCS tool frame are OFF or two or more Verify I/O are ON for more than 1sec.

Remedy: Check Verify I/O status.

### 3.18.11.388 SRVO-417 DCS APSP_C alarm(G%d) %x,%x

Cause: Invalid DCS approach speed check parameter for Cartesian position check.

Remedy: Check DCS approach speed check parameter

### 3.18.11.389 SRVO-418 DCS APSP_J alarm(G%d,A%d) %x,%x

Cause: Invalid DCS approach speed check parameter for Joint position check.

Remedy: Check DCS approach speed check parameter

### 3.18.11.390 SRVO-419 PROFIsafe comm. error %x,%x

Cause: PROFINET Safety communication error occurs.

Remedy: Check PROFINET Safety connection.

<!-- PDF page 1645 -->

### 3.18.11.391 SRVO-420 Safety FL-net comm. error %x,%x

Cause: Safety function by FL-net communication error occurs.

Remedy: Check Safety function by FL-net connection

### 3.18.11.392 SRVO-421 Jnt phs not calibrated(G%d)

Cause: $DMR_GRP.$MASTER_DONE is not ready to be set to TRUE because Universal Joint phase calibration data is not set.

Remedy: When you enter the mastering data via direct entry, enter Universal Joint phase calibration data and set $DMR_M3_GRP.$MASTER2_ENB = TRUE first. After that, set $DMR_GRP.$MASTER_DONE = TRUE

### 3.18.11.393 SRVO-422 Shared TP E-stop

Cause: Emergency stop occurs on other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant group.

Remedy: Clear the source of the fault, and press RESET on ther controller.

### 3.18.11.394 SRVO-423 Shared TP: T1/T2 on other robot

Cause: Any other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant gropu is not AUTO.

Remedy: To start production running in Auto mode, change modes of all controllers in the Shared Teach Pendant group Auto.

### 3.18.11.395 SRVO-424 Shared TP: Mode mismatch

Cause: Robot in T1 mode cannot move if there is T2 mode controller in the group. Robot in T2 mode cannot move if there is T1 mode controller in the group.

Remedy: To move a robot in T1/T2 mode, set the modes of all other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant group to the same or AUTO.

### 3.18.11.396 SRVO-425 Shared TP: Configuration mismatch

Cause: Configuration for Shared Teach Pendant group is mismatched with other controllers in the group.

Remedy: Check configuration for Shared Teach Pendan group.

<!-- PDF page 1646 -->

### 3.18.11.397 SRVO-426 EQZ Try touch detection (G:%d)

Cause: A robot tries to perform Touch Detection.

Remedy: There is no need to take any measures.

### 3.18.11.398 SRVO-427 EQZ No sensitivity at this Pos (G:%d)

Cause: There is no sensitive axis at this posture.

Remedy: Change the robot posture and try Equalization again.

### 3.18.11.399 SRVO-428 EQZ Motion too short (G:%d)

Cause: Length of EQ motion (distance between taught positions) was too short.

Remedy: Modify your TP program to enhance the distance to the destination position of EQ motion. Typically you only need to increase the argument value to EQTCHPOS.

### 3.18.11.400 SRVO-429 EQZ Bad robot posture(G:%d)

Cause: Equalization was infeasible at this robot posture. This message tells you the last EQ was done with Ghost Run mode.

Remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot

### 3.18.11.401 SRVO-430 EQZ Not supported (G:%s)

Cause: Cannot start equalization because this robot does not. support equalization.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.11.402 SRVO-431 EQZ Failed to start (%d)

Cause: Cannot start equalization for some reason.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1647 -->

### 3.18.11.403 SRVO-432 EQZ is aborted (%d)

Cause: Equalization was aborted for some reason, HOLD, E-STOP etc.

Remedy: Equalization is no longer effective in this motion. If you need to try the Equalization motion again, jog the robot away from the part, then restart from the line before equalization motion.

### 3.18.11.404 SRVO-433 EQZ Dir not selected (G:%d)

Cause: Equalization Soft Direction is not selected

Remedy: Select Soft Direction via the setup screen.

### 3.18.11.405 SRVO-434 EQZ Bad robot posture(G:%d)

Cause: Equalization is infeasible at this robot posture. Equalization requires that at least one axis among J1, J2 or J3 is sensitive to the reaction force from the part. This alarm means there is no sensitive axis.

Remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

### 3.18.11.406 SRVO-435 EQZ Move Limit (G:%d)

Cause: Motion with equalization exceeded the Robot Move Limit.

Remedy: This alarm indicates an overrun of the robot motion.

1. Check if the workpiece exists.
2. If this alarm is posted without an obvious overrun, increase Robot Move Limit via the setup menu.

### 3.18.11.407 SRVO-436 EQZ Stroke Limit (G:%d,A:%d)

Cause: Robot reached to its stroke range limit during Equalization motion.

Remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (F/N, U/D, T/B) and turn number of the robot.

### 3.18.11.408 SRVO-437 EQZ Singular (G:%d)

Cause: Robot wrist axis is near the singular point. In other words, J5 is near 0.

<!-- PDF page 1648 -->

Remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

### 3.18.11.409 SRVO-438 EQZ Speed Excess (G:%d)

Cause: An instantaneous high speed motion was detected. One possible cause is that robot posture is bad (near SRVO-434 condition)

Remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

### 3.18.11.410 SRVO-439 EQZ Trq not restored(G%dA%d)

Cause: Ending process of EQ motion was not normally done.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.411 SRVO-440 EQZ Invalid argument

Cause: Some arguments in KAREL are invalid.

Remedy: Correct the arguments in the KAREL program

### 3.18.11.412 SRVO-441 EQZ GunMntTyp not selected

Cause: Gun Mount Type is not selected.

Remedy: Select Gun Mount Type via the setup screen.

### 3.18.11.413 SRVO-442 EQZ FUP time out (G:%d)

Cause: Robot kept moving when Equilization is about to end.

Remedy: Check if the part is firmly fixed.

### 3.18.11.414 SRVO-443 EQZ Pos not calculated

Cause: Because EQTCHPOS was not called or not successfully processed, destination position of EQ motion is not calculated.

<!-- PDF page 1649 -->

Remedy: 1. Check if EQTCHPOS is called before EQ start. If not called, add call EQTCHPOS before EQ start. 2. If EQTCHPOS causes SRVO-440 or other alarm, modify arguments of EQTCHPOS to eliminate the alarm.

### 3.18.11.415 SRVO-444 EQZ error (%s)

Cause: (1): Failed to get destination angle of last motion segment before EQ. (2): Failed to calculate EQ position by forward kinematics, probably because of stroke limit.

Remedy: (1): Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. (2): Check joint position when EQTCHPOS was called.

### 3.18.11.416 SRVO-445 EQZ Can't use with softfloat (G:%d)

Cause: Both Equalization and Softfloat become enabled.

Remedy: Don't use Equalization and Softfloat at the same time.

### 3.18.11.417 SRVO-446 DCS LS Fence open %x,%x

Cause: In Auxiliary axis servo off (Local stop) function, the safe I/O assigned to the fence input is OFF when the auxiliary axis is not servo off condition. The value displayed in the message shows the No. of local stop that the alarm occurs. The value is hexadecimal, and each bit is corresponded to each item in DCS local stop menu (1:No.1, 2:No.2, 4:No.3, 8:No.4, 10:No.5, 20:No.6, 40:No.7, 80:No.8).

Remedy: Set the safe I/O assigned to the fence input to ON, or set the auxiliary axis servo to off.

### 3.18.11.418 SRVO-447 DCS LS STO-FB alarm %x,%x

Cause: In Auxiliary axis servo off (Local stop) function, mismatch of STO-OUT and STO-FB is detected. The value displayed in the message shows the No. of local stop that the alarm occurs. The value is hexadecimal, and each bit is corresponded to each item in DCS local stop menu (1:No.1, 2:No.2, 4:No.3, 8:No.4, 10:No.5, 20:No.6, 40:No.7, 80:No.8).

Remedy: 1: Check the setting of DCS local stop menu. 2: Check the connection between emergency stop board and auxiliary axis servo amplifier. 3: Replace the cable between emergency stop board and auxiliary axis servo amplifier. 4: Replace the emergency stop board. 5: Replace the auxiliary axis servo amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1650 -->

### 3.18.11.419 SRVO-448 DCS PLSCHK alarm (SFDO%d)

Cause: The monitored signal of safety output is not OFF even though OFF pulse is output. The signal name that the trouble is detected is displayed after the alarm message.

Remedy: 1. Check the cabling of safety output circuit. 2. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board. 3. Replace the emergency stop board.

### 3.18.11.420 SRVO-449 DCS DOMON alarm (SFDO%d)

Cause: The monitored signal of safety output is different from the output command. The signal name that the trouble is detected is displayed after the alarm message.

Remedy: 1. Check the cabling of safety output circuit. 2. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board. 3. Replace the emergency stop board.

### 3.18.11.421 SRVO-450 Drvoff circuit fail(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The two drive off inputs are not in the same status.

Remedy: 1. Check the line of the two drive off inputs. 2. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.422 SRVO-451 Internal S-BUS fail(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the serial bus communication in the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.423 SRVO-452 ROM data failure(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the ROM data in the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.424 SRVO-453 Low volt driver(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Driver supply voltage in the servo amplifier is low.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1651 -->

### 3.18.11.425 SRVO-454 CPU BUS failure(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error was found in CPU bus data in the amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.426 SRVO-455 CPU watch dog(G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error occurred in CPU operation in the amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.427 SRVO-456 Ground fault (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the motor current detection data in the servo amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.428 SRVO-457 Ground fault(PS) (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: Ground fault occurs in the motor power line.

Remedy: 1. Check the ground fault of the motor and the motor power cable. 2. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 3. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.429 SRVO-458 Soft thermal(PS) (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the Power Supply (alpha iPS) exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the Power Supply (alpha iPS) from damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection of the brake cable 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Auxiliary brake unit failure for auxiliary axis 7. The Power Supply (alpha iPS) failure 8. The servo amplifier failure

Remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly. 4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the auxiliary brake unit, check the fuse on the auxiliary brake unit. 7. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 8. Replace the servo amplifier.

<!-- PDF page 1652 -->

### 3.18.11.430 SRVO-459 Excess regeneration2%s (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the discharge circuit in the 6-axis amplifier.

Remedy: Replace the 6-axis amplifier.

### 3.18.11.431 SRVO-460 Illegal parameter%s (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the setting of the parameters in the Power Supply (alpha iPS) or servo amplifier.

Remedy: 1. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 2. Replace the servo amplifier.

### 3.18.11.432 SRVO-461 Hardware error%s (G:%d A:%d)

Cause: An error is found in the circuit in the Power Supply (alpha iPS) or servo amplifier.

Remedy: 1. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS).

### 3.18.11.433 SRVO-468 TmpDetachedNode exists in FLSF

Cause: Temporary detached node exists in Safety function by FL-net.

Remedy: This alarm occurs at start-up and for user to pay attention, so this alarm is defeasible by reset. Change the detached node to ENTRY not to occur this alarm at start-up.

### 3.18.11.434 SRVO-470 Wireless sensor data error

Cause: Wireless data sequence number is wrong.

Remedy: Please call FANUC service center.

### 3.18.11.435 SRVO-471 I/O Link i slave(%d-%d) status abnormal

Cause: A chain alarm was detected with the I/O Link i slave signal. (x-x) shows signal number.

Remedy: 1. Check whether I/O Link cable is connected correctly. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal for I/O Link i slave satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace CPU card. Replace main board.

<!-- PDF page 1653 -->

### 3.18.11.436 SRVO-472 A%d is moved in stop check

Cause: The suspended axis is moved when the contact stop status of Collaborative Robot is ESCP.

Remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### 3.18.11.437 SRVO-473 DCS CLLB CC_EXTF alarm

Cause: The result is different in 2 CPU for Collaborative Robot.

Remedy: Check the other alarms for more information. Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.438 SRVO-474 Escape speed lim exceed

Cause: The speed of movement by Push to Escape of Collaborative Robot exceeds the limit.

Remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### 3.18.11.439 SRVO-475 Escape direction alarm

Cause: The direction of movement by Push to Escape of Collaborative Robot exceeds is invalid.

Remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### 3.18.11.440 SRVO-476 CLLB alarm %x,%x

Cause: Internal error of the collaborative robot function.

Remedy: Restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### 3.18.11.441 SRVO-477 Calibration data error

Cause: The sensor calibration data of the collaborative robot are wrong.

Remedy: Copy "CLLB.CM" file from the CD-R which is appendix of the collaborative robot to a memory card or USB memory. Perform the same file with a teach pendant, set the sensor calibration parameter. After this change, perform “APPLY TO DCS PARAMETER”. Refer to “1.3 Apply to DCS parameter” in ”Dual Check Safety Function Operator ’s manual” for detail.

<!-- PDF page 1654 -->

As this file is unique to each collaborative robot, do not use other robot's file. Check that the serial number which is printed on CD-R is same as the number which is written on collaborative robot sensor.

### **3.18.11.442 SRVO-478 Temperature difference too large**

**Cause:** The force sensor temperature difference is too large.

**Remedy:** Please make sure that the environment temperature does not change greatly, and then restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### **3.18.11.443 SRVO-479 Temperature changes too fast**

**Cause:** The force sensor temperature changes too fast.

**Remedy:** Please make sure that the environment temperature does not change greatly, and then restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

### **3.18.11.444 SRVO-480 FORCE alarm %x,%x**

**Cause:** Force sensor is abnormal.

**Remedy:** 1. Restart the controller. 2. Replace the force sensor cable. 3. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

### **3.18.11.445 SRVO-481 Invalid payload number**

**Cause:** Current payload number of Collaborative Robot is invalid. By default, the payload number is 0 (invalid setting).

**Remedy:** Set the payload number between 1 and 10.

### **3.18.11.446 SRVO-482 Robot is moved in stop check**

**Cause:** Collaborative Robot moved when the contact stop status is STOP.

**Remedy:** Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

<!-- PDF page 1655 -->

### 3.18.11.447 SRVO-483 Input AUTO confirmation signal

Cause: Mode was chnaged to AUTO by mode switch on TP screen.

Remedy: Input AUTO confirmation singal by the switch outside of safeguard.

### 3.18.11.448 SRVO-484 Safe I/O consistency alarm %x,%x

Cause: In Safe I/O consistency check function, mismatch of Safe I/O is detected.

Remedy: 1. Check the setting of Safety I/O consistency check function.

2. Check the cabling of safety I/O circuit.

3. Check failure of the device that cabled to safety I/O.

Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

### 3.18.11.449 SRVO-485 Hand Guidance overspeed

Cause: Operation speed by Hand Guidance exceeds limit.

Remedy: Check limit speed setting of Hand Guidance.

### 3.18.11.450 SRVO-486 Hand Guidance E-stop

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Hand Guidance device was pressed.

Remedy: 1. Release EMERGENCY STOP on the Hand Guidance device, then press RESET. 2. Check setting and connection to Safety I/O board. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Hand Guidance device.

### 3.18.11.451 SRVO-487 Hand Guidance Deadman switch

Cause: The DEADMAN switch of Hand Guidance device was not pressed.

Remedy: 1. Press the DEADMAN switch to release it, then press RESET. 2. If you want to use with Collaborative robot, enable Contact stop. 3. Set Hand Guidance disable I/O to ON if you do not use Hand Guidance function then. 4. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Hand Guidance device.

<!-- PDF page 1656 -->

**Cause:** Cartesian Position Check function detected that robot speed exceeds limit. The first value : Cartesian Position Check No. G : Group number N : Speed limit Number

**Remedy:** Decrease speed if the CPC is UNSF

# **3.18.11.453 SRVO-489 DCS DMA alarm %x,%x**

# **3.18.11.454 SRVO-490 FORCE alarm 2 (%x,%x)**

**Cause:** Force sensor error.

# **3.18.11.455 SRVO-491 Collaborative stroke limit (G:%d A:%s)**

**Cause:** Interference angle exceeds the limit

# **3.18.11.456 SRVO-492 Collaborative speed over**

**Cause:** Speed over of Collaborative Robot

**Remedy:** Decrease robot speed.

# **3.18.11.457 SRVO-493 Contact Stop Distance limit**

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed. Or, the EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator panel was pressed.

### 3.18.11.463 SRVO-602 TP/External E-stop

Cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed. Or, the external EMERGENCY STOP button was pressed.

Remedy: Twist the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button clockwise to release it, then press RESET. If you are using the external emergency stop, clear the source of the fault, and press RESET.

<!-- PDF page 1658 -->

### 3.18.11.464 SRVO-603 Deadman switch/NTED released

Cause: The deadman switch was not pressed when the teach pendant was enabled. Or, the NTED (non-teacher enabling device) was detected.

Remedy: 1. Press the deadman switch to release it, then press RESET. If the deadman switch is three position switch type, press the deadman switch to middle position to release it, then press RESET. 2. Press the NTED (non-teacher enabling device), and then press RESET. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the teach pendant. Or, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

### 3.18.11.465 SRVO-498 MPG E-stop

### 3.18.11.466 SRVO-499 MPG Enabling switch

Remedy: 1. Press the Manual Pulse Generator to release it, then press RESET. 2. Set disable Manual Pulse Generator in the setting screen, if you do not use Manual Pulse Generator then. 1. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Manual Pulse Generato.

2. Check for other alarms that occurred at the same time.

### 3.18.12 SSPC Alarm Code

#### 3.18.12.1 SSPC-001 (G:%d) Waiting space gets clear

Cause: Special checking space is not clear.

Remedy: Wait for the special checking space to clear.

#### 3.18.12.2 SSPC-002 (GMSK:%d) Dead lock condition

Cause: More independent groups are within a common space.

Remedy: Jog the robot out of the common space.

#### 3.18.12.3 SSPC-003 AccuPath not allowed

Cause: Space Check function is not compatible with AccuPath. AccuPath is not allowed.

Remedy: Not use AccuPath or disable space check function

#### 3.18.12.4 SSPC-004 CTV option not allowed

Cause: Space Check function is not compatible with Continuous Turn CTV option. The CTV motion option is not allowed.

Remedy: Remove CTV option or disable space check function

#### 3.18.12.5 SSPC-005 Disabled while waiting

Cause: The space is disabled while waiting.

Remedy: None.

#### 3.18.12.6 SSPC-006 (G:%d) Space is cleared

Cause: Space is cleared.

Remedy: Continues to move.

<!-- PDF page 1661 -->

### 3.18.12.7 SSPC-007 (G:%d) Miss Space NUM

Cause: Common space is 0.

Remedy: Select a common space.

### 3.18.12.8 SSPC-101 (G:%d) is close to target

Cause: Interaction is detected.

Remedy: You can reset the alarm with SHIFT+RESET and can jog the robot to the out of the interacted area. This key operation disable the interaction check temporarily while the SHIFT key is being pressed.

### 3.18.12.9 SSPC-102 (G:%d) is close to target(qstop)

Remedy: You can reset the alarm with SHIFT+RESET and can jog the robot to the out of the interacted area. This key operation disable the interaction check temporarily while the SHIFT key is being pressed.

### 3.18.12.10 SSPC-103 (G:%d) is near to target

Remedy: You can reset the alarm with SHIFT+RESET and can jog the robot to the out of the interacted area. This key operation disable the interaction check temporarily while the SHIFT key is being pressed.

### 3.18.12.79 SSPC-212 Invalid Comb Pair Num(%d)

Cause: Invalid Combination Pair number.

Remedy: Enter a valid Combination Pair number.

### 3.18.12.80 SSPC-213 Invalid Critical Zone #(%d)

Cause: Invalid Critical Zone number.

Remedy: Enter a valid Critical Zone number. A valid Critical Zone number is a valid obstacle model number.

### 3.18.12.81 SSPC-214 Invalid Position Register(%d)

Cause: Invalid Position Register number, or invalid Position Register content. Only XYZWPR type in PR is supported, Joint representation is not supported.

<!-- PDF page 1672 -->

**Remedy:** Enter a valid Position Register number, and a valid Position Register content.

# **3.18.12.82 SSPC-215 Invalid AutoZone Sched #(%d)**

**Cause:** An invalid AutoZone Schedule number was specified.

**Remedy:** Enter a valid AutoZone Schedule id.

# **3.18.12.83 SSPC-216 Too many AutoZone buffers**

**Cause:** Too many autozone buffers between AutoZone Start and AutoZone End.

**Remedy:** Reduce the number of motion lines between AutoZone Start and AutoZone End.

# **3.18.12.84 SSPC-217 (G:%d) Outside Virtual Sphere**

**Cause:** Robot is outside the boundary of the sphere virtual fence.

**Remedy:** Disable the combination pair temporarily, jog the robot back inside the sphere virtual fence, and re-enable the combination pair.

# **3.18.12.85 SSPC-218 (G:%d) Outside Vir Cylinder**

**Cause:** Robot is outside the boundary of the cylinder virtual fence.

**Remedy:** Disable the combination pair temporarily, jog the robot back inside the cylinder virtual fence, and re-enable the combination pair.

# **3.18.12.86 SSPC-219 (G:%d) Outside Vir Inf Plane**

**Cause:** Robot is outside the boundary of the infinite plane virtual fence.

**Remedy:** Disable the combination pair temporarily, jog the robot back inside the infinite plane virtual fence, and re-enable the combination pair.

# **3.18.12.87 SSPC-220 (G:%d) Outside Vir Fin Plane**

**Cause:** Robot is outside the boundary of the finite plane virtual fence.

**Remedy:** Disable the combination pair temporarily, jog the robot back inside the finite plane virtual fence, and re-enable the combination pair.

<!-- PDF page 1673 -->

### 3.18.12.88 SSPC-221 (G:%d) Outside Virtual Box

Cause: Robot is outside the boundary of the box virtual fence.

Remedy: Disable the combination pair temporarily, jog the robot back inside the box virtual fence, and re-enable the combination pair.

### 3.18.12.89 SSPC-222 (Dev:%d) Comm Timeout

Cause: Communication time to the device has exceeded the specified maximum time allowed.

Remedy: Confirm that Ethernet setup and hardware communication to the device is configured correctly.

### 3.18.12.90 SSPC-223 Invalid ICMA Dev Id(%d)

Cause: The device id provided for Interference Check Karel built-in routine is invalid.

Remedy: Confirm that both my device id and other device id for the Karel built-in routine are valid.

### 3.18.12.91 SSPC-224 (G:%d) is close to :%s

Cause: Interaction is detected.

Remedy: You can reset the alarm with SHIFT+RESET and can jog the robot out of the interacted area. This key operation disable the interaction check temporarily

### 3.18.12.92 SSPC-225 (G:%d) Both robots are inside

Cause: Both robots are inside the critical zone.

Remedy: Only one robot is allowed to stay inside the zone, move another robot to outside the zone, or correct the input in the Combination setup.

### 3.18.12.93 SSPC-226 %s %d robot bypassed

Cause: The robot is configured to be bypassed in MASH setup menu.

Remedy: This is a warning message. No action is required if the robot is configured to be bypassed.

<!-- PDF page 1674 -->

### 3.18.12.94 SSPC-227 (G:%d) Stationary Fence Only

Cause: Support stationary virtual fence only.

Remedy: The virtual fence model should be taught with respect to the world frame of the taught group. Line Tracking Schedule number should be set to 0 in the fixture Element setup menu.

### 3.18.12.95 SSPC-228 Invalid Cen Plane Sched #(%d)

Cause: Invalid Central Plane Schedule number.

Remedy: Enter a valid Central Plane Schedule id.

### 3.18.12.96 SSPC-229 Invalid Cen Plane Gmask (%d)

Cause: Invalid Central Plane Group Mask.

Remedy: Central Plane Check TP instruction requires a valid group mask. Set the Group mask of the TP program to an appropriate robot group.

### 3.18.12.97 SSPC-230 Too few C Pairs/ Fixts(%d,%d)

Cause: Too few total number of combination pairs or fixtures. Central Plane Check starts at certain combination pairs and fixtures.

Remedy: Set $IA_NUM_CHK to 60 and $IA_NUM_FOBJ to 60, then Controlled Start and Cold Start to increase the combination pairs and fixtures.

### 3.18.12.98 SSPC-231 Invalid Line Track Frame (%d)

Cause: Invalid Line Tracking frame.

Remedy: Set a valid Line Tracking frame for the associated motion group.

### 3.18.12.99 SSPC-240 DSP not available

Cause: No IIC DSP is available. Dedicated DSP is required for IIC.

Remedy: Add a DSP to support IIC.

<!-- PDF page 1675 -->

### 3.18.13 SVGN Alarm Code

#### 3.18.13.1 SVGN-001 Serious Internal error

Cause: Internal Servo Gun error

Remedy: Record error and report to hotline.

#### 3.18.13.2 SVGN-002 No sysvar pointer

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Record error and report to hotline.

#### 3.18.13.3 SVGN-004 Unable to Allocate Memory

Cause: A failure occurred while allocating memory.

Remedy: Check amount of memory being used by the system. Perform a cold start on the controller. Record error and report to hotline.

#### 3.18.13.4 SVGN-005 Wrong TPP inst. format

Cause: Internal servogun program error.

Remedy: Repower, go to control start, and then back to cold start. This action re-generates the internal servogun program and may correct the problem. Record the error and report to hotline, if the problem persists.

#### 3.18.13.5 SVGN-008 Syntax error

Cause: Instruction syntax error. This instruction is for air gun spot.

Remedy: Reteach the instruction. Reteach servo gun SPOT instruction.

#### 3.18.13.6 SVGN-009 Motion Group config. mismatch

Cause: The robot group and/or gun group are not enabled, in the group mask of this teach pendant program.

<!-- PDF page 1676 -->

**Remedy:** Determine the robot group number and gun group number for this equipment, then re-create the program, with these groups enabled.

### **3.18.13.7 SVGN-010 Invalid SG group config.**

**Cause:** Invalid servo gun group number (greater than total number of groups).

**Remedy:** Check the group number assigned to this servogun (equipment).

### **3.18.13.8 SVGN-011 Can not execute instruction(s).**

**Cause:** Incremental, offset or tool offset instructions can not execute with servo gun SPOT instruction at the same program line.

**Remedy:** Delete the incompatible motion option.

### **3.18.13.9 SVGN-012 Invalid value for index**

**Cause:** The register index specified in the instruction is invalid.

**Remedy:** Check the index value.

### **3.18.13.10 SVGN-013 Pressure exceeds limit**

**Cause:** The Pressure specified in the pressure schedule, or pressure instruction, exceeds the Max Pressure for the gun.

**Remedy:** Reduce the Pressure in the pressure schedule or program, or increase the Max Pressure item on the Servo Gun General SETUP screen. Confirm that the new pressure value does not exceed the mechanical limitation of the gun.

### **3.18.13.11 SVGN-015 Setup Configuration error**

**Cause:** Pointer to gun, schedule, backup or distance data is invalid.

**Remedy:** Check servo gun configuration data. Record error and report to hotline.

### **3.18.13.12 SVGN-016 Specified pressure too low**

**Cause:** The pressure specified in the pressure schedule or pressure instruction is lower than the lowest reachable pressure on the calibration curve.

<!-- PDF page 1677 -->

Remedy: Increase the Weld Pressure, set weld pressure = 0, or recalibrate pressure. Note 1: when weld pressure = 0, the minimum possible pressure (actual tip force may not be 0) is used. SVGN-016 will not be posted even if the calibration curve does not contain a point where weld pressure = 0. Note 2: add a calibration point at or below the specified pressure to ensure the gun can achieve the low pressure. Note 3: reducing the contact speed might make it possible to achieve lower pressures.

### 3.18.13.13 SVGN-017 Invalid pressure coefficient

Cause: Single-segment calibration method is enabled and prm_a1 is invalid (less than 0.0001 OR greater than 100.0).

Remedy: Change the calibration method to the multi-linear segment method if possible. Do this by setting the sysvars $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, then perform the pressure calibration again.

### 3.18.13.14 SVGN-018 Illegal torque limit value

Cause: The torque value is illegal (less than $sgsyscfg.$minimum_trq OR greater than max rated torque). This alarm can occur at the following times: SPOT[], PRESS_MOTN[], or PRESS[]kgf execution.

Remedy: Confirm that the pressure calibration data is valid.

### 3.18.13.15 SVGN-019 Pressure shortage: Gun%d

Cause: Same as SVGN-020, but severity is WARN. Note: SVGN-019 can occur during autotuning or if $sgsyscfg.$pst_ertype = 1; SVGN-020 occurs otherwise.

Remedy: See remedy for SVGN-020.

### 3.18.13.16 SVGN-020 Pressure shortage%d: Gun%d

Cause: The SPOT, PRESS_MOTN or TIPDRESS, instruction failed because gun closure was not detected(1) or gun pressure was unstable(2). The number after pressure shortage (1 or 2) identifies the failure type. Scan the list below for the cause that most nearly matches the condition at hand, then refer to the remedy for that cause.

Shortage 1) The instruction completed - gun tip moved to the pushing depth position - without torque increasing to the gun close detection value (1/2 Std Overtorque Value).

- 1A) If gun moved to current close axis limit (ClosLim from SVGN-177) without achieving pressure, then axis limit is too small.

<!-- PDF page 1678 -->

- 1B) Pushing depth parameter in pressure schedule is not large enough to overcome gun bending at target pressure plus tip wear amount since last measurement.
- 1C) Part thickness parameter (Thk from SVGN-177) is much larger than actual part thickness
- 1D) Gun zero master position is incorrect (if tips are worn and user chooses to not use tip wear comp, then start with 1B)
- 1E) Gun close detection torque may be excessive (or larger than Max Motor torque) due to a large restriction in gun mechanism.

Shortage 2) The torque for pressuring varied from the target value. There are (2) likely causes:

- 2A) Target pressure is at very low or high end of gun operating range (tips are likely touching part)
- 2B) Friction in gun mechanism has increased considerably since gun was autotuned (tips are likely NOT touching part)

# Remedy:

# Shortage 1)

- 1A) When tip wear compensation is used, close axis limit is adjusted to avoid over-stroking gun (ClosLim becomes smaller than StdLim when caps are worn). To extend axis limit, change tips, then run tip wear comp update program when using tip wear comp. Next, check the original close limit (StdLim) setting on servo gun setup screen and adjust if not correct.
- 1B) Increase pushing depth in pressure schedule (set $sgsyscfg.$sho_pshdpth=TRUE to see pushing depth parameter)
- 1C) Reduce part thickness in the pressure schedule so it is closer to actual part thickness.
- 1D) If using tip wear compensation, re-master the gun by running the tip wear compensation update program. Otherwise, refer to 1B or re-master the gun with new tips from the gun master screen.
- 1E) Adjust the gun mechanism to relieve the restriction. Re-tune the gun (autotune) and calibrate pressure after adjustment.

# Shortage 2)

- 2A) Re-tune the gun (autotune) then confirm pressure calibration. If problem persists, or if the alarm occurs during tip wear measurement, autotune with Initial Filter set to a value between 10-30. To see Initial Filter item, set $sgsyscfg.$sho_atn_cfg=TRUE then press enter on Auto Tune item from Gun Setup Utility before tuning.
- 2B) Re-tune the gun (autotune) to adjust the gun close detection limit, then confirm pressure calibration. If required, adjust the gun mechanism to relieve the cause of friction increase.

### 3.18.13.17 SVGN-021 Uninitialized BU condition

Cause: The BU schedule number (condition) is not initialized or is invalid.

<!-- PDF page 1679 -->

Remedy: Set a valid backup schedule number (greater than or equal to 0, AND less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$back_elm) into the instruction in the teach pendant program.

### 3.18.13.18 SVGN-022 Uninitialized Pres. condition

Cause: The pressure schedule number (condition) is not initialized or is invalid.

Remedy: Set a valid Pressure schedule number (greater than or equal to 1, AND less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$sch_elm) into the instruction in the teach pendant program.

### 3.18.13.19 SVGN-023 Incomplete Pressure calibration

Cause: Incomplete pressure calibration.

Remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General SETUP screen, select Pressure calibration, and perform pressure calibration procedure.

### 3.18.13.20 SVGN-024 Incomplete Wear Down calibration

Cause: Tip Wear Compensation setup (calibration) is not complete.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

### 3.18.13.21 SVGN-025 Illegal BU condition number

Cause: Invalid BU schedule (condition) number (greater than $sgsyscfg.$back_elm, or less than 0).

Remedy: Specify a backup condition number within the range above.

### 3.18.13.22 SVGN-026 Illegal P condition number

Cause: Invalid P schedule (condition) number ( greater than $sgsyscfg.$sch_elm, or less than 1 ).

Remedy: Specify a pressure condition number within the range above.

### 3.18.13.23 SVGN-027 Untaught element encountered

Cause: Some program elements (like positional data for example) have not been recorded.

<!-- PDF page 1680 -->

Remedy: Enter data for the missing program elements.

### 3.18.13.24 SVGN-028 Pos. type is JOINT

Cause: Position type is JOINT.

Remedy: Change position type to XYZWPR.

### 3.18.13.25 SVGN-029 Over max motor torque value

Cause: The motor torque required to achieve the pressure specified in the pressure schedule or pressure instruction exceeds the Max Torque value specified on the Servogun SETUP screen.

Remedy:

1. Reduce the Pressure value.
2. Check Pressure Calibration data.
3. Calibrate Pressure again if the data is incorrect.
4. Increase the Max Motor Torque value on the Servo Gun General SETUP screen, if possible. Note: motor torque value on the General SETUP screen can be regarded as a fractional percentage of the maximum allowable torque. The screen will not allow this value to be set larger than amp + motor rating.

### 3.18.13.26 SVGN-030 Tip Stick detection

Cause: Tip stick detection DI is ON.

Remedy: Jog the gun open or use a tool to separate the tip from the part, if the tip is stuck. If the tip is not stuck, then determine why the tip stick input is on.

### 3.18.13.27 SVGN-031 Tear Off is executing

Cause: When tear off function is executing, program cannot be started.

Remedy: Restart program after tear off function finished.

### 3.18.13.28 SVGN-032 Tip increased error(Gun)

Cause: The measured tip wear on the gun side (moving tip) indicates that the tip has grown by an amount greater than the Gun Increased Error(mm) setting.

<!-- PDF page 1681 -->

Remedy: First confirm the condition of the tip. If the tip is not ok, then replace it, and perform tip wear measurement again. If a chip from tip dressing remains on the tip, remove this chip then re-measure the tip wear. If new tips were installed after the previous tip wear measurement, be sure the tip wear update program was run with the New Tips Parameter set to (1) in the Call instruction for the tip wear macro. If this parameter was not set correctly, then press fault reset and run the tip wear update program again with the New Tips Parameter set to (1). If the tip is OK and the new tip parameter was set correctly, then perform the tip wear measurement again. Observe the gun closely during this operation. Be sure the tips touch during the 1st step of the tip wear measurement and be sure the gun tip touches the fixture during the 2nd step (if used). If the gun tip does not close fully during either step, then the gun friction has probably increased. To compensate, run Autotuning then Pressure Calibration and perform the tip wear setup procedure again with new tips. Inspect the gun to find the reason for the increase in friction. If both steps of the measurement perform correctly then it might be necessary to increase the value of the Increase Error(mm) setting for the robot side tip. Do this on the Tip Wear Detection screen (SETUP-SERVO GUN-GENERAL SETUP).

### 3.18.13.29 SVGN-033 Tip increased error(Robot)

Cause: The measured tip wear on the robot side (stationary tip) indicates that the tip has grown by an amount greater than the Robot Increased Error(mm) setting

Remedy: First confirm the condition of the tip. If the tip is not ok, then replace it, and perform tip wear measurement again. If a chip from tip dressing remains on the tip, remove this chip then re-measure the tip wear. If new tips were installed after the previous tip wear measurement, be sure the tip wear update program was run with the New Tips Parameter set to (1) in the Call instruction for the tip wear macro. If this parameter was not set correctly, then press fault reset and run the tip wear update program again with the New Tips Parameter set to (1). If the tip is OK and the new tip parameter was set correctly, then perform the tip wear measurement again. Observe the gun closely during this operation. Be sure the tips touch during the 1st step of the tip wear measurement and be sure the gun tip touches the fixture during the 2nd step (if used). If the gun tip does not close fully during either step, then the gun friction has probably increased. To compensate, run Autotuning then Pressure Calibration and perform the tip wear setup procedure again with new tips. Inspect the gun to find the reason for the increase in friction. If both steps of the measurement perform correctly then it may be necessary to increase the value of the Increase Error(mm) setting for the robot side tip. Do this on the Tip Wear Detection screen (SETUP-SERVO GUN-GENERAL SETUP).

### 3.18.13.30 SVGN-034 Excessive robot tip difference.

Cause: The Tip Wear difference between the robot tips on the dual gun exceeds the specified tolerance.

Remedy: Replace or dress the tips (and tip holder if necessary) and run the tip wear update program for each gun. Alternatively, increase the difference tolerance in the Tip Wear Detection screen (Press MENUS. Select SETUP. Select SERVO GUN. Select GENERAL SETUP.)

<!-- PDF page 1682 -->

### 3.18.13.31 SVGN-035 Pressure enable time out

Cause: The pressure enable signal (input) did not turn on before the wait time expired.

Remedy: Determine why the pressure enable signal did not turn on. Or, increase the value of time out($SPOTEQSETUP[].$PEN_TMOUT) if it is too short.

### 3.18.13.32 SVGN-036 Comp confirmation time out

Cause: The comp confirmation signal (input) did not turn on before the wait time expired.

Remedy: Check the reason that the comp confirmation signal is off. Or, increase the value of time out($SPOTEQSETUP[].$NSE_TMOUT), if it is too short.

### 3.18.13.33 SVGN-037 Illegal pressure enable signal

Cause: The pressure enable signal number is illegal.

Remedy: Map the pressure enable input to a valid input index via ($SPOTEQIO[].$DI_PEN_I).

### 3.18.13.34 SVGN-038 Illegal comp confirmation signal

Cause: The comp confirmation signal number is illegal.

Remedy: Map the comp confirmation input to a valid input index via ($SPOTEQIO[].$DI_NSE_I).

### 3.18.13.35 SVGN-039 Thickness:%smm Out Of Tolerance %s.

Cause: Same as SVGN-040, but with a WARN severity.

Remedy: See SVGN-040.

### 3.18.13.36 SVGN-040 Thickness:%smm Out Of Tolerance %s

Cause: The Measured part thickness deviates from the specified value more than the Under or Over thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. Note: the alarm message indicates the detected(measured) thickness. This value is also displayed on the servogun status screen. Please refer to the secondary alarm code for more specific diagnostic information.

Remedy: Check the master position for the gun axis and make sure the tips touch at the zero position (+/- 0.1mm). Confirm that tip wear and gun sag compensation are enabled and that the compensation values are correct. Check the part or re-enter the part thickness in the pressure schedule. Alternatively, increase the Under and Over thickness limits in the Part Thickness

<!-- PDF page 1683 -->

check screen found on the Servo Gun General Setup screen. Resume the program, to retry the measurement. Perform thickness check calibration again, if the problem persists.

### 3.18.13.37 SVGN-041 No more available memory(PERM)

Cause: There is not enough permanent memory. It is impossible to allocate the system variable.

Remedy: Please increase the size of S-RAM module. Or, decrease the value of $SGSYSCFG.$M_GUN_NUM.

### 3.18.13.38 SVGN-042 Lack of $SGGUN

Cause: The number of $SGGUN is less than total number of axes in the servo gun group(s).

Remedy: Increase $SGSYSCFG.$M_GUN_NUM to the minimum value required to accommodate all servo gun axes. After changing this sysvar, go to control start, and then perform a Cold start, to make the change effective.

### 3.18.13.39 SVGN-043 AutoTuning Started.

Cause: User has started Servo Gun autotuning.

Remedy: No remedy required. This is a warning message to log the event.

### 3.18.13.40 SVGN-044 AutoTune Successfully Complete

Cause: User has successfully completed auto tuning.

Remedy: User should cycle power to use servo gun.

### 3.18.13.41 SVGN-045 AutoTuning Failed.

Cause: Auto Tuning Could not be completed.

Remedy: Restart Auto tuning on the tuning menu, and try the operation again.

### 3.18.13.42 SVGN-046 FAULTS must be reset.

Cause: The user executed autotuning while the system was faulted.

Remedy: Clear ALL FAULTS and start tuning again.

<!-- PDF page 1684 -->

# **3.18.13.43 SVGN-047 Step mode must be disabled.**

**Cause:** STEP mode is enabled.

**Remedy:** Disable STEP mode, and start tuning again.

# **3.18.13.44 SVGN-048 Machine lock must be disabled.**

**Cause:** Machine Lock is enabled for the servo gun group.

**Remedy:** Disable Machine lock from the TEST CYCLE Menu, and start tuning again.

# **3.18.13.45 SVGN-049 Hold must be cleared.**

**Cause:** Hold is active.

**Remedy:** Clear the HOLD, and start tuning again.

# **3.18.13.46 SVGN-050 Autuning: Re-power required**

**Cause:** Re-power is required to make some parameter changes effective.

**Remedy:** Cycle power before proceeding.

# **3.18.13.47 SVGN-051 Backup stroke is not selected.**

**Cause:** SHIFT + backup (hardkey) was pressed but no Backup Schedule (stroke) was selected.

**Remedy:** Select a backup schedule by pressing the backup hardkey (without the SHIFT key).

# **3.18.13.48 SVGN-052 Motion group mismatch.**

**Cause:** The motion group number of the user program for manual pressure or manual backup is not matched to the Servo Gun group.

**Remedy:** Change the motion group number of the program to match the Servo Gun.

# **3.18.13.49 SVGN-053 Backup stroke is not set.**

**Cause:** The specified backup schedule (stroke) index is not valid.

<!-- PDF page 1685 -->

Remedy: Set a valid backup schedule number.

### 3.18.13.50 SVGN-054 $EQNUM is invalid number.

Cause: $EQNUM is not use in the system.

Remedy: Set the valid equipment number to $EQNUM.

### 3.18.13.51 SVGN-055 $EQNUM is not Servo Gun.

Cause: The equipment specified by $EQNUM is not assigned to the Servo Gun

Remedy: Set the equipment number which is assigned to Servo Gun to $EQNUM.

### 3.18.13.52 SVGN-056 $GUNNUN is invalid number.

Cause: Specified number is not valid for $GUNNUM.

Remedy: $GUNNUM can be set only 1 or 2 which is corresponding to GUN1 or GUN2

### 3.18.13.53 SVGN-057 Tip Wear Down Cal. is INCOMP.

Cause: Tip Wear Compensation setup is not complete.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

### 3.18.13.54 SVGN-058 UT or UF is different.

Cause: The tool frame number or user frame number is different from the standard position.

Remedy: Change the frame number to same number of standard position.

### 3.18.13.55 SVGN-059 Cannot read specified PR[].

Cause: System cannot read the position register which is specified by $PRINDEX.

Remedy: Check the number of $PRINDEX.

<!-- PDF page 1686 -->

# **3.18.13.56 SVGN-060 Pressure program is not set.**

**Cause:** The pressure program name is not set correctly.

**Remedy:** Set correct program name in manual operation setup screen.

# **3.18.13.57 SVGN-061 Backup program is not set.**

**Cause:** The backup program name is not set correctly.

**Remedy:** Set correct program name in manual operation setup screen.

# **3.18.13.58 SVGN-062 Pressure data is not selected.**

**Cause:** Shift + GUN hardkey was pressed, but no Pressure Schedule was selected.

**Remedy:** Select a pressure schedule, by pressing GUN hardkey, without shift key.

# **3.18.13.59 SVGN-063 Pressure data is not set.**

**Cause:** The GUN hardkey was pressed (to select pressure), but no Pressure Schedule was enabled.

**Remedy:** Enable Pressure Schedule(s) for Manual Operation by setting the Manual item to TRUE in the Pressure Schedule data table.

# **3.18.13.60 SVGN-064 Manual Weld Verif. Enabled**

**Cause:** Manual Weld Verification feature was enabled.

**Remedy:** Just a notification, no action necessary.

# **3.18.13.61 SVGN-065 Manual Weld Verif. Disabled**

**Cause:** Manual Weld Verification feature was disabled.

**Remedy:** Just a notification, no action necessary.

# **3.18.13.62 SVGN-066 Manual Weld Verif. Activated**

**Cause:** Manual Weld Verification feature was activated.

<!-- PDF page 1687 -->

Remedy: Just a notification, to let user know he is in this mode and that groups may be disabled automatically for him

### 3.18.13.63 SVGN-067 Manual Weld Verif. De-Activated

Cause: Manual Weld Verification feature was activated.

Remedy: Just a notification, to let user know he is in this mode and that groups may be enabled automatically for him

### 3.18.13.64 SVGN-068 Could not load program %s

Cause: Could not load tp program for tip wear measurement. See cause code for reason.

Remedy: Resume the program, to re-attempt the load. If the load is successful, then the tip wear measurement will continue.

### 3.18.13.65 SVGN-069 Pressure position is near close limit.

Cause: The actual position of the gun during pressuring (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) is approaching the gun's close limit: the distance between the gun tip (position) and the close limit < $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL.

Remedy: Check the master position and close stroke limit for the gun. If these values are incorrect, then update them. If these values are correct, then install new tips OR, reduce the value in $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL (mm) to withhold this alarm until the gun tip is closer to the close stroke limit. Set $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL (mm) = 0, to disable this alarm.

### 3.18.13.66 SVGN-070 Gun Change is DISABLED.

Cause: The gun change function is disabled.

Remedy: Enable Gun change.

### 3.18.13.67 SVGN-071 Machine lock is ENABLE.

Cause: Machine lock for robot axes is enabled at gun attach instruction.

Remedy: Release machine lock.

<!-- PDF page 1688 -->

### 3.18.13.68 SVGN-072 Illegal assignment of gun axis.

Cause: Gun number assignment are wrong.

Remedy: Confirm Gun number assignment.

### 3.18.13.69 SVGN-073 Gun not detached (AXISORDER).

Cause: Gun is not detached. Some AXISORDER are not 0.

Remedy: GUN ATTACH instruction can be executed only when no gun is attached.

### 3.18.13.70 SVGN-074 Gun not detached.

Cause: Gun is not detached. Gun attach input signal is OFF.

Remedy: GUN ATTACH instruction can be executed only when no gun is attached.

### 3.18.13.71 SVGN-075 Gun not attached.

Cause: Gun is not attached. Gun attach input signal is ON.

Remedy: GUN DETACH instruction can be executed only when a gun is attached.

### 3.18.13.72 SVGN-076 Another process is executing.

Cause: Another program is executing GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction.
$CHG_PHASE is not 0 at executing the instruction.

Remedy: Wait until another program end GUN ATTACH/DETACH instruction.

### 3.18.13.73 SVGN-077 Gun identify signal is OFF.

Cause: Gun identify signal is OFF.

Remedy: Confirm the setting for Gun identify signal.

### 3.18.13.74 SVGN-078 Gun set signal is OFF.

Cause: Gun set signal is OFF.

<!-- PDF page 1689 -->

Remedy: Confirm the setting for Gun set signal.

### 3.18.13.75 SVGN-079 Gun change canceled.

Cause: GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction is canceled while executing the instruction.

Remedy: Do COLD START the system.

### 3.18.13.76 SVGN-080 Gun change timeout.

Cause: GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction become timeout while executing the instruction.

Remedy: Do COLD START the system.

### 3.18.13.77 SVGN-081 Gun mastering data is lost.

Cause: Mastering data of the gun is lost by a pause while mastering.

Remedy: Do COLD START the system. Then master the gun by manual operation.

### 3.18.13.78 SVGN-082 Gun mastering is failed.

Cause: Gun mastering is failed by a pause while mastering.

Remedy: Continue to retry mastering.

### 3.18.13.79 SVGN-083 GUN ATTACH is failed (E%d)

Cause: GUN ATTACH instruction failed. Please see cause code.

Remedy: Please see cause code.

### 3.18.13.80 SVGN-084 GUN DETACH is failed (E%d)

Cause: GUN DETACH instruction failed. Please see cause code.

Remedy: Please see cause code.

<!-- PDF page 1690 -->

### 3.18.13.81 SVGN-085 Robot not mastered(Gun axis).

Cause: The mastering of servo gun axis has not been performed yet. System variable $master_done set FALSE.

Remedy: Please perform the mastering of the servo gun axis.

### 3.18.13.82 SVGN-086 Robot not calibrated(Gun axis).

Cause: The calibration of servo gun axis has not been performed yet. System variable $calibrate set FALSE.

Remedy: Please calibrate the servo gun axis.

### 3.18.13.83 SVGN-087 Ref pos not set(Gun axis).

Cause: Reference position has not been set when quick mastering.

Remedy: Quick mastering may not be possible. Fixture or zero master.

### 3.18.13.84 SVGN-088 Another gun is attached.

Cause: The gun number specified by the GUN DETACH instruction is different than the currently attached gun.

Remedy: Verify the gun number of GUN DETACH instruction.

### 3.18.13.85 SVGN-089 Calibrate motion is failed.

Cause: While the calibrate motion, the detect condition was not triggered.

Remedy: Verify the detect condition in the gun change setup screen.

### 3.18.13.86 SVGN-090 PR[] index is not set.

Cause: The PR[] index for the calibrate motion is not set.

Remedy: Please set PR[] index for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

<!-- PDF page 1691 -->

### 3.18.13.87 SVGN-091 Touch torque is not set.

Cause: The Touch torque for the calibrate motion is not set.

Remedy: Please set Touch torque for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

### 3.18.13.88 SVGN-092 Detect signal is not set.

Cause: The Detect signal for the calibrate motion is not set.

Remedy: Please set Detect signal for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

### 3.18.13.89 SVGN-093 Gun does not stop.

Cause: At the Gun Zero Master[] instruction, Servo gun axis does not stop.

Remedy: After servo gun axis stops, execute the Gun Zero Master[] instruction.

### 3.18.13.90 SVGN-094 GUN EXCHANGE failed (E%d)

Cause: At the Gun exhange[] instruction, the new gun could not be activated.

Remedy: Make sure that the each servogun has valid axisorder

### 3.18.13.91 SVGN-095 Gun type is not opposable.

Cause: Opposable gun type is required for target gun.

Remedy: Set gun type as opposable, if appropriate.

### 3.18.13.92 SVGN-096 Gun close is disabled.

Cause: This operation cannot be performed while Gun Close (stroke enable) is disabled.

Remedy: Set the Gun operation to stroke (stroke enable) on the SoftPanel screen. Note: The SoftPanel screen can be accessed from the TEST CYCLE menu.

<!-- PDF page 1692 -->

### 3.18.13.93 SVGN-097 Tip wear down misdetection.

Cause: The tips did not touch during the 1st step of tip wear measurement due to an increase in gun friction or the tips touched but they are now longer than the reference tips by an amount greater than the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm)

Remedy: If the tips are not fully closed when the alarm occurs, then the re-master operation failed during tip wear measurement. This usually happens because the gun friction has increased since the gun was last Autotuned. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the cause of the friction increase. After this is complete, put new tips on the gun and perform the tip wear setup procedure again. If the tips are closed when the alarm occurs, then the tips are longer than allowed. The tips measured during tip wear setup are the reference tips. New tips can only be longer than the reference tips by an amount equal to the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm) specified in the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Either increase the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm) or replace the tips with shorter tips. If the tips seem to be the correct length, then perform the tip wear setup procedure again to establish new reference tips.

### 3.18.13.94 SVGN-098 Invalid inform signal(Gun).

Cause: The Digital Output assigned for notification of excessive Gun Tip Wear (amount) is invalid.

Remedy: Check the present setting of the Inform Signal for the Maximum Wear Check (gun) found on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Change the DO number to one that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

### 3.18.13.95 SVGN-099 Invalid inform signal(Robot).

Cause: The Digital Output assigned for the notification of excessive Robot Tip Wear (amount) is invalid.

Remedy: Check the present setting of the Inform Signal for the Maximum Wear Check (robot) found on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Change the DO number to one that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

### 3.18.13.96 SVGN-100 Invalid register number.

Cause: Specified register number is out of range.

Remedy: Set a valid register number.

<!-- PDF page 1693 -->

### 3.18.13.97 SVGN-101 Invalid position reg number.

Cause: The specified position register number is out of range.

Remedy: Set a valid position register number.

### 3.18.13.98 SVGN-102 Increased err. not set(Gun).

Cause: The increased error limit for Gun(movable) tip is set to 0.0mm

Remedy: Set the Increased error to a value greater than 0.0mm if Increased Error checking is needed. This item is set on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen).

### 3.18.13.99 SVGN-103 Increased err. not set(Robot).

Cause: Increased error limit for Robot(stationary) tip is set to 0.0mm

Remedy: Set the Increased error to a value greater than 0.0mm if the Increased Error checking is needed. This item is set on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen).

### 3.18.13.100 SVGN-104 Excessive load detected.

Cause: An excessive load is detected, during tip wear setup or tip wear update. The gun zero position might be incorrect.

Remedy: Remove any foreign object between the tips, and/or re-master the gun. Resume the tip wear setup or update operation. If the alarm still occurs, then the gun friction has increased since it was last Autotuned. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the gun to determine the cause of the friction increase.

### 3.18.13.101 SVGN-105 Failed to reset pulse coder.

Cause: The pulse coder alarm was not reset.

Remedy: Reset the pulse coder alarm again.

### 3.18.13.102 SVGN-106 Tip wear uninitialized.

Cause: Tip Wear Compensation is uninitialized.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

<!-- PDF page 1694 -->

### 3.18.13.103 SVGN-107 Tip wear no load threshold.

Cause: The load threshold used to detect contact with the fixture for the second step of tip wear measurement has not been set.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

### 3.18.13.104 SVGN-108 Tip wear no standard pulse.

Cause: The reference zero position (i.e. standard pulse) used for tip wear measurement has not been set.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

### 3.18.13.105 SVGN-109 Tip wear no standard opening.

Cause: The reference open position (i.e. standard opening) used for the second step of tip wear measurement has not been set.

Remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

### 3.18.13.106 SVGN-110 Tip wear no detect DI index.

Cause: The Tip wear Detection Type is set to DI, but no DI index is specified.

Remedy: Confirm that DI detection is the desired type (LOAD detection is the default type). If so, then assign an available DI point to the tip wear detection sensor and set that index value into the Detect Signal item on the Tip Wear Detection Screen.

### 3.18.13.107 SVGN-111 Failed to touch fixture.

Cause: The gun tip reached the master position without detecting the fixture (i.e. tip wear plate) during the second step of tip wear measurement.

Remedy: Confirm that the zero position is correct, then confirm that a rigid fixture is between the tips during the second step of tip wear measurement.

<!-- PDF page 1695 -->

### 3.18.13.108 SVGN-112 Incomplete Servo tuning.

Cause: Tip wear measurement or thickness check calibration started, but Servo tuning is incomplete.

Remedy: Complete servo auto-tuning. Go to the Gun Setup Utility (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and select the Auto Tune item. The Auto Tune program can be started after completing the previous steps in the utility.

### 3.18.13.109 SVGN-113 Gun must be open.

Cause: The tip wear setup or update program started with the gun closed.

Remedy: Open the tips, then execute the tip wear measurement program again. If the problem persists, master the gun, then execute the tip wear measurement program again.

### 3.18.13.110 SVGN-114 Tip wear misdetection.(FIX).

Cause: The moving tip did not touch the fixture during the second step of tip wear measurement due to an increase in gun friction, or the fixture and/or robot master position has changed since tip wear was initialized.
