Remedy: If the moving tip is not pressing into the fixture when the alarm occurs, the fixture touch load (i.e. pressing force) was reached without actually touching the fixture. This usually happens because the gun friction has increased since the tip wear setup program was run. Increase the Margin of Load item in the Tip Wear Detection Screen to overcome the increase in friction. Doing this can affect the tip wear measurement, so the tip wear setup procedure should be performed again. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the gun for the cause of the friction increase. If the moving tip is pressing into the fixture when the alarm occurs then the fixture position has moved relative to the robot master position, the robot master data has changed, or the points in the program TW_MV2PT.tp have changed. Perform the tip wear setup procedure again.

### 3.18.13.111 SVGN-115 MP detection failed.

Cause: Magnet Phase detection failed.

Remedy: Retry the operation. Make sure that there is some separation (at least a few mm ), between the guntip/fixedtip and drive mechanism/open_hardstop.

### 3.18.13.112 SVGN-116 MP detection unavailable.

Cause: Magnet Phase detection is unavailable with the current calibration motion type.

Remedy: Change the calibration motion type(to 7or8) in the Gun change screen.

<!-- PDF page 1696 -->

### 3.18.13.113 SVGN-117 Ref pos auto-setup failed.

Cause: The Gun closing motion to set the reference position failed.

Remedy: Confirm that the Touch torque(%) on the Gun SETUP screen is set appropriately.

### 3.18.13.114 SVGN-118 Max wear exceeded (Gun Tip).

Cause: The maximum tip wear amount has been exceeded on the gun tip.

Remedy: Replace the gun tip or re-run tip wear setup.

### 3.18.13.115 SVGN-119 Max wear exceeded (Rbt Tip).

Cause: The maximum tip wear amount has been exceeded on the robot tip.

Remedy: Replace the robot tip or re-run tip wear setup.

### 3.18.13.116 SVGN-120 Skipped max gun torque update: Gun%d.

Cause: Max gun torque was not updated due to an invalid parameter.

Remedy: See the cause code to identify the reason for the update failure. Correct the problem as described by the remedy for the alarm specified in the cause code.

### 3.18.13.117 SVGN-122 Pressure is not invertible.

Cause: The specified pressure cannot be used, it does not lie on the calibration curve (2nd order).

Remedy: Change the calibration method to the multi-linear segment method if possible. Do this by setting the system variables $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, then perform the pressure calibration again. Alternatively, perform pressure calibration again, or reduce max pressure.

### 3.18.13.118 SVGN-123 Over-torque protection disabled.

Cause: Overtorque protection has been disabled. This is merely a warning to notify the operator.

Remedy: Enable overtorque protection, if desired.

<!-- PDF page 1697 -->

### 3.18.13.119 SVGN-124 Max gun torque must be > floor.

Cause: The Max Gun Torque parameter in OverTorque Protection is less than the Standard OverTorque Value. The Max Gun Torque is the torque required to achieve the Max Pressure of the gun (according to the Pressure Calibration data). The Standard OverTorque Value is the lowest torque (i.e. floor) where an abnormal torque condition can be accurately observed due to gun friction.

Remedy: To eliminate this alarm either the Max Gun Torque must be increased or the Standard OverTorque Value needs to be lower. If OverTorque Protection is still enabled, there might be no action necessary. View the Parameter Summary in OverTorque Protection to judge whether the values are acceptable. The Max Gun Torque can be increased by increasing the Max Pressure on the Servo Gun General Setup Screen. If OverTorque Protection is presently disabled, be sure to enable it after this. If the Pressure Calibration is not complete or the data is old, perform the Pressure Calibration again.

### 3.18.13.120 SVGN-125 Max gun torque must be < ceil.

Cause: The Max Gun Torque parameter in OverTorque Protection is set higher than the maximum torque of the servo motor.

Remedy: Make sure Pressure Calibration of the gun is complete and the data is entered correctly. Perform Pressure Calibration again if possible. Decrease The Max Gun Torque by decreasing the Max Pressure of the gun via the Servogun General SETUP Screen.

### 3.18.13.121 SVGN-126 Servo parameters exceed max gun torque.

Cause: Overtorque protection is enabled, but one or more of the parameters responsible for limiting torque exceeded the max gun torque.

Remedy: Disable, then re-enable overtorque protection, in order to re-write servo parameters. Alternatively, disable overtorque protection OR enable machine lock on the servogun group to disable this alarm.

### 3.18.13.122 SVGN-127 DSP max gun torque update timeout.

Cause: Timeout, waiting for acknowledgement of new overtorque parameters.

Remedy: Cycle power or toggle overtorque protect enable to write parameters again.

### 3.18.13.123 SVGN-128 Invalid thickness value specified.

Cause: A string parameter or a value less than 0.0 was passed into the THK_VAL macro.

<!-- PDF page 1698 -->

Remedy: Re-enter a parameter value greater than or equal to 0.0 into the thickness value macro.

### 3.18.13.124 SVGN-129 Invalid thickness tolerance specified.

Cause: A string parameter or a value less than 0.0 was specified for the THK_TOL macro.

Remedy: Re-enter a parameter value greater than or equal to 0.0 into the thickness tolerance macro.

### 3.18.13.125 SVGN-130 Invalid thickness severity specified.

Cause: A string parameter or a value other than 1 or 2 was specified for the THK_SEV macro.

Remedy: Re-enter a parameter value of 1 or 2 into the thickness severity macro.

### 3.18.13.126 SVGN-131 Invalid gun index specified.

Cause: A string parameter or a value other than 1, 2, or 3 was specified for gun index in a THK_macro.

Remedy: This parameter is optional but if it is specified, set it as follows: 1: Gun.A only 2: Gun.B only (dual gun case) 3: Gun.A+B (dual gun case)

### 3.18.13.127 SVGN-132 Invalid inform signal (dualgun max wear diff).

Cause: An invalid output index is assigned for notification of excessive difference between fixed tip wear amounts (on gunA and gunB).

Remedy: Confirm that the setting of rack, slot and start point is valid. Cycle power if necessary, to make the io assignment effective. Set index=0 to disable this signal.

### 3.18.13.128 SVGN-133 Encoder scale is NULL.

Cause: An encoder scale value of 0.0 was detected.

Remedy: Re-enter the gear ratio on the NOBOT Maintenance menu.

### 3.18.13.129 SVGN-134 Thickness Check Calibration Incomplete.

Cause: Thickness Check Calibration was never performed or did not complete successfully.

<!-- PDF page 1699 -->

Remedy: Go to Gun Setup Utility screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute the Thickness Check Calibration.

### 3.18.13.130 SVGN-135 Thickness check cal err: bad torque

Cause: A thickness check calibration point has a torque value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.

Remedy: Go to the Gun Setup Utility Screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute the Thickness Check Calibration.

### 3.18.13.131 SVGN-136 Thickness check cal err: bad deflection

Cause: A thickness check calibration point has a deflection value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.

Remedy: Go to the Gun Setup Utility Screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute Thickness Check Calibration. If the error still occurs, re-master and re-execute Thickness Check Calibration.

### 3.18.13.132 SVGN-137 Invalid Number of Thickness Cal pts.

Cause: The number of Thickness Check calibration points is less than 2 or greater than 4.

Remedy: Display the system variable screen and enter a value of 2, 3, or 4 into $sgthkset#.$num_cal_pts, where # = gun number.

### 3.18.13.133 SVGN-138 Invalid tipwear ratio.

Cause: The tip wear ratio for one step wear measurement is invalid (less than 0.0 or greater than 1.0).

Remedy: Set the wear ratio in the Tip Wear measurement macro program to a value between 0 and 1. The macro program WR_UPDAT is used to perform the Tip Wear measurement with the 1-Step Method. Set the wear-ratio which is found as a parameter in a CALL instruction to the program TWKCALC2, or a similar name. Follow the program comments to find the proper parameter to adjust: CALL TWKCALC2(wear-ratio,AR[2]).

### 3.18.13.134 SVGN-139 Could not read tip stick detect input.

Cause: Tip stick detect input could not be read, due to an I/O error.

Remedy: Check the I/O mapping/configuration and I/O device status.

<!-- PDF page 1700 -->

### 3.18.13.135 SVGN-140 Uninitialized start distance number.

Cause: The specified start distance number is not valid.

Remedy: Specify a start distance number greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$dst_elm.

### 3.18.13.136 SVGN-141 Uninitialized end distance number.

Cause: The specified end distance number is not valid.

Remedy: Specify an end distance number greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$dst_elm.

### 3.18.13.137 SVGN-142 Illegal decel option.

Cause: The decel rate option setting is incompatible with the speed calibration specification.

Remedy: Set $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv=3 OR contact FANUC America Corporation for assistance. Note: $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv==3 is the default setting for this variable, so absolute speed calibration is a non-standard setting.

### 3.18.13.138 SVGN-143 Stoperlim:%.1fmm < PushDepth:%.1fmm.

Cause: Automaster operation is executing and position error due to push depth exceeds stoperlim. Stop error excess alarm may occur.

Remedy: Increase $SGGUN#.$SETUP.$STOPERLIM or decrease pushing depth.

### 3.18.13.139 SVGN-144 Thickness check bias(%smm) overtol

Cause: Gun deflection at torque = 0 exceeds $SGTHKSET#.$MAX_D0BIAS. Gun deflection should be ~0 at torque=0, so gun master position may be incorrect.

Remedy: 1. Remaster gun – if system is setup to do tip wear measurements, run the tip wear measurement program (typ. wr_updat or tw_updat). If not doing tip wear measurements, go to gun master screen and execute mastering with new tips. 2. Execute Thickness Check Calibration (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP). 3. If problem persists, increase $SGTHKSET#.$MAX_D0BIAS (default = 1.0mm).

<!-- PDF page 1701 -->

### 3.18.13.140 SVGN-146 Joint velocity limit too low.

Cause: Joint velocity limit must be greater than zero, for mm/sec pressure calibration speed specification.

Remedy: Update joint velocity limit using one of the following methods: 1. Re-enter the gear ratio via the Servo Gun Axes item on the Maintenance menu, at Control start. 2. Directly enter the Max Joint Speed on the Axis Data screen of the Servo Gun Setup menu, at control start.

### 3.18.13.141 SVGN-147 Sync/speed min distance =%s.

Cause: The minimum gun opening distance required to achieve the specified contact speed for this Pressure Schedule is larger than the opening specified by the Start Distance schedule used in the SPOT or Press_Motion instruction. The correct contact speed might not have been achieved during execution of this instruction.

Remedy: Increase the Start Distances assigned to the Distance Schedule that is used when this alarm occurs. Go to the Distance Schedule data table (DATA-DISTANCE) and increase the gun and/or robot distances.

### 3.18.13.142 SVGN-148 Can't identify routine name.

Cause: Can't identify routine name corresponding to the standalone instruction. Refer to cause code for root cause.

Remedy: See remedy for cause error.

### 3.18.13.143 SVGN-149 CP enable is required.

Cause: CP mode is not enabled, but synchronize move to pressure position is enabled AND/OR linear distance is enabled.

Remedy: Enable CP mode (set $cpcfg.$cp_enable=TRUE) or contact FANUC America Corporation for assistance.

### 3.18.13.144 SVGN-150 Synchronization enable is required.

Cause: The linear distance function is enabled, but synchronize move to pressure is not enabled.

Remedy: Enable synchronize move to pressure position (set $sgsyscfg.$sync_mv2prs=TRUE) OR disable linear distance (set $sgsyscfg.$lin_dst_enb=FALSE).

<!-- PDF page 1702 -->

### 3.18.13.145 SVGN-151 Cannot add file to backup/restore list.

Cause: Servogun sysvar file(s) could not be added to backup/restore list.

Remedy: Report problem to FANUC America Corporation.

### 3.18.13.146 SVGN-152 Invalid increase signal(Gun).

Cause: The Digital Output assigned to notify of increased error on the Gun Tip is invalid.

Remedy: Check the present value of $sggun#.$setup.$tipincioidx (on the system variable screen). Change this value to the number of a DO that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

### 3.18.13.147 SVGN-153 Invalid increase signal(Robot).

Cause: The Digital Output assigned to notify of increased error on the Robot Tip is invalid.

Remedy: Check the present value of $sggun#.$setup.$rbtincioidx (on the system variable screen). Change this value to the number of a DO that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

### 3.18.13.148 SVGN-154 Tipwear update cancelled.

Cause: Tip wear update did not complete, due to cancel or gun close error. Refer to cause code for specific reason.

Remedy: Correct the condition identified in the cause code, then run tip wear update again.

### 3.18.13.149 SVGN-155 Cancel or ffr was selected.

Cause: Pressure shortage occurred during zero calibration and “Cancel tip wear update and exit” or “Initiate fast fault recovery” was chosen on the alarm recovery screen.

Remedy: Correct the issue that caused the pressure shortage, then run tip wear update again.

### 3.18.13.150 SVGN-156 Gun close NOT detected.

Cause: Gun close reference position was NOT recorded (for tip wear gun close check). PRESS_MOTN[] instruction did not complete or was skipped, during zero calibration.

Remedy: Run tip wear update again.

<!-- PDF page 1703 -->

### 3.18.13.151 SVGN-157 Gun not closed at zero cal process end.

Cause: Zero calibration was not performed because gun is not closed (gun is too far from close position). Note1: the condition for SVGN-157 detection is: |a-b| > c, where: a = Gun position after PRESS_MOTN[] instruction executes in zero calibration program (TWZRCLB2). b = Gun position when Gun Zero Master[] instruction executes in zero calibration program(TWZRCLB2). c = Gun close error tolerance (default: 2.0mm). Note2: Items a-b and c are karel variables in program: TWKINIT. a-b: Posdiff is stored in [TWKINIT]gcls_posdif[ eq# ] c: Close error tol is stored in [TWKINIT]gcls_err_tol Note3: Posdiff can be thought of as position b, with position a as Zero master position. For example, if a is more closed than b, and gun open direction is negative, then posdif polarity is negative (magnitude equals distance between a and b).

Remedy: 1. If gun position is changing after PRESS_MOTN[] (inverted gun that drops/drifts for example) then correct this condition so zero calibration is accurate. 2. Increase gcls_err_tol, if gcls_err_tol is too small. 3. Perform tip wear update again. 4. Disable gun close error check by setting [TWKINIT]gcls_err_enb = FALSE.

### 3.18.13.152 SVGN-158 Thk%s,Push(Exp%s,Aval%s,Max%s)mm.

Cause: This alarm provides information to identify the root cause of the pressure shortage alarm. Parameters meanings are: Thk: Thickness expected (value specified in pressure schedule) Push.Exp: Pushing depth expected (larger of pushing depth in pressure schedule and speed depth) Push.Aval: Pushing depth available (thk + current close stroke limit) Push.Max: Pushing depth maximum (thk + standard close stroke limit)

Remedy: If thickness and/or pushing depth are incorrect, then adjust them. If stroke limit has become too small, install new tips.

### 3.18.13.153 SVGN-159 Pressure margin conversion error.

Cause: Pressure margin conversion for touchup process failed. See cause code for reason.

Remedy: Refer to cause code's remedy.

### 3.18.13.154 SVGN-160 Invalid calibration point: bad torque.

Cause: A pressure calibration point has a torque value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.

Remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that both torque and pressure increase at each successive calibration point.

<!-- PDF page 1704 -->

### 3.18.13.155 SVGN-161 Invalid calibration point: bad speed.

Cause: A Speed value in the Pressure Calibration table is less than the min speed or greater than the max speed.

Remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that the Speed for each point in the Pressure Calibration table is within the operating range of the gun.

### 3.18.13.156 SVGN-162 Invalid calibration point: bad pressure.

Cause: A pressure calibration point has a pressure (force) value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.

Remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that both torque and pressure increase, at each successive calibration point.

### 3.18.13.157 SVGN-163 Invalid calibration model setting.

Cause: The calibration model setting ($sgsyscfg.$cal_model) is not supported. The following settings are supported: 3: Single linear segment pressure and speed model 12: Multiple linear segment pressure and speed model piece-wise pressure calibration.

Remedy: Change setting to one of the settings above, and reperform calibration if necessary.

### 3.18.13.158 SVGN-164 Invalid pressure/speed convert setting.

Cause: Pressure to speed conversion specification ($sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv) is not supported. The following setting combinations are supported: $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 3 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 0: Single linear segment, JNT%. $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 3 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, Single linear segment, mm/sec converted at spot. $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, Multiple linear segments, mm/sec converted at spot.

Remedy: Change setting to one of the settings above, and re-perform calibration if necessary. Note: $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv==3 is the default setting for this variable.

### 3.18.13.159 SVGN-165 Gun opened < equalizer trigger distance.

Cause: The open distance condition for equalization pressure trigger, was not met before the start of motion to pressure position, for the next spot. The equalization trigger state for the next spot might have been delayed, in this case.

Remedy: Increase the end and/or start distance value on the distance schedule screen, or decrease the open distance for the equalization pressure trigger AFTER the SPOT.

<!-- PDF page 1705 -->

### 3.18.13.160 SVGN-166 Invalid equalizer trigger type.

Cause: The specified equalization pressure trigger type is not supported.

Remedy: Select a valid trigger on the Spot equipment SETUP screen.

### 3.18.13.161 SVGN-167 Invalid equalizer trigger event.

Cause: The specified equalization pressure trigger event is undefined.

Remedy: Go to the spot equipment setup screen, and select a valid trigger event.

### 3.18.13.162 SVGN-168 Push depth %s[mm] exceeds strokelimit

Cause: The pushing depth specified in the pressure schedule or the minimum pushing depth, exceed the strokelimit. The contact speed might be slightly lower than specified as a result of this alarm.

Remedy: Update one or more of the parameters used to specify pushing depth: $sgsch#[].$push_depth and $sggun.$setup.$push_margin. If these parameters cannot be reduced, then increase the strokelimit, if possible. Note that this is only a warning.

### 3.18.13.163 SVGN-169 PushDepth%s[mm]clampd, speed affected

Cause: The minimum push depth (internally calculated distance) required to decelerate from the contact speed exceeds the maximum possible pushing depth: part thickness + close stroke limit. The value of the minimum pushing depth (specified in the alarm message) was clamped to the maximum possible pushing depth.

Remedy: Decrease $sggun#.$setup.$push_margin, or increase the close stroke limit. Although this alarm has a warn severity, this condition should be corrected since the minimum push depth has been clamped to a value that is small enough to affect contact speed and/or contact speed persistence. Note 1: SVGN-169, basically indicates that the close limit value is abnormal, since minimum push depth is typically less than 5mm. Note 2: part thickness is automatically added to the pushing depth value during tryout mode to compensate for the missing part.

### 3.18.13.164 SVGN-170 Incompatible PRESS_MOTN format.

Cause: The instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] cannot be used with the setting $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB=FALSE. GunB must use GunA data, for this instruction.

Remedy: If you want to use the instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] then set $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB=TRUE. If you do not want to use the instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] then change the instruction to PRESS_MOTN[SD=(,),P=(,)] (

<!-- PDF page 1706 -->

the setting of $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB is ignored for the format PRESS_MOTN[SD=(,),P=(,)] ).

### 3.18.13.165 SVGN-171 Requested torque > max gun torque.

Cause: The Pressure[]kgf or Pressure level Gun instruction was executed, and the requested torque > max gun torque (OTP torque limit mode).

Remedy: Perform autotuning or disable overtorque protection.

### 3.18.13.166 SVGN-172 Can not move gun during interrupt

Cause: A SPOT[] or PRESS_MOTN[] instruction was performed during an interrupt routine (Ex. TB,TA,DB,program monitor etc).

Remedy: Adjust the trigger timing of interrupt routine. Also, wait until the interrupt routine completes then run the servo gun instruction

### 3.18.13.167 SVGN-173 Timeout G%d A%d %x %d

Cause: A timeout occurred during power-up Gun-attach sequence. Possible causes are: 1. A servo problem interrupted the servo startup sequence, and caused the attach sequence to fail. For example, fuse FS1 on servo amp is blown. 2. The servo gun is NOT connected correctly. For example pulsecoder cable is disconnected.

Remedy: Check alarm log for servo errors and and correct the issue if one is found. For example: SRVO-058 FSSB %d init error (%d) If no servo problem is found, then check cable connections for servogun. Also, check motor and gun change board. If this problem persists contact your FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.13.168 SVGN-174 SPCALL error fcod:%x, stat:%x

Cause: The Servo Gun softpart could not be notified of the event. Refer to the function code(fcod) and status(stat).

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

### 3.18.13.169 SVGN-175 Position not recorded

Cause: GunTouchup(F3) or AutoTouchup(F4) was requested but touchup did not occur. This alarm (SVGN-175) only indicates that touchup failure has occurred, SVGN-176 identifies cause of SVGN-175. Note: SVGN-175 is not posted during program touchup.

<!-- PDF page 1707 -->

Remedy: See SVGN-176. NOTE: SVGN-175 is an optional alarm (enabled by default). Set $SGSYSTCH.$PTNOTRECALM = FALSE to disable SVGN-275.

### 3.18.13.170 SVGN-176 %s

Cause: Refer to message in string.

Remedy: Refer to remedy for message in string.

### 3.18.13.171 SVGN-177 Thk%smm,CloseLim%smm,StdLim%smm

Cause: This is information at pressure shortage.

Remedy: Incorrect thickness or/and gun close limit would cause a pressure shortage If thickness or/and gun close limit is incorrect, gun tip can not go correct push depth for setpoint pressure The Thk is value which is specified in pressure schedule. Check if thickness value in pressure schedule is correct for actual thickness. This CloseLim is present gun close limit,and the StdLim is gun close limit of no-wear down. If CloseLim is too shorter than StdLim, replace gun tip then perform wear down update program. If StdLim is already too short, set the correct standard limit in servo gun setup screen.

### 3.18.13.172 SVGN-178 Open/CloseLim=%s

Cause: This is information of standard stroke limit.

Remedy: Gun storke limit is compensated by tip wear down. The standard value is stroke limit when TW_SETUP or WR_SETUP is performed an original value. This shorter standard storke limit may cause pressure shortage. If the standard storke limit is shorter than original value,set correct standard limit in servo gun setup screen.

### 3.18.13.173 SVGN-179 More than two groups

Cause: The program attempted the servogun command with more than 2 groups.

Remedy: The servogun option supports a maximum of 2 groups due to complex synchronization. Use a program with less than 3 groups in the group mask, or remove servogun command (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) from the program.

### 3.18.13.174 SVGN-180 Pressure persist is canceled

Cause: Persisted pressure after HOLD is canceled

<!-- PDF page 1708 -->

Remedy: Pressure could not be persisted during BWD or ABORT So Persisted pressure is canceled This is warning massage for blowing out. Please check panel status if you are welding.

### 3.18.13.175 SVGN-181 Nominal thickness:%s MinAllowable:%s

Cause: The Measured part thickness is less than the under-thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. NOTE: This message displays the nominal (expected/programmed) thickness and the under-thickness (MinAllowable) limit.

Remedy: See SVGN-040.

### 3.18.13.176 SVGN-182 Nominal thickness:%s MaxAllowable:%s

Cause: The Measured part thickness is greater than the over-thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. NOTE: This message displays the nominal (expected/programmed) thickness and the over-thickness (MaxAllowable) limit.

Remedy: See SVGN-040.

### 3.18.13.177 SVGN-183 %s/%s/%s/%s

Cause: Gun touchup function has modified position of spot point. This message is provided for informational purposes only, it is not a fault/problem. Note: SVGN-183 is not posted during program touchup.

Remedy: The 4 parameters in SVGN-183 p1/p2/p3/ p4 provide details about the modified point. p3: Corrected value is the difference between new recorded position and old recorded position. Note: robot close direction is positive polarity, so if new position is shifted in robot open direction (relative to old position) corrected value will be negative. p4: Thickness value is actual thickness measured during thickness check. Note: If thickness check is disabled, nominal thickness (value in pressure schedule) is reported.

### 3.18.13.178 SVGN-184 Point touchup cancelled.

Cause: Spot point touchup was cancelled, because shift key was released and program edit screen was de-selected (new screen was selected).

Remedy: Execute point touchup again, and don't exit editor screen.

### 3.18.13.179 SVGN-185 Gun monitor buffer overflow

Cause: Data collected during search process exceeded storage buffer. Note: SVGN-185 only occurs during unpress (a process that is no longer used), so it is basically obsolete.

<!-- PDF page 1709 -->

Remedy: Reduce unpress time by increasing speed ($SGGUN#.$TEACH.$LWDT_CLOSPD) or decreasing observation time ($SGGUN#.$TEACH.$LWDT_OBSLEN).

### 3.18.13.180 SVGN-186 Wdn,Old:%smm->New:%smm

Cause: This indicates information for tip increased error. The left value indicates the last wear down. The right value indicates current measured wear down. Since the current measured wear down is incorrect, so increased alarm is posted. Difference of the right value from the left value becomes increased error amount.

Remedy: Please see remedy for SVGN-32 and/or SVGN-33. Note: If current measured wear down is nearly 0, update program might be performed without new tip flag.

### 3.18.13.181 SVGN-187 Do gun zero mastering with new tip

Cause: Tip wear setup was performed, without performing gun zero mastering first. This condition can lead to incorrect mastering for tip wear reference position and cause gun stroke limit to become incorrect.

Remedy: Perform gun zero mastering in gun zero mastering screen with new tip.

### 3.18.13.182 SVGN-188 Restart info incomplete:%d/%d/%d

Cause: An internal error has occurred. Execution restart information is incomplete.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.18.13.183 SVGN-189 Tipwear overstroke protection is off

Cause: Tipwear had been setup, but a BZAL alarm occurred and tipwear zero reference (pls0) is not up to date. Pls0 must be updated after BZAL to maintain proper stroke limit (Overstroke protection is turned of after BZAL to avoid invalid strokelimit values).

Remedy: Go to gun master screen and execute recalibrate or master. Either action updates pls0, and turns overstroke protection on.

### 3.18.13.184 SVGN-190 Backup pos clamped for search:%smm

Cause: Open (search start) distance for upper panel detection exceeded gun stroke limit, so open distance was clamped to gun open limit. Note: Gun open distance for upper panel search depends on touchup type: if point touchup: open distance = initial pos + search prep dist if prog touchup: open distance = thk.nom+thk.err.max+pos.err.max+searchprep dist SVGN-190 does not cause any

<!-- PDF page 1710 -->

problem if panel contact occurs AFTER search start. However, if panel contact occurs BEFORE search start, excessive push and/or touchup failure may result. Note: backup pos = org pos + search_backup_dist + rbt_bkup_dist. Search backup distance is distance required in order to detect panel at org_pos. Search backup distance + robot backup distance is distance required to detect panel at org_pos AFTER robot moves fixed tip away from panel. I.E. robot backup distance does not affect guntip to panel distance and is considered optional. Therefore, in case where gun open distance is sufficient to accomodate panel detection after moving fixed tip from panel (by robot backup distance), SVGN-386 (and not SVGN-190) is posted. However, if open limit is too small to even accomodate backup distance for search then both SVGN-386 and SVGN-190 are posted.

Remedy: If point touchup is being performed, close gun (jog) to reduce open distance. If program touchup is being performed, reduce one or more of the following parameters: upper panel detect distance, max thickness error, max pos error.

### 3.18.13.185 SVGN-191 Thickness Check Calib Updated.

Cause: Thickness Check Calibration was successful - parameters were updated. Note: This alarm is merely status information, it is not a fault/problem.

Remedy: None.

### 3.18.13.186 SVGN-192 Thickness Check Calib Not Updated.

Cause: Thickness Check Calibration parameter is not updated Thickness Check Calibration could not finished correctly Note: If thickness Check Calibration had done before, the last parameter is restored.

Remedy: Please see cause code or other relative alarm on alarm screen Remove cause that makes pausing stopping sequence Then retry Thickness Check Calib sequence to updated parameter.

### 3.18.13.187 SVGN-193 Automastered:%.1fmm from old masterpos.

Cause: Automaster operation was successful, and mm distance between old and new master position is provided for reference.

Remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

### 3.18.13.188 SVGN-194 Automaster failed.

Cause: Automaster operation failed. Refer to cause code for reason.

Remedy: Formulate remedy based on cause code.

<!-- PDF page 1711 -->

### 3.18.13.189 SVGN-195 Masterct(old:%d,new:%d).

Cause: Automaster operation was successful, and master count values - old and new - are provided for reference.

Remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

### 3.18.13.190 SVGN-196 TW recalibrated:%.1fmm from old pulse0.

Cause: Auto wear calibrate operation was successful, and mm distance between old and new pulse0 value is provided for reference.

Remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

### 3.18.13.191 SVGN-197 TW recalibrate failed.

Cause:Auto wear calibrate operation failed. Refer to cause code for reason.

Remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

### 3.18.13.192 SVGN-198 Pulse0ct(old:%d,new:%d).

Cause: Auto wear calibrate operation was successful, and master count values - old and new - are provided for reference.

Remedy: Refer to cause code for specific information.

### 3.18.13.193 SVGN-199 Automaster message.

Cause: Status information about automaster operation is being posted.

Remedy: Refer to cause code for specific information.

### 3.18.13.194 SVGN-200 FCTRL must be off for automaster.

Cause: Automaster was requested while gun was still in force control. Automaster cannot start until fctrl is cleared.

Remedy: Press fault reset and execute automaster again. (SVGN-200 alarm automatically resets force control).

<!-- PDF page 1712 -->

### 3.18.13.195 SVGN-201 Gun index 1

Cause: The posted error occurred on GunA (gun index 1) of the dual gun.

Remedy: Correct the error on the gun number corresponding to GunA (gun index 1).

### 3.18.13.196 SVGN-202 Gun index 2

Cause: The posted error occurred on GunB (gun index 2) of the dual gun.

Remedy: Correct the error on the gun number corresponding to GunB (gun index 2).

### 3.18.13.197 SVGN-203 GunA, GunB contact speed is different

Cause: The contact speed used in this Pressure Schedule is different for Gun A and Gun B - but contact speed must match to achieve synchronized contact with the part.

Remedy: Set the contact speed of the Pressure Schedule to the same value for both guns. This is done by adjusting the pressure calibration data which determines the contact speed. The Speed at a given Pressure must be the same for both guns. It is recommended to use matching Pressure and Speed values for each calibration point for both guns. Then, find the unique torque% required to achieve the pressure for each gun. OR, just set the contact speed for all points in the Pressure Calibration table for both guns to the same value.

### 3.18.13.198 SVGN-204 GunA, GunB pushing depth is different

Cause: Pushing depth is different for GunA and GunB. Equal pushing depth is required, for synchronized move to pressure position.

Remedy: Set $sgsch/[].$pushing depth, and $sggun#.$setup.$push_margin to same value, for both guns.

### 3.18.13.199 SVGN-205 GunA, GunB creep distance is different

Cause: The creep distances are different for GunA and GunB. Equal creep distance is required to achieve synchronized contact with the part.

Remedy: Set the system variable $sggun#.$setup.$creep_dst to the same value, for both guns on this dual-gun (# represents the gun number).

<!-- PDF page 1713 -->

### 3.18.13.200 SVGN-206 GunA, GunB part thickness is different

Cause: The Part Thickness used in this Pressure Schedule is different for GunA and GunB. Equal thickness is required to achieve synchronized contact with the part.

Remedy: Set the part thickness to same value, for both guns.

### 3.18.13.201 SVGN-208 GunA, GunB linear distance is different

Cause: Linear distance values are different.

Remedy: Specify the same linear distance value for GunA and GunB.

### 3.18.13.202 SVGN-209 GunA, GunB joint velocity limits differ.

Cause: Joint velocity limits are different for gunA and gunB. Joint velocity limit must be equal to achieve synchronized contact with the part.

Remedy: Use the Gun Setup Utility to set the Maximum Speed (i.e. joint velocity limit) of both Gun A and B to the same value. - Go to UTILITIES - GUN SETUP - Press the F6 key, DG_CHECK - Press the F4 key, SETSPD and reply YES to the prompt to set the speed to same value - Cycle Power to activate the change

### 3.18.13.203 SVGN-210 GunA, GunB accel times differ

Cause: Acceleration Times are different for gunA and gunB. The acceleration times must be equal to achieve synchronized contact with the part.

Remedy: Use the Gun Setup Utility to set the Acceleration Times of both Gun A and B to the same value. - Go to UTILITIES - GUN SETUP - Press the F6 key, DG_CHECK - Press the F5 key, SETACC and reply YES to the prompt to set the accel time to same value - Cycle Power to activate the change

### 3.18.13.204 SVGN-211 Incomp weight calc in ATUN

Cause: Weight calculation in the autotuning is not completed. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Complete weight calculation of the autotuning screen.

<!-- PDF page 1714 -->

### 3.18.13.205 SVGN-212 Incomp weight calc for X gun

Cause: Weight calculation for X gun is not completed. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Complete weight calculation by executing WT_MEAS.TP.

### 3.18.13.206 SVGN-213 Can't detect pressure posture

Cause: Can't detect pressurizing posture.

Remedy: The setting of the tool coordinate system is wrong. It is necessary to set the tool coordinate system to the servo gun tips of fixed side. Moreover, +Z tool coordinate axial direction should be the same as the gun open direction.

### 3.18.13.207 SVGN-214 Servo gun type is not set

Cause: Servo gun type is not set. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Confirm the weight compensation gun type of the Servo Gun General Setup screen.

### 3.18.13.208 SVGN-215 Incomp manual wt comp setup

Cause: Incomplete manual weight compensation setup was performed. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General Setup screen, select Manual weight compen. Complete compensation formula.

### 3.18.13.209 SVGN-216 Illegal wt compens val: Gun%d,P%d

Cause: The weight compensation value is too large. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Confirm the contents of the setup of the weight compensation function.

### 3.18.13.210 SVGN-217 Do press calib over again

Cause: There is mistake in the setting of weight compensation function at pressure calibration.

Remedy: Confirm the weight compensation gun type of the Servo Gun General Setup screen
Confirm the setting of tool coordinate system Execute pressure calibration again.

<!-- PDF page 1715 -->

### 3.18.13.211 SVGN-218 This press can't be compensated

Cause: Because this command pressure was lower than the value of WT compensation press low lim of Servo Gun General Setup screen, this command pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Confirm the value of WT compn press low lim of the Servo Gun General Setup screen.

### 3.18.13.212 SVGN-219 Angle is wrong

Cause: A set value of the angle is wrong.

Remedy: The interval between angle and angle at pressure calibration should be away by 70 degrees or more. Confirm the set value of the angle.

### 3.18.13.213 SVGN-220 Set value is wrong

Cause: A set value is wrong. The calculated weight has become negative.

Remedy: The interval between angle and angle at pressure calibration should be away by 70 degrees or more. Confirm the set value of the angle. The pressure or the command pressure might be wrong. Confirm the set values of the pressure and the command pressure.

### 3.18.13.214 SVGN-221 Incomp semi-auto wt comp setup

Cause: Incomplete semi-auto weight compensation setup has occurred. Therefore, the pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General Setup screen, and select the Semi-auto weight compensation. Complete semi-auto weight compensation setup.

### 3.18.13.215 SVGN-222 UT correct ang is out of range

Cause: The UT correct angle is out of range. Therefore, the position of the gun was not able to be calculated.

Remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General Setup screen. Set up the WT compen UT correct angle between 0 and 360.

### 3.18.13.216 SVGN-223 Max disturbance excess G%d

Cause: Max disturbance torque exceeds the tolerance.

Remedy: Check the pressure calibration.

<!-- PDF page 1716 -->

### 3.18.13.217 SVGN-224 Average disturbance excess G%d

Cause: Average disturbance torque exceeds the tolerance.

Remedy: Check the pressure calibration.

### 3.18.13.218 SVGN-225 Min disturbance excess G%d

Cause: Min disturbance torque exceeds the tolerance.

Remedy: Check the pressure calibration

### 3.18.13.219 SVGN-226 Servogun Diagnosis is failed.

Cause: Servogun diagnosis is failed.

Remedy: Remedy internal error.

### 3.18.13.220 SVGN-230 Manual weight setup err: Gun%d,P%d

Cause: A mistake is found in the setting of the manual weight compensation. Therefore, pressure was not able to be compensated.

Remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General Setup screen, select Manual weight compen. Confirm the setting of the manual weight compensation function.

### 3.18.13.221 SVGN-231 Can't detect pressure posture

Cause: Pressurizing posture cannot be detected.

Remedy: The setting of the tool coordinate system is wrong. It is necessary to set the tool coordinate system to the servo gun tips of fixed side. Moreover, +Z tool coordinate axial direction should be the same as the gun open direction.

### 3.18.13.222 SVGN-232 This gun cannot use AUTO

Cause: This gun cannot use the auto weight compensation type.

Remedy: Set the gun to another weight compensation type.

<!-- PDF page 1717 -->

### 3.18.13.223 SVGN-233 This gun cannot use AUTO

Cause: This gun cannot use the auto weight compensation type.

Remedy: Set the gun to another weight compensation type.

### 3.18.13.224 SVGN-234 Recorded touchup log.

Cause: This message is posted if user presses F2(rec) fkey when prompt "Is tip on panel" is presented. SVGN-234 is merely a status message, it is not a problem.

Remedy: Set $SGSYSTCH.$LOG_FLAG=FALSE and/or $SGSYSTCH.$MAN_LOG_ENB=FALSE, if you do not wish to record touchup log.

### 3.18.13.225 SVGN-235 Already recorded touchup log

Cause: User notification that touchup log already exists. This message is posted if F2(rec) fkey is pressed more than once, when tip on panel prompt is presented.

Remedy: Press F2(rec) fkey only once.

### 3.18.13.226 SVGN-236 [PauseMod]Det/Thk/Pos Err :Eq%d

Cause: Program execution paused because position and/or thickness is out of tolerance. This pause occurs when DET/THK/POS error pause severity is set to warn or alarm, and one more of the following conditions exist: upper panel mis-detect: SVGN-240, thickness out of tolerance: SVGN-239, position out of tolerance: SVGN-237.

Remedy: Set Det/Thk/Pos error pause Sev in the gun teach setup screen to DISABLE if you do not want robot to pause when the alarms above occur.

### 3.18.13.227 SVGN-237 Program pos NOT intol:(Eq:%d,Ln:%d)

Cause: Measured position error is greater than maximum allowable position error or less than min allowable position error.

Remedy: Increase maximum allowable position error or decrease min allowable position error, on gun teach setup screen. If problem persists, take the following actions: 1. Confirm the position error offset in the spot program touchup setup screen. This alarm might be generated immediately after the position error offset is changed. 2. Confirm the parameter to correct position for Xgun in the spot program touchup setup screen. This alarm might be generated immediately after the parameter to correct position for Xgun is changed. 3. Confirm the master position for the gun axis and make sure the tips touch at the zero. Position error correction might not be correctly calculated when the master position for the gun axis is not correct. 4. Confirm the tip wear amount

<!-- PDF page 1718 -->

is correct. Re-execute the tip wear measurement when the tip wear amount is not correct. 5. Re-execute the thickness check calibration.

### 3.18.13.228 SVGN-238 [PauseMod]SpotProgTouchDsb:Eq%d

Cause: Program execution paused because TCHDSB is attached to spot instruction, and SpotprogTouch_DSB pause severity = warn or alarm.

Remedy: If you do not want the robot to pause, either: a. set SpotProgTouch_Dsb pause Sev in the gun teach setup screen to DISABLE OR b. remove TCH_DSB from spot instruction.

### 3.18.13.229 SVGN-239 Thickness chk2 NOT intol:(Eq:%d,Ln:%d

Cause: Measured thickness is out of tolerance. Note: SVGN-242 Act thick:x.x, Nom thick: y.y is posted as cause code for SVGN-239.

Remedy: Confirm that: 1. actual panel thickness is correct. 2. nominal thickness in the pressure schedule is correct. 3. OverThickness and UnderThickness tolerance values on gun teach setup screen are appropriate

### 3.18.13.230 SVGN-240 Up panel Not intol:(Eq:%d,Ln:%d)

Cause: Upper panel detection distance is larger (gun more open) than max detect distance. where: max detect distance = pos.err.max + thk.nom + thk.err.max This alarm occurs only during program touchup (not point touchup). Note: SVGN-243 ActDetDist:x.x, MaxDetDist: y.y is posted as cause code for SVGN-240.

Remedy: Confirm that: 1. no obstruction exists between guntip and panel. 2. actual panel thickness is correct 3. nominal thickness in pressure schedule is correct. 4. OverThickness tolerance (on gun teach setup screen) is large enough. 5. Max allowable Pos error (on gun teach setup screen) is large enough.

### 3.18.13.231 SVGN-241 PosDiff%smm>MaxPosDiff:%smm

Cause: Position error exceeds Max allowable pos error. SVGN-241 supplies the actual position error and maximum allowable position error for alarm SVGN-237.

Remedy: See SVGN-237.

### 3.18.13.232 SVGN-242 Measured thick:%smm Nom thick:%smm

Cause: Thickness error exceeds OverThickness tolerance or UnderThickness tolerance. SVGN-242 supplies the actual thickness and nominal thickness for SVGN-239.

<!-- PDF page 1719 -->

Remedy: See SVGN-239.

### 3.18.13.233 SVGN-243 ActDetDis:%smm MaxDetDis:%smm

Cause: Detect distance (observed) exceeds Max Detect distance. SVGN-243 supplies the actual detection distance and max detect distance for SVGN-240.

Remedy: See SVGN-240.

### 3.18.13.234 SVGN-244 Retry Thickness Check calibration

Cause: Thickness check calibration (0kgf) is incomplete. Thickness check calibration is required for touchup.

Remedy: Execute thickness check calibration on gun setup util.

### 3.18.13.235 SVGN-245 Gun not open to undeflect pos

Cause: Position register (PR) that stores undeflect (relax) position for gun/robot could not be set. Note that undeflect pos is starting point for thickness check, it removes deflection at lower panel detect end. Note that Refer to cause code for specific reason.

Remedy: Correct problem identified in cause code, and retry touchup.

### 3.18.13.236 SVGN-246 Machinelock required for PNLSIM.

Cause: Panel simulation is enabled, but machinelock is disabled on robot group or gun group. Machinelock must be ENABLED on both robot group and gun group, when panel simulation is enabled.

Remedy: Disable panel simulation($SGSYSTCH.$SIM_PNL_ENB=FALSE) or ENABLE machinelock on robot group and gun group.

### 3.18.13.237 SVGN-247 Concurrent multiarm touchup unsupported.

Cause: Touchup is already in progress on an arm and touchup is being requested on another arm (at the same time). Touchup can only be performed on one arm at a time.

Remedy: Wait for touchup operation that is already in progress to complete, before starting touchup on another arm.

<!-- PDF page 1720 -->

### 3.18.13.238 SVGN-248 Panel not detected.

Cause: Upper or lower panel search ended, but panel was not detected. I.E. gun speed never fell below speed threshold, during search. The following conditions can cause this problem: 1. missing panel 2. large gun friction 3. large pressure margin

Remedy: 1. ensure that panel is present. 2. increase $sggun#.$teach.$pnldflctdst. 3. decrease pressure margin. If problem persists, contact a FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.18.13.239 SVGN-249 Panel Detection was failed

Cause: Panel was not detected during second part of upper panel search. Internal condition for search termination was not met. This can occur if panel is soft.

Remedy: Retry touchup.

### 3.18.13.240 SVGN-250 Spot program touchup enabled !

Cause: A tp program started (or resumed) and spot program touchup function is enabled with execution mode = TOUCHUP. Touchup mode means that points will be evaluated AND positions will be modified.

Remedy: If verify (not touchup) mode is desired, change execution mode via Touchup setup screen: a. if tp is disabled, set Execution mode for AUTO = VERIFY mode, b. if tp is enabled, set Execution mode for TEACH = VERIFY mode, If normal spot (not touchup or verify) operation is desired, disable program touchup via: a. DIN, if tp is enabled. b. Touchup mode setup screen, if tp is disabled.

### 3.18.13.241 SVGN-251 PosDiff:%smm<MinPosDiff:%smm

Cause: Position error (change between observed position and recorded position) is less than MinPosError. This message is posted to display magnitude of observed position error and minimum pos error, when SVGN-237 occurs. Note that min pos error is used in conjunction with max pos error to control when points are touched up. Points are only touched up if position error is greater than or equal to min pos error and less than or equal to max pos error. Min pos error tolerance identifies when position change is small and/or insignificant.

Remedy: If position error is acceptable, decrease min pos error and execute touchup again. Set min pos error = 0.0, to disable min pos error check completely.

<!-- PDF page 1721 -->

### 3.18.13.242 SVGN-252 Panel Detection was failed.(%d)

Cause: Upper panel detection failed. The integer parameter ()identifies the failure type: type1: gun tip did not contact panel during search motion (internal condition to terminate search was not met). type2: exact position of detection could not be found (no distinct transition in the data)

Remedy: Confirm that: 1. no obstruction exists between guntip and panel. 2. actual panel thickness is correct 3. nominal thickness in pressure schedule is correct. 4. Over thickness tolerance (on gun teach setup screen) is large enough. 5. Max allowable pos error (on gun teach setup screen) is large enough.

### 3.18.13.243 SVGN-254 Thickness chk1 NOT intol:(Eq:%d,Ln:%d)

Cause: Measured thickness was too large at lower panel detection.

Remedy: Confirm that: 1. no obstruction exists between panel and either tip, 2. actual panel thickness is correct, 3. nominal thickness in pressure schedule is correct.

### 3.18.13.244 SVGN-255 Search motion is unsuccess.

Cause: Detection data for the second upper panel search is invalid.

Remedy: Retry spot program touchup. Confirm that gun tip contacts panel at upper panel detection. If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire the diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.13.245 SVGN-256 Invalid parameter in SPTCH_XXX

Cause: Register specified for SPTCH_OFS or SPTCH_RSD is invalid. Note: SPTCH_OFS is attached to spot instruction to specify offset/adjustment value that is added to final offset for point modification. SPTCH_RSD is attached to spot instruction to specify offset distance for robot tip.

Remedy: Set a valid parameter for the instruction: 1. SPTCH_OFS: Greater than -2.0mm and less than 2.0mm 2. SPTCH_RSD: greater than or equal to 0.0mm and less than or equal to 20.0mm

### 3.18.13.246 SVGN-257 Invalid register number.

Cause: Register specified for SPTCH_OFS or SPTCH_RSD is invalid.

Remedy: Specify a valid register number in SPTCH_OFS or SPTCH_RSD instruction: min: 1 max: posreg max (position registers item, on program limits setup screen)

<!-- PDF page 1722 -->

### 3.18.13.247 SVGN-258 Spot prog touchup retry:(Num:%d)

Cause: Initial touchup attempt failed, but retries are enabled, and touchup will be attempted again.

Remedy: This message is provided for information purposes only.

Note Set the maximum retry number = 0 on the gun teach setup screen to disable retries.

### 3.18.13.248 SVGN-259 Retry number > Max retry number

Cause: Initial touchup attempt and retries failed.

Remedy: Examine log and determine reason for failure.

### 3.18.13.249 SVGN-260 Search motion is unsuccess.

Cause: Upper panel detection failed. Robot motion stopped before gun tip touched panel. Data for the detection is invalid.

Remedy: Retry search motion.

### 3.18.13.250 SVGN-261 Disturbance of gun is abnormal.

Cause: Gun torque command is erratic. This gun may have mechanical issues.

Remedy: Examine the servo gun. Confirm that there is no actuator damage or binding. If gun is ok, retry touchup function.

### 3.18.13.251 SVGN-262 Disturbance of gun is abnormal.

Cause: Gun torque command is erratic. This gun may have mechanical issues.

Remedy: Examine the servo gun. Confirm that there is no actuator damage or binding. If gun is ok, retry touchup function.

### 3.18.13.252 SVGN-263 Variation in disturbance is too much.

Cause: Gun torque command is erratic. This gun may have mechanical issues.

Remedy: Examine the servo gun. Confirm that there is no actuator damage or binding. If gun is ok, retry touchup function.

<!-- PDF page 1723 -->

### 3.18.13.253 SVGN-264 Variation in disturbance is too much.

Cause: Gun torque command is erratic. This gun may have mechanical issues.

Remedy: Examine the servo gun. Confirm that there is no actuator damage or binding. If gun is ok, retry touchup function.

### 3.18.13.254 SVGN-265 Mech Comp Calib. succeeded

Cause: Mechanical calibration for point/program touchup function completed successfully.

Remedy: This is a status message for informational purposes.

### 3.18.13.255 SVGN-266 Comp Dist: %s mm (%s)

Cause: This message shows the compensation value for point/program touchup function. Value in () means Num of Successful calibration / Specified Num of calibrations.

Remedy: Remedy: This is a status message for informational purposes.

### 3.18.13.256 SVGN-267 Mech Comp Calib. failed

Cause: Mechanical calibration for point/program touchup function failed.

Remedy: Refer to SVGN-268 for cause.

### 3.18.13.257 SVGN-268 %s

Cause: This message identifies cause of gun mechanical compensation (calibration) failure. It is posted, along with SVGN-267. input data is invalid - parameter specified in SGKTCHCL() is invalid. The remedy depends on the parameter (p1-p5) that is identified: Invalid gun number. Specify Gun number between 1 and $SGSYSCFG.$GUN_NUM Invalid thickness: Specify thickness value greater than or equal to 1.0 Invalid Gun Open Distance: Specified gun tip open distance is not invalid. Invalid Robot Open Distance: Specified robot tip open distance is not invalid. Invalid Num of Calib: Calibration iterations (number) is invalid. Minimum=1 Check system status:Calibration cannot proceed due to system error or illegal condition. - Any alarm occur, and/or HOLD is turn on - Enable single step and/or machine lock - Disable gun stroke (mode) - Spot program touchup disabled ALL Calib. NOT SUCCESS: Calibration failed due to one of the following: - Alarm or HOLD occurs during calibration. - Misdetect error - Thickness out of tolerance - Position out of tolerance

Remedy: Invalid gun number. Correct gun number between 1 and $SGSYSCFG.$GUN_NUM Invalid thickness: Correct thickness value greater than or equal to 1.0 Invalid Gun Open Distance: Correct gun tip open distance. Invalid Robot Open Distance: Correct robot tip open distance.

<!-- PDF page 1724 -->

Invalid Num of Calib: Correct calibration iterations (number) Check system status: Calibration cannot proceed due to system error or illegal condition. - Rest nny alarm occur, and/or HOLD. - Disable single step and/or machine lock - Enable gun stroke (mode) - Enable Spot program touchup ALL Calib. NOT SUCCESS: Calibration failed due to one of the following: - Reset alarm or HOLD. - Identify cause of misdetect error - Correct thickness for fixture - Correct position for fixture

### 3.18.13.258 SVGN-269 Spot program touchup disabled

Cause: This indicates spot program touchup is disabled.

Remedy: Enable spot program touchup via TEST CYCLE or CELL INTERFACE I/O

### 3.18.13.259 SVGN-270 Too large torque limit.(Upper)

Cause: Gun tip contacted upper panel surface before search motion started. Torque limit became unexpectedly-large during upper panel detection step1.

Remedy: Confirm that distance of gun panel contact is not larger than search start distance. Retry spot program touchup. If gun tip contacts upper panel surface before search start distance, increase start distance(SD) for gun tip. If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.13.260 SVGN-271 Too large torque limit.(Lower)

Cause: Robot tip contacted lower panel surface before search motion started. Torque limit became unexpectedly-large during lower panel detection.

Remedy: Confirm that distance of panel contact is not larger than search start distance. Retry spot program touchup. If robot tip contacts lower panel surface before search start distance, increase start distance(SD) for robot tip and/or lower panel detection distance. Refer to Chapter "20.6 LOWER PANEL DETECTION DISTANCE CLAMP" or "20.13 SPTCH_RSD INSTRUCTION" for more information about the lower panel detection distance If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.13.261 SVGN-272 Lower Det start pos was wrong.

Cause: Open distance of a gun axis was too short at start position of lower panel detection.

Remedy: Confirm that robot tip has enough clearance from panel surface at start position. If distance between robot tip and panel is too short, increase start distance(SD) for robot tip

<!-- PDF page 1725 -->

an/or lower panel detection distance. Refer to Chapter "20.6 LOWER PANEL DETECTION DISTANCE CLAMP" or "20.13 SPTCH_RSD INSTRUCTION" for more information about the lower panel detection distance. Retry spot program touchup. If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire the diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative.

### 3.18.13.262 SVGN-273 Det was irregular stop.R:%d P:%d

Cause: A gun tip was contacted an upper panel surface on a free running section before search motion.

Remedy: R:1 means that error occurred during upper panel detection. Confirm that gun tip has enough clearance from upper panel surface at start position. If distance between the tip and the panel is too short, increase start distance(SD) for gun tip. R:3 means that error occurred during lower panel detection. Confirm that robot tip has enough clearance from panel surface at start position and that there is no obstacle between the panel and the robot tip at start position. If distance between the tip and the panel is too short, increase start distance(SD) for robot tip and/or lower panel detection distance. Refer to Chapter "20.6 LOWER PANEL DETECTION DISTANCE CLAMP" or "20.13 SPTCH_RSD INSTRUCTION" in OPERATOR'S MANUAL of Servo Gun Function for more information about the lower panel detection distance. Retry spot program touchup. If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative. Note: This alarm is posted when the time to execute phases2,3 take longer than anticipated, during upper1 detection and lower detection. R: Request number. R:1 is upper1 detection. R:3 is lower detection. P: Phase number. P:2 is phase of acceleration. P3: is phase to collect data to calculate threshold. If the tip touch panel during above phase, this alarm is posted. Please check whether the tip touch panel or the gun is closed(or grabbed panel) at position of search start.

### 3.18.13.263 SVGN-274 Speed threshold is too low

Cause: Threshold to detect panel contact became unexpectedly-low.

Remedy: If gun tip contacted panel surface at start position, increase start distance(SD) for gun tip. If robot tip contacted lower panel surface at start position, increase start distance(SD) for robot tip and/or lower panel detection distance. Refer to Chapter "20.6 LOWER PANEL DETECTION DISTANCE CLAMP" or "20.13 SPTCH_RSD INSTRUCTION" for more information about the lower panel detection distance. Retry spot program touchup. If this problem persists after taking the above actions, perform the following actions: 1. Acquire the diagnostic data. See the procedure for diagnostic data collection at Troubleshooting section. 2. Contact a FANUC technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1726 -->

### 3.18.13.264 SVGN-275 Search starts@:%smm (%s desired).

Cause: Search start distance was clamped due to gun open limit. SVGN-275 is posted as cause code for SVGN-190. Actual search start distance is displayed, along with desired (unclamped) search start distance.

Remedy: See SVGN-190.

### 3.18.13.265 SVGN-276 Search mode was not selected.

Cause: Search mode was not selected. Therefore, position detection was not done.

Remedy: Set $SGSYSTCH.$ACCUDET_ENB = TRUE, and then restart.

### 3.18.13.266 SVGN-277 OpenLim too small:%.1fmm required.

Cause: Gun open deistance required for normalization search is larger than open limit. Normalization process aborts because of this condition.

Remedy: Initiate normalization process with smaller gun open distance or increase gun open limit (if possible).

### 3.18.13.267 SVGN-278 Averaging speed is enabled.

Cause: Axis speed will be varied during search motion. So counter-measure is turned ENABLE automatically.

Remedy: If the gun has no abnormality, there is no remedy.

### 3.18.13.268 SVGN-279 Averaging speed is used.

Cause: Axis speed will be varied during search motion. So counter-measure is used automatically.

Remedy: If the gun has no abnormality, there is no remedy. Turn Use averaging speed OFF/ON manually if you want to disable this message.

### 3.18.13.269 SVGN-280 Excessive Wear down Comp (Gun).

Cause: Wear down amount of gun side is exceeded to max compensation tolerance. Cap tip may be worn out and/or shank may be shorter than original length. Gun axis will run over away mechanical stroke limit and gun tip would interfere object/panel if gun tip clearance is small.

Remedy: Change tip to new tip. If shank is shorter than original length, change to new shank

<!-- PDF page 1727 -->

### 3.18.13.270 SVGN-281 Excessive Wear down Comp (Rbt).

Cause: Wear down amount of robot side is exceeded to max compensation tolerance. Cap tip may be worn out and/or shank may be shorter than original length. Gun axis will run over away mechanical stroke limit. And gun tip and robot would interfere object/panel if tip clearance is small.

Remedy: Change tip to new tip. If shank is shorter than original length, change to new shank.

### 3.18.13.271 SVGN-282 Wear ratio updated:%s->%s

Cause: Wear ratio was updated. Displayed value means old wear ratio -> new wear ratio.

Remedy: This is just information. There is no remedy.

### 3.18.13.272 SVGN-283 Wear ratio(%s) Not updated

Cause: Wear ratio was updated. (However wear down was updated ) System can not calcarate when tips are not WORN.DOWN( = cap tip is increased ). There are some causes - Cap has been replaced. But new tip flag is OFF - Cap wear has been hardly changing. Wear ratio could not be updated in too short cycle See SVGN-284 to confirm wear down changing.

Remedy: Turn on new tip when tip is replaced in next time. Also Perform 2step after tip dressing several times

### 3.18.13.273 SVGN-284 Gun:%s,Rbt:%s

Cause: This indicates wear down changing: The last 2step wear down -> Current 2step wear down If The last 2step wear down is larger than current 2step wear down, tip would be replaced If cap wear has been hardly changing, 2 step is performed with too short cycle

Remedy: Turn on new tip when tip is replaced in next time. Also Perform 2step after tip dressing several times.

### 3.18.13.274 SVGN-285 Wear ratio Out of Tolerance

Cause: This indicates calculated wear down is exceeded user's tolerance - Cap has been replaced. But new tip flag is OFF - Cap wear has been hardly changing. Wear ratio could not be updated in too short cycle

Remedy: Turn on new tip when tip is replaced in next time. Also Perform 2 step after tip dressing several times. User's tolerance can be changed in TWD setup screen

<!-- PDF page 1728 -->

### 3.18.13.275 SVGN-286 Wear ratio:%s > Max:%s

Cause: This indicates calcurated wear down and user's tolerance(Max)

Remedy: See SVGN-286

### 3.18.13.276 SVGN-287 Wear ratio:%s < Min:%s

Cause: This indicates calcurated wear down and user's tolerance(Max)

Remedy: See SVGN-286

### 3.18.13.277 SVGN-288 New tip !! Use 2step TWD

Cause: 1step performed with new tip flag. Do not perform 1step with new tip falg when auto update wear ratio is enable.

Remedy: Perform 2step with new tip falg agin.

### 3.18.13.278 SVGN-289 Update Wear ratio

Cause: Wear ratio has not been updated for long time.

Remedy: Please update wear ratio.

### 3.18.13.279 SVGN-290 Do press calib over again:G%d

Cause: There is mistake in the setting at pressure calibration

Remedy: Execute pressure calibration again

### 3.18.13.281 SVGN-292 Invalid AI,GI conversion factor:G%d

Cause: Invalid AI,GI conversion factor setting is not correct.

<!-- PDF page 1729 -->

Remedy: Confirm the AI,GI conversion factor setting.

### 3.18.13.282 SVGN-293 Temp info from motor isn't obtained:G%d

Cause: Temperature information cannot be obtained from this pulse corder.

### 3.18.13.283 SVGN-294 Temp exceed abnormal up lim:G%d

Cause: Temperature exceeded abnormal motor temperature upper limit value.

Remedy: Confirm the temperature sensor is not out of order.

### 3.18.13.284 SVGN-295 Temp below abnormal low lim:G%d

Cause: Temperature fell below abnormal motor temperature lower limit value.

Remedy: Confirm the temperature sensor is not out of order.

### 3.18.13.285 SVGN-296 Invalid temperature coefficient:G%d

Cause: Temperature coefficient setting is not correct.

Remedy: Confirm the temperature coefficient setting.

### 3.18.13.286 SVGN-297 Temp info from AI isn't obtained:G%d

Cause: Temperature information cannot be obtained from AI

Remedy: Confirm the AI setting.

### 3.18.13.287 SVGN-298 Temp info from GI isn't obtained:G%d

Cause: Temperature information cannot be obtained from GI

### 3.18.13.288 SVGN-299 Invalid thickness: t=**

Cause: Instruction for which invalid thickness was specified was executed.

Remedy: Confirm the thickness in the instruction.

### 3.18.13.289 SVGN-300 Early welding OFF at resuming

Cause: Program is paused when gun is closing with early welding. Early welding is disabled for resumed gun closing.

Remedy: This is just warning massage. Early welding is disabled for the only resumed gun closing. In next spot line, early welding is enabled again. And, if program is executed with BWD, early welding is enabled for the SPOT.

### 3.18.13.290 SVGN-301 Early weld calibration INCOMP

Cause: Early weld calibration is incomplete. Early welding can not be enabled.

Remedy: Execute early weld calibration on gun setup utility screen.

### 3.18.13.291 SVGN-302 Welding in pressure shortage

Cause: When pressure did not reach target pressure, weld init would asserted in pressure shortage.

Remedy: Please refer to remedy of SVGN-020 Also, Execute early weld calibration again.

### 3.18.13.292 SVGN-303 Gun%d: Disabled early welding

Cause: in pressure of dual gun, either gun disable early welding. Weld init will assert when pressure of gun that disables early welding reaches target pressure.

Remedy: Enable/Disable early welding for both gun.

### 3.18.13.293 SVGN-304 Invalid early welding time

Cause: Invalid early welding time was specified. Early welding time is too large

Remedy: Correct early welding time. Early welding time can not larger than torque up time of gun

<!-- PDF page 1731 -->

### 3.18.13.294 SVGN-305 OVR < 100%,Early Welding Disabled

Cause: General override is not 100%. Early welding time can work correctly with OVR 100%

Remedy: Set override 100%.

### 3.18.13.295 SVGN-306 Thickness Check Calib Retrying...

Cause: Thickness check calibration is retrying.

Remedy: This is just a message. It's no remedy.

### 3.18.13.296 SVGN-314 Thickness%d not read, deflect cal incomp

Cause: Thickness could not be read because deflection calibration is incomplete. Number after thickness refers to type of thickness that could not be read 1=before weld, 2=after weld.

Remedy: Perform deflection calibration or disable thickness read ($RDTHK_ENB=TRUE).

### 3.18.13.297 SVGN-315 Torque value not in deflect cal table.

Cause: Torque value for current pressure is not in deflection calibration table - deflection value is obtained via interpolation. Accuracy of deflection estimate may improve if deflection is performed again.

Remedy: 1. Go to pressure calibration screen and add present pressure to pressure calibration table (if it is not there already). 2. Set pressure calibration to complete. 3. perform deflection calibration. OR disable this alarm(SVGN-315), by setting $SGCFG[].$DFLINTRPALM=0

### 3.18.13.298 SVGN-320 Thickness1 error requires reset.

Cause: Thickness error has occurred and operator attention is required.

Remedy: Refer to cause and remedy of thickness error. Note that this alarm is posted AFTER gun has opened. Actual thickness error is posted BEFORE gun open, when thickness error is detected.

### 3.18.13.299 SVGN-321 Thickness after weld NOT ok (%.1f).

Cause: Expected change in thickness (decrease) was NOT observed.

Remedy: Execute SPOT[] again, if possible.

<!-- PDF page 1732 -->

### 3.18.13.300 SVGN-322 Decrease=%.1f (Min decrs=%.1f)mm

Cause: Observed thickness decrease and minimum thickness decrease are presented.

Remedy: None. This alarm is for informational purposes only.

### 3.18.13.301 SVGN-323 Decrease=%.1f (Max decrs=%.1f)mm

Cause: Observed thickness decrease and maximum thickness decrease are presented.

Remedy: None. This alarm is for informational purposes only.

### 3.18.13.302 SVGN-324 Thickness after weld ok (%.1f).

Cause: Thickness measured (#.#) after weld was within tolerance.

Remedy: None. This alarm is for informational purposes only.

### 3.18.13.303 SVGN-325 Decrease=%.1fmm.

Cause: Thickness change from before weld to after weld (#.#) is provided. Note: Thickness decrease is displayed as a positive value.

Remedy: None. This alarm is for informational purposes only.

### 3.18.13.304 SVGN-326 Thickness2 error requires reset.

Cause: Thickness error has occurred and operator attention is required.

Remedy: Refer to cause and remedy of thickness error. Note that this alarm is posted AFTER gun has opened. Actual thickness error is posted BEFORE gun open, when thickness error is detected.

### 3.18.13.305 SVGN-327 Thickness:%.1fmm in tolerance

Cause: Measured thickness is within tolerance (ok). This warning is posted for information purposes only.

Remedy: Disable thickness ok message to suppress this warning.

<!-- PDF page 1733 -->

### 3.18.13.306 SVGN-328 Thickness1 undertol.

Cause: Measured thickness before weld was smaller than nominal thickness + under thickness limit. Note that this alarm is posted as cause code for SVGN-193. SVGN-193 and SVGN-270 are posted after gun opens to SD.

Remedy: 1. Confirm that panel is ok, and that robot is at correct location on panel. 2. Confirm that nominal thickness is correct. 3. Confirm that underthickness limit is large enough to accomodate normal panel variation and measurement error.

### 3.18.13.307 SVGN-329 Thickness1 overtol.

Cause: Measured thickness before weld was larger than nominal thickness + over thickness limit. Note that this alarm is posted as cause code for SVGN-193. SVGN-193 and SVGN-271 are posted after gun opens to SD.

Remedy: 1. Confirm that panel is ok, and that robot is at correct location on panel. 2. Confirm that nominal thickness is correct. 3. Confirm that overthickness limit is large enough to accomodate normal panel variation and measurement error.

### 3.18.13.308 SVGN-330 Setdown undertol.

Cause: Difference between thickness measured before and after weld was smaller than Setdown tolerance min(mm). I.E. thickness decrease was smaller than expected. Note that this alarm is posted as cause code for SVGN-199. SVGN-199 and SVGN-272 are posted after gun opens to SD.

Remedy: 1. Confirm that weld settings are ok. 2. Confirm that Setdown tolerance min(mm) is not too large.

### 3.18.13.309 SVGN-331 Setdown overtol.

Cause: Difference between thickness measured before and after weld was larger larger than Setdown tolerance max(mm). I.E. thickness decrease was larger than expected. Note that this alarm is posted as cause code for SVGN-199. SVGN-199 and SVGN-273 are posted after gun opens to SD.

Remedy: 1. Confirm that weld settings are ok. 2. Confirm that Setdown tolerance max(mm) is not too small.

Cause: This alarm is posted if [sgprscfg]sho_thr_inf = TRUE. The alarm provides torque command (fcmd_trq) and close threshold(p183) values.

The alarm provides feedback on gun disturbance torque, for following events: a. force control command status($fctrl) changes from false to TRUE b. thickness (distance) is reached c. force control enable status ($fcenb) changes from false to TRUE

Remedy: None. This alarm is posted to provide feedback on gun control parameters, during close stroke. Set [sgprscfg]sho_pos_inf = FALSE, to disable this alarm.

### 3.18.13.313 SVGN-336 ClsThrshLo(obs:%d,cur:%d,std:%d)

Cause: This alarm is posted if $sggun#.$setup.tc_okmsg=TRUE (thickness check ok). The alarm provides feedback on thickness setpoint for this spot, along with thickness check tolerances.

Remedy: None. This alarm is posted to provide feedback on gun control parameters, during close stroke. Set $sggun#.$setup.tc_okmsg=FALSE, to disable this alarm.

### 3.18.13.315 SVGN-338 Specify thickness in instruction

Cause: Macro THK_KVAL is obsolete.
