Remedy: None. &new_line *$369 +SYER_WARN, SY_LDTR_FCDST ?syst_help369 $- +a, syst_help369 &new_line

### 3.19 T

### 3.19.1 TANG Alarm Code

### 3.19.1.1 TANG-001 Reference position not found

Cause: Reference position can not be found.

Remedy: Record the reference position with TA_REF motion modifier.

### 3.19.1.2 TANG-002 Invalid reference position

Cause: Reference position is not valid.

Remedy: Re-teach the reference position with TA_REF motion modifier.

<!-- PDF page 1819 -->

### 3.19.1.3 TANG-003 PR number not found

Cause: PR number can not be found.

Remedy: Specify the PR number in TA_REF PR[] motion modifier.

### 3.19.1.4 TANG-004 Invalid PR number(%d)

Cause: Position Register number is not valid.

Remedy: Enter a valid Position Register number in TA_REF PR[] motion modifier.

### 3.19.1.5 TANG-005 Uninitialized PR number(%d)

Cause: Position Register is uninitialized.

Remedy: Enter an initialized Position Register.

### 3.19.1.6 TANG-006 Not a robot arm gmask(%d)

Cause: Trying to use TA_REF in a TP program that does not include a robot arm motion group.

Remedy: Use TA_REF in a TP program that includes at least one robot arm motion group.

### 3.19.1.7 TANG-007 Reference axis recorded

Cause: A reference axis for the work angle calculation has been recorded.

Remedy: This is a warning message.

### 3.19.1.8 TANG-008 Uninitialized TA_REF ref frm

Cause: TA_REF reference frame is uninitialized.

Remedy: Move cursor to TA_REF, align the torch with the reference axis, then shift F3 to record reference frame.

### 3.19.1.9 TANG-009 Illegal interpolated point

Cause: Illegal robot interpolated point data is detected.

<!-- PDF page 1820 -->

Remedy: Internal error, please call FANUC Robotics customer service.

### 3.19.1.10 TANG-010 Unit vector formation error

Cause: Unit vector formation error.

Remedy: Internal error, please call FANUC Robotics customer service.

### 3.19.1.11 TANG-011 Group number mismatch

Cause: MOVE_TO TP jog group does not match recorded reference position group.

Remedy: Change TP jog group to match recorded reference position group.

### 3.19.1.12 TANG-012 Exceed max TA_REF robot grps

Cause: TP instruction TA_REF is used in a TP program that has more than 2 robot groups.

Remedy: Use TA_REF PR[] in a TP program that has more than 2 robot groups.

### 3.19.1.13 TANG-013 TA_REF PR[] for COORD motion

Cause: TP instruction TA_REF is used in a coordinated motion.

Remedy: Use TA_REF PR[] in the coordinated motion. TA_REF records position of follower robot only, whereas TA_REF PR[] records positions of both leader and follower groups.

### 3.19.1.14 TANG-014 Travel angle limit

Cause: Jogging was stopped as the torch travel angle began to exceed the travel angle tolerance.

Remedy: This is a warning. Jogging can be continued.

### 3.19.1.15 TANG-015 Work angle limit

Cause: Jogging was stopped as the torch work angle began to exceed the work angle tolerance.

Remedy: This is a warning. Jogging can be continued.

<!-- PDF page 1821 -->

### 3.19.1.16 TANG-016 Large travel angle chg %d dg

Cause: The difference between current travel angle and desired travel angle has exceeded the configured system variable $tor_ang_cfg.$max_tvl_dif.

Remedy: Limit the travel angle difference, or increase the system variable $tor_ang_cfg.$max_tvl_dif.

### 3.19.1.17 TANG-017 Large work angle chg %d dg

Cause: The difference between current work angle and desired work angle has exceeded the configured system variable $tor_ang_cfg.$max_wrk_dif.

Remedy: Limit the work angle difference, or increase the system variable $tor_ang_cfg.$max_wrk_dif.

### 3.19.1.18 TANG-018 Cannot update while moving

Cause: The torch angles cannot be updated while the robot is moving.

Remedy: Wait for the robot motion to stop before using the update function.

### 3.19.1.19 TANG-019 Press SHIFT with the MOVE_TO key

Cause: The MOVE_TO function key was pressed without holding the SHIFT key.

Remedy: Press and hold the SHIFT key with the MOVE_TO key to move the robot torch to the target work and travel angles.

### 3.19.1.20 TANG-020 E%d WP%d S%d Wrk=%3.1f Trv=%3.1f

Cause: The UPDATE function key was pressed.

Remedy: The current torch work and travel angles were copied to the reported weld procedure weld schedule.

### 3.19.1.21 TANG-021 Ref Pos for COORD motion

Cause: The current reference position is not feasible for a coordinated motion.

Remedy: Add a TP instruction TA_REF PR[] to the current coordinated motion. TA_REF PR[] records positions of both the leader and the follower groups.

<!-- PDF page 1822 -->

### 3.19.1.22 TANG-022 Ref Pos for non-COORD motion

Cause: The current reference position is not feasible for a non-coordinated motion.

Remedy: Add a TP instruction TA_REF to the current non-coordinated motion. TA_REF records position of non-coordinated robot only.

### 3.19.1.23 TANG-023 (G:%d) Ref Frame not ready

Cause: Torch Angle reference frame for the specified motion group is not ready.

Remedy: Execute a motion instruction in a TP program associated with the specified motion group to initialize Torch Angle reference frame.

### 3.19.1.24 TANG-024 P[%d] Illegal position type

Cause: Illegal robot position type is detected.

Remedy: Use touchup to teach a new position.

### 3.19.1.25 TANG-025 Invalid pre-plan data, line %d

Cause: Invalid pre-plan robot position is detected.

Remedy: This is a warning message. No action is required. Current position will be used.

### 3.19.2 TAST Alarm Code

### 3.19.2.1 TAST-000 unknown error (TAST00)

Cause: Internal system error

Remedy: Cold start controller

### 3.19.2.2 TAST-001 TAST global vars failure

Cause: The Through Arc Seam Tracking (TAST) variables are not loaded

Remedy: Perform a controlled start to initialize motion softparts

<!-- PDF page 1823 -->

### 3.19.2.3 TAST-002 TAST error IO allocation

Cause: An IO memory allocation error has occurred

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.19.2.4 TAST-003 TAST IO initialization failed

Cause: An analog port number error has occurred

Remedy: Check a connection of process IO board

### 3.19.2.5 TAST-004 TAST IO start failed

Cause: IOSETRTN error has occurred

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.19.2.6 TAST-005 TAST time tick missing

Cause: Time tick missing in TAST IO memory

Remedy: Change the value of weaving frequency to be lower or the value of comp timing on TAST data screen to be longer

### 3.19.2.7 TAST-006 TAST memory dispose failure

Cause: An IO memory disposition error has occurred

Remedy: Perform a cold start of controller

### 3.19.2.8 TAST-007 TAST RPM saving failure

Cause: RPM data saving error has occurred

Remedy: Check RPM softparts was loaded correctly If same position IDs are used at same RPM record section, change position IDs to different one

### 3.19.2.9 TAST-008 TAST incorrect schedule num

Cause: An invalid TAST schedule number was specified

<!-- PDF page 1824 -->

**Remedy:** Change the schedule number to be in range (1 - 20)

# **3.19.2.10 TAST-009 TAST weave freq is too low**

**Cause:** An invalid weaving frequency was specified for TAST

**Remedy:** Change the frequency value to be higher

# **3.19.2.11 TAST-010 TAST software error (SRIF)**

**Cause:** Internal system error (SRIF)

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start of controller

# **3.19.2.12 TAST-011 TAST software error (PMPT)**

**Cause:** Internal system error (PMPT)

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start of controller

# **3.19.2.13 TAST-012 TAST software error (INTP)**

**Cause:** Internal system error (INTP)

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start of controller

# **3.19.2.14 TAST-013 TAST software error**

**Cause:** Internal system error

**Remedy:** Perform a cold start of controller

# **3.19.2.15 TAST-014 TAST weave freq is too high**

**Cause:** Weaving frequency is too high for TAST

**Remedy:** Change the value of weaving frequency to be lower

<!-- PDF page 1825 -->

### 3.19.2.16 TAST-015 Force Beyond High Limit

Cause: Measured force is beyond its limit

Remedy: check the system or change the up limit

### 3.19.2.17 TAST-016 Force Below Low Limit

Cause: Measured force is below its low limit

Remedy: check the system or change the low limit

### 3.19.2.18 TAST-017 Sensor is not calibrated

Cause: Sensor is not calibrated

Remedy: Calibrate the sensor

### 3.19.2.19 TAST-018 Exceed lateral tracking limit

Cause: Exceed TAST/AVC lateral tracking limit

Remedy: Re-teach the welding path, or adjust L_tracking limit in TAST/AVC Schedule setup screen

### 3.19.2.20 TAST-019 Exceed vertical tracking limit

Cause: Exceed TAST/AVC vertical tracking limit

Remedy: Re-teach the welding path, or adjust V_tracking

### 3.19.3 TCPP Alarm Code

### 3.19.3.1 TCPP-000 Unknown (TC00)

Cause: System internal error.

Remedy: Notify FANUC America Corporation.

<!-- PDF page 1826 -->

### 3.19.3.2 TCPP-001 No global variables

Cause: TCP Speed Prediction global variables are not loaded.

Remedy: Perform a controlled start and initialize motion softparts.

### 3.19.3.3 TCPP-002 No mmr pointer

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.4 TCPP-003 No mir pointer

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.5 TCPP-004 No sysvar pointer

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.6 TCPP-005 No tcppir pointer

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a controlled start and initialize the motion softparts.

### 3.19.3.7 TCPP-006 Error allocating memory

Cause: A failure occured while allocating memory.

Remedy: Check amount of memory being used by system.

### 3.19.3.8 TCPP-007 Error making TCPP mailbox

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

<!-- PDF page 1827 -->

### 3.19.3.9 TCPP-008 Error making TCPP spmktsk

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.10 TCPP-009 Pnts too close before line:%d^5

Cause: The program positions prior to this line are too close together to allow proper speed prediction to be performed. It is also most likely that the robot can not perform at the programmed speed either.

Remedy: The positions being executed prior to the one specified should be moved further apart, or the programmed speed should be decreased.

### 3.19.3.11 TCPP-010 Error writing PLAN mailbox

Cause: This is an internal system error.

Remedy: Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.12 TCPP-011 Pred time skips first motion

Cause: The first motion segment time (time between first two taught points) is shorter than the prediction equipment delay time as specified by $TCPPIR.$TCDELAY.

Remedy: Extend time of first motion segment (increase distance or decrease speed) to allow TCP Speed Prediction to begin during the first motion segment.

### 3.19.3.13 TCPP-012 Invalid TCPP filter type

Cause: The motion was commanded using an invalid motion filter type.

Remedy: Check program setup to ensure proper program header data, motion types, and position data.

### 3.19.3.14 TCPP-013 Invalid TCPP start pos

Cause: The start position is not valid.

Remedy: Check the values for the current and previous positions.

<!-- PDF page 1828 -->

### 3.19.3.15 TCPP-014 Invalid TCPP destination pos

Cause: The destination position is not valid.

Remedy: Check the values for the current and previous positions.

### 3.19.3.16 TCPP-015 Invalid time into segment

Cause: The time computed for the current segment exceeds the segment length.

Remedy: Check the value for the current position data.

### 3.19.3.17 TCPP-016 No cfseg data

Cause: The Cartesian Filter data is not valid.

Remedy: Check to make sure that the Cartesian Filter option has been properly loaded and initialized.

### 3.19.3.18 TCPP-017 Modone computation error

Cause: The internal Motion Done computation generated an error.

Remedy: No action is necessary, but the TCP Speed value will not be valid for several motions.

### 3.19.3.19 TCPP-018 Begin Error Mode at line:%d^5

Cause: The program positions beginning with this line have caused an error condition which makes further speed prediction invalid. The speed prediction task has therefore entered an error handling mode within which it discontinues speed prediction but provides the actual robot speed as an output reference with an affective equipment delay time of 0. (That is, with $TCPPIR.$TCDELAY = 0.)

Remedy: Check the error log to find speed limit errors which may be causing this TCPP error to occur. Check the program beginning with this line to determine if the robot can not function as programmed. Modify the program to avoid all such speed limit errors. In cases which list speed limit errors for the wrist axes, the error can often be eliminated by changing the motion command from using mm/sec speed commands to using deg/sec speed commands which better control motion with large wrist orientation changes.

<!-- PDF page 1829 -->

### 3.19.3.20 TCPP-019 Speed Ovrd Mode at line:%d^5

Cause: A speed override occured beginning with this line causing an error condition which makes further speed prediction invalid. The speed prediction task has therefore entered an error handling mode within which it discontinues speed prediction but provides the actual robot speed as an output reference.

Remedy: Normal prediction will resume automatically once the speed override has propagated through the system. No further action is required. The user should avoid this during production program execution and should be aware that it may invalidate live application testing since neither the robot nor the speed prediction task are performing as programmed.

### 3.19.3.21 TCPP-020 TCPP internal cartseg error

Cause: Internal error when searching cart segment.

Remedy: No action is necessary, but the TCP Speed value will not be valid.

### 3.19.3.22 TCPP-021 Allocate TCPP/VC memory error

Cause: Internal error when allocating memory to TCPP AccuPath segment.

Remedy: Check amount of memory being used by system. Perform a cold start on the controller.

### 3.19.3.23 TCPP-022 Invalid delay time specified

Cause: Internal error specified delay time for TCP extention is too big

Remedy: System problem. Need to fix the problem by modifying code.

### 3.19.3.24 TCPP-070 Speed output failed (T_S[%d])

Cause: A failure occured while writing I/O or a register.

Remedy: Check the program to determine whether both target type and index are valid.

### 3.19.3.25 TCPP-071 Min.speed >= Max.speed (T_S[%d])

Cause: The minimum speed is not less than maximum speed.

Remedy: Correct the speed values.

<!-- PDF page 1830 -->

### 3.19.3.26 TCPP-072 Invalid index (T_S[%d])

Cause: The specified index of TCP_SPD[] is invalid.

Remedy: Correct the index.

### 3.19.3.27 TCPP-073 Unknown target type

Cause: The specified target type is invalid.

Remedy: Correct the target type.

### 3.19.4 TG Alarm Code

### 3.19.4.1 TG-000 unknown error (TG00)

Cause: Internal system error

Remedy: Cold start controller

### 3.19.4.2 TG-001 Error allocating data

Cause: Not enough memory

Remedy: Check memroy configuration to see if it meets the requirement

### 3.19.4.3 TG-002 Illegal I/O Port

Cause: Illegal IO Port

Remedy: Reassign IO port

### 3.19.4.4 TG-003 Illegal I/O Port Type

Cause: Illegal IO Port Type

Remedy: Reassign IO port type

<!-- PDF page 1831 -->

### 3.19.4.5 TG-004 Bad Command Value

Cause: Motion trigger has been told to set a I/O port to a value which that port cannot be set to.

Remedy: A digital port must always be set to 1 or 0. You must set the corresponding command_value to a 1 or 0

### 3.19.4.6 TG-005 Bad Alternate Value

Cause: Motion trigger has been told to set a I/O port to a value which that port cannot be set to.

Remedy: A digital port must always be set to 1 or 0. You must set the corresponding command_value to a 1 or 0

### 3.19.4.7 TG-006 Bad Time Before

Cause: Illegal Time Before

Remedy: Time before must be greater than -0.1 seconds

### 3.19.4.8 TG-007 Bad Schedule Number

Cause: schedule number out of range

Remedy: Reassign to a valid schedule

### 3.19.4.9 TG-008 Could not trigger I/O

Cause: An I/O port was not triggered when it was supposed to. This is usually caused by too many I/O events being set up to fire within too short a time frame.

Remedy: You must adjust your path so that it does not try to fire so many I/O events within a such a short time. Start by moving the last few motions before this error occured further apart and/or slowing them down.

### 3.19.4.10 TG-009 Adjust Trig Sch:%d^2 Ev:%d^3 L:%d^5

Cause: This is a warning to indicate that the trigger time for the specified TG event was miscalculated, so the event was fired immediately. No user action is required.

Remedy: None.

<!-- PDF page 1832 -->

### 3.19.4.11 TG-010 Pts Too Close %s^4 L:%d^5 Sch:%d^2 Ev:%d^3

Cause: This is a warning indicating that two taught points containing triggering events were too close to each other, such that the second point trigger time had to be adjust to prevent firing before the first point trigger.

Remedy: Modify the position of the node (line number and program number) indicated so that it is further away from the preceding position in the program.

### 3.19.4.12 TG-011 Cannot Allocate Memory

Cause: An internal error occurred while attempting to allocate memory.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, including an All File Backup from the time of the error if possible, and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

### 3.19.4.13 TG-012 Bad Num ISDT in Sch %d^2 Ev%d^3

Cause: A trigger schedule (system variable $TGSCHED[num], where “num” is the schedule indicated in the alarm text) has an event defined with an invalid process axis number.

Remedy: Generally this alarm occurs when a process axis related option is loaded, but the process axes have not been properly setup. Go to controlled start and run the process axis setup from the MAINTENANCE menu.

### 3.19.4.14 TG-013 Invalid IO Port in Sch%d^2 Ev%d^3

Cause: In the trigger schedule number $TGSCHED[num] indicated by the alarm text, the indicated event number has an invalid port type specified.

Remedy: Change $TGSCHED[Sch].$PORT_TYPE[Ev] to a valid port type. Note that Robot Digital Input and Group Input are not allowed. If you have not modified these variables since loading, then obtain a file backup and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

### 3.19.4.15 TG-014 Gun Queue is Full

Cause: The number of outstanding trigger events exceeds the maximum. This indicates either an excessive number of very short segments in a TP program with trigger instructions, or an internal error.

Remedy: Examine the TP programs running at the time of the error for a very large number of motion lines that have instructions with trigger events and that are very close together or the same point. If this condition is not found, obtain as much information as possible about the

<!-- PDF page 1833 -->

events leading up to the error as well as a file backup and easy debug (if available) and contact FANUC America Corporation Technical Support.

### 3.19.4.16 TG-015 Trigger Overrun

Cause: This alarm is not used.

Remedy: If this alarm appears, obtain a controller backup (image at least) and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

### 3.19.4.17 TG-016 Bad Time Before in Sch%d^2 Ev%d^3

Cause: The indicate trigger schedule event in $TGSCHED[Sch] has an invalid value for time before.

Remedy: The time before (or anticipator) value cannot be less than (i.e. more negative than) -100 msec. Check all anticipator values defined in the application to be sure none indicate a time after (i.e. negative time before) greater in magnitude than 100 msec.

### 3.19.4.18 TG-017 Invalid Schedule Number %d^2

Cause: An internal error occurred during processing of a TP instruction.

Remedy: Obtain a controller backup and easy debug (if available) and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

### 3.19.4.19 TG-018 Trigger Buffer is Full

Cause: There are too many outstanding trigger events that have not yet been fired. This indicates either an excessive number of short motion segments with trigger instructions, or else an internal error.

Remedy: Examine the TP programs executing at the time of the error to confirm that there are not a large number of short or zero length motion segments back-to-back with application instructions. If this condition does not exist, then obtain a controller backup (and easy debug if available) from the time of the error and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

### 3.19.4.20 TG-019 Internal Timing Data Error

Cause: This alarm is currently not used.

Remedy: If this alarm appears, obtain an image backup and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

<!-- PDF page 1834 -->

### 3.19.4.21 TG-020 Error planning app instruction

Cause: This indicates an error occurred in the planning of an application TP instruction and is always accompanied by another TG-XXX alarm.

Remedy: Examine the alarm log for the other TG-XXX alarm that was posted at the same time and proceed according to the cause/remedy for that alarm.

### 3.19.5 THSR Alarm Code

### 3.19.5.1 THSR-001 Illegal instruction sequence

Cause: Trying to execute a touch sensing instruction out of sequence. For example, a Search Start instruction follows a Offset start instruction without Offset end in between.

Remedy: Please check the touch sensing instruction sequence, or abort the current program and start again.

### 3.19.5.2 THSR-002 Illegal schedule number

Cause: The input schedule number is beyond the allowable range.

Remedy: Choose a schedule number from 1 to 32.

### 3.19.5.3 THSR-003 Illegal work frame number

Cause: The input work frame number is beyond the allowable range

Remedy: Choose a work frame number from 1 to 32.

### 3.19.5.4 THSR-004 Illegal output PR number

Cause: The input position register number is beyond the allowable range.

Remedy: Choose an appropriate position register number.

### 3.19.5.5 THSR-005 Illegal search PR number

Cause: The specified position register for search result is beyond the allowable range.

Remedy: Choose an appropriate position register number.

<!-- PDF page 1835 -->

### 3.19.5.6 THSR-006 Search without search start

Cause: Search instruction without search start.

Remedy: Add search start instruction.

### 3.19.5.7 THSR-007 Invalid touch I/O assignment

Cause: The touch I/O assignment is incorrect.

Remedy: Please check touch I/O setup screen under the setup menu.

### 3.19.5.8 THSR-008 Arc enable detected

Cause: The arc weld circuitry is enable.

Remedy: Please disable arc welding circuitry before enabling touch sensing.

### 3.19.5.9 THSR-009 Teach pendant not enabled

Cause: The Teach pendant is disable.

Remedy: Enable the teach pendant.

### 3.19.5.10 THSR-010 Illegal motion state

Cause: The motion system is in error state.

Remedy: Hit the reset button to reset the controller.

### 3.19.5.11 THSR-011 Illegal sensor port number

Cause: The specified search port is beyond the allowable range.

Remedy: Change the port type and port number in the touch I/O sub-menu.

### 3.19.5.12 THSR-012 Illegal search pattern

Cause: The specified search pattern is not recognizable.

Remedy: Change the search pattern in the touch sensor schedule.

<!-- PDF page 1836 -->

# **3.19.5.13 THSR-013 Illegal number of search**

**Cause:** Number of searches is not coincident with the search pattern.

**Remedy:** Change the search pattern or add/delete search instructions.

# **3.19.5.14 THSR-014 Illegal search distance**

**Cause:** This is a warning message. The specified search distance is beyond the allowable range. A default speed is used.

**Remedy:** Change the search speed in the touch sensor schedule.

# **3.19.5.15 THSR-015 Illegal search speed**

**Cause:** The specified search speed is beyond the allowable range.

**Remedy:** Change the search speed in the touch sensor schedule.

# **3.19.5.16 THSR-016 Illegal return speed**

**Cause:** The specified return speed is beyond the allowable range. A default speed is used.

**Remedy:** Change the return speed in the touch sensor schedule.

# **3.19.5.17 THSR-017 No contact with part**

**Cause:** The search produces no contact with the part

**Remedy:** Use touchup to teach a new search start position.

# **3.19.5.18 THSR-018 Too many searches**

**Cause:** Too many searches for the specified search pattern.

**Remedy:** Delete unnecessary search instructions

# **3.19.5.19 THSR-019 Mixing search types**

**Cause:** NONE search type can not be mixed with directional search within one search pattern.

<!-- PDF page 1837 -->

Remedy: Delete all searches with NONE type or delete coordinated searches.

### 3.19.5.20 THSR-020 Geometric computing error

Cause: The searches do not generate a satisfactory offset.

Remedy: Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### 3.19.5.21 THSR-021 Points are too close

Cause: The touched positions are too close to each other.

Remedy: Teach new search start positions

### 3.19.5.22 THSR-022 Part is not mastered

Cause: Search instructions have no master data.

Remedy: Mastering the part first

### 3.19.5.23 THSR-023 No search start

Cause: The search instruction does not have a search start.

Remedy: Add search start before search

### 3.19.5.24 THSR-024 No offset start

Cause: The offset end instruction does not have an associated offset start instruction.

Remedy: Add offset start instruction

### 3.19.5.25 THSR-025 Nested search start

Cause: The search start instruction is nested inside another search start instruction.

Remedy: Add a search_end instruction in appropriate place or delete extra search start

<!-- PDF page 1838 -->

### 3.19.5.26 THSR-026 Nested offset start

Cause: The offset start instruction is nested inside another offset start instruction.

Remedy: Add a offset_end instruction in appropriate place or delete extra offset start

### 3.19.5.27 THSR-027 Preplan is not allowed

Cause: No preplan motion inside search start.

Remedy: It is normal to issue an stop error when preplan is on within search start

### 3.19.5.28 THSR-028 Group number mismatch

Cause: The search motion has to be in group 1. motion.

Remedy: Use group 1 to record search motions.

### 3.19.5.29 THSR-029 No contact warning

Cause: The search produces no contact with the part

Remedy: Use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### 3.19.5.30 THSR-030 Contact before search

Cause: Wire makes contact with part before search motion starts

Remedy: Check part and wire, or teach a new search start position.

### 3.19.5.31 THSR-031 Illegal register number

Cause: The input register number is illegal, and it is reset by the software to the maximum available number.

Remedy: Check the input data.

### 3.19.5.32 THSR-032 Position type mismatch

Cause: The position type in the position register should be XYZWPR type. Joint representation is not allowed.

<!-- PDF page 1839 -->

Remedy: Change the position representation to XYZWPR type.

### 3.19.5.33 THSR-033 Not enough points

Cause: Touch sensing system does not have enough points to compute the geometry

Remedy: Record more points

### 3.19.5.34 THSR-034 No bwd on search motion

Cause: Touch sensing does not allow backward execution on search motion

Remedy: Do not Shift-BWD on search

### 3.19.5.35 THSR-035 Error Allocating Data

Cause: Not enough memory

Remedy: Remove unneeded loaded variables and programs

### 3.19.5.36 THSR-036 Coord pair is not available

Cause: Coord motion is not installed or not calibrated

Remedy: Install coord motion and calibrate cd pair

### 3.19.5.37 THSR-037 Illegal motion ref. grp.

Cause: Simple search must have schd_ref_grp = 1

Remedy: Modify reference grp

### 3.19.5.38 THSR-038 Not matches to leader grp.

Cause: Touch frame or schedule reference grp mismatches leader grp

Remedy: Modify reference grp

<!-- PDF page 1840 -->

### 3.19.5.39 THSR-039 Reference grp mismatch

Cause: None simple search requires frame Reference grp equal to schedule reference grp

Remedy: Modify reference grp

### 3.19.5.40 THSR-040 Search Distance Short

Cause: Search distance in touch schedule is too short

Remedy: Increase search distance in touch schedule

### 3.19.5.41 THSR-041 Invalid touch group mask

Cause: An invalid touch sensing group mask in the program detail, or the Search routine was not performed prior to Touch Offset.

Remedy: Check that the Touch Schedule and Robot Group Mask together with Reference Group should be equal to the group mask in the teach pendant program header. Also, the Search routine should be performed directly before the Touch Offset.

### 3.19.5.42 THSR-042 Maint Program not allowed

Cause: Touch Sensing does not support a Maintenance Program.

Remedy: Disable the Maintenance Program in the Error Recovery menu, or use Resume Program in teach pendant program for error recovery. To display the Error Recovery menu:

1. Press MENUS.
2. Select SETUP.
3. Press F1, [TYPE].
4. Select Err recovery.

### 3.19.5.43 THSR-043 Calibration File not found

Cause: The touch sensing analog input calibration file was not found.

Remedy: Create an analog input calibration file called th_calib.dt. The calibration file needs to be stored in frs: via the SMON command

SMON(ppc) > rep th_calib.dt

then turn off and then turn on the controller for the calibration file to take effect.

<!-- PDF page 1841 -->

### 3.19.5.44 THSR-044 Invalid TH Calibration Data

Cause: The analog input calibration file has an invalid data format.

Remedy: Correct the data format in the analog input calibration file, including configuration data and lookup table. Refer to the Analog Input Calibration Data section in the Touch Sensing chapter of the ArcTool Setup and Operations Manual for the correct data format.

### 3.19.5.45 THSR-045 Analog Input Not Calibrated

Cause: Analog input support has not been calibrated.

Remedy: Create an analog input calibration file with the correct data format. Refer to the Laser Analog Input Calibration Data section in the Touch Sensing chapter of the ArcTool Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

### 3.19.5.46 THSR-046 Invalid Analog Input Data

Cause: The analog input data is not valid.

Remedy: Analog input data needs to be within a valid range. The valid range of analog input value is defined by MaxAnalogInput and MinAnalogInput specified in the same calibration file th_calib.dt.

### 3.19.5.47 THSR-047 Can Not Construct A Circle

Cause: The searches do not generate a satisfactory circle.

Remedy: Check the OD/ID search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### 3.19.5.48 THSR-048 Illegal Num of 1D Search Dir

Cause: An illegal number of 1D/1D+R search directions exists.

Remedy: Check the 1D/1D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 1D/1D+R search directions should be exactly 1.

### 3.19.5.49 THSR-049 Illegal Num of 2D Search Dir

Cause: An illegal number of 2D/2D+R search directions exist.

<!-- PDF page 1842 -->

**Remedy:** Check the 2D/2D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 2D/2D+R search directions should be exactly 2.

### **3.19.5.50 THSR-050 Illegal Num of 3D Search Dir**

**Cause:** An illegal number of 3D/3D+R search directions exists.

**Remedy:** Check the 3D/3D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 3D/3D+R search directions should be exactly 3.

### **3.19.5.51 THSR-051 Err Compute Along 1st Srch Dir**

**Cause:** An error occurred computing the offset along the first search direction.

**Remedy:** Check search instructions with the first search direction. The first search direction is specified in the first search instruction in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### **3.19.5.52 THSR-052 Err Compute Along 2nd Srch Dir**

**Cause:** Error computing the offset along the 2nd search direction.

**Remedy:** Check the search instructions with the 2nd search direction. The 2nd search direction is the first new search direction other than the 1st search direction in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### **3.19.5.53 THSR-053 Err Compute Along 3rd Srch Dir**

**Cause:** An error occurred computing the offset along the 3rd search direction.

**Remedy:** Check search instructions with the 3rd search direction. The 3rd search direction is the first new search direction other than the 1st and the 2nd search directions in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

### **3.19.5.54 THSR-054 Err Simple Search Master Flag**

**Cause:** The master flag in the schedule is ON during simple search.

**Remedy:** Set the master flag in the schedule to OFF during simple search.

<!-- PDF page 1843 -->

### 3.19.5.55 THSR-055 Search Speed Outside Limit

Cause: The search speed is outside the default search speed limit configured by the system variable th_default.

Remedy: Set the search speed within the default search speed limit.

### 3.19.6 TJOG Alarm Code

### 3.19.6.1 TJOG-001 Invalid Tracking Jog Mode

Cause: An attempt was made to jog multiple arms at an invalid jog mode.

Remedy: Set $track_mode to the correct value.

### 3.19.6.2 TJOG-002 Multiple Arm Hardware required

Cause: An attempt was made to start the tracking jog feature on a single arm controller.

Remedy: Start the tracking jog feature on a controller with multiple arm hardware.

### 3.19.6.3 TJOG-003 TJOG disabled in $track_jog

Cause: An attempt was made to start the tracking jog feature when TJOG is disabled in $track_jog.$enable.

Remedy: Enable $track_jog.$enable before starting the tracking jog feature.

### 3.19.6.4 TJOG-004 G%d is not a robot arm group

Cause: Trying to start the tracking jog feature on a non-robot motion group.

Remedy: Change to a robot motion group before starting the tracking jog feature.

### 3.19.7 TMAT Alarm Code

### 3.19.7.1 TMAT-000 Offset is out of range

Cause: TorchMate has found that the offset of the torch from the original TCP is beyond the offset limits in the SETUP screen.

<!-- PDF page 1844 -->

**Remedy:** Determine if the Torch needs to be replaced at this time. Replace it if necessary, or increase the offset limits in the TorchMate SETUP screen.

### 3.19.7.2 TMAT-001 Sensor is ON before search

**Cause:** The wire is in contact with the touch plate or is grounded prior to executing the touch move; CAUSE 1: The wire stickout is too long; CAUSE 2: The starting position for the touch move is to close to the touch plate; CAUSE 3: The weld equipment touch circuit or user provided external touch circuit has shorted.

**Remedy:** REMEDY1: Shorten the wire stickout before TorchMate execution by retracting the wire or clipping the wire; REMEDY 2: Increase the value of the Start Search position in the TorchMate SETUP menu; REMEDY 3: Contact the manufacturer for proper use of their touch sense circuit (ie. the welder may require a blocking diode) and inspect any touch circuit hardware for correct installation or for damaged components.

### 3.19.7.3 TMAT-002 Sensor failed during search

**Cause:** Cause1: The TorchMate sensor circuit indicates the wire is in contact with the touch plate before the search move (too much stickout-the search start distance is too small.) Cause 2: An electrical short exists in the touch circuit (for example, some circuits require a blocking diode on the power supply.)

**Remedy:** Remedy1: Decrease the stickout, increase the search start distance, or replace the bent torch. Remedy 2: Contact the supplier of your weld equipment regarding the touch circuit requirements and auxiliary wiring (if needed.)

### 3.19.7.4 TMAT-003 Z offset is not mastered

**Cause:** This error indicates that Z compensation was disabled while mastering and enabled during TorchMate adjustment. TorchMate cannot compensate for Z offset if it is not mastered.

**Remedy:** Disable Z compensation in the TorchMate SETUP screen.

### 3.19.7.5 TMAT-004 Program paused while mastering

**Cause:** Mastering was stopped by releasing the SHIFT key.

**Remedy:** Select the MASTER softkey to execute mastering. Press and hold the SHIFT key until mastering is complete.

<!-- PDF page 1845 -->

### 3.19.7.6 TMAT-005 WO[1] is not available for output

Cause: The TorchMate output signal has been assigned to the Weld Start output.

Remedy: Reassign the TorchMate output signal to the welder's touch sense circuit, or to an external circuit designed to provide the touch input when the wire contacts the touch plate.

### 3.19.7.7 TMAT-006 Override must be 100 %

Cause: The speed override must be 100% during both mastering and TorchMate Adjustment.

Remedy: Set the override to 100%, and execute mastering or TorchMate Adjust again.

### 3.19.7.8 TMAT-007 Dry run is not allowed

Cause: TorchMate does not function if DRY RUN is turned on.

Remedy: Display the Test Cycle menu, and turn DRY RUN off.

### 3.19.7.9 TMAT-008 TorchMate is not mastered

Cause: CAUSE1: TorchMate Adjustment was attempted before mastering. CAUSE 2: TorchMate Ajustment has Z offset enabled, but the mastering was done with Z offset disabled. CAUSE 3: TorchMate Ajustment has Z offset disabled, but the mastering was done with Z offset enabled.

Remedy: Calibrate the TCP correctly before using TorchMate Adjustment.

### 3.19.7.10 TMAT-009 No unassigned MACRO is available

Cause: The automatic setup of macros during installation cannot find an unused Macro number. No macro table entry will be automatically assigned to TM_ADJST, TM_ADJ2, TM_ADJ3.

Remedy: The Macro teach pendant program will be loaded on the controller. Remove an unused Macro from the Macro table, and assign TM_ADJST to that number if you require the TorchMate macro assignment in the Macro table.

### 3.19.7.11 TMAT-010 Cannot run TorchMate in T1 Mode

Cause: An attempt was made to run TorchMate adjust or mastering in T1 mode on a CE or Control reliable controller. This error applies to TorchMate and TorchMateII on R-J, R-J2, and early software releases on R-J3 controllers. This restriction does not apply to software releases on R-J3 and later controllers.

<!-- PDF page 1846 -->

Remedy: On the affected controllers, change the Teach mode to T2 and rerun mastering or TorchMate adjustment.

### 3.19.7.12 TMAT-011 Multiple equipment is not defined

Cause: TorchMate mastering or TorchMate adjustment has been attempted on an undefined equipment.

Remedy: Set up multiple equipment prior to mastering or using TorchMate adjustment on this equipment.

### 3.19.7.13 TMAT-012 System Utool is not defined

Cause: The UTOOL that you are trying to adjust or master is not defined.

Remedy: Set up your UTOOL using the six-point method.

### 3.19.7.14 TMAT-013 %s is corrupt or does not exist

Cause: The UTOOL that you are trying to adjust or master is not defined.

Remedy: On the ATFLASH release media for your robot, locate the the programs PRODUCT\TORCHMAT\TMTMPLT.TP and PRODUCT\TORCHMAT\TMTPSET1.TP. Copy these to the root level of the media. Insert the media into the port on the controller SOP. From the MENU/FILE screen, perform a [DIR] on the memory card (MC:) for *.TP. Load these files selecting to OVERWRITE when prompted.

### 3.19.7.15 TMAT-014 Abort program using G:%s

Cause: During TorchMate mastering, the MOVETO operation in the TorchMate SETUP screen, or TorchMate adjustment was attempted on a motion group currently held by a PAUSED or RUNNING program.

Remedy: Abort the PAUSED or RUNNING program prior to executing any of these functions.

### 3.19.7.16 TMAT-015 G:%s does not support TorchMate

Cause: TorchMate mastering or TorchMate adjustment was used on a motion group that is not associated with the robot(s) in your system. CAUSE 1: At mastering, the group is determined by the currently selected jog motion group as shown in the TP status line. You have selected for jogging a motion group associated to a positioner, nobot, or index device. CAUSE 2: TorchMate adjustment has macros for each robot group installed on your system. The currently executing

<!-- PDF page 1847 -->

program includes a TorchMate macro and does not include that correct robot motion group, or it does not contain a robot motion group at all.

Remedy: REMEDY1: Select for jogging a motion group that is associated with the robot(s) in your system. REMEDY 2: Correct the programming error.

### 3.19.7.17 TMAT-016 Run TorchMate before edit

Cause: This indicates that the TorchMate Touchup Monitor has been turned on (Touchup monitor value is > 0.0 Hrs.), that the program contains a robot motion group(s), and that a TorchMate adjustment has not been done within the allotted time.

Remedy: This is cleared by pressing the ENTER key. It is recommended that you execute TorchMate adjust for the motion group(s) in this program prior to touching up any points.

### 3.19.7.18 TMAT-017 Collision! Run TorchMate

Cause: This indicates that the TorchMate collision monitor has been turned on and that it has detected that a collision detect alarm, a disturbance excess alarm, or a move/stop error excess alarm has occurred.

Remedy: This alarm causes a prompt box to be displayed. Press the ENTER key to clear the prompt box. Inspect the torch for collision damage. Run TorchMate adjust if necessary.

### 3.19.7.19 TMAT-018 DCS tool frame is not allowed

Cause: TorchMate cannot use for DCS tool frame.

Remedy: Do not perform TorchMate for DCS tool frame. If you want to use TorchMate for the current tool number, remove the setup

### 3.19.8 TMSN Alarm Code

### 3.19.8.1 TMSN-000 Invalid GIN Port Number.

Cause: Invalid GIN port number.

Remedy: Check the GIN port or use a valid GIN port number.

### 3.19.8.2 TMSN-001 Internal system error.

Cause: Time Synchronization internal system error.

<!-- PDF page 1848 -->

Remedy: Power off to recover. If problem persists, please reload the controller.

### 3.19.8.3 TMSN-002 Invalid TP parameter.

Cause: Invalid KAREL program parameter

Remedy: Please use an integer or a real in calling END_MTN_TIM KAREL program.

### 3.19.8.4 TMSN-003 Time Sync is not installed.

Cause: The Time Synchronization software is not properly . installed.

Remedy: Re-install the time synchronization software.

### 3.19.8.5 TMSN-004 No RECD_MTN_TIM Call.

Cause: No RECD_MTN_TIM call before calling END_MTN_TIM program.

Remedy: Check TP program logic and add RECD_MTN_TIM call before calling END_MTN_TIM.

### 3.19.8.6 TMSN-005 No motion group in program.

Cause: The TP program does not have motion control.

Remedy: Check TP program group mask use DETAIL function key in select menu.

### 3.19.8.7 TMSN-006 Record aborted when pause.

Cause: Motion Time recording aborted due to program pause/abort

Remedy: Re-run the TP program without pause or abort to record correct motion time.

### 3.19.8.8 TMSN-007 No Time Synchronization.

Cause: Time Synchronization is not enabled for this motion.

Remedy: Check the GIN port number

<!-- PDF page 1849 -->

### 3.19.8.9 TMSN-008 No support for Backward exec

Cause: Time synchronization is disabled for backward program execution.

Remedy: None.

### 3.19.8.10 TMSN-009 No support for short motion.

Cause: Motion is too short. Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.

Remedy: Use SyncTime on long motion or change previous motion termination type to FINE.

### 3.19.8.11 TMSN-010 Please use 100% spd override

Cause: Please use 100% speed override for time recording.

Remedy: Set speed override to 100%

### 3.19.8.12 TMSN-011 Constant Path is required.

Cause: Time synchronization requires Constant Path option.

Remedy: Please enable constant path if Constant Path option is is installed.

### 3.19.8.13 TMSN-012 No support for Circular motn

Cause: Circular Motion Type. Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.

Remedy: Please use JOINT or LINEAR motion type when using the time synchronization.

### 3.19.8.14 TMSN-013 No support for ARC motion

Cause: ARC Motion Type. Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.

Remedy: Please use JOINT or LINEAR motion type when using the time synchronization.

### 3.19.8.15 TMSN-014 No SEC/MSEC speed type

Cause: Time synchronization does support SEC or MSEC speed

Remedy: Please change the speed unit to other type.

<!-- PDF page 1850 -->

### 3.19.9 TOOL Alarm Code

### 3.19.9.1 TOOL-001 Tool Change is DISABLED.

Cause: When tool change was disabled on the servo tool initial setup screen, an attempt was made to execute a tool change instruction (TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH).

Remedy: Perform a Controlled start, open the servo tool initial setup screen, then set the tool change function to ENABLE.

### 3.19.9.2 TOOL-002 Machine lock is ENABLED.

Cause: 1) A machine lock is applied to the robot axis when the TOOL ATTACH instruction or the TOOL DETACH instruction is executed. 2) A machine lock is applied to the servo tool axis when the TOOL DETACH instruction is executed.

Remedy: Release the machine lock applied to the robot axis or the servo tool axis.

### 3.19.9.3 TOOL-003 Illegal assignment of Tool axis.

Cause: The tool number assignments are wrong.

Remedy: Confirm the tool number assignment.

### 3.19.9.4 TOOL-004 Tool not detached (AXISORDER).

Cause: An attempt was made to execute the TOOL ATTACH instruction when a servo tool was not detached. System variable $AXISORDER should have been changed to 0.

Remedy: If any tool is attached, the TOOL ATTACH instruction cannot be executed.

### 3.19.9.5 TOOL-005 Tool not detached.

Cause: An attempt was made to execute the TOOL ATTACH instruction when a servo tool was not detached. The servo tool attach confirmation signal is ON.

Remedy: If any tool is attached, the TOOL ATTACH instruction cannot be executed.

<!-- PDF page 1851 -->

### 3.19.9.6 TOOL-006 Tool not attached.

Cause: While no servo tool was attached, an attempt was made to execute the TOOL DETACH instruction. The servo tool attach confirmation signal is OFF.

Remedy: Unless a tool is attached, the TOOL DETACH instruction cannot be executed.

### 3.19.9.7 TOOL-007 Another process is executing.

Cause: Another program is executing a TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction.

Remedy: After the TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction being executed by the other program is completed, rerun the program.

### 3.19.9.8 TOOL-008 Tool identify signal is OFF.

Cause: The servo tool identification signal is OFF.

Remedy: Check whether the tool number taught in the instruction and the actual tool match. Check whether the servo tool identification signal is set correctly.

### 3.19.9.9 TOOL-009 Tool set signal is OFF.

Cause: The servo tool mount signal is OFF.

Remedy: Check whether the tool is mounted correctly. Check whether the servo tool mount signal is set correctly.

### 3.19.9.10 TOOL-010 Tool Change canceled.

Cause: The TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction is canceled while executing the instruction.

Remedy: Perform a cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1852 -->

### 3.19.9.11 TOOL-011 Tool Change timeout.

Cause: The TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction times out while executing the instruction.

Remedy: Perform a cold start:

1. Turn off the robot.
2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys.
3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.9.12 TOOL-012 Tool mastering data is lost.

Cause: Mastering data of a servo tool was lost because of an unexpected stop during mastering of the tool.

Remedy:

1. The tool pulse values and mastering data are lost. So, first move the tool by manual feed to cancel the “SRVO-075 Pulse not established” alarm. This alarm may not be occurring. If so, skip this step and proceed to the next step.
2. Next, carry out tool 0 position mastering and calibration manually.

### 3.19.9.13 TOOL-013 Tool mastering is failed.

Cause: Tool mastering failed.

Remedy: Continue to retry mastering.

### 3.19.9.14 TOOL-014 TOOL ATTACH is failed (G%d)

Cause: The TOOL ATTACH instruction failed. Refer to the cause code for details.

Remedy: Refer to the cause code for details.

### 3.19.9.15 TOOL-015 TOOL DETACH is failed (G%d)

Cause: The TOOL DETACH instruction failed.

Remedy: See the cause code for more information.

<!-- PDF page 1853 -->

### 3.19.9.16 TOOL-016 Robot not mastered(Tool axis).

Cause: Mastering of the servo tool axis has not been performed.

Remedy: Perform mastering of the servo tool axis.

### 3.19.9.17 TOOL-017 Robot not calibrated(Tool axis).

Cause: The servo tool axis has not been calibrated.

Remedy: Calibrate the servo tool axis.

### 3.19.9.18 TOOL-018 Ref pos not set(Tool axis).

Cause: A reference position required for quick mastering is not set.

Remedy: Set the reference position.

### 3.19.9.19 TOOL-019 Another tool is attached.

Cause: The attached tool is not the tool specified in the TOOL ATTACH instruction.

Remedy: Check the tool number specified in the TOOL ATTACH instruction.

### 3.19.9.20 TOOL-020 Calibrate motion is failed.

Cause: The detection condition (touch torque or the detection signal) was not satisfied during calibration.

Remedy: Check the detection condition on the Tool Change SETUP screen. REMEDY 1

1. The tool pulse values and mastering data are lost. So, move the tool by manual feed to cancel the “SRVO-075 Pulse not established” alarm.
2. Carry out tool 0 position mastering and calibration manually. The tool 0 position may be an approximate position.
3. Execute the detach instruction to temporarily detach the tool. Also, physically detach the tool from the robot. Otherwise, the tool will not be calibrated at the next attach operation.
4. Execute the attach instruction again to attach the tool. Calibration this time is carried out at the reference position to restore the position.

REMEDY 2

<!-- PDF page 1854 -->

1. Directly change the system variable to detach the tool. To do this, set the following system variable to 0:
$SCR_GRP[servo tool operation group No. (normally, 2)].$AXISORDER[all 1 to 9]
2. Turn the controller power OFF then back ON.
3. The robot starts up with the tool in a detached state. Move the robot by manual feed to physically attach the robot and tool.
4. Execute the attach instruction to attach the tool.

### 3.19.9.21 TOOL-021 PR[] index is not set.

Cause: For the calibration motion type 3 to 6, no position register number is set.

Remedy: Set the position register number on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

### 3.19.9.22 TOOL-022 Touch torque is not set.

Cause: For the calibration motion type 3 or 4, no touch torque is set.

Remedy: Set touch torque on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

### 3.19.9.23 TOOL-023 Detect signal is not set.

Cause: For the calibration motion type 5 or 6, no detection signal is set.

Remedy: Set the detection signal on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

### 3.19.9.24 TOOL-024 Tool does not stop.

Cause: At the calibration motion, Servo tool axis does not stop.

Remedy: After servo tool axis stops, execute calibration motion

### 3.19.9.25 TOOL-025 Illegal AXISORDER.

Cause: $SCR_GRP[].$AXISORDER[] of the tool was set to an illegal value.

Remedy: Set $SCR_GRP[].$AXISORDER[] of the tool to zero, and turn off and on the controller.

<!-- PDF page 1855 -->

### 3.19.9.26 TOOL-026 Battery type OFF.

Cause: The battery type of the multi-axis tool was set to OFF.

Remedy: Set the battery type of the multi-axis tool to ON.

### 3.19.9.27 TOOL-027 Timeout G%d A%d %x %d

Cause: A timeout occurred during Tool-attach or -detach at the start.

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

### 3.19.9.28 TOOL-028 Internal error

Cause: System internal error

Remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

### 3.19.10 TPIF Alarm Code

### 3.19.10.1 TPIF-001 Mnemonic editor error (%s^1)

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.2 TPIF-002 Operating system error (%s^1)

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

<!-- PDF page 1856 -->

### 3.19.10.3 TPIF-003 Window I/O error (%s^1)

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.4 TPIF-004 Memory write error

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.5 TPIF-005 Program is not selected

Cause: The program was not selected yet, when the program was displayed at the TEACH screen.

Remedy: Select a program in the SELECT screen.

### 3.19.10.6 TPIF-006 SELECT is not taught

Cause: This taught statement needed the SELECT statement before the current line.

Remedy: Teach the SELECT statement before the current line.

### 3.19.10.7 TPIF-007 Robot is not calibrated

Cause: The robot has not been calibrated properly.

Remedy: Calibrate the robot properly..

### 3.19.10.8 TPIF-008 Memory protect violation

Cause: The program is write protected.

Remedy: Release protection of the program on the SELECT screen.

<!-- PDF page 1857 -->

### 3.19.10.9 TPIF-009 Cancel delete by application

Cause: Program is protected

Remedy: Release protection of the program on the SELECT screen then delete the program.

### 3.19.10.10 TPIF-010 Cancel enter by application

Cause: Program is protected

Remedy: Try edit after release protection by application

### 3.19.10.11 TPIF-011 Item is not found

Cause: Item is not found below this line

Remedy: Try another item or close search function

### 3.19.10.12 TPIF-012 Kinematics solution is invalid

Cause: Cannot translate position data

Remedy: Check the configuration of robot and $MNUTOOL/$MNUFRAM system variables

### 3.19.10.13 TPIF-013 Other program is running

Cause: You cannot select a program when another program is running or paused.

Remedy: Select a program after aborting the program which is currently run ning or paused.

### 3.19.10.14 TPIF-014 Teach pendant is disabled

Cause: You cannot edit a program when the teach pendant is disabled.

Remedy: First enable the teach pendant, then edit the program.

### 3.19.10.15 TPIF-015 Bad position register index

Cause: Specified aa invalid index of position register

Remedy: Check the index of position register

<!-- PDF page 1858 -->

### 3.19.10.16 TPIF-016 Memory access failed (%s^1)

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.20 TPIF-020 Mnaction search error

If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.35 TPIF-043 External change is valid

Remedy: Set system variable $MULTI_ROBO.CHANGE_SDI to ZERO

### 3.19.10.36 TPIF-044 Program is unsuitable for robot

Cause: The group mask of program differs from selected robot (group)

Remedy: Check selected robot (group) or check program attributes group mask

### 3.19.10.37 TPIF-045 Pallet number is over max

Cause: Cannot teach more than 16 Palletizing instructions in one program,

Remedy: Teach another program.

### 3.19.10.38 TPIF-046 Motion option is over max

Cause: Too many motion options for default motion

Remedy: Decrease motion options for default motion

### 3.19.10.39 TPIF-047 Invalid program is selected

Cause: Program type is wrong

Remedy: Select TPE program

### 3.19.10.40 TPIF-048 Running program is not found

Cause: There is currently no program running that can be monitored.

### 3.19.10.41 TPIF-049 Port number is invalid

<!-- PDF page 1862 -->

Remedy: Set port for outside device

### 3.19.10.42 TPIF-050 Macro does not exist

Cause: A program is not assigned to this macro command

Remedy: Assign a program to this macro command

### 3.19.10.43 TPIF-051 Program has been selected by PNS

Cause: When a program has been selected by PNS, you cannot select program from SELECT screen

Remedy: Turn off the PNSTROBE signal.

### 3.19.10.44 TPIF-052 FWD/BWD is disabled

Cause: When the Disabled FWD function has been selected, you cannot execute the program by TP

Remedy: Select the Disabled FWD in the function menu, then you can release from the Disable FWD

### 3.19.10.45 TPIF-053 Not editing background program

Cause: The program has not been selected by BACKGROUND editing

Remedy: Select the BACKGROUND program in the SELECT screen

### 3.19.10.46 TPIF-054 Could not end editing

### 3.19.10.48 TPIF-056 This program is used by the CRT

Cause: The program of BACKGROUND cannot be selected by the CRT and TP at the same time

Remedy: End editing by the END_EDIT of [EDCMD] at the CRT

### 3.19.10.49 TPIF-057 This program is used by the TP

Cause: The program of BACKGROUND cannot be selected by the CRT and TP at the same time

Remedy: End editing by the END_EDIT of [EDCMD] at the TP

### 3.19.10.50 TPIF-060 Can't record on cartesian (G:%d)

Cause: This current position is in singularity

Remedy: You can record this position on joint type only by selecting the function key.

### 3.19.10.51 TPIF-061 Group[%s] has not recorded

Cause: This position data has not been changed to displayed groups because you selected the function key which did not record the position, when checking in singularity

Remedy: Check this recorded position again before execution

### 3.19.10.52 TPIF-062 AND operator was replaced to OR

Cause: All AND operators on this line were replaced with OR operators.

Remedy: You cannot mix AND and OR operator on a the same line. Verify that all logical operators on this line are the same before execution.

### 3.19.10.53 TPIF-063 OR operator was replaced to AND

Cause: All OR operator on this line were replaced by AND operators. You cannot mix AND OR operaotr on a the same line

Remedy: Verify all logical operators on this line before execution

<!-- PDF page 1864 -->

### 3.19.10.54 TPIF-064 Too many AND/OR operator(Max.4)

Cause: Too many AND/OR operators (Max.4 on a single line)

Remedy: Teach the logical operation on another line

### 3.19.10.55 TPIF-065 Arithmetic operator was unified to +- or */

Cause: Arithmetic operator on this line was changed to +- or */. Cannot mix arithmetic + and - operators with * and / operators on the same line.

Remedy: Verify all arithmetic operators on this line before execution

### 3.19.10.56 TPIF-066 Too many arithmetic operator(Max.5)

Cause: Too many arithmetic operators (Max.5 on a single line)

Remedy: Teach the arithmetic operation on another line

### 3.19.10.57 TPIF-067 Too many arguments (Max.30)

Cause: Too many arguments (Max.30 for a program or a macro)

Remedy: Check arguments of the program/macro

### 3.19.10.58 TPIF-068 Too many items

Cause: This instruction contains too many items. You can add only a limited number of items to a line. It is limited by the fact that a single line can be only 255 bytes long. The number of items depends on how much memory each item takes.

Remedy: Split this long complex line into several simpler lines.

### 3.19.10.59 TPIF-069 Use background edit

Cause: You cannot foreground edit a program from the CRT or from the Internet. You can only edit using a background program.

Remedy: Select the BACKGROUND program in the SELECT screen.

<!-- PDF page 1865 -->

### 3.19.10.60 TPIF-070 Cannot teach the instruction

Cause: Cannot teach the instruction.

Remedy: Check the sub type of the program.

### 3.19.10.61 TPIF-071 Cannot change sub type

Cause: Cannot change sub type

Remedy: Check sub type of the program

### 3.19.10.62 TPIF-072 Cannot change motion group

Cause: Cannot change motion group

Remedy: Check sub type of the program

### 3.19.10.63 TPIF-090 This program has motion group

Cause: The program specified in $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI and $PWR_NORMAL must not have motion group.

Remedy: Set * to all motion group in program detail screen on TP.

### 3.19.10.64 TPIF-091 PREG access error

Cause: An error occurred when accessing a position register.

Remedy: Refer to the error cause code on the ALARM log screen.

### 3.19.10.65 TPIF-092 Value %d expected %s

Cause: The value_array that was passed to a built-in was incorrectly specified. The error line shows the index into value_array where the error occurred and the type expected by the built-in.

Remedy: Make sure the value_array specifies the correct names for the variables and that the types expected are correct.

<!-- PDF page 1866 -->

### 3.19.10.66 TPIF-093 USER menu must be selected

Cause: A KAREL program called a user interface built-in which required the USER menu to be displayed on the teach pendant or CRT.

Remedy: Use FORCE_SPMENU(tp_panel, SPI_TPUSER, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the teach pendant. Use FORCE_SPMENU(crt_panel, SPI_TPUSER, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the CRT.

### 3.19.10.67 TPIF-094 USER2 menu must be selected

Cause: A KAREL program called a user interface built-in which required the USER2 menu to be displayed on the teach pendant or CRT.

Remedy: Use FORCE_SPMENU(tp_panel, SPI_TPUSER2, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the teach pendant. Use FORCE_SPMENU(crt_panel, SPI_TPUSER2, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the CRT.

### 3.19.10.68 TPIF-095 Execution history table error

Cause: Software internal error

Remedy: Perform a controlled start (it is not necessary to re-set the new item)

### 3.19.10.69 TPIF-097 Can't display running task's history

Cause: The execution history of the executing program cannot be displayed

Remedy: Use this screen when the program is paused or aborted.

### 3.19.10.70 TPIF-098 %s was not run

Cause: The program of $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI or $PWR_NORMAL is not executed

Remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use the Alarm Log screen.

### 3.19.10.71 TPIF-099 This program is being edited

Cause: The program specified in $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI and $PWR_NORMAL is not executed, when the program is in editing.

Remedy: Select the other program

<!-- PDF page 1867 -->

### 3.19.10.72 TPIF-100 No vacant table space

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.73 TPIF-101 No such menu

Cause: Illegal case occured on software.

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.74 TPIF-102 E.STOP is asserted

Cause: FWD execution is selected while, E.STOP is asserted.

Remedy: Turn the E.STOP off. Then select FWD execution

### 3.19.10.75 TPIF-103 Dead man is released

Cause: FWD execution is selected while, DEADMAN switch is released.

Remedy: Press and hold down the DEADMAN, then select FWD execution

### 3.19.10.76 TPIF-104 Teach Pendant is disabled

Cause: FWD execution is selected while, TP is disabled.

Remedy: Enable the teach pendant. Then select FWD execution.

### 3.19.10.77 TPIF-105 Program is not selected

Cause: FWD execution is requested without selection of program.

Remedy: Select a proram for execution Then select FWD execution

<!-- PDF page 1868 -->

### 3.19.10.78 TPIF-106 Program is already running

Cause: FWD execution is requested when program is running.

Remedy: Abort the running program before requesting FWD execution

### 3.19.10.79 TPIF-107 FWD/BWD is disabled

Cause: When the Disabled FWD function has been selected, you cannot execute the program by TP

Remedy: Select the Disabled FWD in the function menu, then you can release from the Disable FWD

### 3.19.10.80 TPIF-108 Form error, line %d, item %d

Cause: The Form Manager detected an error on the specified line with the specified item.

Remedy: Refer to the cause code on the ALARM log screen for the actual error.

### 3.19.10.81 TPIF-109 %v not specified correctly

Cause: The Form Manager detected an error when displaying a %v item.

Remedy: To specify the %v enumeration type in a form dictionary, use lower case v followed by the dictionary element which specifies the program name and variable name of the variable which contains the display values. For example: "Enum Type: " "-%6v(enum_fkey)" $-,enum_fkey "TPEX" &new_line "CHOICE_ARRAY" In the above example, CHOICE_ARRAY is a KAREL string array variable in program TPEX which contains the enumeration choices. The enumeration choices are displayed in a subwindow.

### 3.19.10.82 TPIF-110 Screen used by other device

Cause: The screen you are attempting to use on the TP is currently displayed on CRT or the screen you are attempting to use on the CRT is currently displayed on TP

Remedy: Exit from the screen on the other device

### 3.19.10.83 TPIF-116 System variable error: %s

Cause: System variable name is invalid

Remedy: Check the spelling and format of the name.

<!-- PDF page 1869 -->

### 3.19.10.84 TPIF-117 Cannot backup to device: %s

Cause: The default device is not valid for backup

Remedy: Select a valid device and try again

### 3.19.10.85 TPIF-118 File error for %s

Cause: File error

Remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

### 3.19.10.86 TPIF-119 File compression failed

Cause: Failed creating compressed file

Remedy: Check backup device

### 3.19.10.87 TPIF-120 Device failure

Cause: Device failure

Remedy: Check device and try again

### 3.19.10.88 TPIF-121 Invalid copy. Use MOVE key.

Cause: Cannot COPY a file on a Memory device to the same Memory device.

Remedy: Use the MOVE key and try again

### 3.19.10.89 TPIF-128 Verify logic of pasted line(s)

Cause: The reverse motion copy function does not support the following motion option instruction. 1. Application command 2. Skip, Quick Skip 3. Incremental 4. Continuous turn 5. Time before

Remedy: Check the above motion option instruction. And modify the copied statement correctly.

<!-- PDF page 1870 -->

# **3.19.10.91 TPIF-131 Please set application mask data**

**Cause:** This program has no application mask or the equipment mask does not agree with the TP Header Detail.

**Remedy:** Please set the application mask in the program detail screen. For irCalibration, make sure the selected program used with Program name has no mask.

# **3.19.10.92 TPIF-132 Can't recover this operation**

**Cause:** Because the data for UNDO can not be saved, this operation can not recover by UNDO function
